title: [Dozer] Player resume-construction never paths the dozer so scaffolds never progress
description:
## C++
`DozerAIUpdate::privateResumeConstruction` (DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1836) -> `newTask(DOZER_TASK_BUILD, obj)` (1943) computes dock points via `findGoodBuildOrRepairPositionAndTarget`, then `DozerActionPickActionPosState::update` issues `ai->aiMoveToPosition(&goalPos, CMD_FROM_AI)` (line ~228) so the dozer physically walks to the scaffold before `DozerActionDoActionState` builds. Same flow in WorkerAIUpdate.cpp.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/Main/src/command_executor/construct.rs` `execute_resume_construction` (~223) only calls `self.game_logic.resume_construction(units, target_id)`. `world_scripts/rebuild_dozer.rs` `resume_construction` (853-885) sets `target`/`AIState::Constructing`/`builder_id` but never issues a path. The AI path explicitly compensates (Main/src/ai.rs:708-712: "resume_construction creates the authoritative dock; this command restores the corresponding movement/path" -> `unit_command_begin_construct`); the player path does not. `world_tick/production.rs` `update_construction` only progresses when the dozer is within `BUILDER_RANGE = 30.0` of the building, and `world_objects/support_states.rs` has no Constructing approach branch (Repairing only).

## Evidence
- construct.rs:229 `if self.game_logic.resume_construction(units, target_id)` — no movement call, contrast construct.rs:125 `path_to_goal_with_state(unit_id, location, AIState::Constructing)` in `execute_dozer_construct` and leftover.rs:545 `begin_support_order(..., AIState::Repairing)` in `execute_repair`.
- rebuild_dozer.rs:860-867 sets state/builder only.
- production.rs:10 `BUILDER_RANGE: f32 = 30.0` gates `nearby_dozers`.
- rebuild_dozer.rs:841-846 `can_resume_construction_of` returns false while any same-player dozer is `Constructing` on the target — the wedged dozer also blocks reassignment.

## Player-visible
Select dozer, right-click / Alt+E resume on a distant unfinished building: dozer never moves, shows the constructing state, building percent stays 0 forever, and no other dozer can be assigned (resume of others refused). Only the skirmish-AI path actually walks there.
close_reason: Live resume_construction now paths via path_approach_with_state to dozer_repair_approach_position (C++ DozerAIUpdate::privateResumeConstruction -> newTask -> DozerActionPickActionPosState::update aiMoveToPosition, DozerAIUpdate.cpp:1837/1948/211). Player execute_resume_construction uses that GameLogic path.

title: [SlowDeath] Live SlowDeathBehavior never dispatched
description:
## C++
SlowDeathBehavior is a Die+Update module; onDie begins death, update runs phases.

## Rust
contain_module_overrides/death.rs boxes concrete SlowDeathBehavior; object/mod.rs dispatch_update/disabled_mask/phase macros lack SlowDeathBehavior; module_die_kind does not recognize it. Proxy warns 'No update dispatcher' and sleeps Forever.

## Evidence
dispatch lists ~1854-2140; factory 251-267; call_on_die_hooks requires module_die_kind.

## Player-visible
INI SlowDeath never runs; host residual uses hardcoded infantry/vehicle timings.
close_reason: Live SlowDeathBehavior now dispatched: module_die_kind + ModuleUpdateProxy::dispatch_update/disabled_mask/phase downcast the concrete type boxed by contain_module_overrides/death.rs (C++ SlowDeathBehavior::onDie/update, SlowDeathBehavior.h getInterfaceMask UPDATE|DIE). Initial wake is UPDATE_SLEEP_FOREVER until beginSlowDeath.

title: [TerrainLogic] Edge-point spawns use max pathfind extent instead of active boundary extent
description:
C++:
TerrainLogic.cpp:2036-2116 findClosestEdgePoint/findFarthestEdgePoint both call getExtent(). W3DTerrainLogic::getExtent (W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:176-193) returns the ACTIVE boundary: hi = m_boundaries[m_activeBoundary] * MAP_XY_FACTOR.

Rust:
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs find_closest_edge_point / find_farthest_edge_point call self.get_maximum_pathfind_extent(), i.e. the LARGEST boundary, not get_extent() (the active-boundary version that already exists and is used by action_manager is_point_on_map).

Evidence:
Callers on both sides: OCL CreateAtEdge* (paradrop, A10 strike, artillery barrage, aurora, carpet bomb, fuel air bomb, nuclear missile, OCLUpdate, OCLSpecialPower), SpectreGunshipDeploymentUpdate edge spawns, DeliverPayloadAIUpdate map-enter point, AIUpdate guard-position clamp, GameLogicDispatch beacon placement. After a ChangeMapBoundary/setActiveBoundary script shrinks the playable area, Rust still picks edge points on the old largest boundary.

Player-visible:
On campaign/skirmish maps that shrink the map boundary mid-game, aircraft (Spectre, paradrops, strikes) and OCL spawns enter from off-map edges of the OLD boundary instead of the shrunken playable area; guard positions and beacons clamp to the wrong edge.
close_reason: Live find_closest_edge_point/find_farthest_edge_point now call get_extent() (active boundary, W3DTerrainLogic.cpp:176-193) instead of get_maximum_pathfind_extent(), matching TerrainLogic.cpp:2039 and :2091 getExtent().

title: [TerrainLogic] Bridge attack-point fallback returns map origin instead of bridge object position
description:
C++:
TerrainLogic.cpp:1905-1934 getBridgeAttackPoints: when no Bridge in the list matches the object ID, both attack points fall back to the bridge OBJECT position: attackInfo->attackPoint1/2 = *bridge->getPosition().

Rust:
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs:3311-3356 get_bridge_attack_points: fallback sets attack_point1/2 = Coord3D::origin() (0,0,0). Also weapon_range.rs leaves the freshly-newed (origin) info untouched when the terrain lock fails.

Evidence:
Rust callers that consume the fallback: weapon/weapon_range.rs:63-78 (is_within_attack_range, KindOf::Bridge targets), ai/turret.rs:534-538, weapon/weapon_template.rs:739-742. C++ callers: Weapon.cpp:822, 2165, 2256; TurretAI.cpp:1006; AIUpdate.cpp:1886. Any bridge-kind object not registered in TerrainLogic bridge list (script/OCL-created bridge objects, or lock unavailable) gets range-measured against the map corner.

Player-visible:
Units/turrets engaging an unregistered bridge object compute distance to (0,0,0): weapons show out-of-range and never fire, or fire from absurd ranges; turret target-point picking lands at the map corner.
close_reason: Live TerrainLogic::get_bridge_attack_points fallback now copies the bridge object position (TheGameLogic::find_object_by_id) for both attack points when no Bridge list entry matches, matching TerrainLogic.cpp:1936-1937 getBridgeAttackPoints. Origin remains only if the object itself is gone.

title: [AIGroup] Live tighten dissolves stamped formations; C++ never tightens them
description:
## C++
`groupMoveToPosition` (`AIGroup.cpp:1559-1566`) only tests the click-to-gather rect when `!isFormation`. A stamped formation always takes `friend_computeGroundPath` + `friend_moveFormationToPos` (`:1612-1615`) and is never tightened. Helipad/aircraft members can force `isFormation = FALSE`.

## Rust
Live `execute_move` (`command_executor/movement.rs:26-32`) calls `should_tighten_group_move` **before** any formation check. `execute_tighten_to_position` → `unit_command_tighten_to` (`unit_commands.rs:434-461`) does `set_formation(0, ZERO)` and paths every member to the raw click.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:1559-1566`, `:1612-1615`
- Live `movement.rs:26-32`; `unit_commands.rs:434-461`

## Player-visible
A player who created a formation and clicks inside the group's footprint gets the formation dissolved and every unit crammed onto the click. Retail slides the formation as a shape.
close_reason: leftover group_move_to_position only tightens when !is_formation; stamped formations take friend_move_formation_to_pos (GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs). Live execute_move matches.

title: [AIGroup] Live group-path distance counts aircraft and no-AI members
description:
## C++
`friend_computeGroundPath` (`AIGroup.cpp:517-549`) only measures distance for members with `AIUpdateInterface` that are `KINDOF_INFANTRY` or `KINDOF_VEHICLE`. Aircraft `continue` (`:542-544`); no-AI objects are skipped (`:537-539`).

## Rust
Leftover `friend_compute_ground_path` ports the C++ filters (dual-world gated).
Live `compute_ground_path_should_group` (`command_executor/group.rs:281-292`) sets `closest_sqr` from **every alive member** — aircraft, structures, no-AI props included. That value then fails the `min_d` / `distanceRequiresGroup` tests (`:302-304`).

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:534-549`
- Live `group.rs:281-304`; callers `movement.rs:33`, `:51`

## Player-visible
Select jets + tanks and order a short/medium move: the aircraft's distance to the click suppresses group pathing, so the tanks fan out individually. Retail ignores aircraft distance and group-paths the ground units.
close_reason: leftover friend_compute_ground_path measures only AI infantry/vehicle (skips aircraft/no-AI). Live compute_ground_path_should_group matches.

title: [AIGroup] Live group special power fires only the first caster
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupDoSpecialPower` / `AtLocation` / `AtObject` (`AIGroup.cpp:2614-2735`) loop **every** member. Each object with a matching `SpecialPowerModule`, science, and `canDoSpecialPower*` fires `doSpecialPower*`.
`getSpecialPowerSourceObject` (`:3170-3186`) is only a cursor/ActionManager query (first capable member), **not** the fire loop.
Dispatch (`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:653-745`) calls `currentlySelectedGroup->groupDoSpecialPower*` on the whole selection.

## Rust
Leftover `group_do_special_power*` (`ai/group.rs:986-1018`) fans the leftover common helper (dual-world gated).
Live `execute_special_power` (`command_executor/special_power.rs:179-187`) comments that C++ "only the module owner fires" and sets `casters = vec![src]` from `special_power_source_object` (first living member whose cooldown map contains the power). Fallback to all units only when **no** member tracks the power.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:2614-2735` vs `:3170-3186`
- Live `special_power.rs:70-90`, `:179-187`

## Player-visible
Multi-select four Tank Hunters and click TNT: one charge plants, three sit idle. Same for any duplicated unit special power (demo charge, microwave, etc.). Retail fires every selected unit that can do the power.
close_reason: leftover group_do_special_power* already fans every capable member. Live execute_special_power now fires all tracked casters.

title: [AIGroup] Live combat drop never unloads / rappels passengers
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupCombatDrop` (`AIGroup.cpp:2867-2889`) calls `ai->aiCombatDrop(target, pos, cmdSource)` on each member. The transport flies to the target and rappels/unloads passengers there.

## Rust
Leftover `group_combat_drop` (`ai/group.rs:1343+`) exists on the leftover path (dual-world gated).
Live `execute_combat_drop` (`command_executor/transport.rs:614-643`) only `path_to_goal_with_state(..., AIState::Entering)` and optionally `unit_command_set_order_target`. Nothing unloads passengers at the drop zone. Host combat-chinook residual documents rappel/combat-drop as fail-closed.

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:2867-2889`
- Live `transport.rs:614-643`

## Player-visible
Chinook combat drop (Alt+C / combat-drop command): the transport flies to the marked point and hovers with troops still aboard. Troops never rappel out.
close_reason: leftover group_combat_drop fans aiCombatDrop. Live execute_combat_drop now move-to-and-evacuates so passengers unload.

title: [AIGroup] Mixed infantry+vehicle groups never column-pack
description:
## C++
`groupMoveToPosition` (`AIGroup.cpp:1550-1553`) calls `friend_moveInfantryToPos` then `friend_moveVehicleToPos` on the **same** member list. Each pass packs only its kind (infantry 3-col, vehicles 2-col). The later free-move loop skips already-columned infantry/vehicles (`:1637-1650`).

## Rust
Live `group_column_destinations` (`command_executor/movement.rs:456-461`) requires `all_infantry || all_vehicles`. Any mixed selection returns `None` and falls through to nearest-unit offset free-move (or a single shared spine).

## Evidence
- C++ `AIGroup.cpp:1550-1553`, `:1637-1650`
- Live `movement.rs:456-461`

## Player-visible
Select Rangers + Paladins and move across the map: retail marches infantry 3-abreast and tanks 2-abreast. Live moves the whole blob as offsets/one spine — units jam and mill at the destination.
close_reason: leftover group_move_to_position calls friend_move_infantry then friend_move_vehicle on the same list. Live group_column_destinations packs kinds independently.

title: [Selection] Ctrl+digit CREATE_TEAM stores non-locally-controlled units
description:
## C++
`SelectionXlat.cpp:1031-1059` `MSG_META_CREATE_TEAM0-9` walks drawables and appends IDs only when `drawable->isSelected() && drawable->getObject() && drawable->getObject()->isLocallyControlled()`.

## Rust
Live host Ctrl+digit (`hotkeys.rs:12-19`) `self.control_groups.insert(group_num, self.selected_objects.clone())` with no locally-controlled filter. Point-select can include enemies/allies (`mouse.rs:361-370` `is_point_selectable_click_target`), so those IDs are baked into the group.

## Evidence
C++ SelectionXlat.cpp:1051 `isLocallyControlled()`.
Host hotkeys.rs:18 `selected_objects.clone()`.

## Player-visible effect
Ctrl+N after selecting an enemy or allied unit stores that unit in the control group. Recalling the group can re-select or camera-jump to units the player does not own.
close_reason: Live CREATE_TEAM local-only + leftover Player.squads write; Shift+# ADD_TEAM; MaxSelectionSize via host_set_selection; SELECT_HERO first-hero lookAt+contain unwrap; SELECT_ALL skips IGNORES_SELECT_ALL; drag-box rejects structures; SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT=KINDOF_AIRCRAFT; lookAt last live; CREATE evicts other squads; VIEW_TEAM group>=1

title: [LookAt] RMB scroll never mouse-locks or restores the previous cursor
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp:50-77` `setScrolling` saves `prevCursor`, `TheInGameUI->setScrolling(TRUE)`, `TheTacticalView->setMouseLock(TRUE)`, and starts StatsCollector scroll time. `stopScrolling` clears scrolling, unlocks the mouse, and restores `prevCursor`.

## Rust
Live host RMB down (`input.rs:470-477`) only sets `rmb_scroll_anchor` / `is_rmb_scrolling`. RMB up (`input.rs:528-530`) only clears those flags. No mouse lock, no cursor save/restore, no InGameUI scrolling flag. Leftover crate `look_at_xlat.rs:100-114` sets InGameUI scrolling and forces arrow cursor but is unused.

## Evidence
C++ LookAtXlat.cpp:55-70 `setMouseLock(TRUE)` / `setCursor(prevCursor)`.
Host input.rs:474-475, 528-529 flag-only.

## Player-visible effect
During RMB-drag the OS cursor can leave the window and the previous cursor (select/attack/build) is not restored when the drag ends.
close_reason: Host start/stop_rmb_lookat_scroll saves prev cursor, TheInGameUI setScrolling, tactical setMouseLock; leftover look_at_xlat.rs matches. input.rs RMB down/up wired.

title: [Selection] Shift+digit mutates the stored group instead of adding it to selection
description:
## C++
`SelectionXlat.cpp:1136-1213` `MSG_META_ADD_TEAM0-9` (Shift+digit) does **not** rewrite the stored squad. If not a double-tap, it deselects a currently selected structure (Jan 2005 group force-attack exploit), posts `MSG_ADD_TEAMN`, and `selectDrawable`s the squad’s live objects onto the current selection. Double-tap within 20 frames `lookAt`s the last live member.

## Rust
Live host `handle_control_group_hotkey` Shift branch (`hotkeys.rs:26-41`) **writes the current selection into `control_groups[n]`**. It never selects the stored group, never deselects a structure, and never lookAts. Leftover crate SelectionTranslator is not on the OS path.

## Evidence
C++ SelectionXlat.cpp:1183-1205 structure deselect then select squad members.
Host hotkeys.rs:31-36 `entry.push(*id)` into the stored group.

## Player-visible effect
Shift+1 in retail adds group 1 to the current selection. In the port it silently grows group 1’s roster from whatever is selected and does not change the on-screen selection.
close_reason: Live CREATE_TEAM local-only + leftover Player.squads write; Shift+# ADD_TEAM; MaxSelectionSize via host_set_selection; SELECT_HERO first-hero lookAt+contain unwrap; SELECT_ALL skips IGNORES_SELECT_ALL; drag-box rejects structures; SELECT_ALL_AIRCRAFT=KINDOF_AIRCRAFT; lookAt last live; CREATE evicts other squads; VIEW_TEAM group>=1

title: [LookAt] Arrow keys still pan during box-select and RMB-drag
description:
## C++
`LookAtXlat.cpp:174-175` on RAW_KEY: `if (TheInGameUI->isSelecting() || (m_isScrolling && m_scrollType != SCROLL_KEY)) break;` Arrow keys cannot start or stop keyboard scroll while a selection box is being dragged, and cannot start while RMB-scrolling.

## Rust
Live host `update_camera` (`mouse.rs:1011-1030`) only gates on Ctrl/Shift/Alt and chat/diplomacy. `is_dragging` is set for box-select (`mouse.rs:220`) but never consulted. RMB + arrow vectors accumulate into the same `screen_scroll` (`mouse.rs:1074-1103`). Leftover crate `look_at_xlat.rs:246-250` has the C++ gate but is not on the OS path.

## Evidence
C++ LookAtXlat.cpp:174 `isSelecting() || (m_isScrolling && m_scrollType != SCROLL_KEY)`.
Host mouse.rs:1016-1031 no `is_dragging` / `is_rmb_scrolling` check.

## Player-visible effect
Dragging a selection box while tapping arrows pans the camera under the rubber-band. RMB-drag plus arrows double-scrolls. Neither happens in retail.
close_reason: update_camera gates arrow pan with lookat_keyboard_scroll_blocked(is_dragging, is_rmb_scrolling) matching LookAtXlat.cpp:174-175.

title: [LookAt] doDisableInput resetModes never clears live host camera modes
description:
## C++
`ScriptActions.cpp:3188` `doDisableInput` calls `TheLookAtTranslator->resetModes()` so scroll/rotate/pitch/FOV flags drop when a cinematic or script disables input (`LookAtXlat.h:22`).

## Rust
`script_action_handler.rs:383` `request_look_at_reset_modes()` sets a `LOOK_AT_RESET` atomic. The only drain is leftover crate `look_at_xlat.rs:230` `take_look_at_reset_modes()` — host `mouse.rs` / `input.rs` never read it. `is_rmb_scrolling`, `is_mmb_rotating`, `mmb_anchor`, and `camera_*_held` survive the cinematic.

## Evidence
C++ ScriptActions.cpp doDisableInput → resetModes.
Rust script_action_handler.rs:386-394 store-only; host never calls `take_look_at_reset_modes`.

## Player-visible effect
Start an RMB-drag or KP-rotate, have a mission script disable input, then after input returns the camera keeps scrolling/rotating from the stale gesture.
close_reason: update_camera drains take_look_at_reset_modes() into apply_look_at_reset_modes which clears RMB/MMB/key rotate-zoom flags.

title: [Die] EjectPilotDie air/ground split uses 1.0 height not 9.0 gravity
description:
## C++
`EjectPilotDie.cpp:86` picks `m_oclInAir` vs `m_oclOnGround` via `getObject()->isSignificantlyAboveTerrain()`. `Thing.cpp:308-313` implements that as `getHeightAboveTerrain() > -(3*3)*TheGlobalData->m_gravity`. Default gravity is `-1.0` (`GlobalData.cpp:810`), so the threshold is **9.0** (INI-tunable via Gravity).

## Rust
Live `eject_pilot_die.rs:266-270` correctly calls `object.is_significantly_above_terrain()`. The helper in `object_triggers.rs:230-232` is hardcoded `get_height_above_terrain() > 1.0` and never reads gravity.

## Evidence
C++ `Thing.cpp:308-313` `-(3*3)*m_gravity` with gravity -1 → 9.0. Rust `object_triggers.rs:232` `> 1.0`. Consumer `eject_pilot_die.rs:266-270`.

## Player-visible effect
A vehicle dying 1–9 world units above terrain (low-hover helo, bridge/ledge) ejects the **parachute** AirCreationList pilot in Rust, but the **standing** GroundCreationList pilot in ZH.
close_reason: EjectPilotDie::is_significantly_above_terrain now uses Thing::isSignificantlyAboveTerrain -(3*3)*m_gravity (Thing.cpp:308-313; default 9.0)

title: [Die] DieMux DeathTypes/VeterancyLevels parse starts from NONE not ALL
description:
## C++
`INI.cpp:1817-1846` `parseDeathTypeFlags` starts `flags = DEATH_TYPE_FLAGS_ALL` (and `parseVeterancyLevelFlags` at `:1727-1759` starts `VETERANCY_LEVEL_FLAGS_ALL`). Tokens must be `ALL`, `NONE`, `+Name`, or `-Name`. A subtractive-only line such as `DeathTypes = -SUICIDED` therefore means "all deaths except suicided".

## Rust
Live `object/die/mod.rs` `parse_death_type_flags_tokens` (`:78-113`) and `parse_veterancy_level_flags_tokens` (`:116-154`) start from `*_FLAGS_NONE`, then apply tokens. `DeathTypes = -SUICIDED` clears a bit on an empty mask and stays NONE. Same for `VeterancyLevels = -HEROIC`.

## Evidence
C++ `INI.cpp:1819` `DeathTypeFlags flags = DEATH_TYPE_FLAGS_ALL;` and `:1838-1841` `-` clears from that ALL default. Rust `die/mod.rs:83` `let mut flags = DEATH_TYPE_FLAGS_NONE;` then `:95-108` apply `+/-`. Defaults on the struct (`DieMuxData::default` `:221-222`) are still ALL; only the INI parser seed is wrong.

## Player-visible effect
Any die module authored with subtractive-only DieMux (`DeathTypes = -CRUSHED`, `VeterancyLevels = -HEROIC`, no leading ALL/NONE) never fires. C++ still runs those FX/OCL/crate/hole modules for every other death.
close_reason: parse_death_type_flags_tokens/parse_veterancy_level_flags_tokens start ALL like INI::parseDeathTypeFlags (INI.cpp:1819) and parseVeterancyLevelFlags (INI.cpp:1729)

title: [Die] RebuildHoleExposeDie setMaxHealth uses FullyHeal not SAME_CURRENTHEALTH
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:140-141` after spawning the hole: `body->setMaxHealth(modData->m_holeMaxHealth);`. `BodyModule.h:152` / `ActiveBody.h:81` default the second argument to `SAME_CURRENTHEALTH`. A freshly created hole starts at the template's max health; SAME_CURRENTHEALTH only changes the cap (clamping if current > new max). If `HoleMaxHealth` is *above* the template max, current health stays at the template value.

## Rust
Live `object/die/rebuild_hole_expose_die.rs:284-286` calls `set_max_health(hole_max_health, MaxHealthChangeType::FullyHeal)`, which raises the cap and heals to the new max.

## Evidence
C++ `RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:141` one-arg `setMaxHealth`. C++ default `MaxHealthChangeType healthChangeType = SAME_CURRENTHEALTH`. Rust `:286` explicit `FullyHeal`.

## Player-visible effect
GLA / rebuild holes whose INI `HoleMaxHealth` differs from the hole ThingTemplate max health spawn at full hole-max instead of keeping the template current health. Holes look healthier than ZH (or skip the intended "damaged foundation" HP) and take more hits to finish off.
close_reason: RebuildHoleExposeDie::create_hole set_max_health uses SameCurrentHealth matching RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:141 one-arg setMaxHealth (BodyModule.h:152)

title: [Die] DieMux death names drop NORMAL, NONE, and EXTRA_2
description:
## C++
`Damage.h:177-200` `TheDeathNames[]` is `NORMAL`, `NONE`, `CRUSHED`, …, `EXTRA_2`…`EXTRA_8`, `POISONED_GAMMA`. `INI::parseDeathTypeFlags` (`INI.cpp:1832-1841`) resolves `+Name`/`-Name` via `scanIndexList(..., TheDeathNames)`. `ALL -NORMAL` is the stock way to restrict a die module to non-gunfire deaths.

## Rust
Live `object/die/mod.rs` `death_type_from_name` (`:261-283`) has no `NORMAL` or `NONE` and only accepts `EXTRA2`…`EXTRA8` (no underscore). Unknown names are silently dropped (`:103-109`). PUC's sibling parser (`particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:284-306`) already lists `NORMAL`/`NONE`/`EXTRA_2`.

## Evidence
C++ `TheDeathNames[0]=="NORMAL"`, `[1]=="NONE"`, `[13]=="EXTRA_2"`. Rust match arms start at `"CRUSHED"` and use `"EXTRA2"`. `getDeathTypeFlag` / `get_death_type_flag` both use `(dt - 1)` so the C++ name *does* toggle the same quirky bit Rust would if it parsed the token.

## Player-visible effect
`DeathTypes = ALL -NORMAL` (very common on FXListDie / CreateObjectDie / special wreck modules) still fires on ordinary bullet/shell deaths. `+NONE` / `+EXTRA_2` authored filters are ignored.
close_reason: death_type_from_name now accepts NORMAL/NONE/EXTRA_2 like TheDeathNames (Damage.h:177-200)

title: [Main Loop] execute WaitUntil is added after drive_frame instead of including it
close_reason: Live WaitUntil uses execute_wait_deadline(prev_time, limit) so GameEngine::execute (GameEngine.cpp:856-866) includes update()+draw; period is max(work, limit) not work+limit.

title: [Main Loop] Live match reset never runs GameEngine::reset
description:
## C++
`GameEngine::reset` (`GameEngine.cpp:685-711`) is the map-teardown overlay:
1. `TheWindowManager->winCreateLayout("Menus/BlankWindow.wnd")`, unhide, bringForward, clear WIN_STATUS_IMAGE on first window
2. If `TheGameLogic->isInMultiplayerGame()`, remember to delete `TheNetwork`
3. `TheSubsystemList->resetAll()`
4. Delete `TheNetwork` if flagged
5. Destroy the BlankWindow layout

Callers: `GameLogicDispatch` new-game/clear (`GameLogicDispatch.cpp:256`), `GameState` load (`GameState.cpp:658,701`), `PopupSaveLoad` (`PopupSaveLoad.cpp:397`). Players see a black cover while subsystems reset so the previous map/UI cannot flash.

## Rust
Crate `GameEngine::reset` now has `show_blank_window_overlay` (hq-1t15 closed). The **live** host never calls it.

`reset_match_state` (`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/start_game.rs:1590-1596`) only `host_reset_game_logic()` + new `ResourceManager`. Boot `reset_all` runs once at end of `CnCGameEngine::new` (`boot.rs:638-645`, matching init's trailing `resetAll`), not on later new-game/load/exit-to-menu.

No live `BlankWindow.wnd`, no per-match `TheSubsystemList->resetAll()`, no MP `TheNetwork` teardown from `GameEngine::reset`.

## Evidence
```
// GameEngine.cpp:688-704
WindowLayout *background = TheWindowManager->winCreateLayout("Menus/BlankWindow.wnd");
...
TheSubsystemList->resetAll();
if (deleteNetwork) { delete TheNetwork; TheNetwork = NULL; }
```

```
// start_game.rs:1590-1596
pub(super) fn reset_match_state(&mut self) {
    ...
    self.host_reset_game_logic();
    self.resource_manager = ResourceManager::new();
```

## Player-visible effect
Starting a new skirmish, loading a save, or returning to the shell leaves the previous map/UI on screen (no BlankWindow cover) and leaves client/radar/audio/network subsystem state from the last match. Distinct from hq-1t15 (crate overlay exists; live run_loop/start_game never invokes GameEngine::reset).
close_reason: Live reset_match_state and complete_parked_match_start call host_game_engine_reset: BlankWindow.wnd + TheSubsystemList->resetAll + TheNetwork teardown (GameEngine::reset GameEngine.cpp:685-711).

title: [Main Loop] Live boot skips GameLODManager::init after command line
close_reason: CnCGameEngine::new calls load_game_lod_ini_presets_and_options after parseCommandLine, before Water/Weather — GameLODManager::init (GameEngine.cpp:360-361).

title: [Main Loop] Live run_loop never calls TheRadar->UPDATE
close_reason: drive_frame calls host_update_the_radar → RadarSystem::update before audio/client/logic — TheRadar->UPDATE (GameEngine.cpp:732).

title: [ThingFactory] Live new_object drops statusBits so onCreate misses UNDER_CONSTRUCTION
description:
## C++
`ThingFactory::newObject` (`ThingFactory.cpp:281-321`) passes `statusBits` into `TheGameLogic->friend_createObject(tmplate, statusBits, team)` **before** `CreateModuleInterface::onCreate()`. Comment at `:299-300`: status must be set prior to onCreate (constructing).

`BuildAssistant.cpp:361-368` sets `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION` on that mask for `KINDOF_STRUCTURE` so instant-build / dozer-like spawn does not fire power-creation and other create hooks as if the building were finished. `GrantUpgradeCreate::onCreate` (`GrantUpgradeCreate.cpp:62-67`) grants only when ExemptStatus includes UnderConstruction **and** the object is **not** currently under construction.

## Rust
Live spawn is `helpers/lookup.rs` `TheThingFactory::new_object` (`:583-620`), `new_object_with_team_handle`, and `new_object_optional_team`. All three always pass `ObjectCreationFlags::from_template()` (`object_manager.rs:95-97`, `status_mask: NONE`). There is no statusBits argument.

`object_factory.rs:228-252` constructs with `template.get_initial_object_status()`, then `init_modules_for`, then `init_object()` which runs `on_create` (`object_lifecycle.rs:209-214`).

Callers set UnderConstruction **after** that:
- `build_placement.rs:429-443` (player place)
- `impl_dozer.rs:229-260` (AI dozer)

`build_assistant_bridge.rs:56-82` never sets UnderConstruction at all (only `construction_percent = 0` and health 1).

Common leftover `thing_factory.rs:570-629` has a status_bits param and onCreate, but the live helper does not use it.

## Evidence
C++ `ThingFactory.cpp:281-321`, `BuildAssistant.cpp:361-368`, `GrantUpgradeCreate.cpp:59-67`.
Rust `helpers/lookup.rs:583-690`, `object_factory.rs:228-252`, `object_lifecycle.rs:209-214`, `build_assistant_bridge.rs:56-82`, `build_placement.rs:429-443`, `impl_dozer.rs:229-260`.

## Player-visible
Foundations run create modules as completed buildings: power plants add energy at place, GrantUpgradeCreate with ExemptStatus=UNDER_CONSTRUCTION grants on the pad, and AI/script instant-build via BuildAssistant never gets the bit so the same hooks fire twice (create + construction-complete).
close_reason: ThingFactory::newObject statusBits applied before CreateModuleInterface::onCreate (ThingFactory.cpp:281-321; BuildAssistant.cpp:361-368 UNDER_CONSTRUCTION).

title: [ThingFactory] Leftover Transport/Wander factories skip inherited AIUpdateModuleData
description:
## C++
`addModule(TransportAIUpdate)` / `addModule(WanderAIUpdate)` (`ModuleFactory.cpp:446-447`) use `classname::friend_newModuleData`.

Both classes use `MAKE_STANDARD_MODULE_MACRO` only (`TransportAIUpdate.h:21`, `WanderAIUpdate.h:21`) and inherit `AIUpdateInterface`, which defines `friend_newModuleData` via `MAKE_STANDARD_MODULE_MACRO_WITH_MODULE_DATA(AIUpdateInterface, AIUpdateModuleData)` (`AIUpdate.h:214`). Static lookup therefore creates **`AIUpdateModuleData`** and runs `AIUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse` (`AIUpdate.cpp:106-124`: Turret, AltTurret, AutoAcquireEnemiesWhenIdle, MoodAttackCheckRate, ForbidPlayerCommands, TurretsLinked).

Headers warn that any future custom data must inherit `AIUpdateModuleData` so locomotors keep working. Top-level `Locomotor = SET_*` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:220`) writes through `friend_getAIModuleInfo()` (`ThingTemplate.cpp:1029-1040`) which returns the first `isAiModuleData()` blob and C-casts it to `AIUpdateModuleData*`.

## Rust
Live leftover factory (`contain_module_overrides/leftover.rs:58-95`) uses `empty_ai_update_factories!` for TransportAIUpdate and WanderAIUpdate: data factory ignores INI and returns `TransportAIUpdateModuleData` / `WanderAIUpdateModuleData` default (tag key only, `transport_ai_update.rs:15-35`, `wander_ai_update.rs:14-34`). Those types set `is_ai_module_data() == true` but do **not** embed `AIUpdateModuleData`.

`template_locomotor.rs:80-83` explicitly cannot downcast those types; top-level Locomotor names stay on the ThingTemplate map. Live `object_factory.rs:335-343,596-648` only tests the **name** `TransportAIUpdate` / `WanderAIUpdate`, constructs `TransportAIUpdate::new(object_id)` with no module data, and never `or_else`s Transport/Wander into `ai_update_module_data` (unlike Chinook/Jet/Dozer/…). `apply_ai_update_module_data` therefore never runs for Transport/Wander-only units.

Leftover `TransportAIUpdateModule` / `WanderAIUpdateModule` are stub `Module`s (no Update). Live passenger-relay / wander tick is the parallel `UnitAIUpdate` path; INI locomotors/turrets still never reach it.

`module_overrides/ai.rs` archival factories are the same empty stubs and are not in the crate install path.

## Evidence
C++ `ModuleFactory.cpp:446-447`, `Module.h:115-149`, `AIUpdate.h:185,214`, `AIUpdate.cpp:106-124`, `ThingTemplate.cpp:220,1029-1040`, `TransportAIUpdate.h:21-27`, `WanderAIUpdate.h:21-27`.
Rust `leftover.rs:58-95`, `install.rs:454-470`, `template_locomotor.rs:46-83`, `object_factory.rs:335-343,596-671`, `transport_ai_update.rs:15-86`, `wander_ai_update.rs:14-85`.

## Player-visible
Humvees, APCs, Combat Cycles, Technicals, Battle Buses, and other `Behavior = TransportAIUpdate` units (and wander civilians/animals) never receive INI `Locomotor = SET_*`, Turret blocks, or AutoAcquire from that module. They sit still or use host defaults instead of retail loco sets.
close_reason: TransportAIUpdate/WanderAIUpdate inherit AIUpdateModuleData::buildFieldParse like ModuleFactory.cpp:446-447 / AIUpdate.h:214.

title: [SquishCollide] Host crush test uses selection-radius circle, not 1.0 victim geom
description:
## C++
`SquishCollide::onCollide` (`SquishCollide.cpp:79-86`) copies the victim `GeometryInfo`, forces `setMajorRadius(1.0f)` / `setMinorRadius(1.0f)`, then `ThePartitionManager->geomCollidesWithGeom` against the crusher's real geometry and orientation. The tank must actually overlap a 1-world-unit victim disk.

## Rust
Live host `within_squish_radius` (`host_squish_collide.rs:43-53`) is a 2D XZ circle: `dist <= crusher_radius.max(1.0) + 1.0`. `physics_motion.rs:181-182` passes `crusher_r = self.selection_radius.max(5.0)`, so the hit radius is typically selection_radius+1 (often 6-16 wu), not a 1.0 victim geom.

Crate `squish_collide.rs:413-429` ports the 1.0 major/minor geom copy but is not on the live host path.

## Evidence
C++: `myGeom.setMajorRadius(1.0f); myGeom.setMinorRadius(1.0f); geomCollidesWithGeom(...)`
Rust: `dist <= crusher_radius.max(1.0) + SQUISH_CRUSH_RADIUS` with `crusher_r = selection_radius.max(5.0)`

## Player-visible effect
Tanks and other crushers squash infantry from much farther away than retail. Near-misses that C++ would leave standing are instant crush kills.
close_reason: host_squish_collide.rs + physics_motion.rs: live crush uses victim GeometryInfo with major/minor forced to 1.0 then geomCollidesWithGeom (squish_geom_collides), not selection_radius+1 circle.

title: [SabotageSuperweapon] Host resets one special-power slot, not all modules
description:
## C++
`SabotageSuperweaponCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` and `SabotageCommandCenterCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`SabotageSuperweaponCrateCollide.cpp:117-126`, `SabotageCommandCenterCrateCollide.cpp:117-126`) walk every behavior module, take `getSpecialPower()`, and call `startPowerRecharge()` on each. A command center / strategy center / superweapon with multiple special powers (Spy, Emergency Repair, CIA, etc.) resets all timers.

## Rust
Live host `apply_superweapon_sabotage_recharge` (`heroes_and_plans.rs:219-238`) writes a single object-level `special_power_cooldown` / `special_power_ready` plus `special_power_strikes.reset_timers_for_source_object`. Comment: "Host Object has a single special-power slot residual — one startPowerRecharge." Crate sabotage modules walk `get_behavior_modules()` but are not the live saboteur path (`support_states.rs:2746` PendingSpecialAbility::Sabotage → host residual).

## Evidence
C++: `for (BehaviorModule **m = other->getBehaviorModules(); *m; ++m) { if (sp) sp->startPowerRecharge(); }`
Rust: `target.set_special_power_ready(false); target.special_power_cooldown_remaining = target.special_power_cooldown;`

## Player-visible effect
Sabotaging a Command Center or Strategy Center only rewinds one superweapon timer. Other ready special powers stay available.
close_reason: heroes_and_plans.rs apply_superweapon_sabotage_recharge walks every template SpecialPower module and leftover cooldown keys and startPowerRecharge()s each (Spy+Repair+CIA).

title: [SquishCollide] Host skip is template peel, not goal+Hijacker/TNT-active
description:
## C++
`SquishCollide::onCollide` (`SquishCollide.cpp:51-70`) skips crush only when the victim's AI `getGoalObject() == other` AND (`findUpdateModule("HijackerUpdate")` exists OR `findSpecialAbilityUpdate(SPECIAL_TANKHUNTER_TNT_ATTACK)` is active). A hijacker / tank hunter / Jarmen Kell that is not targeting the crusher is still squished.

## Rust
Live host residual `host_squish_collide::should_skip_squish_for_goal_ability` (`host_squish_collide.rs:56-59`) returns true for any template whose name contains `hijacker`, `jarmen`, or `tankhunter`, with no goal-object or ability-active test. `physics_motion.rs:176` applies that skip before the crush.

Crate `squish_collide.rs:174-202` matches C++ but is gated on `OBJECT_REGISTRY` (Wave 408 empty dual-world → no-op). Live crush is the host residual.

## Evidence
C++: `if (ai && ai->getGoalObject() == other) { if (hijackUpdate) return; if (saUpdate && saUpdate->isActive()) return; }`
Rust host: `n.contains("hijacker") || n.contains("jarmen") || n.contains("tankhunter")`

## Player-visible effect
Jarmen Kell, Tank Hunters, and Hijackers walking past tanks are never run over, even when they are not targeting the vehicle. C++ only protects them while they are actively hijacking or placing TNT.
close_reason: host_squish_collide.rs + physics_motion.rs: skip crush only when victim goal==crusher AND (HijackerUpdate exists OR SPECIAL_TANKHUNTER_TNT_ATTACK is active). Template peel alone no longer skips.

title: [SabotageSupplyDropzone] Host classify never treats dropzones
description:
## C++
`SabotageSupplyDropzoneCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`SabotageSupplyDropzoneCrateCollide.cpp:92-167`) requires `KINDOF_FS_SUPPLY_DROPZONE`, then `OCLUpdate::resetTimer()` plus the same cash-steal / EVA / GUI:AddCash/LoseCash path as supply centers. The saboteur is a mobile crate with this module in addition to SabotageSupplyCenterCrateCollide.

## Rust
Live `classify_sabotage_target` (`host_saboteur.rs:467-476`) explicitly skips drop zones ("drop zone module commented in retail") and only maps supply-center KindOf/names to `SupplyCenter`. No `FSSupplyDropzone` arm, no OCL timer reset. Crate `sabotage_supply_dropzone_crate_collide.rs:347-396` ports reset+steal but is not invoked from `PendingSpecialAbility::Sabotage`.

## Evidence
C++: `if (!other->isKindOf(KINDOF_FS_SUPPLY_DROPZONE)) return FALSE;` then `update->resetTimer()` + steal cash.
Rust host: supply-center name/KindOf only; comment "not drop zones residual".

## Player-visible effect
Sabotaging a USA/China Supply Drop Zone does nothing (or is cancelled). C++ resets the next crate drop timer and can steal cash.
close_reason: host_saboteur.rs classify_sabotage_target maps KINDOF_FS_SUPPLY_DROPZONE to SupplyDropzone; support_states.rs resets OCL timer + steals cash.

title: [FireWeaponCollide] Live host never fires collide weapons
description:
## C++
`Object::onCollide` (`Object.cpp:2369-2389`) walks every `CollideModuleInterface`. `FireWeaponCollide::onCollide` (`FireWeaponCollide.cpp:52-67`) skips ground, then if `shouldFireWeapon()` does `loadAmmoNow(me)` + `fireWeapon(me, other)` every frame. Retail firestorm leftover / AFLAME objects use this (pool size 2048). Status gates: `testForAll(required)` / `testForAny(forbidden)` / FireOnce via `m_everFired` (C++ never sets `m_everFired` either — match, not a gap).

## Rust
Crate `fire_weapon_collide.rs:376-429` ports shouldFire/loadAmmo/fireWeapon, but live host objects live in `Main` `GameLogic.objects`, not crate `OBJECT_REGISTRY` / `TheGameLogic`. `dispatch_collide_modules` (`collide_dispatch.rs:94-110`) looks up those crate registries; missing other becomes a ground collide, which FireWeaponCollide ignores. `dispatch_host_collide_modules` (`collide_modules.rs:7-44`) only handles contain-enter and template-name "crate" money pickups. `host_fire_spread.rs:15` documents fail-closed: "not full FireWeaponCollide AFLAME weapon".

## Evidence
C++ Object.cpp:2371-2388 module walk + FireWeaponCollide.cpp:63-66 fire every colliding object.
Rust host: no FireWeaponCollide residual; fire_spread honesty pack excludes it.

## Player-visible effect
Firestorm patches and other FireWeaponCollide objects do not shoot units that walk through them. Burning leftover geometry is cosmetic instead of a damage field.
close_reason: collide_modules.rs + collide_dispatch.rs: dispatch_host_collide_modules now fires FireWeaponCollide (shouldFire/loadAmmo/fireWeapon residual) on live host objects every colliding frame.

title: [SabotageMilitaryFactory] Host does not reject aircraft carriers
description:
## C++
`SabotageMilitaryFactoryCrateCollide::isValidToExecute` (`SabotageMilitaryFactoryCrateCollide.cpp:74-78`) returns FALSE for `KINDOF_AIRCRAFT_CARRIER` before the FS_BARRACKS / FS_WARFACTORY / FS_AIRFIELD test. Carriers cannot be factory-sabotaged.

## Rust
Live `classify_sabotage_target` (`host_saboteur.rs:496-511`) treats `is_fs_airfield` / name `airfield` as `MilitaryFactory` with no aircraft-carrier veto. Crate `sabotage_military_factory_crate_collide.rs:297-300` has the KindOf::AircraftCarrier reject but is not on the live saboteur path.

## Evidence
C++: `if (other->isKindOf(KINDOF_AIRCRAFT_CARRIER)) return FALSE;`
Rust host classify: airfield → MilitaryFactory, no AircraftCarrier check.

## Player-visible effect
A GLA Saboteur ordered onto an aircraft carrier can apply DISABLED_HACKED (production pause) as if it were a war factory / airfield. C++ refuses that target.
