title: [Pathfind] Bridge layers are an AABB, not a classified PathfindLayer cell grid
description:
## C++
`PathfindLayer` (`AIPathfind.h:363-412`) is a sub-rectangle of PathfindCells. `classifyLayerMapCell` (`AIPathfind.cpp:3647-3724`) counts how many of the 4 cell corners sit on the bridge polygon:
- 4 → CELL_CLEAR (deck)
- 1–3 → CELL_BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE (edge) unless on end/entry (CLEAR + connectLayer=GROUND)
- 0 → CELL_IMPASSABLE (getCell returns NULL)
`setDestroyed` reclassifies that layer matrix. Ground under a low deck is marked BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE only when `groundHeight + LAYER_Z_CLOSE_ENOUGH_F > bridgeHeight`.

## Rust
`pathfind_complete` `BridgeLayer` is bounds + entry cells, no per-cell matrix. `get_cell_type_at_cell` (`line_passable.rs:623-632`): if coord is inside AABB → Clear, or BridgeImpassable if destroyed; else None. `change_bridge_state` (`snap.rs:770-793`) stamps the **entire ground A*** AABB to BridgeImpassable on destroy (including off-deck cells).

## Evidence
C++ 4-corner `isPointOnBridge` + `isCellOnSide/OnEnd/EntryPoint` vs Rust `b.contains(coord)` then `Some(Clear)` / `Some(BridgeImpassable)`. Destroy path: `for bx in lo.x..=hi.x { set_cell_type(..., BridgeImpassable) }` on the ground grid.

## Player-visible effect
Units treat the whole bridge bounding box as walkable deck (including air beside the span) and, when the bridge dies, the whole box becomes impassable on the **ground** (blocking the riverbank/underpass). Ramps/entry connect cells are only the two attach points. Distinct from hq-6htk (terrain rubble/splat) and hq-c23o (host not calling crate search).
close_reason: BridgeLayer now has a classified per-cell matrix (4/1-3/0 corner rules). get_cell_type_at_cell reads cell_type_at; destroy reclassifies. pathfind_layer_classify.rs + types.rs/line_passable.rs.

title: [Partition] getPropShroudStatusForPlayer is missing — trees/props never fog
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::getPropShroudStatusForPlayer` (`PartitionManager.cpp:3038-3060`) samples four partition cells around the prop (world pos minus half a cell, then (x,y)/(x+1,y)/(x+1,y+1)/(x,y+1)). Mixed cell shroud → OBJECTSHROUD_PARTIAL_CLEAR; all shrouded → SHROUDED; all clear → CLEAR; else FOGGED. `W3DPropBuffer` and `W3DTreeBuffer` skip/draw/topple using this (props vanish in shroud; fogged trees freeze topple).

## Rust
No `get_prop_shroud_status_for_player` anywhere under GeneralsRust. Live `get_shroud_status_for_player` only returns CellShroudStatus for a single point via the 50wu shroud_manager grid. Tree/prop draw paths have nothing to call.

## Evidence
Repo-wide grep of `get_prop_shroud` / `getPropShroudStatusForPlayer` is empty on the Rust side. C++ W3DPropBuffer.cpp:341 and W3DTreeBuffer.cpp:1843 call ThePartitionManager->getPropShroudStatusForPlayer.

## Player-visible effect
Trees and civilian props stay fully drawn in unexplored shroud and keep animating (topple) while fogged. Distinct from object-ghost FOW (hq-2hqt / shroud_manager lookers) and from W3D ST_SHROUD_TEXTURE (hq-qipd.1).
close_reason: Added get_prop_shroud_status_for_player on collide PartitionManager and live game_logic_impl partition (four-cell sample at loc-halfCell). partition_shroud.rs.

title: [Partition] Shroud looker grid is 50wu, not PartitionCellSize 40
description:
## C++
Shroud/looker/shrouder circles are drawn on the same PartitionCell grid as objects (`m_cellSize` = GameData `PartitionCellSize = 40`). `getShroudStatusForPlayer(player, loc)` maps world→cell with that size. W3D FOW (`BaseHeightMap.cpp:1759`) inits the visual shroud with `m_partitionCellSize`.

## Rust
Live shroud queries go through `system/shroud_manager.rs`, not the 40wu collide partition:
```
const SHROUD_GRID_CELL_SIZE: f32 = 50.0;
```
`ShroudGrid::new` / `world_to_grid` / `do_shroud_reveal` all use 50. `ThePartitionManager::get_shroud_status_for_player` (`object_queries.rs:672-692`) reads this 50wu grid.

## Evidence
`shroud_manager.rs:63` `SHROUD_GRID_CELL_SIZE = 50.0` vs C++ `PartitionManager.cpp:2567` + GameData 40. Helper maps Visible/Explored/Hidden onto CELLSHROUD_CLEAR/FOGGED/SHROUDED from the 50wu cells.

## Player-visible effect
Fog-of-war tiles, reveal/cover circles, and script map-reveal snap to a 50wu lattice. Vision edges and minimap FOW do not line up with retail 40wu cells; a unit that just barely reveals a cell in ZH may leave it shrouded (or vice versa).
close_reason: Partition looker/shroud grid is PARTITION_CELL_SIZE=40wu. get_shroud_status_for_player on collide + live GameLogic partition uses that grid.

title: [Pathfind] PathfindLayerEnum is not C++ 0/1/2–14/LAYER_WALL=15
description:
## C++
`GameType.h:167`: `enum PathfindLayerEnum { LAYER_INVALID=0, LAYER_GROUND=1, LAYER_WALL=15, LAYER_LAST=15 }`. Layers 2–14 are unnamed bridge slots (`m_layers[LAYER_LAST+1]`). `Pathfinder::getCell(layer,x,y)` uses `layer > LAYER_GROUND && layer <= LAYER_LAST` to hit the bridge/wall cell matrix. Object `m_layer` and path nodes store these values.

## Rust
Live A* enum (`pathfind_astar.rs:54-59`) is only `Invalid=0, Ground=1, Top=2`. `get_cell_type_at_cell` takes that enum so layers 3–15 cannot be queried. Parallel `common/types/enums.rs:463-475` invents `Bridge1=3 … Wall=7, Tunnel=8, Water=9, Air=10, Last=11`; `from_u32(15)` returns Invalid. Host leftover (`pathfinding_system.rs`) maps 2 to Air.

## Evidence
C++ `LAYER_WALL = 15` vs crate A* `Top = 2` and common `Wall = 7` / `from_u32(15) → Invalid`. `line_passable.rs:620-632` can only special-case Ground/Invalid vs “everything else as Top/bridge 2”.

## Player-visible effect
Units cannot be on the correct bridge layer (3–14) or China/GLA wall-walk layer (15). Object/path xfer of layer 15 becomes Invalid; infantry never path on wall tops even when wall cells exist. Distinct from hq-c23o (host find_path_ex not calling crate internals) and hq-hvac (wall cell types).

## Split hint
One PathfindLayerEnum matching GameType.h (0,1,2–14,15); delete Top/Air/Tunnel inventions.
close_reason: Live A* PathfindLayerEnum is C++ 0/1/2-14/Wall=15 with from_u32(15)=Wall. path.rs Wall=15. pathfinding_system no longer maps layer 2 to Air.

title: [Partition] Live GameLogic closest-object grid uses 100wu cells, not retail 40
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::init` (`PartitionManager.cpp:2567-2571`) sets `m_cellSize = TheGlobalData->m_partitionCellSize` (GameData.ini `PartitionCellSize = 40.0`, clamped to >= 1). `worldToCell` floors `(wx - extents.lo) / cellSize`. Closest-object rings (`FASTER_GCO`), COI fills, threat/value, and shroud looker circles all share this 40wu grid.

## Rust
Closed hq-805q only fixed `object/collide/partition_manager.rs` (`PARTITION_CELL_SIZE = 40.0`). The **live** iterator used by `ThePartitionManager::get_objects_in_range` / `get_closest_object*` is `system/game_logic_impl/partition.rs`:
```
cell_size: 100.0,  // PartitionManager::new
position_to_cell: (position.x / self.cell_size).floor()
```
That leftover is what GameLogic owns and what AI/scripts query. collide PM is a parallel store.

## Evidence
C++ `m_cellSize = TheGlobalData->m_partitionCellSize` vs Rust `partition.rs:29` `cell_size: 100.0`. Helper `object_queries.rs:71-74` calls `logic.partition_manager().find_objects_in_radius`.

## Player-visible effect
Closest-object / in-range cells are 2.5× too coarse. Objects that C++ places in different 40wu cells share one 100wu bucket; ring walks and xfer `cellSize` checks (C++ throws on mismatch) diverge from ZH.

## Split hint
Keep collide/partition_manager.rs as the live grid; delete GameLogic leftover `partition.rs` cell hash or make it read GlobalData 40.
close_reason: Live game_logic_impl/partition.rs cell_size 100.0 -> 40.0 (retail PartitionCellSize).

title: [Physics] Landing bounce skips right-up, stun kill, and bounce sound
description:
## C++
`handleBounce` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:481-530) + landing in `update` (822-825):
- If vz<0, setAngles(yaw, 0, roll 0-or-PI) then after bounce setAngles(yaw, 0, 0)
- bounceForce.z>0 → testStunnedUnitForDestruction (upside-down / off-map / cliff / water without loco → kill)
- WAS_AIRBORNE_LAST_FRAME && now grounded && !IMMUNE → doBounceSound(prevPos) then onCollide(NULL)

## Rust
`handle_bounce` (`physics_update.rs:646-676`) computes stiffness force and YPR damping 0.7 only. No setAngles, no testStunnedUnitForDestruction. `update_simple` never calls doBounceSound (bounce_sound is stored, never played). ExtraBounciness is unused in C++ too — not a gap.

## Evidence
Rust handle_bounce returns Some(bounce_force) or None. update_simple has no addAudioEvent / do_bounce_sound. No test_stunned_unit_for_destruction symbol.

## Player-visible effect
Bouncing debris/wrecks stay tilted. Stunned units that land upside-down, off-map, or in cliffs/water survive. Landing thumps/debris bounce audio never play.

## Split hint
`physics_bounce.rs` (right-up + stun test + sound).
close_reason: physics_bounce.rs: handleBounce rights yaw/roll (0 or PI), testStunnedUnitForDestruction on bounceForce.z>0, doBounceSound on landing before onCollide(NULL).

title: [Physics] onCollide is a stub: no crash weapons, crush, or push-apart
description:
## C++
`PhysicsBehavior::onCollide` (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1141-1400) + `checkForOverlapCollision` (1424-1749):
- ProjectileHandleCollision first
- Ground/containment/parachute early-outs
- Infantry steal of DISABLED_UNMANNED vehicles
- Crush (front/back/total crush points, DAMAGE_CRUSH)
- Push-apart forces (structure stiffness, MINBOUNCESPEED)
- Vehicle vs building: fire VehicleCrashesIntoBuildingWeapon then destroyObject
- Vehicle vs non-building: fire VehicleCrashesIntoNonBuildingWeapon
- Sets m_lastCollidee

## Rust
`PhysicsBehaviorUpdate::on_collision` (`physics_update.rs:1003-1018`) only writes last_collidee and dispatches dumb-projectile collision. Crash weapon template names are parsed into module data and never fired.

## Evidence
```
fn on_collision(&mut self, _object_id: ObjectID, other_id: ObjectID) {
    handle.state.last_collidee = other_id;
    dispatch_dumb_projectile_handle_collision(...);
}
```

## Player-visible effect
Cars/tanks passing through each other. No crush of infantry. Vehicles falling onto buildings do not explode/die. Hijack of unmanned vehicles from collide is missing.

## Split hint
`physics_collide.rs` (push-apart + crash weapons), `physics_crush.rs` (overlap crush points).
close_reason: physics_collide.rs + physics_crush.rs implement C++ onCollide: projectile early-out, ground/containment, unmanned infantry steal, crush overlap, crash weapons, push-apart.

title: [Locomotor] Live move_towards kinematically integrates instead of applyMotiveForce
description:
## C++
`locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition` (Locomotor.cpp:929-1141) dispatches to Legs/Climb/Wheels/Treads/Hover/Wings/Thrust/Other. Each applies mass-scaled forces via `physics->applyMotiveForce`. PhysicsBehavior::update is the single Euler integrator (accel→vel→pos). Only braking cheat and Z-snap modes call setPosition.

## Rust
`Locomotor::move_towards` (`move_towards.rs:4-189`) calls the `*_physics` helpers then `advance_position` / `step_angle` (pos += heading * speed * dt). No PhysicsBehavior applyMotiveForce. Closed hq-8b1j/hq-fdyh fixed host dual-world / double-integrate, not this GameLogic locomotor algorithm.

## Evidence
```
let new_speed = (current_speed + accel * delta_time).clamp(0.0, max_speed);
let new_pos = self.advance_position(current, target, new_angle, new_speed, delta_time, false);
(new_pos, new_angle, new_speed)
```

## Player-visible effect
Units slide on rails at clamped speed instead of accelerating through friction/mass. Motive-skip of forward friction never engages. Wheels donut/3-point and legs wander compute an angle but the pose is teleported along the heading.

## Split hint
`move_towards` should only apply motive forces; delete advance_position from the live AI path.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Xfer] Drawable::xfer load does not updateHiddenStatus for hidden/stealth modules
description:
## C++
Drawable::xfer load (Drawable.cpp:5269-5278) sets m_stealthLook = STEALTHLOOK_NONE so the next stealth update re-applies hide/shadow state, then if (m_hidden || m_hiddenByStealth) updateHiddenStatus() so every draw/client-update submodule is hidden immediately.

## Rust
BasicDrawable::xfer (GameClient/src/drawable/drawable/snapshot.rs:505-511) sets stealth_look = StealthLook::None and stop_ambient_sound() on load. It never calls update_hidden_status (or equivalent) when hidden / hidden_by_stealth is true.

## Evidence
C++ Drawable.cpp:5274-5278 STEALTHLOOK_NONE then updateHiddenStatus().
Rust snapshot.rs:505-511 stealth reset + stop_ambient_sound only.

## Player-visible effect
Stealthed or script-hidden units can show draw modules, shadows, and attached client effects after load until a later stealth/hidden update runs (or never, if nothing dirties stealth).
close_reason: Drawable::xfer load calls update_hidden_status when hidden || hidden_by_stealth (Drawable.cpp:5276-5278)

title: [Drawable] Condition flags never dirty-apply to draw modules
description:
## C++
`Drawable::clearAndSetModelConditionFlags` (`Drawable.cpp:4021-4039`) updates `m_conditionState` then, with `DIRTY_CONDITION_FLAGS`, sets `m_isModelDirty`. `getDrawModules` (:3961-3986) on first use walks every DrawModule `ObjectDrawInterface::replaceModelConditionState(m_conditionState)` and clears the dirty bit. `replaceModelConditionFlags` force-replace applies immediately. This is how damage/night/snow/door/firing bits swap W3D models, hide/show lists, and animations.

## Rust
Mapped live Drawable (`GameClient/src/drawable/drawable/basic_core.rs:137-261`) `clear_and_set_model_condition_flags` / `replace_model_condition_flags` only mutate `model_condition_flags`. There is no dirty bit and no dispatch. GameClient `DrawModule` (`draw_module.rs:38-166`) has no `replace_model_condition_state` at all (comment: \"when the full W3D draw module system is ported\"). GameClient TOD/weather residual (`impl_update.rs:1125-1149`) therefore only stamps BasicDrawable bits. `compute_render_condition_flags` maps a small overlay subset (DAMAGED/NIGHT/SNOW/…) — not a full `W3DModelDraw::setModelState`.

GameLogic `W3DModelDraw::replace_model_condition_state` exists on the object-module path, but the mapped Drawable.cpp port never calls it.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_isModelDirty) { di->replaceModelConditionState(m_conditionState); m_isModelDirty = false; }`
Rust BasicDrawable: `self.model_condition_flags.clear_and_set(clr, set);` — no module loop. DrawModule trait has no replace-condition method.

## Player-visible effect
On the GameClient Drawable path (including host NIGHT/SNOW residuals and presentation body-damage bits), units do not swap to night/snow/damaged/door/firing ConditionState models, hide/show lists, or transition anims. Those swaps only happen if a separate GameLogic Object drawable happens to propagate.

## Split hint
Add dirty flag + `replace_model_condition_state` on GameClient `DrawModule`, apply in a `get_draw_modules` equivalent; keep W3D matching in `w3d_model_draw_impl`.
close_reason: Added is_model_dirty + DrawModule::replace_model_condition_state; flush in get_draw_modules_mut/update/render.

title: [Drawable] Detected stealth uses invented 0.3 first-pass opacity
description:
## C++
`Drawable::setStealthLook` (`Drawable.cpp:2588-2596`) for `STEALTHLOOK_VISIBLE_DETECTED` sets `m_hiddenByStealth = false` and `m_secondMaterialPassOpacity = 1.0` (0 for mines). It does **not** change first-pass opacity. `Drawable::draw` (:2629-2630) only `setShadowsEnabled(look != VISIBLE_DETECTED)`. The scene omits the first material pass and draws heat-vision on the second pass. `getEffectiveOpacity` is `m_explicitOpacity * m_effectiveStealthOpacity` with no 0.3 factor.

## Rust
Live `basic_drawable_trait.rs:181-186` `get_opacity`: `StealthLook::VisibleDetected => self.opacity * 0.3`. `apply_stealth_look` (`basic_core.rs:862-869`) correctly sets second-pass opacity, but `render` (`:368-371`) early-returns when `get_opacity() <= 0` and otherwise submits the unit at 30% as a normal transparent mesh. hq-0mcc closed the missing heat-vision *pass*; this invented first-pass scale remains.

## Evidence
C++ VISIBLE_DETECTED branch: hiddenByStealth=false, secondMaterialPassOpacity=1, no opacity multiply.
Rust: `StealthLook::VisibleDetected => self.opacity * 0.3`.

## Player-visible effect
Detected stealthed units (heat-vision reveal) render as 30% ghosts on the regular pass instead of an opaque heat-vision overlay with shadows off. Distinct from friendly stealth opacity (hq-2v9).

## Split hint
`get_opacity` should use explicit*stealth like C++ `getEffectiveOpacity`; heat-vision belongs only on the second material pass.
close_reason: get_opacity is explicit*stealth (getEffectiveOpacity); dropped invented 0.3 VisibleDetected first-pass scale.

title: [Drawable] setEffectiveOpacity doubles stealth transparency
description:
## C++
`Drawable::setEffectiveOpacity` (`Drawable.cpp:1102-1115`) if `explicitOpacity != -1` writes **only** `m_stealthOpacity` (clamped). It then sets `m_effectiveStealthOpacity = m_stealthOpacity + (1-m_stealthOpacity)*pulseFactor`. `getEffectiveOpacity` is `m_explicitOpacity * m_effectiveStealthOpacity`. Pulse callers (StealthUpdate) pass the pulse factor and optionally a new stealth floor; they do not overwrite explicit/override alpha.

## Rust
Live `basic_core.rs:703-711` `set_effective_opacity`: when `explicit_opacity` is `Some`, it writes **both** `stealth_opacity` and `explicit_opacity` to that value, then `effective_stealth_opacity = stealth + pulse`. `get_effective_opacity` (`:659-661`) is still `explicit_opacity * effective_stealth_opacity`.

Example: `set_effective_opacity(0.0, Some(0.5))`
- C++: stealth=0.5, effectiveStealth=0.5, getEffective = 1.0 * 0.5 = 0.5
- Rust: stealth=0.5, explicit=0.5, effectiveStealth=0.5, getEffective = 0.5 * 0.5 = 0.25

## Evidence
C++: `m_stealthOpacity = MIN(1, MAX(0, explicitOpacity));` — no write to `m_explicitOpacity`.
Rust: `self.stealth_opacity = explicit.clamp(...); self.explicit_opacity = self.stealth_opacity;`

## Player-visible effect
Friendly stealth pulse (and any script/module that passes an explicit stealth floor) makes units twice as transparent as authored FriendlyOpacityMin/Max. Distinct from hq-2v9 (which wired the friendly floor itself).

## Split hint
`set_effective_opacity` must only touch `stealth_opacity` / `effective_stealth_opacity`, never `explicit_opacity`.
close_reason: set_effective_opacity writes only stealth_opacity/effective_stealth_opacity, never explicit_opacity.

title: [PlaceEvent] Line-build uses Barrier/name heuristic, not KINDOF_LINEBUILD
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant::isLineBuildTemplate` (`BuildAssistant.cpp:1200-1209`) returns true only when `tTemplate->isKindOf(KINDOF_LINEBUILD)`. `PlaceEventTranslator.cpp:149` and `InGameUI::handleBuildPlacements` (`InGameUI.cpp:1489`) use that helper for `MSG_DOZER_CONSTRUCT_LINE` vs `MSG_DOZER_CONSTRUCT` and for tiling extra place icons.

## Rust
Crate `PlaceEventTranslator` (`place_event_translator.rs:264`) and `InGameUI::handle_mouse_input` (`gui/ingame_ui/impl_input.rs:137`) use `template.is_kind_of(KindOf::Barrier)`. Live host (`ui_commands.rs:468-475`, `mouse.rs:572-605`) uses `is_wall_structure_template` name contains `"wall"`/`"fence"`/`"chainlink"`. `KindOf::LineBuild` exists (`kindof.rs`) and `BuildAssistant::is_line_build_template` is implemented but unused by these live click paths.

## Evidence
C++: `if( tTemplate->isKindOf(KINDOF_LINEBUILD) ) return TRUE;`
Rust crate: `let is_line_build = template.is_kind_of(KindOf::Barrier);`
Rust host: `n.contains("wall") || n.contains("fence") || ...`

## Player-visible effect
LINEBUILD objects that are not Barrier (or whose template name lacks "wall"/"fence") place as a single building instead of a drag-line. Name-heuristic false positives (e.g. "Bunker"+"wall") start a wall-drag when C++ would not.
close_reason: Line-build uses KindOf::LineBuild / is_line_build_template_name, not Barrier or wall/fence name heuristic (place_event_translator.rs, impl_input.rs, ui_commands.rs).

title: [InGameUI] Building place ghost is not a 3D place-icon drawable
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::placeBuildAvailable` (`InGameUI.cpp:2957-3078`) creates `TheThingFactory->newDrawable(build, DRAWABLE_STATUS_NO_STATE_PARTICLES)`, sets player indicator color, `getPlacementViewAngle()`, opacity `placementOpacity` (0.45), captures the mouse, and stores it in `m_placeIcon[0]`. `handleBuildPlacements` (`1380-1564`) follows the mouse, tints illegal red, adds/removes faction bibs, and for LINEBUILD tiles extra drawables via `BuildAssistant::buildTiledLocations` up to `m_maxLineBuildObjects`. `destroyPlacementIcons` destroys those drawables.

## Rust
Live host `begin_structure_placement_from_ui` / `collect_ground_marker_circles` (`ui_commands.rs:396-409`, `start_game.rs:1367-1378`) arms a HUD `PlacementPreview` and draws a green/red ground circle from footprint half-extents. Crate leftover `start_building_placement` only stores a 2D `PlacementPreview`; `TheInGameUI::place_build_available` (`helpers.rs:1468-1482` / `subsystems.rs:1598-1608`) records the template name and does not spawn a drawable. No `m_placeIcon` array, no `DRAWABLE_STATUS_NO_STATE_PARTICLES`, no LINEBUILD tiling of extra icons.

## Evidence
C++: `draw = TheThingFactory->newDrawable( build, DRAWABLE_STATUS_NO_STATE_PARTICLES ); draw->setDrawableOpacity( placementOpacity );`
Host: `let radius = half.0.max(half.1).max(8.0);` circle marker only.

## Player-visible effect
Dozer placement shows a flat legal/illegal disk instead of a translucent 3D building at the cursor. Wall lines do not preview tiled segments. Distinct from closed hq-3hfm (ground bibs).

## Split hint
Keep crate `gui/ingame_ui` placement vs host `ui_commands` HUD preview; implement one live `placeBuildAvailable` that owns the drawable icons.
close_reason: place_build_available_icons creates DRAWABLE_STATUS_NO_STATE_PARTICLES 3D ghosts at 0.45 opacity; handle_build_placements follows mouse, tints illegal, tiles LINEBUILD extras up to 50 (place_icons.rs).

title: [CommandXlat] SELECT_NEXT/PREV_UNIT does not lookAt and includes non-mobiles
description:
## C++
`CommandTranslator::translateGameMessage` `MSG_META_SELECT_NEXT_UNIT` / `PREV` (`CommandXlat.cpp:2346-2451` and the matching prev block). Walks drawables and only selects objects that are `isMobile()`, `isLocallyControlled()`, `!isContained()`, `!isKindOf(KINDOF_NO_SELECT)`. Then posts `MSG_CREATE_SELECTED_GROUP`, `selectDrawable`, and `TheTacticalView->lookAt` on the new unit.

## Rust
Crate `CommandTranslator` (`command_translate.rs:203-206`) does not handle `MetaSelectNextUnit` / `MetaSelectPrevUnit` (falls through KeepMessage). Live host `cycle_friendly_selection` (`Main/src/cnc_game_engine/selection.rs:110-139`) cycles `alive_selectable_friendly_ids` (structures, contained, non-mobile included) and only `host_set_selection` + select sound — no `lookAt` / camera focus. Worker cycle (`142-185`) has the same missing camera snap.

## Evidence
C++: `TheTacticalView->lookAt(newDrawable->getPosition());` after mobile/local/not-contained filter.
Host: `self.host_set_selection(...); self.play_sound_effect(SoundType::Select);` — no camera.

## Player-visible effect
N/P (and worker cycle) can land on buildings or contained units and never snap the camera, so the newly selected unit is often off-screen. Distinct from closed hq-04jn (control-group double-tap lookAt).
close_reason: MetaSelectNext/PrevUnit walks mobile, locally-controlled, not-contained, not-NO_SELECT units, CreateSelectedGroup, and lookAt. Host cycle_friendly_selection uses is_mobile + host_center_camera_on (select_meta.rs, command_translate.rs, selection.rs).

title: [PlaceEvent] Illegal place click skips VoiceNoBuild and NoCanDoSound
close_reason: Illegal place click plays builder VoiceNoBuild plus UI NoCanDoSound then unhooks the placement anchor (place_event_confirm.rs, place_event_translator.rs, ui_commands.rs).

title: [PlaceEvent] Confirm-place skips canMakeUnit cash/queue/maxed and EVA funds
close_reason: Confirm-place re-checks can_make_unit; CANMAKE_NO_MONEY plays EVA_InsufficientFunds and GUI:NotEnoughMoneyToBuild; queue/parking/maxed keep placement armed (place_event_confirm.rs, place_event_translator.rs, ui_commands.rs).

title: [CommandXlat] SELECT_ALL includes dozers, harvesters, and structures
description:
## C++
`MSG_META_SELECT_ALL` (`CommandXlat.cpp:2864-2902`) builds `disqualifyingKindofs` = `KINDOF_DOZER | KINDOF_HARVESTER | KINDOF_IGNORES_SELECT_ALL`. If the current selection contains those kinds or a structure, it `deselectAllDrawables` first (1.03 SCUDSTORM exploit fix), then `InGameUI::selectAllUnitsByType`. `kindOfUnitSelection` (`InGameUI.cpp:95-140`) further requires locally controlled, not contained, not dead, `isMassSelectable()`, not off-map, and enforces `getMaxSelectCount` with `GUI:MaxSelectionSize`.

## Rust
Crate `CommandTranslator` never matches `MetaSelectAll`. Live host `select_all_friendly_units` (`selection.rs:1466-1476`) assigns `frame.alive_selectable_friendly_ids(team)` with no dozer/harvester/IGNORES_SELECT_ALL / structure / mass-selectable / max-select filters and no incompatible-selection clear.

## Evidence
C++: `disqualifyingKindofs.set(KINDOF_DOZER); ... set(KINDOF_HARVESTER); ... set(KINDOF_IGNORES_SELECT_ALL);` + `selectAllUnitsByType`.
Host: `let selection = frame.alive_selectable_friendly_ids(team); self.host_set_selection(...)`.

## Player-visible effect
Pressing Q/Select-All grabs dozers, supply trucks, and buildings (and can exceed the select cap). Retail leaves those out so the army can be ordered without accidentally moving workers or issuing mixed structure commands.
close_reason: MetaSelectAll / select_all_units_by_type excludes DOZER/HARVESTER/IGNORES_SELECT_ALL/structures, requires mass-selectable, enforces max-select GUI:MaxSelectionSize. Host select_all_friendly_units matches (select_all.rs, select_meta.rs, selection.rs).

title: [Production] Crate ProductionUpdate never calls ExitInterface
description:
## C++
ProductionUpdate::update (ProductionUpdate.cpp:712-855) on 100% unit completion calls getObjectExitInterface(), reserveDoorForExit if DOOR_NONE_AVAILABLE, opens door flags, then ThingFactory::newObject plus exitInterface->exitObjectViaDoor (Default/Queue/SpawnPoint/SupplyCenter). That applies UnitCreatePoint, natural/custom rally, Queue delay/burst, airborne kick, and SupplyCenter setForceWantingState(true).
queueCreateUnit also reserves a parking door via ParkingPlaceBehavior::shouldReserveDoorWhenQueued before enqueue.

## Rust
Live factory (contain_module_overrides/production.rs) instantiates ProductionUpdateComplete. spawn_unit (production_update_complete.rs:1082-1109) only calls self.exit_strategy.spawn_unit(...). set_exit_strategy is never called from any crate/Main caller (definitions only). On missing strategy it returns Err("No exit strategy configured"); update does let _ = self.spawn_unit(...).
queue_create_unit_with_id does not reserve parking doors. Door index is rotated (current_door + 1) instead of the reserved ExitDoorType.
Host BuildingData + world_tick/production.rs is the playable spawn/rally/force-wanting residual and does not drive the factory module ExitInterface.

## Evidence
Grep set_exit_strategy: only the setter in production_update_complete.rs and leftover production_update.rs.
update: if is_complete { let _ = self.spawn_unit(current_frame); }

## Player-visible effect
Crate ProductionUpdate can mark a batch complete and never place the unit on UnitCreatePoint / rally / supply Wanting. Dual-world objects using the factory module silently drop completed units. Host residual covers some producers but not parking-door reservation or crate ExitInterface.

## Split hint
Delete ProductionExitStrategy and call the building live ModuleExitInterface (already implemented on the four production_exit_behavior.rs modules). Wire parking reserve in queue_create_unit.
close_reason: production_update_complete.rs: spawn_unit uses owner ModuleExitInterface + ThingFactory::new_object + exit_object_via_door; queue_create_unit reserves parking doors.

title: [Main Loop] Snow/Anim2D advance 1/30s every 45 Hz present
description:
## C++
`GameClient.cpp:560-565` runs `TheSnowManager->UPDATE()` and `TheAnim2DCollection->UPDATE()` once per `GameClient::update`. In single-player that is once per `GameEngine::execute` iteration, which is also one logic frame (`LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND=30`, W3D 30 ms draw cap). Extra client spins (network) set `freezeTime` via `lastFrame == m_frame` so drawable/effect work does not re-run; snow/Anim2D sit above that gate but still run only when `update()` is called at the execute rate (~30 Hz), not with a forced 1/30 s dt on a faster present clock.

## Rust
Live host ticks snow/Anim2D from `host_update_cpp_snow_and_anim2d` (`camera_drain.rs:1287-1293`) and the menu shell (`:1345-1347`) with a hardcoded `SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL` (1/30 s) on **every** windowed present. Present cap is `DEFAULT_MAX_FPS=45` (`run_loop.rs:22-30`). The call is not gated on `logic_steps_run == 0` or `should_freeze_visual_time`. InGame post-presentation residuals call it again (`camera_drain.rs:1880`).

## Evidence
```
self.game_client.update_cpp_snow_and_anim2d(
    game_engine::common::game_common::SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL,
);
```
called from Loading/Paused/Endgame/InGame residual paths every `drive_frame`, while logic is a 30 Hz accumulator.

## Player-visible effect
Snowfall and 2D world animations run at present_hz/30 (about 1.5× at 45 FPS, faster if FPS is unlocked). Retail snow/Anim2D stay locked to the ~30 Hz client/logic cadence.

## Split hint
Pass 0 dt (or skip) when this present ran 0 logic steps; keep the helper in `camera_drain.rs`.
close_reason: camera_drain.rs host_update_cpp_snow_and_anim2d now passes 0 dt on extra 45 Hz presents (logic_steps_run==0); InGame locked to logic cadence; menu/pause/loading use a 30 Hz wall-clock gate. Menu shell uses the same helper dt.

title: [Assets] Boot Object INI skips Default/Object.ini and FileSystem directory load
description:
## C++
`GameEngine.cpp:458` `initSubsystem(TheThingFactory, ..., \"Data\\\\INI\\\\Default\\\\Object.ini\", NULL, \"Data\\\\INI\\\\Object\")`. `SubsystemInterfaceList::initSubsystem` (`SubsystemInterface.cpp:135-146`) does `ini.load(path1)` then `ini.loadDirectory(dirpath, TRUE, INI_LOAD_OVERWRITE)`. `INI::loadDirectory` (`INI.cpp:193-229`) asks `TheFileSystem->getFileListInDirectory(..., TRUE)` — local files **and** mounted BIG entries — loads files in the directory first (sorted), then subdirectories. FileSystem open is local-then-archive (`FileSystem.cpp:142-155`).

## Rust
Live boot (`cnc_game_engine/shell.rs:1561-1610`) after `init_thing_system()` enumerates only top-level `Data/INI/Object/*.ini` from the first disk extract root, else `AssetManager::list_all_files()` filtered to `data/ini/object/*.ini`, then `extract_ini_text_from_archives` (archive bytes only). It never loads `Data/INI/Default/Object.ini`. `ThingFactory::discover_object_ini_sources` (`thing_factory.rs:1330-1416`) can see Default/Object.ini but only as a **disk** path (no BIG listing, no recursion).

## Evidence
C++ path1+dirpath: Default/Object.ini then recursive FileSystem Object dir.
Rust boot loop: `object_ini_paths.push(format!(\"Data/INI/Object/{name}\"))` / archive filter `starts_with(\"data/ini/object/\")` — no Default/Object.ini, no `loadDirectory` subdirectory pass.

## Player-visible effect
Base Object.ini defaults that live only in `Default/Object.ini` inside INIZH.big never apply. Nested Object INI folders and loose `Data/INI/Object` overrides that C++ FileSystem would find are missed or applied in the wrong order, so templates (stats, draw modules, upgrades) diverge from retail.

## Split hint
One FileSystem-backed `load_directory(\"Data/INI/Object\")` used by both ThingFactory init and the boot worker; do not keep a second archive-only enumerator.
close_reason: New object_ini_boot.rs lists Default/Object.ini then FileSystem+disk+archive Data/INI/Object (current dir then nested). shell.rs boot worker uses that list instead of top-level Object/*.ini only.

title: [Main Loop] lastFrame visual freeze reads crate GameLogic frame 0
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GameClient.cpp` `GameClient::update` (621-630): `freezeTime` includes camera/script/pause plus `lastFrame == m_frame`. `m_frame` is the live simulation frame — `GameLogic::update` (`GameLogic.cpp:3595-3596`) does `TheGameClient->setFrame(TheGameLogic->getFrame())` before incrementing. Extra client presents (network wait, or any execute() without a new logic frame) freeze drawable/ghost/particle-local updates so effects stay at logic pace. `lastFrame` starts at `~0` so the first frame is not frozen.

## Rust
Live host is `CnCGameEngine` 30 Hz `tick_logic_frame` (`host_authority.rs`) + 45 Hz present (`run_loop.rs`). Presentation shell `should_freeze_visual_time` (`GameClient/src/core/game_client/impl_update.rs:1318-1330`) compares `last_visual_time_frame` to `TheGameLogic::get_frame()` — the **crate** singleton (`game_logic_impl/globals.rs:288-289`). Default dual-tick is AuthorityOnly and never calls `tick_gamelogic_crate` (`camera_drain.rs` Wave 916). Crate frame stays 0.

## Evidence
C++: `freezeTime = freezeTime || (lastFrame == m_frame); lastFrame = m_frame;` after `TheGameClient->setFrame(now)` from live GameLogic.
Rust: `let logic_frame = TheGameLogic::get_frame(); freeze_time = freeze_time || (self.last_visual_time_frame == logic_frame);` with `last_visual_time_frame` init `u32::MAX`. After the first shell tick, `logic_frame` is always 0 so every later present freezes `update_drawables_local` / `update_effects`.

## Player-visible effect
Client drawable modules (tints, fades, icon flashes, local FX) update once then freeze while the host keeps presenting at 45 Hz. C++ only freezes extras when the live 30 Hz logic frame did not advance. Units still move via presentation-pose copy, but client-side animation/FX stall.

## Split hint
Keep freeze in `impl_update.rs`; feed it host `game_logic.get_frame()` / presentation `frame` instead of the crate singleton.
close_reason: GameClient should_freeze_visual_time now compares last_visual_time_frame to self.frame (host-fed via set_frame). host_tick_game_client_presentation_shell calls game_client.set_frame(game_logic.frame) so extra presents freeze drawable/FX like C++ lastFrame==m_frame.

title: [Assets] -mod/loadMods never mounts into the live Main archive
description:
## C++
`Win32BIGFileSystem::init` (`Win32BIGFileSystem.cpp:31-49`) mounts cwd `*.big` then registry base-Generals `InstallPath` `*.big` (overwrite default FALSE — first wins). After command line, `TheArchiveFileSystem->loadMods()` (`ArchiveFileSystem.cpp:142-166`, called from `CommandLine.cpp:1269`) opens `m_modBIG` and/or `loadBigFilesFromDirectory(m_modDir, \"*.big\", TRUE)` so **only** the user mod overwrites the live directory tree. `FileSystem::openFile` then prefers loose local files over that same archive tree.

## Rust
Live W3D/INI extract uses Main `assets/archive.rs` → core BIG index (`AssetManager::extract_file`). `CnCGameEngine::load_mods_best_effort` (`boot.rs:981-1005`) inits and mutates `game_engine::common::system::archive_file_system` — a **different** singleton. Common `ArchiveFileSystem::load_mods` (`archive_file_system.rs:96-102`) then remounts **every** configured search path with `overwrite: true`, not just `mod_dir`/`mod_big`. Boot Science/Rank/Weapon/Upgrade/etc. use `extract_ini_text_from_archives` (archive bytes only); they do not go through Common FileSystem local-then-archive.

## Evidence
C++: one `TheArchiveFileSystem`, `loadMods` overwrite TRUE only for the -mod BIG/dir.
Rust: `get_archive_file_system().load_mods()` vs `manager.extract_file(virtual_path)` on Main's facade. Common `load_mods` loop: `for path in self.search_paths { load_big_files_from_directory(..., true) }`.

## Player-visible effect
`-mod` folders/BIGs and loose `Data/INI` overrides do not change live units, maps, or art. C++ players drop a mod BIG or extracted INI next to the exe and see it. If Common search paths were ever populated, remount-with-overwrite would also let later base-Generals BIGs replace ZH entries.

## Split hint
Point `load_mods_best_effort` at the same archive instance `AssetManager` already mounted; only overwrite from `mod_big`/`mod_dir`.
close_reason: load_mods_best_effort now mounts -mod BIG/dir into the live Main AssetManager archive (archive.rs load_user_mods overwrite=true only for mod_big/mod_dir). No longer mutates the unused Common ArchiveFileSystem singleton or remounts every search path.

title: [Xfer] GameLogic::xfer load skips pathfinder newMap after polygon triggers
description:
## C++
GameLogic::xfer version>=3 (GameLogic.cpp:4799-4882): xfer polygon trigger count + each trigger snapshot. On load, after all triggers are restored, TheAI->pathfinder()->newMap() is called so water/area polygons that moved at runtime rebuild walkable cells (comment at :4775-4780).

## Rust
xfer_polygon_triggers (xfer_helpers.rs:484-518) xfers count + each trigger snapshot and returns. It never calls Pathfinder::new_map (or any equivalent). xfer_helpers.rs has no pathfinder/new_map references.

## Evidence
C++ GameLogic.cpp:4880 `TheAI->pathfinder()->newMap();`
Rust xfer_helpers.rs:484-518 ends after the trigger loop with `Ok(())`.

## Player-visible effect
Maps whose water or area triggers changed during play (script-lowered rivers, revealed shallows, moved blockade polygons) load with the original map pathfinding. Units refuse to walk newly opened water/land and still path through areas that should be blocked.
close_reason: polygon trigger load calls TheAI pathfinder rebuild_from_terrain (GameLogic.cpp:4880 newMap)

title: [Xfer] Drawable loadPostProcess does not restore transform from attached object
description:
## C++
Drawable::loadPostProcess (Drawable.cpp:5396-5420): if m_object != NULL, setTransformMatrix(m_object->getTransformMatrix()) so the drawable pose is the object's authoritative matrix after load; then startAmbientSound(true)/stopAmbientSound based on ambient flags.

## Rust
BasicDrawable::load_post_process (GameClient/src/drawable/drawable/snapshot.rs:637-644) only starts/stops ambient sound. It never copies the bound object's transform onto the drawable.
Drawable::xfer itself writes a combined translation*instance matrix (snapshot.rs:233-246) and a separate instance matrix (v>=4), which can disagree with the object record restored later in CHUNK_GameLogic / object xfer.

## Evidence
C++ Drawable.cpp:5400-5403 `if (m_object != NULL) { setTransformMatrix(m_object->getTransformMatrix()); }`
Rust snapshot.rs:637-644 ambient-only load_post_process.

## Player-visible effect
After load, units/buildings can render at the drawable's saved pose instead of the object's logic position/orientation (hovering, rotated wrong, or offset from selection/collision) until something else forces a transform update.
close_reason: Drawable::load_post_process copies bound object transform (Drawable.cpp:5400-5403)

title: [Locomotor] handleBehaviorZ no-ops Z snap and lift uses vel_z=0
description:
## C++
`handleBehaviorZ` (Locomotor.cpp:2196-2323) + `calcLiftToUseAtPt` (2022-2110):
- Z_SEA_LEVEL: setPosition z to water or layer height
- Z_FIXED_SURFACE_RELATIVE / Z_FIXED_ABSOLUTE: hard-snap z to preferredHeight (+ surface)
- Z_RELATIVE_TO_GROUND_AND_BUILDINGS: snap to preferred + PartitionManager ground-or-structure height
- Z_SMOOTH_RELATIVE_TO_HIGHEST_LAYER: lift force vs highest layer (bridges)
- Z_SURFACE_RELATIVE / Z_ABSOLUTE: lift force using actual vel.z, speedLimitZ, ultra-accurate negative lift

## Rust
`handle_behavior_z` (`maintain.rs:528-590`):
- SeaLevel / Fixed* / RelativeToGroundAndBuildings return `(0.0, true)` with no setPosition
- Smooth/Surface/Absolute compute lift but pass `vel_z = 0.0` (\"not available in this context\")
- Highest-layer uses get_surface_ht_at_pt, not getHighestLayerForDestination
Callers of `move_towards` do not apply the returned lift as motive Z force.

## Evidence
```
LocomotorBehaviorZ::SeaLevel => { (0.0, true) }
// ...
vel_z, 0.0, // vel_z not available in this context
```

## Player-visible effect
Boats/hover do not stay at sea level. Helis/jets with preferredHeight float or slam instead of damped lift. Bridge-relative flight ignores bridges. Short jet landings lose the ultra-accurate negative-lift cheat.

## Split hint
`locomotor/behavior_z.rs` (snap vs lift), apply lift via PhysicsBehavior::applyMotiveForce.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Locomotor] setPhysicsOptions writes leftover PhysicsState not PhysicsBehavior
description:
## C++
`Locomotor::setPhysicsOptions` (Locomotor.cpp:911-926) on the object's PhysicsBehavior:
- extraFriction = extra2DFriction + (ULTRA_ACCURATE ? 0.5 : 0)
- setAllowAirborneFriction(apply2DFrictionWhenAirborne)
- setStickToGround(stickToGround) — \"walking guys aren't allowed to catch huge (or even small) air\"

## Rust
`set_physics_options` (`maintain.rs:8-23`) mutates leftover `PhysicsState` fields (`friction`, `drag`, `affected_by_gravity`) and never calls `PhysicsBehavior::set_extra_friction` / `set_allow_airborne_friction` / `set_stick_to_ground`. Live PhysicsBehavior therefore never sees locomotor extra friction, airborne 2D friction, or stick-to-ground.

## Evidence
```
physics.friction = extra_friction;
physics.drag = if apply_2d_friction_when_airborne { 0.95 } else { 0.98 };
physics.affected_by_gravity = self.template.stick_to_ground;
```

## Player-visible effect
Infantry hop/catch air. Ultra-accurate landings (jets/helis) do not get the +0.5 friction cheat. Airborne 2D friction for hover/thrust is ignored by the live integrator.

## Split hint
Delete PhysicsState leftover path; set the three PhysicsBehavior flags only.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Locomotor] Thrust skips 3D calcDirectionToApplyThrust motive force
description:
## C++
`moveTowardsPositionThrust` (Locomotor.cpp:1891-2004) + `calcDirectionToApplyThrust` (175-250):
- Preferred-height damps goal Z via getSurfaceHtAtPt
- Quadratic solve for thrust direction accounting for current velocity + gravity
- Clamps thrust to MaxThrustAngle cone around nose via tryToRotateVector3D
- Orients to velocity (3× turn rate while braking)
- `accelVec = thrustDir*maxAccel - curVel*damping`; `physics->applyMotiveForce(mass*accelVec)` (full 3D)

## Rust
`move_towards_position_thrust_physics` (`move_air.rs:4-105`) computes a 2D heading, optionally clamps yaw by max_thrust_angle, and returns a scalar acceleration. `move_towards` then kinematically steps XZ. No quadratic thrust dir, no gravity preload, no applyMotiveForce, no 3D orient-to-velocity.

## Evidence
```
// C++ applies: accelVec = thrustDir * maxAccel - curVel * damping
// We simplify: the acceleration returned is the net effect per frame
let acceleration = max_accel - current_speed * damping;
(current_pos, desired_angle, acceleration)
```

## Player-visible effect
Helicopters, Comanches, Chinooks, SCUDs, and jets cannot climb/dive by thrusting; they yaw in 2D and ignore the authored thrust cone. Maintain-position hover for THRUST is equally flat.

## Split hint
`locomotor/thrust.rs` (calc_direction_to_apply_thrust + applyMotiveForce), keep wings/hover elsewhere.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [ThingTemplate] calc_vision_range invents geometry.height when VisionRange is 0
description:
## C++
`ThingTemplate.cpp:100` `{ "VisionRange", INI::parseReal, offsetof(m_visionRange) }`. Constructor (`ThingTemplate.cpp:976-978`) sets `m_visionRange = 0.0f`, `m_shroudClearingRange = -1.0f`, `m_shroudRevealToAllRange = -1.0f`.
`ThingTemplate.h:405-406` `friend_calcVisionRange()` / `friend_calcShroudClearingRange()` return the raw fields — no geometry fallback.
`Object.cpp:270-273` copies those fields, then if shroud == -1.0f assigns `m_shroudClearingRange = m_visionRange` (so missing VisionRange → 0 sight and 0 shroud clear). Partition look bails when `getShroudClearingRange() <= 0` (`Object.cpp:4818, 4868`).

## Rust
`thing_template.rs:1773-1786` `calc_vision_range` returns `geometry_info.height` whenever `vision_range <= 0`. `calc_shroud_clearing_range` uses that invented vision when shroud is still -1.
Live object ctor `GameLogic/src/object/object_lifecycle.rs:136-144` sets `vision_range` / `shroud_clearing_range` from those helpers. Default geometry height is 1.0, and most authored objects set `GeometryHeight` to tens of world units.

VisionRange **is** parsed (`thing_template.rs:3095-3098`); the gap is the extra fallback C++ does not have.

## Evidence
```
// C++ ThingTemplate.h:405
Real friend_calcVisionRange() const { return m_visionRange; }
```
```
// Rust thing_template.rs:1773-1778
pub fn calc_vision_range(&self) -> Real {
    if self.vision_range > 0.0 { self.vision_range }
    else { self.geometry_info.height.max(0.0) }
}
```
```
// object_lifecycle.rs:136
vision_range: thing_template.calc_vision_range(),
```

## Player-visible effect
Objects that omit VisionRange (trees, props, debris, many civilians) get a nonzero sight/shroud-clear radius equal to their geometry height. They can reveal fog, contribute vision/threat partition, and feed AI engagement range (`identity.rs` uses `calc_vision_range`) instead of seeing nothing like retail.

## Split hint
Make `calc_vision_range` return the raw field (C++ friend_calcVisionRange). Keep the Object.cpp `-1 shroud → vision` fallback only on the object, using the raw 0 vision.
close_reason: calc_vision_range now returns the raw vision_range field (C++ friend_calcVisionRange). No geometry.height fallback. calc_shroud_clearing_range still uses -1 -> vision.

title: [Drawable] Disabled/subdual/frenzy tints never darken models
description:
## C++
`Drawable.cpp:1228-1272` on tint-status edge plays signed additive colors: `DARK_GRAY_DISABLED_COLOR={-0.5,-0.5,-0.5}` (30/30 sustain-forever), `SUBDUAL_DAMAGE_COLOR={-0.2,-0.2,0.8}` (150/150), frenzy `FRENZY_COLOR={0.2,-0.2,-0.2}` or `FRENZY_COLOR_INFANTRY={0.0,-0.7,-0.7}` for `KINDOF_INFANTRY`. `TintEnvelope::update` (:5507-5570) uses vector length to detect peak/rest so negative channels fade in/out. W3D adds `getTintColor()` to lights (can be negative → darker).

## Rust
Live `basic_visual.rs:194-229` `update_tint_status` plays the same disabled/subdual colors but always `FRENZY_COLOR` (no infantry variant; `FRENZY_COLOR_INFANTRY` is missing from `types.rs`). `tint_envelope.rs:198-233` treats attack-complete as `current >= peak` per channel and decay-complete as `current <= 0` on all channels — signed peaks snap to peak in one frame and snap to rest on release. `render_state_from_flags` (`basic_visual.rs:356-360`) then does `tint.x.max(0.0)` so every negative channel is dropped before GPU `emissive_tint`.

## Evidence
C++: `m_colorTintEnvelope->play(isKindOf(KINDOF_INFANTRY) ? &FRENZY_COLOR_INFANTRY : &FRENZY_COLOR, 30, 30, SUSTAIN_INDEFINITELY);` and length-based envelope.
Rust: `envelope.play(FRENZY_COLOR, 30, 30, SUSTAIN_INDEFINITELY);` + `tint.x.max(0.0)` clamp. Disabled `{-0.5,-0.5,-0.5}`: after one attack step `-0.016 >= -0.5` is true, then decay `current <= 0` is already true.

## Player-visible effect
Disabled/hacked units never go deathly gray, subdual never tints blue, frenzy never tints red/cyan. Infantry frenzy cannot use the stronger authored look. Status tints pop (or do nothing) instead of a 30-frame fade.

## Split hint
Fix envelope vector-length math in `tint_envelope.rs`; apply signed additive tint in the render-state mapper; add infantry frenzy color in `update_tint_status`.
close_reason: TintEnvelope vector-length math; signed emissive add; FRENZY_COLOR_INFANTRY for infantry.

title: [Drawable] Selection flash ignores house/white envelope
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/Drawable.cpp` `Drawable::flashAsSelected` (:1335-1360) plays `m_selectionFlashEnvelope` with house color when `TheGlobalData->m_selectionFlashHouseColor` else white `0xffffffff`, then `saturateRGB` by `m_selectionFlashSaturationFactor` (default 0.5) and `play(color, 0, 4)`. `friend_setSelected` (:908-919) flashes only on the rising edge; `onUnselected` (:1006-1009) is empty so the envelope decays naturally. `getSelectionColor` (:1030-1038) returns the envelope independently of the status tint envelope.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/drawable/drawable/basic_drawable_trait.rs` `set_selected` (:154-178) always `play(Vector3::new(0.3, 0.3, 0.3), 5, 10, 0)` and on deselect immediately `selection_flash_envelope = None`. It flashes even when already selected and even when `!selectable` (flash uses the parameter, not `self.selected`). Parallel GameLogic leftover `object/drawable.rs:2163-2175` `flash_as_selected` only pushes a `"SelectionFlash"` VisualEffect string. Main render uses a linear `selection_flash_remaining` residual (`host_saboteur.rs`), not the C++ TintEnvelope.

## Evidence
C++: `m_selectionFlashEnvelope->play(&tempColor, 0, 4);` after saturateRGB.
Rust: `envelope.play(Vector3::new(0.3, 0.3, 0.3), 5, 10, 0);` then `self.selection_flash_envelope = None;` on unselect.

## Player-visible effect
Selected units flash dull gray for ~10 frames (or a linear host residual) instead of a saturated white (or house-color) pop that decays in 4 frames. Deselect cuts the flash off instantly. Contained riders get the leftover VisualEffect stub, not the envelope.

## Split hint
Keep envelope math in `tint_envelope.rs`; selection rising-edge + GlobalData color in `basic_drawable_trait.rs`; do not mix with status tint envelope.
close_reason: Rising-edge flashAsSelected uses house/white saturateRGB play(0,4); deselect leaves envelope to decay.

title: [W3DModelDraw] Muzzle-flash meshes stay visible after fire
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::handleClientRecoil` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:2489-2494`) sets muzzle-flash hidden unless recoil state is `RECOIL_START` (one visible frame). `setModelState` (:2984-2985) always `hideAllMuzzleFlashes` before swapping so leftover flashes cannot survive a condition change. `handleWeaponFireFX` unhides for the shot then recoil hides it next frame.

## Rust
Live `w3d_model_draw_impl/trait_impl.rs:598-603` `handle_weapon_fire_fx` `show_sub_object(..., true)` for the muzzle name. `handle_client_recoil` (`impl_anim.rs:296-339`) only advances shift/rate and never toggles muzzle visibility. `set_model_state` (`impl_anim.rs:3-75`) never calls a hide-all-muzzle helper (none exists). hq-d56s closed the unhide/FX-bone path; the one-frame hide-after-start is still missing.

## Evidence
C++: `Bool hidden = recoils[i].m_state != WeaponRecoilInfo::RECOIL_START; barrels[i].setMuzzleFlashHidden(m_renderObject, hidden);`
Rust recoil loop has no `muzzle_flash_bone` branch; fire path only shows.

## Player-visible effect
After the first shot, authored muzzle-flash subobjects (barrel glow meshes) stay visible on the gun for the rest of the state. Condition swaps do not clear them.

## Split hint
Put one-frame muzzle hide in `handle_client_recoil`; call hide-all from `set_model_state` like C++.
close_reason: handle_client_recoil hides muzzle unless RecoilStart (one visible frame) even when there is no recoil bone; set_model_state calls hide_all_muzzle_flashes before and after the swap. Device handle_client_recoil + hide_all_muzzle_flashes_for_state match. Files: hide_show.rs, impl_anim.rs, Device wthree_d_model_draw.rs.

title: [W3DModelDraw] AnimSpeedFactor never changes playback rate
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::adjustAnimation` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:2193-2198`) after `Set_Animation` does `hlod->Set_Animation_Frame_Rate_Multiplier(GameClientRandomValueReal(m_animMinSpeedFactor, m_animMaxSpeedFactor))`. INI `AnimationSpeedFactorRange` is parsed into those fields (:1342-1345). `setCurAnimDurationInMsec` (:2210-2223) also sets the HLOD multiplier from natural/desired duration (used by `setAnimationLoopDuration` and `adjustAnimSpeedToMovementSpeed`).

## Rust
Live `impl_anim.rs:155-163` stores `current_anim_speed_factor` from the same min/max range, but `tick_animation_state` (:167-218) always advances exactly one frame (`current_anim_frame + 1`) and never reads the factor. `submit_draw_to_bridge` (:515-527) publishes `animation_mode` + `animation_time` fraction with no multiplier field. `set_cur_anim_duration_in_msec` (:434-442) rewrites `current_anim_num_frames` instead of a playback multiplier, fighting the HLOD native rate.

## Evidence
C++: `hlod->Set_Animation_Frame_Rate_Multiplier(factor);`
Rust: `self.current_anim_speed_factor = game_client_random_value_real(...)` then unused; tick is `+ 1` / `rem_euclid`.

## Player-visible effect
Authored AnimationSpeedFactorRange variation (idle fidgets, walk cycles that should not all lock-step) always plays at 1x. Duration overrides and movement-speed matching stretch frame counts instead of speeding the clip, so once/transition timings drift from retail.

## Split hint
Apply the multiplier in the HLOD/animation consumer; keep factor selection in `adjust_animation`.
close_reason: adjust_animation still picks current_anim_speed_factor from AnimationSpeedFactorRange; tick_animation_with_speed advances by that multiplier via a fractional accumulator. set_cur_anim_duration_in_msec sets multiplier = natural/desired instead of rewriting frame count. Device stores anim_speed_factor the same way. Files: anim_playback.rs, impl_anim.rs, draw.rs, Device wthree_d_model_draw.rs.

title: [Production] Supply-center dock never grants GrantTemporaryStealth
description:
## C++
`SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action` (`SupplyCenterDockUpdate.cpp:92-109`).
After draining boxes and depositing cash, if `m_grantTemporaryStealthFrames > 0` and the **center** is `OBJECT_STATUS_STEALTHED`, grant stealth on the docker's default StealthUpdate only when `stealth->isTemporaryGrant() || !docker->testStatus(OBJECT_STATUS_CAN_STEALTH)` so GPS scrambler / innate stealth wins. Retail GLA Supply Stash authors `GrantTemporaryStealth = 20000` ms → 600 frames.

## Rust
Crate live `object/production/dock_update.rs` `SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action` (1432-1447) does call `receive_grant` when the center is stealthed, but skips the `isTemporaryGrant` / `CAN_STEALTH` gate (can overwrite GPS stealth).
Playable host deposit (`world_objects/support_states.rs:3523-3616`) credits cash only. `host_dock_contain_exit_heal_residual.rs` keeps GLA 600-frame constants for honesty tests; no live caller applies them.

## Evidence
Host deposit block has `credit_supplies` / Supply Lines / WorkerShoes and no `receive_grant` / `GrantTemporaryStealth`.
Crate grant: `if owner_guard.test_status(Stealthed) { stealth_guard.receive_grant(...) }` with no temporary/CAN_STEALTH test.

## Player-visible effect
GLA workers/trucks leaving a stealthed Supply Stash stay fully visible for 20s instead of receiving the authored temporary cloak. Crate path, if used, can also clobber a stronger stealth source.

## Split hint
Host deposit should apply the crate grant (with the C++ gate). Keep grant logic next to cash deposit, not in a residual constants file.
close_reason: SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action grants stealth only when is_temporary_grant || !CAN_STEALTH, matching C++ GPS/innate precedence.

title: [Production] SpawnPoint exit bones stay model-space
description:
## C++
`SpawnPointProductionExitUpdate::initializeBonePositions` (`SpawnPointProductionExitUpdate.cpp:118-149`).
`Drawable::getPristineBonePositions(SpawnPointBoneName, 1, NULL, boneTransforms, MAX_SPAWN_POINTS)` then **each** matrix is `Object::convertBonePosToWorldPos` before storing world XY + `Get_Z_Rotation()`. `exitObjectViaDoor` places the unit on that world bone, snaps Z to layer height, marks occupier, `setDisabled(DISABLED_HELD)`.

## Rust
Live factory module `object/behavior/spawn_point_production_exit_behavior.rs` `initialize_bone_positions` (101-136) takes `drawable.get_pristine_bone_transforms` (local/pristine) and uses `to_scale_rotation_translation()` **without** `convert_bone_pos_to_world_pos`. Occupier/Held/pathfinder bits are present.
Host production-exit parser (`spawn_templates.rs:1215-1228`) only recognizes Queue/Default/SupplyCenter — `SpawnPointProductionExitUpdate` is dropped. Stinger Site uses a hardcoded 3-point ring residual (`host_base_defense.rs`) instead of authored bones.

## Evidence
C++: `me->convertBonePosToWorldPos(NULL, currentTransform, NULL, currentTransform)`.
Rust crate: no `convert_bone_pos_to_world_pos` in this file (unlike dock_update.rs which does convert DockStart/Action/End).
Host: `ProductionExitStyle` has no SpawnPoint variant.

## Player-visible effect
Bone-exited units (Stinger soldiers, other SpawnPointBoneName producers) appear at model-space origin / a fake ring, not on the building's spawn bones, and can stack or clip.

## Split hint
Reuse `Object::convert_bone_pos_to_world_pos` already used by dock bones. Host should parse SpawnPointBoneName instead of the stinger-only ring.
close_reason: spawn_point_production_exit_behavior.rs: initialize_bone_positions converts pristine bone matrices with convert_bone_pos_to_world_pos before storing world XY + yaw.

title: [Production] Repair dock heals at flat 35 HP/s not TimeForFullHeal
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/DockUpdate/RepairDockUpdate.cpp` `action` (67-129).
On first docker (`m_lastRepair == 0`) computes `m_healthToAddPerFrame = (maxHealth - health) / m_framesForFullHeal`. INI `TimeForFullHeal` is `parseDurationReal` (retail WarFactory/TechRepairPad 5000ms → 150 frames). Each docked frame `BodyModule::attemptHealing` with `DAMAGE_HEALING` for that sliver; drone (if present) is healed to full max. Default `m_framesForFullHeal = 1.0` (instant).

## Rust
Live factory registers crate `object/production/dock_update.rs` `RepairDockUpdate` (correct sliver formula + `heal_completely` on drone). Playable host path does **not** call that `action`.
`Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/support_states.rs:1617-1629` SeekingRepair uses `HOST_REPAIR_RATE_HP_PER_SEC = 35.0` flat (`host_repair.rs:33`). Comment: "not C++ percent-of-max / TimeForFullHeal matrix". `repair_dock_hp_per_sec()` exists but is unused on the live heal tick.

## Evidence
C++: `(body->getMaxHealth() - body->getHealth()) / modData->m_framesForFullHeal` then `attemptHealing`.
Host: `obj.heal(REPAIR_RATE * dt)` with `REPAIR_RATE = 35.0`.

## Player-visible effect
A 1000 HP tank takes ~28.6s to full-repair instead of retail 5s (or the inverse for tiny HP). War factory / repair pad / China WF dock cadence is wrong.

## Split hint
Keep crate `RepairDockUpdate::action` as the TimeForFullHeal impl; host SeekingRepair should call it (or the same sliver) instead of the 35 HP/s residual.
close_reason: RepairDockUpdate::repair_unit keeps TimeForFullHeal sliver (max-health-health)/frames and now applies it via attempt_healing.

title: [Xfer] GameLogic::xfer load matches objects by template name instead of ThingFactory::newObject
description:
## C++
GameLogic::xfer load (GameLogic.cpp:4732-4785): for each TOC id, beginBlock, findTemplate, if missing skip(block) and continue; else TheThingFactory->newObject(thingTemplate, defaultTeam) then xferSnapshot(obj); if KINDOF_WALK_ON_TOP_OF_WALL, pathfinder->addWallPiece(obj).
prepareLogicForObjectLoad first destroys map-spawned bridges/towers/walls so the world is empty before those newObject calls (GameLogic.cpp:4584-4649). Unknown templates never create stubs.

## Rust
xfer_game_logic_state load (xfer_helpers.rs:323-383): after TOC lookup, scans logic.objects for the first object whose template name equals toc_name and xfers into that existing instance. Only if none exists does it Object::new_with_id(..., None team) or new_for_xfer_load stub, then register_object.
Unknown templates still allocate a stub and xfer into it instead of skip(block).
No addWallPiece after creating a walk-on-wall object.

## Evidence
xfer_helpers.rs:335-354 find_map template-name reuse then continue.
xfer_helpers.rs:360-376 new_with_id / new_for_xfer_load fallback.
C++ GameLogic.cpp:4761-4783 findTemplate + newObject(defaultTeam) + addWallPiece.

## Player-visible effect
A save with two GLAFighters overwrites the first leftover map fighter twice and never creates the second. Objects are not on the neutral default team. Unknown-template patches cannot skip. Wall-walk pieces are omitted from the pathfinder, so troops path through walls after load.
close_reason: GameLogic object load uses newObject(defaultTeam), skips unknown templates, addWallPiece for walk-on-wall

title: [Locomotor] INI omitted-field defaults diverge from C++ ctor
description:
## C++
`LocomotorTemplate::LocomotorTemplate` (Locomotor.cpp:257-334):
- m_braking = BIGNUM (99999)
- m_minTurnSpeed = BIGNUM
- m_pitchStiffness/m_rollStiffness = 0.1
- m_pitchDamping/m_rollDamping = 0.9
- m_uniformAxialDamping = 1.0
- m_airborneTargetingHeight = INT_MAX
- m_wanderLengthFactor = 1.0
- m_preferredHeightDamping = 1.0
- m_closeEnoughDist = 1.0
- m_speedLimitZ = 999999
- damaged maxima = -1 (healed in validate)

## Rust
Common `ini_locomotor.rs` defaults: braking=0, min_turn_speed=0, pitch/roll stiffness=0, pitch/roll damping=0, uniform_axial_damping=0, airborne_targeting_height=0. GameLogic `template.rs::new` is worse: wander_length_factor=0 (divides in `Locomotor::new`), close_enough_dist=5, preferred_height_damping=0.5, speed_limit_z=5, max_speed=10.

## Evidence
C++ comment: \"it's highly unlikely you want zero for the defaults for stiffness and damping\". Rust INI ctor zeros them. GameLogic `Locomotor::new` does `(PI/40) * (rng / template.wander_length_factor)` — 0 default is Inf/NaN.

## Player-visible effect
Locomotors that omit Braking cannot stop (0 vs near-instant). Omitted PitchStiffness/Damping makes vehicles flop instead of sit on springs. Airborne targeting height 0 marks every unit as an AA target. Wander length 0 NaNs infantry wander.

## Split hint
One Default impl matching C++ ctor; GameLogic templates constructed from the Common store, not a second default table.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Locomotor] INI parser skips C++ unit conversions on several keys
description:
## C++
`LocomotorTemplate::getFieldParse` (Locomotor.cpp:417-488):
- MinSpeed / MinTurnSpeed / SpeedLimitZ → `parseVelocityReal` (dist/sec → dist/frame)
- Extra2DFriction → `parseFrictionPerSec` (`* SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME`)
- MaxThrustAngle / FrontWheelTurnAngle → `parseAngleReal` (deg → rad)
- BounceAmount → `parseAngularVelocityReal` (deg/sec → rad/frame)
- SlideIntoPlaceTime → `parseDurationReal` (time → frames)
Speed/TurnRate/Acceleration/Lift/Braking already convert.

## Rust
`ini_locomotor.rs` `parse_locomotor_template_definition` converts Speed (/30), TurnRate (deg→rad/frame), Acceleration/Lift/Braking (/900) but raw-parses MinSpeed, MinTurnSpeed, SpeedLimitZ, Extra2DFriction, MaxThrustAngle, BounceAmount, FrontWheelTurnAngle, SlideIntoPlaceTime.

## Evidence
```
"MinSpeed" => { template.min_speed = value.parse()? }  // no /30
"Extra2DFriction" => { template.extra_2d_friction = value.parse()? }  // no per-sec→frame
"MaxThrustAngle" => { template.max_thrust_angle = value.parse()? }  // no deg→rad
```

## Player-visible effect
Jets/helis with authored MinSpeed run ~30× too fast at idle. Thrust cone is ~30 rad instead of ~30°. Extra2DFriction is 30× too strong. Wheel turn / bounce-kick / slide-in time are wrong.

## Split hint
Share C++ parseVelocityReal / parseAngleReal / parseFrictionPerSec / parseDurationReal helpers with the Common INI locomotor table.
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade
