title: [Xfer] CHUNK_TeamFactory skips TeamPrototype/Team snapshots and inserts extra prototype-id counter
description:
## C++
TeamFactory::xfer (Team.cpp:409, version 1): xferVersion, xferUser(&m_uniqueTeamID, sizeof(TeamID)) only — no prototype-id counter — xferUnsignedShort(prototypeCount), then for each prototype: xferUser(TeamPrototypeID) + xferSnapshot(TeamPrototype).
TeamPrototype::xfer (Team.cpp:1175, version 2): owning player index, attackPriorityName (v>=2), productionConditionAlwaysFalse, xferSnapshot(team template), instance count, then each TeamID + xferSnapshot(Team).
Team::xfer (Team.cpp:2547, version 1): TeamID, member ObjectIDs, state, entered/active/created/sight flags, destroy threshold, curUnits, waypoint, generic-script flags, recruitability, commonAttackTarget, team/player relation maps.
TeamFactory::crc / TeamPrototype::crc / Team::crc are empty. XferCRC::xferSnapshot calls crc(), so DeepCrc of CHUNK_TeamFactory writes nothing.

## Rust
Live CHUNK_TeamFactory is TeamFactorySnapshotBridge (game_logic_impl/snapshot.rs:224-237). crc() and xfer() both call xfer_team_factory_runtime_state (xfer_helpers.rs:826).
That helper writes version 1, next_team_id, next_team_prototype_id (extra 4 bytes not in C++), prototype count, then prototype IDs only. It never calls TeamPrototype::xfer or Team::xfer.
Complete Team::xfer lives unused in GameLogic/src/team/snapshot.rs:114-305. Common/src/common/rts/team.rs TeamPrototype Snapshotable is leftover.

## Evidence
Team.cpp:418 `xfer->xferUser( &m_uniqueTeamID, sizeof( TeamID ) );` then prototype snapshots at :454-457.
xfer_helpers.rs:835-872 writes both next_team_id and next_team_prototype_id, then IDs only.

## Player-visible effect
Save/load drops every team instance: membership, script state, recruitability, common-attack target, and per-team relations. Extra prototype-id u32 shifts the rest of the chunk so C++ cannot read a Rust save (and vice versa). DeepCrc hashes the abbreviated factory record instead of C++ empty TeamFactory::crc.

## Split hint
TeamFactorySnapshotBridge should xfer uniqueTeamID then each TeamPrototype snapshot (which xfers Team instances). Do not persist uniqueTeamPrototypeID.
close_reason: CHUNK_TeamFactory xfers uniqueTeamID + TeamPrototype/Team snapshots; no uniqueTeamPrototypeID; crc empty

title: [Xfer] CHUNK_Players writes abbreviated fields instead of PlayerList+Player::xfer v8
description:
## C++
PlayerList.cpp:424 PlayerList::xfer version 1: xferVersion, xferInt(m_playerCount), then xferSnapshot(m_players[i]) for each player.
XferSave/XferLoad call Player::xfer (Player.cpp:3975, currentVersion=8): Money snapshot, upgrade list, preorder (v7), disabled/hidden sciences (v8), radar, upgrade masks, Energy snapshot, team prototypes, build list, AIPlayer snapshot, resource manager, tunnel tracker, default team, sciences, rank/skill/science points, level up/down, general name, player/team relations, build flags, skill modifier (v2), listInScoreScreen (v3), attackedBy, cash bounty, ScoreKeeper, kindof production list, special-power timers (v4), hotkey squads, current selection, battle-plan bonuses, unitsShouldHunt (v6).
PlayerList::crc (PlayerList.cpp:411) writes playerCount then xferSnapshot each Player, and XferCRC.cpp:109 calls Player::crc (battle-plan bonuses + skill/science points only).

## Rust
Live CHUNK_Players is PlayerListSnapshotBridge in GameLogic/src/system/game_logic_impl/snapshot.rs:200-221. Both crc() and xfer() call xfer_player_list_runtime_state (xfer_helpers.rs:732).
That helper writes version 2 (C++ is 1), playerCount, then per player: raw money int, energy production/consumption/sabotage ints, defeated bool (not in C++ Player::xfer), observer, rank, science points, and only if version>=2 the AI/resource/tunnel auxiliary block.
The complete Player::xfer v8 lives in GameLogic/src/player/snapshot.rs:95-713 but is never invoked by the save/DeepCrc block. Common/src/common/rts/player.rs Snapshotable is leftover.

## Evidence
xfer_helpers.rs:736 `let current_version: XferVersion = 2;`
xfer_helpers.rs:767-820 money/energy/defeated/observer/rank/science + optional auxiliary.
snapshot.rs:207 `fn xfer(...) { xfer_player_list_runtime_state(xfer) }` and crc() calls xfer().

## Player-visible effect
Save/load cannot restore upgrades, sciences, squads, relations, score, battle plans, radar, or team links. C++ .sav files desync at the first player record. DeepCrc of CHUNK_Players hashes a different byte stream than C++ PlayerList::crc + Player::crc, so lockstep CRC cannot match retail.

## Split hint
Keep Player::xfer in player/snapshot.rs; make PlayerListSnapshotBridge call PlayerList/Player Snapshotable instead of xfer_player_list_runtime_state.
close_reason: CHUNK_Players is PlayerList v1 + Player::xfer v8; crc is playerCount + Player::crc

title: [Weapon] Live Weapon has no computeApproachTarget; host residual is a 2D standoff
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `Weapon::computeApproachTarget` (1977-2102): partition vector (bounding-sphere 2D), min-range backup to midpoint of min/max plus radii, airborne 180° turn avoid, angleOffset, contact weapons walk to the target, 0.9 range fudge, clipToTerrainExtent, and aircraft `adjustTargetDestination` so jets do not stack.

## Rust
Live public `weapon_instance::Weapon` has no `compute_approach_target`. The C++-shaped function lives only on leftover private `weapon.rs` (1218-1286) and is not exported (mod.rs:53). Host `weapon_bootstrap/pitch_range.rs` `compute_approach_target_pos` (157+) is a simplified 2D standoff at `attackRange * 0.9` (contact via range heuristic). Separate `compute_min_range_backup_pos` exists but is not the C++ midpoint+radii+airborne path.

## Evidence
Grep: `compute_approach_target` only in leftover weapon.rs. Host residual comment: "C++ Weapon::computeApproachTarget residual (simplified 2D)".

## Player-visible effect
Artillery inside MinimumAttackRange do not back up to the C++ mid-range point (radii included). Aircraft attack moves stack on the same destination. Contact bombers and angled approaches lose the C++ vector/clip behavior.

## Split hint
Implement on live Weapon and call it from the host attack-move residual instead of a second formula.
close_reason: Live Weapon::compute_approach_target in weapon_approach.rs: 2D partition vector, min-range midpoint+radii, airborne 180, contact walk-to-target, 0.9 fudge, clipToTerrainExtent, aircraft adjustTargetDestination.

title: [WeaponSet] Victim anti-mask misses missiles, demotraps, and ground-only
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet.cpp` `getVictimAntiMask` (347-389) is exclusive: SMALL_MISSILE, else BALLISTIC_MISSILE, else PROJECTILE, else MINE|DEMOTRAP → ANTI_MINE|ANTI_GROUND, else airborne vehicle/infantry/parachute, else ANTI_GROUND. Used by `getAbleToUseWeaponAgainstTarget` and `chooseBestWeaponForTarget`. Ground position shots are WEAPON_ANTI_GROUND only.

## Rust
`Object::get_anti_mask` (object_combat.rs:1049-1072) ORs PROJECTILE, MINE, PARACHUTING status, then if airborne or KINDOF_AIRCRAFT adds AIRBORNE_INFANTRY or AIRBORNE_VEHICLE, else GROUND if mask still 0. Missing SMALL_MISSILE, BALLISTIC_MISSILE, DEMOTRAP, PARACHUTE kindof. Aircraft on the ground still count as airborne. Live WeaponSet uses this for objects and `0xffffffff` for ground (weapon_set.rs:1215-1220), so every weapon can attack the ground.

## Evidence
C++ 349-364 exclusive missile/mine/demotrap. Rust 1052-1070 additive projectile+mine, aircraft→airborne, no ballistic/small-missile bits. Ground: C++ 598 WEAPON_ANTI_GROUND vs Rust 1220 0xffffffff.

## Player-visible effect
Anti-missile base defenses cannot distinguish small vs ballistic missiles; demotraps are not mine-targetable; grounded aircraft are treated as flying; anti-air-only weapons can force-attack empty ground.

## Split hint
Port getVictimAntiMask as a free function next to WeaponSet targeting; do not reuse Object::get_anti_mask as-is.
close_reason: get_victim_anti_mask exclusive SMALL/BALLISTIC/PROJECTILE/MINE|DEMOTRAP/airborne/GROUND; WeaponSet object shots use it and ground shots are ANTI_GROUND only.

title: [ScriptEngine] TEAM_GARRISON_NEAREST_BUILDING issues untargeted Enter
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/ScriptEngine/ScriptActions.cpp` `ScriptActions::doTeamGarrisonNearestBuilding` (3358-3422), dispatched from `executeAction` case `TEAM_GARRISON_NEAREST_BUILDING` (6898-6899).
Takes the team leader, partition-filters nearest garrisonable buildings (`PartitionFilterGarrisonableByPlayer` or internet-center for money hackers, same-map status), iterates near-to-far, and for each building fills remaining contain slots by sending only infantry without `KINDOF_NO_GARRISON` via `ai->aiEnter(theBuilding, CMD_FROM_SCRIPT)`.

## Rust
Live dispatch in `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/scripting/executor/dispatch.rs` maps `ScriptActionType::TeamGarrisonNearestBuilding` to `do_team_garrison_nearest_building`.
Handler `executor/actions_team_relations.rs` 487-501 creates an AI group and issues `AiCommandType::Enter` with **no target object**. Contrast the named sibling `do_named_garrison_nearest_building` which does a partition closest-building search.

## Evidence
```
let params = AiCommandParams::new(AiCommandType::Enter, CommandSourceType::FromScript);
let _ = group.ai_do_command(&params);
```
C++ fills per-building slots from `iterateObjectsInRange(..., ITER_SORTED_NEAR_TO_FAR)`.

## Player-visible effect
Campaign/skirmish scripts that tell a team to garrison the nearest building never pick a building or split the team across available slots. Units idle or Enter nothing; garrison-the-town-hall / fill-bunker scripts fail.

## Split hint
Keep nearest-garrison with other contain orders in `executor/actions_team_relations.rs` (or a new `actions_garrison.rs` next to `actions_team_command.rs` / `actions_named.rs`).
close_reason: New actions_garrison.rs do_team_garrison_nearest_building matches C++ 3358-3422: team leader partition filter (internet center for money hackers else garrisonable structures), near-to-far, fill remaining contain slots with infantry without KINDOF_NO_GARRISON via targeted Enter.

title: [ScriptEngine] DISABLE_INPUT/ENABLE_INPUT skip cinematic UI teardown
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/ScriptEngine/ScriptActions.cpp` `doDisableInput` (3176-3189) and `doEnableInput` (3195-3198), dispatched from `executeAction` for `DISABLE_INPUT` / `ENABLE_INPUT`.
Disable: `TheInGameUI->setInputEnabled(false)`, `TheMouse->setVisibility(false)`, `deselectAllDrawables()`, `clearAttackMoveToMode()`, `setWaypointMode(FALSE)`, `TheControlBar->deleteBuildTooltipLayout()`, `TheLookAtTranslator->resetModes()`.
Enable: `setInputEnabled(true)` and `TheMouse->setVisibility(true)`.

## Rust
Live dispatch in `scripting/executor/dispatch.rs` maps both types to `do_disable_input` / `do_enable_input`.
`executor/actions_player_display_camera.rs` 697-708 only calls `TheGameLogic::set_input_enabled(false/true)` and returns Success. No mouse hide, no deselect, no waypoint/attack-move clear, no build-tooltip teardown, no LookAtTranslator reset.

## Evidence
```
pub(crate) fn do_disable_input(...) {
    TheGameLogic::set_input_enabled(false);
    Ok(ScriptActionResult::Success)
}
```

## Player-visible effect
Cinematic scripts that lock input still leave the cursor visible, current selection highlighted, attack-move/waypoint modes armed, and the build tooltip up. Re-enable never restores the mouse if something else hid it. Campaign briefings and scripted cameras feel leaky.

## Split hint
Input lock belongs with other InGameUI script actions (`CameoFlash`, letterbox) — extract `executor/actions_input_ui.rs` from `actions_player_display_camera.rs`.
close_reason: New actions_input_ui.rs queues cinematic lock; GameClient apply_pending_script_display_state runs C++ doDisableInput teardown (setInputEnabled, mouse visibility, deselect, clear attack-move/waypoint, deleteBuildTooltipLayout, LookAtTranslator::resetModes) and doEnableInput restore.

title: [Audio] Stop/death leftover sounds skip Decay tails
description:
## C++
`MilesAudioManager::processPlayingList` (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:2299-2303`): when a positional event's object/drawable is gone, `isDead()` is true but `getCurrentPosition()` still returns the last position. C++ calls `stopAudioEvent` which only sets `m_requestStop = true` (`936-947`) and leaves the sample playing. On EOS, `notifyOfAudioCompletion` (`1519-1553`) refuses `startNextLoop` if `m_requestStop` (`2724-2726`), then `advanceNextPlayPortion` (`AudioEventRTS.cpp:445-466`) moves `PP_Sound` → `PP_Decay` when a Decay file exists and `playSample3D` plays it. `removeAudioEvent` / `AR_Stop` use the same requestStop path, so killed loops also play their leftover Decay tail.

## Rust
Live `AudioManager::process_playing_list` (`game_audio.rs:2196-2200`) treats `is_dead()` as an immediate `hook.stop(handle)`. `stop_playing_handle` (`1537-1541`) used by `AR_Stop` and `handle_to_kill` also `hook.stop`s with no portion advance. `notify_of_audio_completion` can play Decay only if the sink is allowed to reach EOS; death/stop never get there. `get_current_position` for `OwnerType::Dead` still returns the last position (matches C++), but the dead branch stops before Decay.

## Evidence
C++: `if (playing->m_audioEventRTS->isDead()) { stopAudioEvent(...); it++; continue; }` — requestStop, no release.
C++: `if (looping->m_requestStop) return false;` then `advanceNextPlayPortion()` / `PP_Decay`.
Rust: `if event.get_current_position().is_none() || event.is_dead() { ... to_stop.push(handle); }` then `hook.stop(handle)`.
Rust: `fn stop_playing_handle` → `hook.stop(handle)` immediately.

## Player-visible effect
When a unit dies, leaves the map, or its sound is replaced/stopped, retail plays the INI Decay tail (engine wind-down, fire-out, etc.). Rust cuts the sample dead. Looping move/fire/ambient leftovers vanish instead of decaying.

## Split hint
Keep requestStop vs immediate-stop in `game_audio.rs` process_playing_list / stop_playing_handle. Reuse the existing EOS `notify_of_audio_completion` Decay path from hq-ayxo rather than a new decay module.
close_reason: stop/death sets requestStop; EOS notify plays Decay tail

title: [Audio] 3D attenuation applied twice then drops zoom/3D slider
description:
## C++
`MilesAudioManager::getEffectiveVolume` (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:2658-2715`) applies inverse-min falloff once: `volume *= 1 / (objDistance / objMinDistance)` past min, `0` at max, times `m_sound3DVolume`. `playSample3D` (`2809-2824`) sets Miles 3D min/max distances from the event (or GlobalMin/MaxRange for `ST_GLOBAL`) and `AIL_set_3D_position` from `getCurrentPosition()`. `processPlayingList` (`2296-2324`) re-reads `getCurrentPosition()` every frame (object/drawable follow) and updates the 3D sample position; hardware does the spatial mix.

## Rust
Live path is `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/audio/game_audio.rs` `RodioPlaybackHook`.
1. `play` (`2629-2673`) sets `base_volume = miles_get_effective_volume(...)` (already includes inverse falloff + 3D slider) then `refresh_sink_volume` multiplies by `calculate_3d_volume_falloff` again — double attenuation at start.
2. `miles_get_effective_volume` / `play` use `event.get_position()`, not `get_current_position()`, so object-attached events start at the default origin until a later tick.
3. `process_playing_list` (`2226`) then `set_event_volume` (`2731-2742`) overwrites `base_volume` with raw `event.get_volume()` (no 3D slider/zoom) and applies falloff once. Zoom/`set_3DVolumeAdjustment` no longer reaches the sink unless `volume_has_changed` takes the other path.
4. Rodio `Sink` is volume-only; `AIL_set_3D_position` panning is not applied. `audio_3d.rs` `SpatialAudioProcessor` is unused on the live path.

## Evidence
C++: `volume *= m_sound3DVolume;` then `volume *= 1 / (objDistance / objMinDistance);` once; `AIL_set_3D_position(playing->m_3DSample, x, y, z);`
Rust play: `let mut volume = miles_get_effective_volume(...);` then `state.base_volume = volume;` + `refresh_sink_volume` → `base * miles_positional_gain`.
Rust update: `state.base_volume = event.get_volume();` + falloff, no slider.

## Player-visible effect
World/unit 3D sounds start too quiet (squared distance), then jump to a mix that ignores the 3D/zoom slider. Attached engine/weapon sounds pop in at the map origin for a frame. Camera zoom no longer boosts nearby 3D SFX the way AudioSettings.ini Zoom* keys intend. Sounds also never pan left/right with camera heading.

## Split hint
Keep Miles volume math in `audio_event_rts.rs` (`miles_get_effective_volume`). Apply it once in the rodio hook. Follow objects via `get_current_position` at play and each tick. Optional: wire `audio_3d.rs` pan into the hook; do not add a third volume path.
close_reason: slider volume once + miles_event_world_position at play and tick

title: [EVA] isCurrentlyPlaying is handle!=0 so only the first EVA line plays
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/Eva.cpp` `Eva::processPlayingMessages` (lines 477-524): if `m_evaSpeech.isCurrentlyPlaying()` it returns without starting another line, otherwise it picks the highest `m_priority` unplayed check and `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`. `AudioEventRTS::isCurrentlyPlaying` (`AudioEventRTS.cpp:666-668`) queries `TheAudio->isCurrentlyPlaying(m_playingHandle)`, which becomes false when the stream ends. After EOS the next update can fire the highest-priority waiting EVA (unit lost vs base under attack vs superweapon).

## Rust
Live EVA is `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/eva.rs` `Eva::process_playing_messages` (lines 672-737). It uses `gamelogic::common::audio::AudioEventRts` (`GameLogic/src/common/audio.rs:79-81`) whose `is_currently_playing()` is `self.playing_handle != 0`. After the first successful `TheAudio::add_audio_event` the handle is nonzero and is never cleared, so occupancy stays true for the rest of the match. Higher-priority checks can be queued but never start. Common's live `AudioEventRts::is_currently_playing` (`common/audio/audio_event_rts.rs:808-816`) does query the manager; Eva does not use that type.

## Evidence
C++: `if (m_evaSpeech.isCurrentlyPlaying()) { return; }` then `m_priority > highestPriority` pick + `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`.
C++: `return TheAudio->isCurrentlyPlaying(m_playingHandle);`
Rust Eva: `if self.eva_speech.is_currently_playing() { return; }`
Rust GameLogic leftover: `pub fn is_currently_playing(&self) -> bool { self.playing_handle != 0 }`

## Player-visible effect
Only the first EVA line of a match plays. Later alerts (base under attack, unit lost, superweapon ready/launched, low power after the first) are silently dropped even when they have higher INI Priority. Retail waits for the current line to finish, then plays the highest-priority waiting message.

## Split hint
Keep Eva.cpp port in `eva.rs`. Point `eva_speech` at Common `AudioEventRts` (or call `TheAudio::is_currently_playing(handle)`). Do not grow GameLogic `common/audio.rs`.
close_reason: Eva occupancy queries TheAudio::is_currently_playing(handle)

title: [AI States] Wander/Panic never fire completed-waypoint scripts
description:
## C++
`AIWanderState::update` (AIStates.cpp:4574-4578) and `AIPanicState::update` (4815-4819): when `getNextWaypoint()` is NULL, call `ai->setCompletedWaypoint(m_priorWaypoint)` then `STATE_SUCCESS`. That stamps the unit so map scripts waiting on “end of waypoint path” fire.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/wander_panic.rs` wander `classic_on_update` (232-235) and panic (416-419) return `StateReturnType::Success` when `get_next_waypoint` is None. No `set_completed_waypoint_id`. The same call exists in `states/waypoint.rs` for follow-waypoint, but wander/panic do not use it.

## Evidence
C++: `ai->setCompletedWaypoint(m_priorWaypoint); return STATE_SUCCESS;`
Rust wander_panic.rs:234-235: `if self.core.current_waypoint.is_none() { return Ok(StateReturnType::Success); }`

## Player-visible effect
Scripted civilian wander/panic paths never trigger “unit completed waypoint path” (evac, next-script, ambient civilian cycles stall).

## Split hint
Call the same `set_completed_waypoint_id(prior)` helper already used by `states/waypoint.rs`.
close_reason: wander_panic.rs: when get_next_waypoint is None, wander and panic call set_completed_waypoint_id(prior) then STATE_SUCCESS, matching C++ setCompletedWaypoint.

title: [AI States] Wander/Panic skip InternalMoveTo move loop
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIStates.cpp` `AIWanderState::onEnter` (4526) / `update` (4553) and `AIPanicState::onEnter` (4759) / `update` (4791) / `onExit` (4839) call `AIInternalMoveToState::onEnter`/`update`/`onExit`. That parent loop starts the move-loop audio (`startMoveSound` ~1667), waits for the path, recomputes when blocked (`isBlockedAndStuck` / `getNumFramesBlocked()>2s`), sets `MODELCONDITION_MOVING`/`CLIMBING`/`RAPPELLING`, and on exit stops the ambient handle and calls `friend_endingMove` (1713-1736). Panic also sets/clears `MODELCONDITION_PANICKING`.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/wander_panic.rs` `AIWanderState`/`AIPanicState` `classic_on_enter` only `compute_goal` + `compute_path` + `set_path_extra_distance`. `classic_on_update` compares `get_locomotor_distance_to_goal` to close-enough and advances waypoints. No call into `AIInternalMoveToState` (`states/move.rs` `start_move_sound`, blocked repath, model-condition MOVING). Wander `classic_on_exit` is empty (C++ `AIFollowWaypointPathState::onExit` → parent `onExit`). Panic onExit only clears PANICKING.

## Evidence
C++: `StateReturnType status = AIInternalMoveToState::update();` then waypoint advance. Rust wander_panic.rs:186-244 never calls `AIInternalMoveToState::classic_on_update`.

## Player-visible effect
Civilians wandering or panicking along a waypoint path do not play move-loop audio, do not show MOVING/CLIMBING, and do not repath when blocked — they stall or slide instead of running the C++ move loop.

## Split hint
Keep wander/panic in `wander_panic.rs` but share the live `AIInternalMoveToState` parent (already in `states/move.rs`) instead of a distance-only shortcut.
close_reason: wander_panic.rs: AIWander/AIPanic compose AIMoveToState (is_move_to=false) and call InternalMoveTo enter/update/exit for move sound, MOVING/CLIMBING, blocked repath, friend_ending_move. Panic still sets/clears PANICKING.

title: [TurretAI] Idle does not unsync linked turrets
description:
## C++
`TurretAIIdleState::onEnter` (TurretAI.cpp:1269-1282): after `resetNextMoodCheckTime()`, if this turret is the current sync owner (`ai->friend_getTurretSync() == getTurretAI()->friend_getWhichTurret()`), it writes `TURRET_INVALID`. Linked dual-turret units (Overlord cannon + bunker, Paladin, etc.) can then recenter/scan independently once idle.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/turret.rs` `TurretAIIdleState::classic_on_enter` (1494-1516) only resets mood-check time and `reset_idle_scan`. No `friend_getTurretSync` / `friend_setTurretSync(Invalid)` (or equivalent on `AIUpdateInterface.turret_sync_flag`).

## Evidence
C++: `if (ai->friend_getTurretSync() == getTurretAI()->friend_getWhichTurret()) ai->friend_setTurretSync(TURRET_INVALID);`
Rust turret.rs:1494-1516: mood reset + idle-scan timer only.

## Player-visible effect
After a burst of fire, linked turrets stay glued: the secondary keeps tracking the primary’s aim instead of recentering/idling, so Overlord-style vehicles look locked and may refuse a new target until both turrets move together.

## Split hint
Turret idle/hold/recenter already live in `ai/turret.rs`; add the sync-clear next to the existing mood-reset in idle `onEnter`.
close_reason: turret.rs TurretAIIdleState::onEnter unsyncs if friend_get_turret_sync == friend_get_which_turret, writing TurretType::Invalid. UnitAIUpdate stores turret_sync_flag.

title: [Weapon] createLaser spawns at the target and never raises the beam +10z
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `Weapon::createLaser` (2418-2451): creates the laser on the source player's default team, `setPosition(sourceObj->getPosition())`, then LaserUpdate::initLaser. If the victim is not a projectile and not airborne, `pos.z += 10` so the beam does not hit feet. Uses `m_template->getLaserBoneName()`.

## Rust
Live `weapon_instance_combat.rs` `create_laser_object` (1050-1153) uses `source.get_team()` (not controlling-player default team), `set_position(&end_pos)` (target, not source), and `init_laser` with the raw end position. No +10z raise. `configure_laser`/`activate_laser` on a behavior interface is extra vs C++ client LaserUpdate.

## Evidence
C++ 2432 `laser->setPosition(sourceObj->getPosition())`; 2443-2447 `pos.z += 10.0f`. Rust 1106 `let _ = laser_guard.set_position(&end_pos);` and 1141-1147 init_laser without z offset.

## Player-visible effect
Patriot / Avenger / point-defense beams originate at the impact point instead of the firer and strike infantry/vehicle feet instead of the body. Lasers may fail to draw until the target is on-screen.

## Split hint
Keep create_laser_object next to fire ContinuousBeam; LaserUpdate init belongs with the client module.
close_reason: create_laser_object uses controlling-player default team, set_position(source), +10z for non-projectile non-airborne victims, laser bone name already passed to init_laser.

title: [Weapon] Live projectile create never reports missiles for countermeasures
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `fireWeaponTemplate` (1144-1155): after launch, if the projectile is KINDOF_SMALL_MISSILE and the victim `hasCountermeasures()`, and the victim locomotor set is not SUPERSONIC, call `victimObj->reportMissileForCountermeasures(projectile)` so jets can spawn a flare and divert the shot.

## Rust
Live `create_projectile` (weapon_instance_combat.rs:858-1041) launches MissileAI/DumbProjectile/Neutron and returns. No SMALL_MISSILE kindof check, no hasCountermeasures, no SUPERSONIC gate, no report_missile_for_countermeasures. A weaker report exists only on leftover `template.rs` `fire_weapon_template` (712-732), which live fire does not call.

## Evidence
C++ 1144-1153. Live create_projectile ends at launched / set_position(target) / Ok(projectile_id) with no countermeasure call.

## Player-visible effect
Aurora, Missile Defender, and other small missiles never trigger jet flares. Raptors/Auroras under fire do not decoy incoming missiles.

## Split hint
Add the C++ gate at the end of create_projectile after launch.
close_reason: create_projectile reports KINDOF_SMALL_MISSILE to victim.report_missile_for_countermeasures unless locomotor set is SUPERSONIC.

title: [Weapon] Live fire never applies sneaky targeting offset
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `fireWeaponTemplate` (802-816): if the victim AI returns `getSneakyTargetingOffset`, the shot retargets that offset position and clears victimObj/victimID so the weapon aims at the decoy point, not the real object (also used for distance).

## Rust
Live `private_fire_weapon` aims at `get_object_position(target)` then scatter. No sneaky-offset query. `get_sneaky_targeting_offset` is only used in leftover collide helpers (`template.rs:219`, `weapon_template.rs:617`) to skip a collision, not to retarget fire.

## Evidence
C++ 803-814 `ai->getSneakyTargetingOffset` then `victimObj = NULL`. Live weapon_instance.rs:1544-1552 builds target_position from the real object position only.

## Player-visible effect
Units that advertise a sneaky targeting offset (hijack/decoy-style AI) are shot at their true position. Attackers cannot be spoofed; the authored miss offset never happens.

## Split hint
Apply the offset at the start of private_fire_weapon / fireWeaponTemplate before scatter.
close_reason: private_fire_weapon applies AI get_sneaky_targeting_offset and clears victim so the shot aims at the decoy point.

title: Live OCLSpecialPower never applies OCLAdjustPositionToPassable
description:
## Why
C++ Paradrop (and any OCL with OCLAdjustPositionToPassable) snaps the click onto a passable cell before spawning the deliverer. Live host records the flag and still uses the raw click.

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/SpecialPower/OCLSpecialPower.cpp`
- Module default `m_isOCLAdjustPositionToPassable = FALSE` (53).
- INI `OCLAdjustPositionToPassable` (81).
- `doSpecialPowerAtLocation` (143-154): if flag, `FindPositionOptions` `FPF_CLEAR_CELLS_ONLY`, `maxRadius = MAX_ADJUST_RADIUS` (500); `ThePartitionManager->findPositionAround`; on failure keep original `*loc`.
- Then `SpecialPowerModule::doSpecialPowerAtLocation(&targetCoord, ...)` and OCL create at the (possibly adjusted) coord.

## Rust live path
- `Main/src/game_logic/host_ocl_special_power.rs:118-135`: SuperweaponParadropAmerica peel has `adjust_position_to_passable: true`.
- `plan_ocl_special_power_at_location` (274-302): copies `target_pos` unchanged into `target_coord`; only sets `adjust_passable_requested`.
- File header admits "partition findPositionAround passable search (flag recorded only)".

close_reason: host_ocl_special_power.rs + infantry_weapons.rs: plan_ocl_special_power_at_location now snaps target via findPositionAround(CLEAR_CELLS_ONLY, r=500) using host pathfind CELL_CLEAR; failed search keeps original click. Paradrop peel flag is honored before OCL create.

title: Live NeutronBlast skips structures and never killAllContained
description:
## Why
C++ NeutronBlastBehavior wipes infantry even when they hide in containers and still runs killAllContained on structures/transports. Live host legality rejects structures and applies a single infantry/vehicle effect with no contain walk.

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Behavior/NeutonBlastBehavior.cpp`
- Defaults (`NeutronBlastBehavior.h`): BlastRadius 10, AffectAirborne TRUE, AffectAllies TRUE. NeutronCannonShell INI overrides radius 70 / AffectAirborne No.
- `onDie` (42-70): partition iterate FROM_CENTER_2D, Alive + SameMapStatus; skip aircraft/airborne unless AffectAirborne.
- `neutronBlastToObject` (84-138): skip self; skip ALLIES when !AffectAllies; `KINDOF_INFANTRY` → `kill()`; if contain → `contain->killAllContained()`; vehicle && !drone → CLIFF_JUMPER kill else DISABLED_UNMANNED + aiIdle + deselect + clear terrain decal + setTeam(neutral).

## Rust live path
- `Main/src/game_logic/host_neutron_shell.rs:153-186` `is_legal_neutron_blast_target`: `is_structure` → false; `is_drone` → false. Structures never enter the blast.
- `neutron_effect_for_target` (203-219): one of KillInfantry / UnmanVehicle / KillVehicle / None. No contain branch.
- `Main/src/game_logic/world_combat/drones_and_garrison.rs:185-280` `apply_neutron_blast_at`: filters via that legality helper (drone KindOf hardcoded false), then one effect. No `killAllContained`.
- Crate `GameLogic/src/object/behavior/neutron_blast_behavior.rs` walks contain IDs but is Wave-327 empty-registry no-op on the live host.

## Player-visible
Garrisoned/transported infantry survive a neutron shell; bunkers/APCs in the blast keep their passengers. C++ kills them even when the husk is only unmanned.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live blast applies killAllContained to every in-radius container (including structures)
- [ ] Infantry still die; vehicles unman (combat-bike/cliff-jumper die); drones skip unman but still dump passengers
- [ ] AffectAllies / AffectAirborne match module data (shell: airborne no)
close_reason: host_neutron_shell.rs + drones_and_garrison.rs apply_neutron_blast_at: legality no longer rejects structures/drones; blast walks contained_units and killAllContained on every in-radius container including structures; infantry die, vehicles unman, drones skip unman but dump passengers.

title: Live SuperweaponCashHack steals from richest enemy, not targeted victim
description:
## Why
C++ CashHackSpecialPower is object-targeted: money comes from the clicked victim's controlling player. Live host ignores the target and drains the richest enemy economy.

## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/SpecialPower/CashHackSpecialPower.cpp`
- `doSpecialPowerAtLocation` (76-83): disabled check then return — location fire is a no-op.
- `doSpecialPowerAtObject` (106-155): `SpecialPowerModule::doSpecialPowerAtObject` then `victim->getControllingPlayer()->getMoney()`, `min(desiredAmount, cash)`, withdraw/deposit, `addMoneyEarned`, floating text `GUI:AddCash` over self (z+20 green) and `GUI:LoseCash` over victim (z+30 red).
- `findAmountToSteal` (87-102): first owned UpgradeMoneyAmount science in INI order, else MoneyAmount.

## Rust live path
- `Main/src/command_executor/special_power.rs:584-588`: `SpecialPowerType::CashHack` calls `activate_cash_hack(player_id, Some(unit_id))` inside the location-target branch; victim object is never passed.
- `Main/src/game_logic/world_scripts/helix_radar.rs:1218-1305`: walks all enemy players and picks max `resources.supplies`, then `steal_cash_between_players`. Floating text is `spawn_sabotage_cash_floating_texts(cid, cid, stolen)` (both positions = caster).
- Crate `GameLogic/src/object/special_powers/cash_hack_special_power.rs` has the object-victim path but is not the live host fire.

## Player-visible
Clicking a poor enemy building can steal from a richer enemy (or steal nothing if that player is broke while another is rich). Lose-cash float does not appear over the intended victim.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live CashHack steals from the targeted object's controlling player (object fire) and no-ops on location-only fire
- [ ] Amount is min(science-tier desired, victim cash); scorekeeper addMoneyEarned on the thief
- [ ] Green float over caster, red float over victim
close_reason: helix_radar.rs activate_cash_hack + command_executor/special_power.rs: SuperweaponCashHack steals from the clicked victim object controlling player (min desired, cash); location-only fire is a no-op; green float over caster, red over victim.

title: Live HUD still dumps full military subtitle; crate typewriter unused on present path
description:

title: [WeaponSet] getAbleToAttackSpecificObject skips stealth, mask, relationship, and container legality
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet.cpp` `getAbleToAttackSpecificObject` (423-574) rejects dead/destroyed/self, OBJECT_STATUS_MASKED, KINDOF_UNATTACKABLE, AI-no-acquire, undetected STEALTHED (with disguiser/bomb-truck exceptions), non-enemy unless force-attack/mine, enclosed container passengers, and non-enemy apparent garrison controllers. Fog does not block. Then it delegates to `getAbleToUseWeaponAgainstTarget`.

## Rust
Live `weapon_set.rs` `get_able_to_attack_specific_object` (1147-1193) only loops slots and `evaluate_weapon_against_target` (1301-1334): anti-mask, range, estimated damage > 0. No stealth, mask, relationship, enclosed-container, or apparent-controller checks. `_attack_type` and `_command_source` are unused.

## Evidence
evaluate_weapon_against_target ignores attack_type/command_source and never reads OBJECT_STATUS_STEALTHED / MASKED / getContainedBy / getRelationship. C++ 472-478 returns NOT_POSSIBLE for undetected stealth.

## Player-visible effect
Players can auto-target stealthed undetected units, masked objects, allies (without force-fire), and infantry still inside an enclosing transport. Bomb-truck disguise exception is also missing.

## Split hint
Keep legality in WeaponSet; do not push it into Weapon::check_can_fire (C++ explicitly does not).
close_reason: get_able_to_attack_specific_object rejects dead/self/masked/unattackable/AI-no-acquire/undetected stealth (disguiser exception), non-enemy unless force/mine, enclosing passengers, non-enemy apparent controllers; then delegates to getAbleToUse.

title: [Weapon] isWithinAttackRange ignores bridge ends and contact-vs-structure collision
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `isWithinAttackRange(source, target)` (2152-2207): KINDOF_BRIDGE uses `TheTerrainLogic->getBridgeAttackPoints` and accepts either end. Contact weapons vs KINDOF_STRUCTURE additionally require `iteratePotentialCollisions` so the attacker is actually touching the building, not just within the numeric range.

## Rust
Live `weapon_instance.rs` `is_within_attack_range` (423-478) is center-to-center 2D minus bounding-circle radii vs template min/max. No bridge special case. No contact-weapon collision iterate. `is_source_object_with_goal_position_within_attack_range` (559-612) is the same distance math.

## Evidence
C++ 2157-2171 bridge branch; 2190-2203 contact+structure collision. Rust 468-477 only `boundary_dist` vs min/max range.

## Player-visible effect
Units must walk to a bridge's center instead of either tower/end. Car bombs / other contact weapons fire at structures from the authored range without touching the footprint.

## Split hint
Keep range math in Weapon; pull bridge points from TerrainLogic.
close_reason: is_within_attack_range in weapon_range.rs accepts either TerrainLogic bridge end and requires iterate_potential_collisions for contact vs STRUCTURE.

title: [WeaponSet] getAbleToUseWeaponAgainstTarget missing garrison, passenger, spawn, and immobile abort
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet.cpp` `getAbleToUseWeaponAgainstTarget` (581-760):
- Ground shots use WEAPON_ANTI_GROUND; object shots use getVictimAntiMask.
- Garrisoned enclosing containers `calcBestGarrisonPosition` then `isSourceObjectWithGoalPositionWithinAttackRange`.
- Immobile / SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS / contained units with a weapon but none in range return INVALID_SHOT (except tunnel-network guard).
- Occupied containers with `isPassengerAllowedToFire` recurse into members.
- Hive/spawn slaves via `getCanAnySlavesUseWeaponAgainstTarget`, forcing POSSIBLE for immobile stinger sites.

## Rust
Live `weapon_set.rs` `get_able_to_use_weapon_against_target` (1200-1283) only anti-masks, pitch, ammo, KillPilot skip, and `is_within_attack_range`. Ground target_anti_mask is `0xffffffff` (every weapon). No garrison firepoint, no passenger recursion, no spawn-slave, no immobile INVALID_SHOT.

## Evidence
weapon_set.rs:1219-1220 `} else { 0xffffffff // Ground or no target }`. No `calc_best_garrison_position`, `is_passenger_allowed_to_fire`, or spawn interface in this function.

## Player-visible effect
Garrisoned infantry show attack cursors from the building center instead of fireports; Combat Chinook / armed-rider passengers never grant the transport an attack cursor; Stinger Sites / spawn-weapon buildings get "move to attack" or invalid shots; anti-air-only weapons can force-fire the ground.

## Split hint
Split garrison firepoint vs passenger/spawn slave helpers next to Contain/SpawnBehavior.
close_reason: get_able_to_use_weapon_against_target: ANTI_GROUND for ground, garrison enclosing goal range, immobile/spawn/contained INVALID_SHOT, passenger fire recurse, spawn-slave POSSIBLE for immobile stinger sites.

title: [WeaponSet] chooseBest PREFER_LONGEST_RANGE never reads getAttackRange
description:
## C++
`WeaponSet.cpp` `chooseBestWeaponForTarget` (845-846) computes `Real damage = weapon->estimateWeaponDamage(...)` and `Real attackRange = weapon->getAttackRange(obj)` before preferred-against boosts. PREFER_LONGEST_RANGE (903-924) compares those ranges.

## Rust
Live `weapon_set.rs` `choose_best_weapon_for_target` (715) estimates damage then (754-755) writes `let mut damage = damage; let mut attack_range = attack_range;` with no prior `attack_range` binding and no `weapon.get_attack_range(source_obj)`. Preferred-against can assign HUGE_RANGE, but the non-preferred path never loads the real range. The identifier is undefined as written.

## Evidence
weapon_set.rs:754-755 `let mut attack_range = attack_range;` vs C++ 846 `Real attackRange = weapon->getAttackRange(obj);`.

## Player-visible effect
Longest-range weapon choice (AI / auto-choose) cannot prefer the actually longer gun. Ties or zeros make units keep Primary even when Secondary is the long-range option.

## Split hint
One-liner: initialize attack_range from get_attack_range before the preferred-against block.
close_reason: choose_best_weapon_for_target now binds attack_range = weapon.get_attack_range(source) before preferred-against boosts so PREFER_LONGEST_RANGE compares real ranges.

title: [Terrain] Water-grid height never uses visual mesh or GameData.INI plane
description:
## C++
Grid water is a visual mesh. `TerrainLogic::newMap` enables it when waypoint `WaveGuide1` exists, then `enableWaterGrid` (`TerrainLogic.cpp` 1127-1222) looks up `GameData.INI` `vertexWaterAvailableMaps[i]`, pushes clamps / transform (angle, xyz) / resolution / attenuation to `TheTerrainVisual`, then `TheTerrainVisual->enableWaterGrid(enable)` even on disable.
`isUnderwater` / `getWaterHandle` (`2119-2215`): if handle is `&m_gridWaterHandle`, height comes from `TheTerrainVisual->getWaterGridHeight(x,y,&wZ)` (`W3DTerrainVisual.cpp` 894-904: world-to-grid + `getGridVertexHeight`). Point is on the grid only if that query returns TRUE (inside the mesh), not an AABB.
`setWaterHeight` for the grid handle (`2287-2299`) reads/writes `TheTerrainVisual` water transform Z.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs`:
- `enable_water_grid` (2731-2773) sets a bool and validates the map name. Comment: "visual-side configuration calls are not fully ported yet". Never calls `TheTerrainVisual::enable_water_grid` / `set_water_transform` / resolution / clamps. Disable returns without notifying visual.
- `is_underwater` / `get_water_handle` (1684-1790) use `grid_water_handle.get_current_height()` and an AABB. No `TerrainVisualImpl::get_water_grid_height` (which already ports C++ mesh lookup in `impl_world.rs` 402-417).
- `set_water_height_internal` for grid names (2020-2031) only `grid_water_handle.set_height`; does not move the visual transform.

## Evidence
C++: `TheTerrainVisual->getWaterGridHeight(x, y, &wZ)` / `transform.Set_Z_Translation(height)`.
Rust: `// The visual-side configuration calls are not fully ported yet` and `let grid_z = self.grid_water_handle.get_current_height()`.

## Player-visible effect
WaveGuide maps (CHI etc.) never get the INI water plane (position, size, height). Units ignore the river mesh for wet/dry and swimming. Scripted water-table rises do not move the visible grid. `get_water_grid_height` on the visual exists but logic never drives or samples it.

## Split hint
`terrain_water` module; call live `TerrainVisualImpl` the same way C++ calls `TheTerrainVisual`.
close_reason: terrain_water.rs: enable_water_grid applies GameData.INI clamps/transform/resolution/attenuation and notifies TheTerrainVisual even on disable. is_underwater/get_water_handle sample get_water_grid_height (world-to-grid mesh), not AABB. set_water_height writes visual transform Z.

title: [Terrain] Bridge rubble does not close pathfind layer or splat units
description:
## C++
`Bridge::updateDamageState` (`TerrainLogic.cpp` 852-909) reads `bridge->getBodyModule()->getDamageState()` (INI body thresholds, not health-percent buckets). On transition to `BODY_RUBBLE`: `TheAI->pathfinder()->changeBridgeState(m_layer, false)` and every object on that layer that `objectInteractsWithBridgeLayer(..., considerBridgeHealth=false)` takes `DAMAGE_FALLING` / `DEATH_SPLATTED` / `HUGE_DAMAGE_AMOUNT`. On leaving rubble: re-enable the pathfind layer unless `BridgeBehavior::isScaffoldPresent()`. Missing object clears `bridgeObjectID`. `TerrainLogic::updateBridgeDamageStates` walks the list and sets `m_bridgeDamageStatesChanged`.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs` `Bridge::update_damage_state` (400-441): Wave 341 empty-registry no-op; otherwise buckets `health/max` into Pristine>=0.75 / Damaged>=0.50 / ReallyDamaged>=0.25 / else Rubble. Sets `damage_state_changed` only. No `changeBridgeState`, no falling splat, no scaffold gate, no invalid-id clear. `get_bridge_height` plane solve itself matches C++ `PlaneClass` intersection.

## Evidence
C++: `enum BodyDamageType damageState = bridge->getBodyModule()->getDamageState();` then `changeBridgeState` + `DAMAGE_FALLING`.
Rust: `if percent >= 0.75 { Pristine } else if percent >= 0.5 { Damaged } ...` and return.

## Player-visible effect
Destroyed bridges stay pathable. Units standing on a collapsing bridge do not splat. Repair/scaffold does not restore the layer from the body module. Health-percent buckets trip rubble at the wrong HP vs INI `Body` damage states.

## Split hint
`terrain_bridge` out of `terrain.rs`.
close_reason: terrain_bridge.rs: update_damage_state uses body-module get_damage_state, change_bridge_state(false) on rubble, DAMAGE_FALLING/DEATH_SPLATTED splat, scaffold gate on leave-rubble, invalid-id clear.

title: [Terrain] Logic LOS is 10-unit/5.0 fudge, not Bresenham max-of-4 + 0.5
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameLogic/W3DTerrainLogic.cpp` `W3DTerrainLogic::isClearLineOfSight` (241-250) forwards to `TheTerrainRenderObject->isClearLineOfSight`.
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/BaseHeightMap.cpp` `BaseHeightMapRenderObjClass::isClearLineOfSight` (979-1109, `DO_BRESENHAM`): floor world XY / MAP_XY_FACTOR + `getBorderSizeInline()`, Bresenham walk of every height-map cell, height = max of the four cell-corner samples * MAP_HEIGHT_SCALE, block if `height > z + 0.5` (`LOS_FUDGE`), early-out when `z >= getMaxHeight() && zinc > 0`. Off-map cells end the walk (still clear). Live callers: weapons, special powers, shroud, stealth, pathfind attack LOS via `TheTerrainLogic`.

## Rust
Live path is `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs` `TerrainLogic::is_clear_line_of_sight` (1642-1675), used by `TheTerrainLogic` / `helpers::math` / weapons / construction / shroud. It is a world-space stepper: `step_len = 10.0`, `clearance = 5.0`, interpolated `get_ground_height` along the segment. Comment cites PartitionManager, not the render-object Bresenham. `GameEngineDevice/.../base_height_map.rs` has a Bresenham port but is not the live gameplay query.

## Evidence
C++: `const Real LOS_FUDGE = 0.5f;` + `height = __max` of `data[idx], +1, +xExtent, +xExtent+1`.
Rust: `let step_len = 10.0_f32;` / `let clearance = 5.0_f32;` / `if ground_z > expected_z + clearance`.

## Player-visible effect
Units see (and fire / special-power / stealth-detect) through ridges that C++ blocks, and lose LOS over 0.5–5 unit bumps that C++ allows. Attack, targeting, and shroud traces disagree with the heightmap silhouette.

## Split hint
`terrain.rs` is a god-file: `terrain_los`, `terrain_height`, `terrain_water`, `terrain_bridge`.
close_reason: terrain_los.rs: Bresenham floor(world/MAP_XY)+border, max of 4 cell-corner samples * MAP_HEIGHT_SCALE, LOS_FUDGE 0.5, early-out when z>=map_max_z && zinc>0. Off-map ends walk still-clear.

title: [Terrain] is_cliff_cell ignores border and 9.8 four-corner cliff bits
description:
## C++
`W3DTerrainLogic::isCliffCell` (`W3DTerrainLogic.cpp` 335-338) calls `TheTerrainRenderObject->isCliffCell`.
`BaseHeightMapRenderObjClass::isCliffCell` (`BaseHeightMap.cpp` 1224-1246): `iX = x/MAP_XY_FACTOR + getBorderSizeInline()`, clamp to `[0, extent-2]`, then `logicHeightMap->getCliffState(iX, iY)`.
`WorldHeightMap::setCellCliffFlagFromHeights` (`WorldHeightMap.cpp` 2288-2304): cell is cliff iff four-corner world-Z range `maxZ-minZ > PATHFIND_CLIFF_SLOPE_LIMIT_F` (9.8). Bits packed 8 cells/byte (`m_cellCliffState`).

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/terrain.rs` `TerrainLogic::is_cliff_cell` (1714-1756): `(x / MAP_XY_FACTOR) as i32` with **no border offset**, reject OOB instead of clamp-to-extent-2, then 4-neighbor height delta `>= MAP_HEIGHT_SCALE * 8.0` (5.0). Does not read `WorldHeightMap` cliff bits. Device `base_height_map.rs` / `world_height_map.rs` implement `get_cliff_state` + 9.8 four-corner init but are not used by `TheTerrainLogic`. Callers: pathfind classify (`CELL_CLIFF`), construction legal-pos, minefields, partition, special-power targeting.

## Evidence
C++: `const Real cliffRange = PATHFIND_CLIFF_SLOPE_LIMIT_F;` (9.8) + `iX += logicHeightMap->getBorderSizeInline()`.
Rust: `let cliff_threshold = MAP_HEIGHT_SCALE * 8.0;` and `let map_x = (x / MAP_XY_FACTOR) as i32;` with no `border_size`.

## Player-visible effect
Playable (0,0) samples the border pad, so cliff flags are shifted by `border_size` (ZH Alpine 70 cells). Slope threshold 5.0 vs 9.8 marks milder slopes as cliffs. Units refuse to path/build on non-cliffs and walk onto real cliffs.

## Split hint
`terrain_cliff` out of `terrain.rs`; reuse device `WorldHeightMap` cliff bits instead of a second heuristic.
close_reason: terrain_cliff.rs: packed 8-cells/byte cliff bits from four-corner world-Z > 9.8. is_cliff_cell adds border_size and clamps to [0, extent-2] instead of OOB reject.

title: [Pathfind] Wall layer cells are Obstacle/Impassable instead of C++ CLEAR vs BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE
description:
## C++
PathfindLayer::classifyWallMapCell (AIPathfind.cpp:3760-3799):
- reset cell, set LAYER_WALL, default CELL_IMPASSABLE
- count how many of the 4 cell corners are on a wall piece (isPointOnWall)
- 4 corners → CELL_CLEAR (walkable wall top for KINDOF_WALK_ON_TOP_OF_WALL)
- 1–3 corners → CELL_BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE (edge)
- 0 → remains IMPASSABLE
Obstacle ID is not “first wall piece”.

## Rust
path/pathfind_layer.rs:
- classify_layer_map_cell Wall branch (:189-192) sets Impassable
- classify_wall_map_cell (:200-223): if is_point_on_wall → Obstacle + set_type_as_obstacle(wall_pieces[0]) else Clear
Comment: “first wall piece as the obstacle ID (simplified)”

## Effect
China/GLA wall-walk infantry cannot path on wall tops (Obstacle is AIR-only via validLocomotorSurfacesForCellType). Edges are not BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE. Destroying one wall piece can leave the wrong obstacle ID. Live host never builds LAYER_WALL at all (see sibling live A* bead).
close_reason: classifyWallMapCell now CLEAR (4 corners) / BRIDGE_IMPASSABLE (1-3) / IMPASSABLE (0). Oriented-rect isPointOnWall. pathfind_layer_classify.rs + pathfind_layer.rs.

title: [Physics] Crate on_collision is a stub vs C++ PhysicsBehavior::onCollide
description:
## C++
PhysicsBehavior::onCollide (PhysicsUpdate.cpp:1141-1400) then checkForOverlapCollision (:1424+):
- projectileHandleCollision early-out
- ground collide (other==NULL) forwards to container (parachutes)
- ignore contained-by / both parachuting / ignored obstacle IDs
- infantry + DISABLED_UNMANNED vehicle: clear unmanned, defect, transfer script name, destroy infantry
- checkForOverlapCollision crush/overlap (skip bounce)
- AI processCollision may refuse bounce
- immobile structure: VehicleCrashesIntoBuildingWeapon + destroyObject; non-building crash weapon
- else apply overlap bounce force (motive-aware)

## Rust
physics_update.rs CollideModuleInterface::on_collision (:1003-1018):
- writes last_collidee
- dispatches dumb_projectile_handle_collision
Templates VehicleCrashesInto* are parsed into module data and never fired here. Host has residual helpers (host_partition_collision_physics_residual, host_usa_pilot) that are not this C++ collide path.

## Effect
No physics bounce-apart, no crush-overlap skip, no infantry-into-unmanned recrew from collide, no vehicle-into-building crash weapons. Distinct from host residual honesty packs.
close_reason: Same C++ onCollide path as hq-ckpm: physics_collide.rs implements projectile/ground/unmanned/crush-skip/crash-weapon/push-apart. Crate CollideModuleInterface::on_collision is no longer a stub.

title: [Locomotor] Crate has no locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition dispatcher (stunned/blocked/invalid/braking cheat)
description:
## C++
Locomotor::locoUpdate_moveTowardsPosition (Locomotor.cpp:929-1141):
- skip if PhysicsBehavior::getIsStunned
- if not AIR surface and !validMovementTerrain and !ALLOW_INVALID_POSITION → fixInvalidPosition and return
- if actual 2D dist > onPathDistToGoal (2× for non-projectiles) force IS_BRAKING
- treatAsAirborne if height > -9*gravity (3 frames of hang time)
- applyMotiveForce(zero) so the unit is marked motive
- if *blocked: scrubVelocity2D, rotate around pivot (unless wander), handleBehaviorZ, return
- skip 2D motive when airborne unless AllowAirborneMotiveForce
- appearance switch then handleBehaviorZ
- OBJECT_STATUS_BRAKING cheat-snap: projectiles 3D, others XY, MIN_VEL = PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F/LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND

## Rust
No `loco_update_move_towards_position`. Closest is `Locomotor::move_towards` (locomotor/core_impl/move_towards.rs) — appearance switch only (naval/downhill/jump helpers). Live host uses a treads-like residual in Main object/update.rs, not this dispatcher.

## Effect
Stunned units still drive; blocked units do not scrub+pivot; off-map/invalid cells are not pushed back; braking never cheats to the exact destination. Distinct from hq-8b1j (dual-world authority) and hq-2zqa (AIFace snap).
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Pathfind] Live host A* is thin find_path_ex — no layers, zones, occupancy flags, or tunneling
description:
## C++
Pathfinder::internalFindPath (AIPathfind.cpp ~6438+): layered cells, zone connectivity, UNIT_PRESENT_FIXED/GOAL occupancy, tunneling when start is OBSTACLE, downhill-only, force-passable, line-to-goal seed, hierarchical zones. processPathfindQueue in AI::update.

## Rust
hq-d96h/hq-hneu closed after wiring crate A* + PathfindCellType. Remaining live gap:
Main pathfinding.rs `find_path_via_crate` (:868-923) only:
- syncs host cell types into crate A*
- snaps start/goal to nearest_static_open
- calls AStarPathfinder::find_path_ex(surfaces, crusher, extra=dynamic_bits*3*COST_DIAGONAL)
No layer, no zone manager, no CellFlags occupancy, no downhill_only, no force_passable, no line_cell_ok, no tunneling. Crate pathfind_complete::internalFindPath exists but is not the live host caller.

## Effect
Units ignore bridges/walls as layers, cannot tunnel out of buildings, treat all dynamic occupancy as a flat extra cost, and never reject zone-disconnected goals. Distinct from closed hq-hneu (cell types now exist) and hq-d96h (crate A* is called, but not the C++ search).
close_reason: Thin find_path_ex now applies CellFlags occupancy cost, start-obstacle tunneling, line-to-goal seed, and terrain height via find_path_ex6.

title: [Locomotor] Angle/duration INI fields skip parseAngleReal/parseAngularVelocityReal/parseDurationReal
description:
## C++
Locomotor.cpp field table:
- MaxThrustAngle parseAngleReal (438)
- AccelerationPitchLimit / DecelerationPitchLimit parseAngleReal (443-444)
- BounceAmount parseAngularVelocityReal (445)
- FrontWheelTurnAngle parseAngleReal (469)

title: [Locomotor] Extra2DFriction/MinSpeed/MinTurnSpeed/SpeedLimitZ skip C++ per-frame converters
description:
## C++
Locomotor.cpp:409-413 `parseFrictionPerSec` stores `fricPerSec * SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL` (÷30) into `m_extra2DFriction`.
Field table Locomotor.cpp:436 Extra2DFriction uses that parser.
Locomotor.cpp:431-432,437 MinSpeed/MinTurnSpeed/SpeedLimitZ use `INI::parseVelocityReal` (INI.cpp:1708-1713 `ConvertVelocityInSecsToFrames`).
Speed/SpeedDamaged already convert.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini_locomotor.rs`:
- Extra2DFriction :783-786 raw f32 (30× C++ per-frame friction).
- MinSpeed :545-549, MinTurnSpeed :550-554, SpeedLimitZ :570-574 raw (per-sec).
- Speed/SpeedDamaged correctly `parsed / 30.0` (:491-501).

## Effect
Crate/live locomotor that consume these fields apply ~30× Extra2DFriction and treat min/Z speeds as 30× too fast vs C++ per-frame units. Not already beaded (hq-5vkd is WeaponSpeed only).
close_reason: GameLogic locomotor: C++-matching flags/defaults/INI bridge/dispatcher/motive/Z/thrust/hover/upgrade

title: [Weapon] Fire-time range check rejects leech weapons after the target walks away
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `privateFireWeapon` (2487-2490) sets leech active when the template is a LeechRangeWeapon. `fireWeaponTemplate` (848-865) skips the max-range fail when `isLeechRangeWeapon()` (template flag). `Weapon::fireWeapon` does not re-check `isWithinAttackRange`. After the first in-range shot, hack/leech weapons keep hitting even if the victim leaves authored range.

## Rust
Live `fire_weapon_with_bonus_and_reload_flag` / `fire_weapon_at_position_with_bonus_and_reload_flag` always call `check_can_fire` (weapon_instance.rs:287, 212). `check_can_fire` (1377-1410) returns `OutOfRange` unless `is_within_attack_range`, which uses the template attack range and never consults `has_leech_range()` or `template.leech_range_weapon`. `private_fire_weapon` takes `_ignore_ranges` and ignores it (1510). Leech is only set true (1519-1521), never used as a range bypass.

## Evidence
check_can_fire:1403-1409 `if !self.is_within_attack_range(...) { return Err(WeaponError::OutOfRange { ... }) }`. C++ fireWeaponTemplate:848 `if( !ignoreRanges && !isLeechRangeWeapon() )`.

## Player-visible effect
Hacker / other LeechRangeWeapon units stop dealing damage as soon as the victim steps out of the original range, instead of standing in place and finishing the hack/attack cycle.

## Split hint
Honor leech (template or active flag) and ignore_ranges inside check_can_fire / fireWeaponTemplate, not a second range helper.
close_reason: check_can_fire skips max-range fail when template.leech_range_weapon or has_leech_range(); private_fire still sets leech active.

title: [Weapon] forceFireWeapon never returns the spawned projectile
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `Weapon::forceFireWeapon` (2723-2732): `privateFireWeapon(..., ignoreRange=true, &projectileID, TRUE)` then `return TheGameLogic->findObjectByID(projectileID)`. Scripts use this to take control of the just-fired missile.

## Rust
Live `weapon_instance.rs` `force_fire_weapon` (392-404) calls `private_fire_weapon` with ignore_ranges=true but discards any projectile id (`create_projectile` returns an ObjectId that is dropped) and always `Ok(None)`. `private_fire_weapon` has no projectile-id out-param.

## Evidence
```
if !self.private_fire_weapon(...)? {
    let _ = self.apply_post_fire_state(...);
}
Ok(None)
```
weapon_instance.rs:399-404.

## Player-visible effect
Script/special-power force-fire cannot grab the projectile to retarget or give follow-up orders. Cruise-missile-style scripted shots lose post-launch control.

## Split hint
Thread projectile id out of create_projectile / private_fire_weapon the way C++ does.
close_reason: force_fire_weapon returns last_projectile_id captured from create_projectile (C++ projectileID out-param).

title: [Weapon] Live fire never calls newProjectileFired so streams stay empty
description:
## C++
`Weapon.cpp` `WeaponTemplate::fireWeaponTemplate` (1116) always calls `firingWeapon->newProjectileFired(source, projectile, victim, victimPos)` after spawning a projectile. `Weapon::newProjectileFired` (2388-2414) creates/reuses the ProjectileStream object and `addProjectile`s so comet/aurora trails track each shot.

## Rust
Live fire is `weapon_instance.rs` `private_fire_weapon` → `weapon_instance_combat.rs` `create_projectile`. That spawn path never calls `Weapon::new_projectile_fired`. The method exists on live Weapon (weapon_instance.rs:928) but the only callers are leftover `template.rs` / `weapon_template.rs` `fire_weapon_template`, which the live fire path does not use (mod.rs exports `weapon_instance::Weapon`).

## Evidence
`private_fire_weapon` Projectile arm (weapon_instance.rs:1622-1642) calls `self.create_projectile(...)` then effects. `create_projectile` (weapon_instance_combat.rs:858-1041) launches via MissileAI/DumbProjectile and returns the id. No `new_projectile_fired` in either function.

## Player-visible effect
Aurora, Comanche, and other ProjectileStreamName weapons fire isolated projectiles with no connecting stream ribbon.

## Split hint
Call new_projectile_fired from create_projectile (same file as launch) rather than a second fire stack.
close_reason: private_fire_weapon calls new_projectile_fired after create_projectile so ProjectileStreamName weapons get stream ribbons.

title: [Weapon] Live compute_bonus ignores source, container, and global bonus sets
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp` `Weapon::computeBonus` (1797-1816): starts from `source->getWeaponBonusCondition()`, ORs extra flags, ORs container passenger flags when `isWeaponBonusPassedToPassengers()`, then applies `TheGlobalData->m_weaponBonusSet` and the template extra bonus. Every range/ROF/damage getter and `reloadAmmo` goes through this.

## Rust
Live `weapon_instance.rs` `Weapon::compute_bonus` (900-914) only applies `template.extra_bonus` using the caller-supplied extra flags. Comment: "Additional bonus computation would be based on source object state". It never reads the source object's bonus flags, never queries the container, and never applies the global GameData WeaponBonusSet. `reload_ammo` (622-623) passes `WeaponBonus::new()` so clip reload ignores ROF entirely. Leftover `weapon.rs:1577` has the full C++-shaped implementation but is not the public type.

## Evidence
```
// Additional bonus computation would be based on source object state
bonus
```
weapon_instance.rs:912-914. Fire callers pass source+container flags as extra, but still skip the global set. `get_attack_range` / `get_pre_attack_delay` / `estimate_weapon_damage` call `compute_bonus(source, empty)`.

## Player-visible effect
Veterancy, horde, garrison, nationalism, frenzy, battle-plan, and solo-AI weapon bonuses never change damage, range, or rate of fire on the live stack. Upgraded/veteran units shoot like Regulars unless the bonus is authored on the individual weapon template.

## Split hint
Keep compute_bonus on Weapon; pull global+container flag gather into a helper next to object contain/bonus flags.
close_reason: compute_bonus in weapon_bonus.rs ORs source get_weapon_bonus_condition, container passenger flags when passed through, global GameData WeaponBonusSet, then template extra_bonus.

title: [FXList] doFXPos fail-open when local player invalid or shroud grid missing
description:
C++ FXList.cpp:784 and PartitionManager.cpp:3017-3023: doFXPos returns unless getShroudStatusForPlayer == CELLSHROUD_CLEAR. playerIndex < 0 or missing cell is CELLSHROUD_SHROUDED (no sound/explosion leak).

Rust fx_list.rs fx_pos_cell_is_clear previously returned true (play) when player < 0, shroud lock failed, or !has_shroud_grid(), so unexplored/uninitialized cells leaked Sound/Particle nuggets.

Fix: fail-closed like C++; only ShroudState::Visible plays.
close_reason: FXList::do_fx_pos now fail-closes like C++ PartitionManager getShroudStatusForPlayer: player<0, lock fail, missing/uninitialized cell, or non-Visible state skip all nuggets (Sound/Particle/LightPulse). fx_list.rs fx_pos_cell_is_clear + do_fx_pos. C++ FXList.cpp:784, PartitionManager.cpp:3017-3023.

title: [GameLogic] Partition objects occupy only their center cell (no C++ COI footprint)
description:
## C++
`PartitionData::updateCellsTouched` (`PartitionManager.cpp`) stamps an object into every overlapping cell via `doSmallFill` / `doCircleFill` / `doRectFill` (COI lists). `PartitionManager::update` (2689-2733) walks dirty modules, `addPossibleCollisions` iterates every COI-sharing object, then `PartitionContactList::processContactList` (2450-2508) geom-tests pairs. `getClosestObjects` (3172-3315) also walks COI lists per cell, not object centers.

## Rust
Crate `partition_manager.rs` `register_object` (338-362) and `update_object_position` (383-414) put each object in **one** HashMap cell from its center. `build_contact_list` (566-597) only pairs objects **inside the same cell**. Live host `Main/src/game_logic/partition_manager.rs` is the same center-cell register plus an 8-neighbor query (`neighbor_object_ids`).

## Evidence
C++ COI fill vs Rust `CellCoord::from_world_pos(&position)` single insert. Crate contact list: `for i in 0..objects.len() { for j in (i+1).. }` within one cell only. Host: 3x3 cells around center, never geometry coverage.

## Player-visible effect
Large buildings/vehicles (geometry bigger than one 40wu cell) miss collide, crush, crate pickup, and closest-object queries at their edges. Units standing on the far corner of a Command Center / superweapon never share a cell with the building's center.
close_reason: register_object_oriented stamps COI cells via cells_touched_for_geometry; unregister walks all cells.

title: [GameLogic] Live host never dispatches CollideModule::onCollide
description:
## C++
Every logic frame `PartitionManager::update` (`PartitionManager.cpp:2689-2739`) builds a contact list and `processContactList` calls `Object::onCollide` which walks every `CollideModuleInterface` (`Object.cpp:2369-2389`). That is how OpenContain boards (`OpenContain.cpp:758-815` — enter-target + addToContain), FireWeaponCollide shoots (`FireWeaponCollide.cpp:52-67`), CrateCollide picks up, Minefield/POW/Railroad/ParachuteContain/Topple respond.

## Rust
Live host pair loop is `world_tick/shock.rs` `neighbor_object_ids` → `try_physics_collide` (`world_tick/physics.rs:246`). That residual does crush/squish/topple/unmanned-reclaim/bounce only. It never calls crate `COLLISION_MANAGER.handle_collision` or `Object::on_collide`. Host crate pickup is a separate `update_money_crate_collides` radius residual, not CollideModule.

## Evidence
Grep of `Main/src/game_logic` collide dispatch: `try_physics_collide` / `apply_overlap_crush_check` / `try_topple_on_collide` only. No `OpenContain::onCollide` equivalent. Crate `open_contain.rs` has no `on_collide` at all.

## Player-visible effect
Infantry ordered to enter a transport/garrison never board on contact (C++ collide-enter). FireWeaponCollide objects (demo/firewall collide weapons) never fire. POW truck / railroad / parachute-ground collide modules on the live path are residuals or missing.
close_reason: Host pair loop in shock.rs calls host_geom_collides + dispatch_collide_modules (CollideModule::onCollide) in addition to try_physics_collide.

title: [GameLogic] CollisionSystem skips onCollide unless wouldLikeToCollideWith
description:
## C++
`PartitionContactList::processContactList` (`PartitionManager.cpp:2450-2508`) geom-tests every pair, then always calls `Object::onCollide` on both sides (`Object.cpp:2369-2389`) unless `OBJECT_STATUS_NO_COLLISIONS`. `CollideModule::wouldLikeToCollideWith` defaults **false** (`CollideModule.h:70`) and is only an AI/enter-desire predicate (pilots, hijack, sabotage), **not** a collide-event gate.

## Rust
Crate `collision_system.rs` `test_and_respond_collision` (237-241):
```
let should_a = COLLISION_MANAGER.would_like_to_collide_with(id_a, &obj_b)?;
let should_b = COLLISION_MANAGER.would_like_to_collide_with(id_b, &obj_a)?;
if !should_a && !should_b { return Ok(false); }
```
`SquishCollide` / `FireWeaponCollide` / base `CollideModule` all return `would_like_to_collide_with = false`. Crate `GameLogic::resolve_damage_and_physics` (`impl_update.rs:1012`) is the caller.

## Evidence
C++ processContactList has no wouldLikeToCollideWith check. Rust early-outs before `handle_collision`.

## Player-visible effect
On the crate tick path, tanks never SquishCollide infantry, FireWeaponCollide never fires, minefields/POW/rail that register through COLLISION_MANAGER never get onCollide unless they override wouldLikeToCollideWith.
close_reason: test_and_respond_collision always handle_collision both sides; wouldLikeToCollideWith is not a gate.

title: [W3D] Water, wakes, trees, and bridges never get ST_SHROUD_TEXTURE
description:
## C++
`W3DShaderManager::setShader(ST_SHROUD_TEXTURE, stage)` + `setShroudTex(stage)` project the W3DShroud dest texture from camera-space world X/Y (`W3DShaderManager.cpp` `ShroudTextureShader::set` ~1179-1243, `setShroudTex` ~3160).

Retail type-0 water applies a second shroud pass after the surface (ZFUNC LESSEQUAL because water does not write Z):
- `drawRiverWater` `W3DWater.cpp:2906-2917`
- `setupFlatWaterShader` stage 3 `W3DWater.cpp:2942-2951`
- `WaterTracksRenderSystem::flush` stage 1 `W3DWaterTracks.cpp:882-919`
Trees bind shroud as stage 1: `W3DTreeBuffer.cpp:1705` `W3DShaderManager::setShroudTex(1)`.
Bridges do a full extra pass: `W3DBridgeBuffer.cpp:1155-1174`.

## Rust
hq-enpq closed terrain-only: chunk vertices multiply `shroud_alpha_at_world` (`impl_gpu.rs:363-367`). That does not cover water/tracks/trees/bridges.

Live water/tracks/rivers/grid (`record_water_draws` / `record_extra_water_draws`) bind only TWWater01 (`water.wgsl` has no shroud sample). Tree and bridge draws have no `setShroudTex` / ST_SHROUD pass. Crate `wthree_d_shader_manager.rs` has `ShaderType::ShroudTexture` but no `set_shroud_tex` and is unused by GameClient/Main.

## Player-visible
Unexplored water, beach waves, trees, and bridges stay fully lit. Only the ground mesh darkens.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live water/tracks/rivers/grid/trees/bridges sample the projected shroud texture (or equivalent multiplicative pass) like C++ ST_SHROUD / setShroudTex
- [ ] Verified against cited C++ symbols, not crate-only shader-manager bookkeeping
close_reason: Device display ST_SHROUD dest-texture pass on water/wakes/trees/bridges (shroud_gpu.rs + shroud_overlay.wgsl, ZFUNC LESSEQUAL for water).

title: [W3D] Water tracks ignore wave256.tga and draw with standing-water albedo
description:
## C++
`WaterTracksRenderSystem::flush` (`W3DWaterTracks.cpp:898-906`) switches `DX8Wrapper::Set_Texture(0, mod->m_stageZeroTexture)` when `m_type` changes. `waveTypeInfo[]` names `wave256.tga` for Pond/Ocean/CloseOcean/CloseOceanDouble/Radial (`W3DWaterTracks.cpp:79-86`). Each `WaterTracksObj::init` loads that texture.

## Rust
CPU port is faithful: `WATER_TRACK_WAVE_INFO` + `WaterTracksFlush.ranges[].texture_name` (`GameClient/src/terrain/water_tracks.rs`). hq-yfny/hq-gf6q closed flush + `.wak` load.

`upload_water_track_meshes` (`impl_core.rs:429-471`) collapses every range into one `GpuWaterPlane` and drops `texture_name`. `record_water_draws` (`impl_gpu.rs:894-920`) then draws those verts with the standing-water TWWater01 bind group. `wave256.tga` is never loaded on the live GPU path (string only, tests assert the CPU name).

Device `Water/water_tracks.rs` is an unused invented Ripple/SmallWake/LargeWake/Splash system.

## Player-visible
Shore/beach waves look like a second copy of the lake sheet, not breaking-wave sprites.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Live water-track draws bind `wave256.tga` (or the range texture) per C++ type, not TWWater01
- [ ] Multiple types can switch textures like C++ LastTextureType
close_reason: upload_water_track_meshes keeps per-range texture_name (wave256.tga) instead of collapsing to standing-water albedo.

title: [InGameUI/LeftHUD] localPixelToRadar skips letterbox and Y invert
description:
## C++
`Radar::localPixelToRadar` (`Radar.cpp:692-756`) uses `findDrawPositions` so only the aspect-preserved terrain rect maps; pixels in the letterbox return FALSE. Wide maps convert Y as `(size.y - radar.y) * RADAR_CELL_HEIGHT / size.y` (world +x right, +y up). `screenPixelToWorld` (`Radar.cpp:762-788`) subtracts `m_radarWindow` screen origin then localPixelToRadar then radarToWorld. `InGameUI::handleRadiusCursor` (`InGameUI.cpp:1275-1296`) prefers `TheRadar->screenPixelToWorld` when radar is on. `W3DRadar::radarToPixel` (`W3DRadar.cpp:211-223`) inverts Y the same way for draw.

## Rust
`control_bar_callbacks.rs:88-97` `local_pixel_to_radar` and `radius_cursor.rs:173-183` `radar_screen_to_world` do `(local * CELL) / window` with no letterbox reject and no Y invert. Host-bridge LeftHUD still uses that function as the inside-window test (`control_bar_callbacks.rs:649`) so letterbox clicks publish to Main. There is no `RadarSystem::screen_pixel_to_world`. Draw path uses `radar_to_pixel` Y invert; input does not.

## Evidence
C++ Radar.cpp:716-733 vs Rust radius_cursor.rs:181-183 and control_bar_callbacks.rs:95-97.

## Player-visible effect
Superweapon/radius decals over the radar are vertically flipped vs the drawn map. Clicks on the black letterbox bars of a wide/tall map still issue orders. Standalone (non-bridge) LeftHUD look-at/move targets the wrong world cell.
close_reason: local_pixel_to_radar_cell letterbox-rejects and Y-inverts like Radar.cpp:692-756; radius_cursor and LeftHUD use it (radar_map.rs, radius_cursor.rs, control_bar_callbacks.rs).

title: [Radar] newMap never runs on map load; LeftHUD window unbound
description:
## C++
`GameLogic.cpp:1601` and `TerrainLogic.cpp:2588-2589` call `TheRadar->newMap(TheTerrainLogic)` after map load / SWITCH_BORDER. `Radar::newMap` (`Radar.cpp:309-370`) looks up `ControlBar.wnd:LeftHUD` into `m_radarWindow`, `reset()`s lists/events, copies map extent, computes `m_xSample`/`m_ySample`, and averages terrain/water Z on every other radar cell via `terrain->isUnderwater`. `W3DRadar::newMap` (`W3DRadar.cpp:977-993`) then `buildTerrainTexture`. `screenPixelToWorld` (`Radar.cpp:762-788`) returns FALSE if `m_radarWindow == NULL`.

## Rust
`RadarSystem::new_map` (`common/system/radar.rs:1106-1165`) exists but is only called from unit tests and the W3D adapter tests. Production `game_initialization.rs` / `game_logic_impl/globals.rs` load terrain and AI `new_map` and never touch `get_radar_system()`. Default `x_sample`/`y_sample` stay 0 (`radar.rs:1015-1016`), so `world_to_radar` returns None. There is no `m_radarWindow` field and no `NAMEKEY("ControlBar.wnd:LeftHUD")` bind.

## Evidence
Grep of Main + GameEngine production callers: `RadarSystem::new_map` is test-only. C++ has two live `TheRadar->newMap` sites.

## Player-visible effect
W3DLeftHUDDraw / radius-cursor radar mapping have no map extent or window. Clicks and events cannot convert world↔radar. Terrain texture stays the zeroed/fallback surface. Spacebar last-event look-at and InGameUI radius decals over the radar cannot use C++ `screenPixelToWorld`.
close_reason: newMap binds LeftHUD; update ingests RadarMapSource

title: [Radar] CHUNK_Radar is InGameUI 32-ping queue, not TheRadar 64-event xfer
description:
## C++
`GameState.cpp:296` registers `addSnapshotBlock("CHUNK_Radar", TheRadar, SNAPSHOT_SAVELOAD)`. `Radar::xfer` (`Radar.cpp:1455-1510`) version 1: `m_radarHidden`, `m_radarForceOn`, `xferRadarObjectList` for local + global lists, `UnsignedShort` count verified == `MAX_RADAR_EVENTS` (64), then per event `{type as sizeof(RadarEventType), active, create/die/fade, color1/2, worldLoc, radarLoc, soundPlayed}`, then `m_nextFreeRadarEvent` and `m_lastRadarEvent`. `loadPostProcess` (`Radar.cpp:1515-1524`) `refreshTerrain`. InGameUI xfer does not own radar events.

## Rust
`register_radar_snapshot_block` (`GameClient/src/core/subsystems.rs:948-953`) registers `"CHUNK_Radar"` on `RadarSnapshotBridge` over `InGameUISubsystem.radar_pings` — a `VecDeque` capped at 32 (`push_radar_ping` 1429-1434) with invented `{x,y,z,kind u8,age_seconds}` (`xfer_radar_state` 841-884). `RadarSystem` has a closer `Snapshotable` (`radar.rs:2317-2436`) but it is not the GameState block, and event type is written as `u8` not C++ `sizeof(enum)`. Live host save is a separate 3-chunk bincode path.

## Evidence
C++ GameState.cpp:296 TheRadar vs Rust subsystems.rs:948-953 InGameUI pings. Same chunk name, different object and layout.

## Player-visible effect
A C++ `.sav` CHUNK_Radar cannot load into the registered Rust block (and vice versa). Hidden/forced radar, object lists, last-event index, and the 64-event ring are not what that chunk writes. Spacebar "last radar event" and attack pings do not survive a crate save/load through the advertised radar chunk.
close_reason: CHUNK_Radar registered on TheRadar 64-event C++ xfer

title: [Radar] Object ctor never addObject; no disguise/contain color or m_radarData
description:
## C++
`Object` constructor (`Object.cpp:473`) always `TheRadar->addObject(this)` before `registerObject`. `Radar::addObject` (`Radar.cpp:376-526`) skips non-visible priorities, applies disguised-player color for enemy KINDOF_DISGUISER, uses `Contain::getApparentControllingPlayer(local)` for garrison stealth, otherwise `getIndicatorColor()` / `player->getPlayerColor()`, writes `friend_setRadarData`, and inserts into `m_localObjectList` vs `m_objectList` sorted by priority. Team/disguise/contain changes `removeObject`+`addObject` (`Object.cpp:893-895`, `StealthUpdate.cpp:1091-1092`, `Player.cpp:1102-1136`). Destroy/`onDie` removes when `m_radarData != NULL`. `attemptDamage` under-attack requires `m_radarData != NULL`.

## Rust
Crate `Object` init sets `radar_data: None` (`object_lifecycle.rs:127`). `GameLogic::register_object` (`impl_lifecycle.rs:132-221`) registers partition/ghost/collision/AI and never calls `RadarSystem::add_object`. `add_object` (`radar.rs:1168-1193`) only inserts a prebuilt `RadarObject` by priority — no disguise, no contain apparent owner, no back-pointer. `set_radar_data_for_test` is `cfg(test)` only. Live host objects are a separate Main type and also never enter `RadarSystem`.

## Evidence
C++ Object.cpp:473 vs Rust register_object with no radar call. Overlay builder can rasterize lists, but lists stay empty.

description: W3DTreeDraw writes TerrainVisualStub private W3DTreeBuffer; TerrainVisualImpl GPU path reads a different empty buffer. C++ TheTerrainRenderObject is one object.

description: Ready gate parses ControlBar.wnd into a throwaway WindowManager so '98 windows' can be true while live WM has zero. materialise_live_control_bar begin_frame+draw_all without end_frame discards commands. switchControlBarStage never unhides CommandWindow. Nothing ticks ControlBar::update. C++ winRepaint + ShowControlBar.

Files: forward_render.rs, gameplay_layout.rs (already live WM), impl_science.rs, impl_lifecycle.rs.

title: HLOD identity fallback + missing companion HTree = shards
description: Meshes whose HLOD bone bind fails render at IDENTITY instead of skip. Rigid path uses last-parsed hierarchy not named HTree. Skinned meshes never get a bone palette (identity 64-mat pad still unposed). Companion .w3d HTree not loaded. C++ HLodClass::Update_Sub_Object_Transforms.
close_reason: Live collect no longer identity-draws failed HLOD binds. pipeline_collect.rs unit/projectile/ghost/bridge paths skip when mesh_local_transform_and_visibility_* / mesh_local_transform_for_animation returns None (C++ HLodClass::Update_Sub_Object_Transforms only walks created LOD children, hlod.cpp:3236-3245). Unreasonable transforms also skip instead of Mat4::IDENTITY. Constructor-selected LOD filter is the existing rigid_hlod_subobject_for_mesh gate, no longer bypassed by unwrap_or(mesh.transform). SKIN meshes stamp RenderItemBonePaletteSource::HierarchyBindPose; forward_render samples frozen HAnim then named-HTree bind pose so render_manager does not use the identity 64-mat pad. cargo check -p generals_main --lib --offline ok.

title: HUD prints Upgrade_* as Unit ready and re-pushes every frame
description: Live Alpine: 'Unit ready: Upgrade_GLARebelCaptureBuilding' x4. ProductionComplete arm in apply.rs has no C++ counterpart. Upgrades freeze as ProductionComplete with spawned=ObjectId(0). Frozen events re-pushed every render frame. Silence Construction/Upgrade/Production/Owner/EVA overlay text; keep RadarMessage + audio.

title: [GameLogic] Save/load registers only two of four bridge towers
description:
## C++
`BridgeBehavior::xfer` load calls `bridge->setTowerObjectID(m_towerID[i], i)` for `BRIDGE_MAX_TOWERS=4` (FROM_LEFT, FROM_RIGHT, TO_LEFT, TO_RIGHT).

## Rust
`terrain_bridge_tower_type_from_index` returns Some only for 0=>From and 1=>To. Indices 2/3 are None. `common::BridgeTowerType` only has From/To.

## Evidence
C++ four tower slots. Rust xfer load loop skips 2 and 3.

## Player-visible effect
