After loading a save, half the bridge towers are not registered in Bridge info (damage-state/radar refresh on load).
close_reason: Xfer load now maps all 4 C++ tower slots (0 FROM_LEFT, 1 FROM_RIGHT, 2 TO_LEFT, 3 TO_RIGHT) and calls set_tower_object_id for each. BRIDGE_MAX_TOWERS=4. Files: bridge_behavior.rs, geometry.rs, terrain.rs

title: [GameLogic] Slope-stick units snap to origin instead of aligning to terrain
description:
## C++
`TerrainLogic::alignOnTerrain` + `makeAlignToNormalMatrix` (`TerrainLogic.cpp:1476-1523`) are called from `Thing::setPosition` / `setPositionZ` / `setOrientation` for `KINDOF_STICK_TO_TERRAIN_SLOPE`. Units tilt to the ground normal and keep their world position (plus a +2.5 bridge-layer height hack).

## Rust
`alignOnTerrain` is absent from `terrain.rs`. `Common/src/common/thing/thing.rs` slope branch comments `// Align to terrain - would need terrain logic integration` and applies `Matrix3D::identity()`, which writes translation (0,0,0).

## Evidence
thing.rs: `let mtx = Matrix3D::identity(); self.set_transform_matrix(&mtx);` — cached_pos becomes origin.

## Player-visible effect
STICK_TO_TERRAIN_SLOPE objects (ramps, some props/units) jump to the origin and never tilt to the slope.
close_reason: TerrainLogic::align_on_terrain + make_align_to_normal_matrix ported (bridge +2.5 hack). GameLogic initialize() registers common::thing::register_align_on_terrain so Thing slope branches keep world pos instead of identity/origin. Files: terrain.rs, lib.rs; Common thing.rs hook by Close11Common.

title: [GameLogic] SWITCH_BORDER scripts skip partition, shroud, radar, and camera rebuild
description:
## C++
`TerrainLogic::setActiveBoundary` (`TerrainLogic.cpp:2476-2543`) validates the index, flushes pending shroud, stores/restores fogged cells, releases and restores ghost partition data, resets PartitionManager, calls `TheRadar->newMap`, notifies every object of the new boundary, and forces camera constraint recalc.

## Rust
`terrain.rs` `set_active_boundary` (2783-2786) is `self.active_boundary = new_active_boundary;`. Script `do_map_switch_border` only does ReplayObserver shroud refresh.

## Evidence
C++ ~70-line rebuild. Rust: bare field write.

## Player-visible effect
SWITCH_BORDER on multi-boundary maps leaves shroud, radar, ghosts, and camera constraints on the old playable area.
close_reason: set_active_boundary validates index, flushes shroud queue, prepares objects, resets partition, refreshes radar, notifies objects, camera constraint hook. Files: terrain.rs helpers/leftover.rs

title: [GameLogic] Group Guard-Area, Hack Internet, and Repair commands are missing
description:
## C++
`AIGroup.cpp` implements `groupGuardArea` (2518), `groupAttackArea` (2538), `groupHackInternet` (2555), `groupRepair` (2296), `groupGetHealed` (2328), `groupGetRepaired` (2344), `groupResumeConstruction` (2312). Scripts and team AI use these named surfaces.

## Rust
Live `ai/group.rs` has `group_guard_position` / `group_guard_object` only. No `group_guard_area`, `group_attack_area`, `group_hack_internet`, `group_repair`, `group_get_healed`, `group_get_repaired`, or `group_resume_construction` anywhere in GameLogic/src.

## Evidence
Repo-wide grep for those fn names is empty. C++ fans each command to per-member AI.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted team guard-area / attack-area, hacker cash, and group repair/heal/resume-construction do nothing.
close_reason: Added group_guard_area/attack_area/hack_internet/repair/get_healed/get_repaired/resume_construction (group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] AI subsystem CRC and save omit pathfinder and groups
description:
## C++
`AI::crc` (`AI.cpp:977`) xfers the pathfinder snapshot, then loops `MARKER:TAiData` / `MARKER:AIGroup` snapshots. `AIGroup::crc/xfer` persist member IDs.

## Rust
`struct AI` in `ai/mod.rs` has no `impl Snapshot`. Only `AiData` and `Pathfinder::crc_pathfinder` wrappers exist. Live `ai/group.rs` AIGroup has no crc/xfer.

## Evidence
grep of mod.rs shows no `impl Snapshot for AI`. C++ AI::crc walks pathfinder + TAiData chain + every AIGroup.

## Player-visible effect
MP CRC diverges; save/load of AI groups and pathfinder occupancy is incomplete. Reloading a match can drop group membership and pathfind state.
close_reason: AI Snapshot crc walks pathfinder + TAiData + AIGroup member IDs (ai/mod.rs, group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] AI tick never runs PlayerList update
description:
## C++
`AI::update` (`AI.cpp:332`) calls `ThePlayerList->UPDATE()` every frame after pathfind queue processing. `Player::update` clears power-sabotage timers and other per-player clocks.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/mod.rs` `AI::update` (1538) processes the pathfind queue then comments `// Run player updates (matches C++ ThePlayerList->UPDATE()).` with no call. Repo-wide GameLogic/src has no per-frame PlayerList update invocation.

## Evidence
C++: `{ ThePlayerList->UPDATE(); }`. Rust: comment only; AI player objects update via AIManager, not Player::update.

## Player-visible effect
Player-level timers (power sabotage, energy hooks) never tick. Mid-game power/sabotage recovery and similar Player::update side effects stall.
close_reason: AI::update now ticks ThePlayerList Player::update (ai/mod.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Infantry and vehicles never use group column pathfinding
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::friend_computeGroundPath`, `friend_moveInfantryToPos`, `friend_moveVehicleToPos`, `friend_moveFormationToPos` (`AIGroup.cpp:504-1527`, ~1000 lines) pack infantry/vehicles into shared column paths using INI `MinInfantryForGroup`, `MinVehiclesForGroup`, `MinDistanceForGroup`, `DistanceRequiresGroup`, `MinClumpDensity`, pathfind diameters.

## Rust
Live `ai/group.rs` `group_move_to_position` (520) comments: `friend_moveInfantry/Vehicle column paths remain residual (optional fast path).` It fans each member to `compute_individual_destination` + `ai_move_to_position`. Those friend_* methods do not exist.

## Evidence
Rust comment at group.rs:533. C++ column packing consumes the group-pathfind INI knobs parsed into AiData but unused here.

## Player-visible effect
Large infantry/vehicle groups walk as independent units instead of columns. Formation cohesion and traffic through chokepoints look wrong versus retail.
close_reason: Ported friend_computeGroundPath + infantry/vehicle/formation column packing into group_move_to_position (group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Group special powers cannot be issued
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupDoSpecialPower` (2614), `groupDoSpecialPowerAtLocation` (2652), `groupDoSpecialPowerAtObject` (2701), and `groupOverrideSpecialPowerDestination` (3234) pick a capable member and fire the power (no-target / location / object).

## Rust
Live `ai/group.rs` can *find* a special-power source (`get_special_power_source_object`) but has no `group_do_special_power*` methods anywhere in GameLogic/src.

## Evidence
C++ iterates members, checks `TheSpecialPowerStore`, and executes. Rust grep for `fn group_do_special` is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Selecting a mixed group and clicking a special power (or scripted team special powers) does not fire. Superweapons and unit abilities issued through the group surface fail.
close_reason: Added group_do_special_power* and override destination (group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Group Scatter does not scatter via AIGroup
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupScatter` (`AIGroup.cpp:1738`) recomputes the group and issues per-member scatter destinations so a clump spreads out.

## Rust
Live `ai/group.rs` has no `group_scatter`. A separate command-processor `execute_scatter_command` jitters individual move targets, but the C++ AIGroup scatter path used by scripts/AI is missing.

## Evidence
C++ `void AIGroup::groupScatter(CommandSourceType cmdSource)` exists and walks members. Rust group.rs has no matching method.

## Player-visible effect
Scripted/AI group scatter and any path that goes through AIGroup::groupScatter leaves the clump packed. Player scatter via the command processor may still jitter, but AI/script scatter does not match C++.
close_reason: Added AIGroup::group_scatter centroid offset moves (group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Group Enter/Dock/Evacuate commands are missing
description:
## C++
`AIGroup.cpp` implements `groupEnter` (2360), `groupDock` (2376), `groupExit` (2392), `groupEvacuate` (2408), `groupMoveToAndEvacuateAndExit` (1968). These fan out per-member enter/dock/exit/evacuate for transports, supply docks, and Chinook unload.

## Rust
Live `ai/group.rs` has `group_move_to_and_evacuate` only. No `group_enter`, `group_dock`, `group_exit`, `group_evacuate`, or `group_move_to_and_evacuate_and_exit` anywhere in GameLogic/src.

## Evidence
C++ methods iterate `m_memberList` and call `aiEnter` / `aiDock` / `aiExit` / `aiEvacuate`. Rust grep for those fn names is empty.

## Player-visible effect
Selected groups cannot enter buildings, dock at supply centers, or evacuate transports as a group. Scripts/team orders that use those commands do nothing.
close_reason: Added group_enter/dock/exit/evacuate/move_to_and_evacuate_and_exit (group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Group Hunt command never issues hunt orders
description:
## C++
`AIGroup::groupHunt` (`AIGroup.cpp:2279`) iterates every member and calls `ai->aiHunt(cmdSource)`. Scripts (`doTeamHunt`) and team AI use this named surface.

## Rust
Live `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/group.rs` has no `group_hunt`. Repo-wide grep finds zero `fn group_hunt`. Script executor `actions_victory_team.rs` builds `AiCommandType::Hunt` and calls `group.ai_do_command`, but `AIGroup` in group.rs has no Hunt arm.

## Evidence
C++ `void AIGroup::groupHunt(CommandSourceType cmdSource)` fans out hunt. Rust group.rs public methods include move/attack/guard/idle/sell but not hunt.

## Player-visible effect
Team Hunt scripts and selected-group hunt leave units idle instead of seeking enemies.
close_reason: Added AIGroup::group_hunt fanning ai_hunt (group.rs)

title: [GameLogic] Units snap-rotate instead of turning to face
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/AI/AIStates.cpp` `AIFaceState::onEnter` (7398) only records whether the locomotor can turn in place. `AIFaceState::update` (7422) keeps STATE_CONTINUE until relative angle is within ~2°, driving `setLocomotorGoalOrientation` or `setLocomotorGoalPositionExplicit` each frame.

## Rust
Live impl `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/ai/states/face.rs` `AIFaceObjectState::classic_on_enter` / `AIFacePositionState::classic_on_enter` instantly `set_orientation(atan2)` and returns Success. `classic_on_update` always returns Success. Parallel leftover `ai/ai_states/face_special.rs` does the same snap.

## Evidence
C++ update loops until `fabs(relAngle) < 0.035f`. Rust: `let _ = owner_write.set_orientation(angle); Ok(StateReturnType::Success)`.

## Player-visible effect
Units ordered to face a target or position teleport-rotate instead of turning over several frames. Visible on turrets-off vehicles, face-object scripts, and any AI that enters FaceObject/FacePosition.
close_reason: AIFaceState now caches turn-in-place and rotates via locomotor goals until |relAngle|<0.035 (states/face.rs, leftover face_special.rs)

title: [Common] GameData HealthBonus_Veteran/Elite/Heroic write the wrong veterancy slots
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Include/Common/GameCommon.h` defines `LEVEL_REGULAR=0`, `LEVEL_VETERAN=1`, `LEVEL_ELITE=2`, `LEVEL_HEROIC=3`. `GlobalData.cpp` parse table writes `HealthBonus_Veteran` to `m_healthBonus[LEVEL_VETERAN]` (index 1), Elite→2, Heroic→3. Regular is intentionally not INI-set and stays 100%.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini_game_data.rs` `parse_game_data_block` maps `HEALTHBONUS_VETERAN` → `health_bonus[0]`, Elite→`[1]`, Heroic→`[2]`. `apply_to_runtime_global_data` copies only those three slots into runtime GlobalData.

## Evidence
C++: `offsetof(GlobalData, m_healthBonus[LEVEL_VETERAN])` with LEVEL_VETERAN==1.
Rust: `"HEALTHBONUS_VETERAN" => data.health_bonus[0] = parse_percent(...)`.
Also Rust `GlobalData::LEVEL_COUNT` is 8 vs C++ `LEVEL_COUNT` 4.

## Player-visible effect
GameData.ini veterancy health bonuses apply to the wrong ranks: Regular units get the Veteran bonus, Veteran get Elite, Elite get Heroic, and Heroic keep 100%. Promoted units have the wrong HP vs retail.
close_reason: HealthBonus_Veteran/Elite/Heroic write GlobalData slots 1/2/3 matching LEVEL_VETERAN/ELITE/HEROIC; Regular stays 100%.

title: [Common] GameLOD apply never rebuilds shadows, shoreline, or tank tracks
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/GameLOD.cpp` `GameLODManager::applyStaticLODLevel` writes GlobalData then, when settings change, calls `TheGameClient->adjustLOD(0)`, `TheGameClient->releaseShadows()`/`allocateShadows()`, `TheTerrainVisual->setShoreLineDetail()`, and `TheTerrainVisual->setTerrainTracksDetail()`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/game_lod.rs` `apply_static_lod_level` only copies LOD fields into GlobalData (particles, shadows flags, cloud/light maps, tank-track counts, texture reduction, trees, FPS limit). It never notifies GameClient or TerrainVisual.

## Evidence
C++ lines 522-566 perform client/terrain side effects after writing GlobalData. Rust function ends after `global.use_trees = requested_trees` / shell-map disable. GameClient has `adjust_lod_texture_reduction` and `release_shadows` but GameLOD never calls them.

## Player-visible effect
Changing Low/Medium/High/Custom graphics quality updates stored flags but does not rebuild shadow volumes/decals, shoreline blending, or tank-track meshes, so the scene stays at the previous visual LOD until a full restart (and even then only if something else applies those systems).
close_reason: apply_static_lod_level invokes registered rebuild_shadows/rebuild_shoreline/rebuild_tank_tracks/adjust_client_lod hooks after writing GlobalData.

title: [Common] GameLOD never loads GameLOD.ini, presets, or saved graphics options
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/GameLOD.cpp` `GameLODManager::init` loads `Data\INI\GameLOD.ini` and `Data\INI\GameLODPresets.ini` via the INI reader, snapshots Custom from GlobalData, reads OptionPreferences (user StaticGameLOD / IdealStaticGameLOD / texture reduction / shadows / particles / trees), runs `testMinimumRequirements`, optionally benchmarks, then `setStaticLODLevel(userSetDetail)`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini_game_lod.rs` `GameLODManager::init` only clears tables. `common/game_lod.rs` `ensure_game_lod_loaded` only scans raw filesystem `Data/INI/Default/GameLOD.ini` and `Data/INI/GameLOD.ini` for SlowDeathScale into a HashMap — it does not use the INI block parser, archives, GameLODPresets.ini, OptionPreferences, or hardware auto-detect. No `INI::load(".../GameLOD.ini")` call exists in the Rust tree.

## Evidence
C++ init lines 244-338. Rust `init_game_lod_manager` constructs an empty manager. `ensure_game_lod_loaded` uses `std::fs::read_to_string` on disk paths that typically do not exist when INI lives in INIZH.big.

## Player-visible effect
Static/dynamic LOD tables, hardware presets, and the player's saved graphics option never apply. Particle caps, trees, shadows, and texture reduction stay at constructor defaults (or whatever GlobalData.ini set), so Low/High detail and auto-detect do not match retail.
close_reason: GameLODManager init loads GameLOD.ini, GameLODPresets.ini, and Options.ini StaticGameLOD/IdealStaticGameLOD then applies the user level.

title: [Common] AudioManager init never loads AudioSettings.ini or MiscAudio.ini
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/Audio/GameAudio.cpp` `AudioManager::init` (lines 186-202) loads `Data\INI\AudioSettings.ini` then Music/SoundEffects/Speech/Voice (Default+override) then `Data\INI\MiscAudio.ini`. AudioSettings drive sample counts, volumes, zoom, microphone height, cache size. MiscAudio names UI clicks, radar, sabotage, and other global cues.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/audio/game_audio.rs` `load_audio_event_inis` (called from `initialize_global_audio_manager`) only loads Music/SoundEffects/Speech/Voice. `AudioManager::init` only copies already-constructed volume defaults. Parsers exist (`ini_audio_settings::parse_audio_settings_definition`, `ini_misc_audio::parse_misc_audio`) but nothing loads those two INI files on the audio init path.

## Evidence
C++: `ini.load("Data\\INI\\AudioSettings.ini"...)` then later `ini.load("Data\\INI\\MiscAudio.ini"...)`.
Rust `AUDIO_EVENT_INI_FILES` array has no AudioSettings.ini or MiscAudio.ini. Main `host_rank_ui_residual.rs` hardcodes AudioSettings volume residuals (55/70/80/80) instead of reading the INI.

## Player-visible effect
Music/SFX/speech mix, 2D/3D channel counts, zoom volume, and named UI/radar/sabotage cues use constructor/residual defaults instead of retail INI, so audio mix and many interface sounds do not match Zero Hour.
close_reason: AudioManager init loads AudioSettings.ini then Music/SFX/Speech/Voice then MiscAudio.ini and applies settings to the live manager.

title: [Scripts] PartitionSolver bin-pack is a spatial grid, so load-into-transports fails
description:
## C++
`PartitionSolver.cpp` (101 lines) is an NP-complete bin-packer: assign `EntriesVec` (unit sizes) into `SpacesVec` (transport capacities). `ScriptActions.cpp` (~619 and ~1479) uses `PartitionSolver(vecOfUnits, vecOfTransports, PREFER_FAST_SOLUTION)` then issues enter commands from `getSolution()`.

## Rust
Mapped `common/partition_solver.rs` (1217 lines) is a spatial hash-grid (nearby_objects, register_object) — a PartitionManager-like system, not a bin-packer. No `EntriesVec`/`SpacesVec`/`solve()`/`PREFER_FAST_SOLUTION`. Grep finds no bin-pack PartitionSolver in GeneralsRust.

## Evidence
C++ header: "General purpose partition problem-solver". Rust module docs: "Spatial Partitioning System" / "uniform grid".

## Player-visible effect
Map scripts that load a team into transports (campaign airlifts, naval loads) cannot assign units to remaining cargo slots. Units stay on the ground / script stalls.
close_reason: Added C++ BinPartitionSolver (EntriesVec/SpacesVec/PREFER_FAST) and wired TEAM_LOAD_TRANSPORTS. Files: Common/src/common/partition_solver.rs actions_team_relations.rs

title: [GameLogic] Gathering workers never switch to mine-clearing weapons
description:
## C++
`WorkerAIUpdate::update` (`WorkerAIUpdate.cpp`) when `m_workerMachine` is not AS_DOZER runs the supply-truck machine and then `getObject()->setWeaponSetFlag(WEAPONSET_MINE_CLEARING_DETAIL)` so a gathering GLA worker can detonate mines while ferrying.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/supply_system/worker.rs` has dozer + supply dual-mode update but never sets `WeaponSetType::MineClearingDetail` (or any mine-clearing flag). Grep of that file finds no mine-clearing references.

## Evidence
C++ comment: "If we are harvesting, we can be diverted to clear mines." Rust worker update has no equivalent `set_weapon_set_flag`.

## Player-visible effect
GLA workers walking between supply piles and the supply stash will not automatically blow mines in their path the way Zero Hour workers do.
close_reason: Harvesting workers now set WeaponSetType::MineClearingDetail on the live WorkerAIUpdate harvest path (C++ WorkerAIUpdate::update when not AS_DOZER). File: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/supply_system/worker.rs. C++ does not clear the flag in this function when switching back to dozer, so Rust does not either.

title: [Player] killPlayer does not evacuate or destroy the player's units
description:
## C++
`Player::killPlayer` (Player.cpp 2023-2071) evacuates all team containers, sets dead, then `team->killTeam()` on every instance (destroys units/buildings). Single-player AI is then resurrected so scripts can reuse the slot. Local player ControlBar switches to observer scheme. Money is zeroed last.

## Rust
`common/rts/player.rs` `kill_player` (1978-2008) sets `is_player_dead`, `team_prototypes.clear()` (comment: "would evacuate containers"), clears squads/selection/build list/supplies/tunnels, withdraws money. Never calls evacuate or kill on live objects. No SP-AI resurrection. No ControlBar observer switch.

## Evidence
`// Clear all team prototypes (would evacuate containers in full impl)` then only list clears.

## Player-visible effect
When a player is defeated (or a script kills the player), their army and base stay on the map as living units. Campaign "kill this side" does not end their presence.
close_reason: kill_player evacuates then kills owned objects, resurrects SP computer AI, observer ControlBar for local, then zeros money (player.rs).

title: [W3D] RTS cursors never show game textures or 3D models
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DMouse.cpp` `W3DMouse::setCursor` / `draw` / `loadD3DCursorTextures` / `initW3DAssets`.
Four redraw modes: RM_DX8 hardware cursor (animated TGA frames + hotspot, independent thread), RM_W3D 3D interface-scene models (`Create_Render_Obj` + `Get_HAnim`, scroll-rotated), RM_POLYGON `TheDisplay->drawImage` from MappedImage names, RM_WINDOWS OS cursor. `Mouse.ini` supplies ~40 cursor types (AttackObject, MoveTo, BuildPlacement, Repair, etc.) with textureName/W3DModelName/hotSpot/numFrames.

## Rust
Live path: `GameEngine/GameClient/src/input/mouse.rs` `Mouse::set_cursor` only stores the enum. `Main/src/cnc_game_engine/mouse.rs` `sync_context_mouse_cursor` maps a few contexts onto `winit::CursorIcon` (Pointer/Crosshair/Cell). Device `wthree_d_mouse.rs` `W3DMouse::draw` returns a `MouseDrawState` struct and never submits GPU or OS cursor frames; it hardcodes 9 cursors and `set_cursor_direction` is a no-op. INI `CursorInfo` is parsed but never loaded into the W3D mouse.

## Evidence
No `loadD3DCursorTextures`, `initW3DAssets`, or `drawImage` cursor path. Device draw: `MouseDrawState { cursor, texture_frame, hot_spot, ... }` with no render. Main comment: "Fail-closed vs full Mouse.cpp ANI/CUR assets — uses platform icons".

## Player-visible effect
Attack, move, build, repair, rally, and scroll cursors never appear as the retail TGA/W3D cursors. Players only see a generic OS pointer (or nothing when the window hides the system cursor).
close_reason: W3DMouse loads Mouse.ini-style textures and W3D models (AttackObject, MoveTo, BuildPlacement, Repair, etc.) with RM_DX8/W3D/Polygon/Windows; Display draws the live cursor. Files: wthree_d_mouse.rs, display/display.rs

title: [W3D] Building placement uses a 2D box instead of Locater models
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DInGameUI.cpp` `W3DInGameUI::drawPlaceAngle`.
Lazily creates `Locater01` (anchor) and `Locater02` (arrow) via `Create_Render_Obj`, adds/removes them from `m_3DScene` based on `isPlacementAnchored()` and drag length (>= 5px shows arrow). Transform is copied from `m_placeIcon[0]` so the locator sits on the ghost building.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/ingame_ui/impl_update.rs` `draw_placement_cursor` draws a 2D green/red `UIRect` outline from `preview.footprint * 50`. Device `wthree_d_in_game_ui.rs` `draw_place_angle` emits a yellow `WorldLine` of length 20. Neither loads Locater01/Locater02.

## Evidence
C++ `Create_Render_Obj("Locater01")` / `Create_Render_Obj("Locater02")` + `Set_Transform(*m_placeIcon[0]->getTransformMatrix())`. Rust: `renderer.draw_rect_outline_with_scissor(rect, 2.0, border_color, None)`. Distinct from hq-3hfm (terrain bib quads) and hq-061f (ControlBar WND).

## Player-visible effect
Placing a building shows a flat 2D box (or a line) instead of the retail 3D locator arrow/anchor that follows the ghost building's facing.
close_reason: Placement uses Locater01/Locater02 models; arrow shown when drag >= 5px. Files: display/view.rs, wthree_d_in_game_ui.rs

title: [W3D] Move-click 3D hint models never appear
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DInGameUI.cpp` `W3DInGameUI::drawMoveHints`.
For each of MAX_MOVE_HINTS while `elapsed <= 40`, creates `TheGlobalData->m_moveHintName` via `Create_Render_Obj`, loads matching HAnim, adds the object to `W3DDisplay::m_3DScene`, plays ANIM_MODE_ONCE, and aligns the transform to terrain (`alignOnTerrain`) or water surface. Hidden after 40 frames.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/ingame_ui/leftover.rs` `create_move_hint` only pushes `HintData` (start/end/frame). `impl_update.rs` `draw` never instantiates a W3D move-hint model; `draw_team_waypoint_lines` draws 2D lines only for `HintType::Command`. Device `wthree_d_in_game_ui.rs` `draw` has no `draw_move_hints` at all.

## Evidence
C++ `Create_Render_Obj(TheGlobalData->m_moveHintName.str())` + `Add_Render_Object`. Rust stores hints and expires them; no scene object, no HAnim, no terrain/water align.

## Player-visible effect
Right-click move orders show no 3D "go here" marker on the ground. Players get no world-space confirmation of the click point (distinct from ControlBar WND, hq-061f).
close_reason: View::draw_view spawns MoveHint 3D models for 40 frames; W3DInGameUI::draw_move_hints creates scene models from m_moveHintName. Files: display/view.rs, wthree_d_in_game_ui.rs

title: [W3D] Prototype texture swaps never replace materials
description:
## C++
`W3DAssetManager.cpp` `replacePrototypeTexture` / `replaceAssetTexture` / `replaceHLODTexture` / `replaceMeshTexture`.
Walks mesh material texture slots (and HLOD sub-objects) and replaces `oldTex` with `newTex`. Used from `Create_Render_Obj(..., oldTexture, newTexture)` for unique/camo/upgrade skins.

## Rust
`wthree_d_asset_manager.rs` `replace_prototype_texture` is a stub:
```
// PARITY_NOTE: C++ walks sub-objects calling replaceMeshTexture / replaceHLODTexture.
// The Rust port stores texture references differently — actual texture swap deferred
return false;
```
`create_render_obj_customized` calls it when both texture names are present, then caches the un-swapped prototype.

## Evidence
Function always returns `false` and never mutates `AssetPrototype` meshes/`texture_names`. Distinct from hq-2k22 mesh-shard transforms.

## Player-visible effect
Units and objects that C++ retargets onto a new texture (camo, unique skins, some upgrades) keep the original material.
close_reason: replace_prototype_texture walks mesh/HLOD texture_names and replaces oldTex with newTex (C++ replaceMeshTexture/replaceHLODTexture).

title: [W3D] House-color textures never recolor for team
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DAssetManager.cpp` `Create_Render_Obj(name, scale, color, oldTex, newTex)` then `Recolor_Asset` / `Recolor_Mesh` / `Recolor_HLOD`.
Non-black `color` remaps HOUSECOLOR vertex materials and every texture whose name starts with `ZHC` via `Recolor_Texture` (palette row or inverted-alpha house-color blend). Result is cached under a munged prototype name.

## Rust
`wthree_d_asset_manager.rs` `create_render_obj_customized` only stores `custom_proto.object_color = color` and never calls `recolor_texture` / Recolor_Mesh / Recolor_HLOD. `recolor_texture` exists as a helper but is not wired from create. Live Main objects keep a `team_color` RGBA for overlays only.

## Evidence
C++ `if (reallycolor) Recolor_Asset(rendobj,color);` plus ZHC texture replace. Rust create path sets `object_color` then inserts the prototype; no mesh/texture remap. Distinct from hq-2k22 (HLOD shards): this is the house-color algorithm on whatever mesh is drawn.

## Player-visible effect
USA/China/GLA units and buildings keep the default (usually unpainted) house-color regions. Enemy and ally factions do not show their team colors on infantry/vehicle skins.
close_reason: create_render_obj_customized now calls recolor_asset/recolor_mesh/recolor_hlod: HOUSECOLOR meshes store team color and ZHC textures go through Recolor_Texture.

title: [GameLogic] Skirmish/MP victory never kills leftovers, reveals map, or announces defeat
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/ScriptEngine/VictoryConditions.cpp` `VictoryConditions::update` (123-215): for multiplayer/skirmish recorder games, detects last remaining alliance (`m_endFrame`), and for each newly defeated player: `revealMapForPlayerPermanently`, UI `GUI:PlayerHasBeenDefeated`, `GUIMessageReceived` audio, AI slot last-frame mark, `p->killPlayer()`, `PopulateInGameDiplomacyPopup()`. Also handles local-player defeat.

## Rust
Mapped `GameLogic/src/script_engine/victory_conditions.rs` re-exports `scripting/victory.rs`, a generic campaign-objective system (TotalDestruction/Survive/etc.) that is not the C++ class.

Live tick uses `system/game_logic_impl/impl_update.rs` `update_victory_conditions` (~1364-1440) plus `system/victory_conditions.rs` flags. It only sets `player.set_defeated(true)`. Comments explicitly defer: partition reveal, InGameUI message, audio, and `killPlayer()`.

TheVictoryConditions helper (`helpers/leftover.rs`) is a single `LOCAL_ALLIED_VICTORY` bool.

## Evidence
impl_update.rs:1430-1439 "Deferred — partition manager integration / UI/audio / killPlayer()". No last-alliance `m_endFrame` / local-defeat handling.

## Player-visible effect
When a skirmish/MP player loses all units+buildings, leftover infantry/vehicles stay, the map is not revealed, no defeat banner/sound, diplomacy popup does not refresh, and the match does not end when one alliance remains.
close_reason: Newly defeated players get permanent map reveal, GUI:PlayerHasBeenDefeated + GUIMessageReceived, leftover objects destroyed. File: impl_update.rs

title: [GameLogic] Sim tick never posts MSG_LOGIC_CRC or ticks Recorder/StatsCollector
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/GameLogic.cpp` `GameLogic::update` (3625-3665):
- On MP/solo CRC interval, `m_CRC = getCRC(CRC_RECALC)` then `TheMessageStream->appendMessage(GameMessage::MSG_LOGIC_CRC)` with CRC + playback flag.
- Then `TheStatsCollector->update()` and `TheRecorder->UPDATE()`.

## Rust
Live tick is `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/system/game_logic_impl/impl_update.rs` `GameLogic::update`.
- Computes `self.crc_cache = self.compute_crc()` on interval only.
- Never appends MSG_LOGIC_CRC / CommandType::LogicCrc to the message stream.
- Command processor (`commands/command_processor_impl/handler_dispatch.rs`) treats `LogicCrc` as `Success` no-op.
- No `TheRecorder->UPDATE()` or `TheStatsCollector->update()` call in the tick.

## Evidence
impl_update.rs ~149-153 only caches CRC. handler_dispatch.rs:147-148 `CommandType::DoAttackSquad | SetReplayCamera | LogicCrc => Success`. No recorder/stats collector update in the phase list after processCommandList.

## Player-visible effect
Replays and lockstep MP never exchange per-frame logic CRCs. Replay recording/playback and desync detection do not run. In-game stats collector does not advance.
close_reason: GameLogic::update posts LogicCRC to the message stream and ticks StatsCollector + Recorder. File: system/game_logic_impl/impl_update.rs

title: [GameLogic] RevealToAll kindof never unshrouds enemies
description:
## C++
`Object::look` (Object.cpp:4943-4946): if `isKindOf(KINDOF_REVEAL_TO_ALL)`, `lookingMask = PLAYERMASK_ALL` so the unit's normal shroud-clearing range is applied for every player. Separate from the template `ShroudRevealToAllRange` path (allies vs enemies/neutral).

## Rust
`object/object_vision.rs` `look()` builds `looking_mask` only from allied players plus `vision_spied_mask`. It never tests `KindOf::RevealToAll`. The later `get_shroud_reveal_to_all_range()` path is implemented, but that is the different smaller-range feature.

## Evidence
C++: `if ( isKindOf(KINDOF_REVEAL_TO_ALL) ) { lookingMask = PLAYERMASK_ALL; }`
Rust look() has no `RevealToAll` / `PLAYERMASK_ALL` branch. KindOf::RevealToAll exists elsewhere (battle_plan_update name table).

## Player-visible effect
Objects marked RevealToAll (certain campaign/special units) do not punch enemy fog at their vision range; enemies stay shrouded where C++ would show the map.
close_reason: Object::look sets looking_mask = PLAYERMASK_ALL for KindOf::RevealToAll. File: GameLogic/src/object/object_vision.rs

title: [GameClient] Campaign maps keep persisted rank instead of starting at 0
description:
## C++
`CampaignManager::getRankPoints` in `Include/GameClient/CampaignManager.h` 123-130 **always returns 0**. Comment: campaign and Challenge maps were not designed with rank persistence; starting rank on map load is forced to 0. `setRankPoints` still stores `m_currentRankPoints` for xfer, but gameplay start uses the getter.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/campaign_manager.rs` `get_rank_points` returns `self.current_rank_points` (whatever `set_rank_points` stored).

## Evidence
C++: `return 0;` with explicit design note (08/09/03).
Rust:
```
pub fn get_rank_points(&self) -> i32 {
    self.current_rank_points
}
```

## Player-visible effect
Campaign / Generals Challenge missions start with leftover generals rank/XP from a previous mission instead of a clean rank-0 start, changing unit unlocks and starting power.
close_reason: CampaignManager::get_rank_points always returns 0 while set_rank_points still stores for xfer, matching CampaignManager.h:123-130.

title: [GameLogic] Rank.ini never populates the in-game Player rank store
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/System/RankInfo.cpp` `RankInfoStore::friend_parseRankDefinition` (lines 96-151) parses Rank INI (`RankName`, `SkillPointsNeeded`, `SciencesGranted`, `SciencePurchasePointsGranted`) into the single `TheRankInfoStore` singleton. `Player` rank-up / science-purchase-point grants read that same store (`getRankInfo(level)` 1-based).

## Rust
Two disconnected stores:
- INI load writes `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/ini/ini_rank.rs` (`parse_rank_definition`).
- GameLogic Player (`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/player/science_management.rs`) reads `crate::system::rank_info::the_rank_info_store()`.
- Mapped `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/system/rank_info.rs` `init_global_rank_info_store()` is never called from INI parse; `the_rank_info_store()` returns None or an empty store.

## Evidence
Mapped rank_info.rs header: "Those systems are not yet available in the Rust port". `the_rank_info_store_mut` / `apply_rank_definition` have no callers outside unit tests. Player `set_rank_level_impl` / `add_skill_points_impl` / `reset_sciences_impl` all `use crate::system::rank_info::the_rank_info_store`.

## Player-visible effect
Generals rank-up, science purchase points, and rank-granted sciences from Rank.ini never apply. Players stay at rank 1 / 0 SPP even after earning skill points.
close_reason: the_rank_info_store() syncs from Common INI RankInfoStore (Rank.ini). File: system/rank_info.rs

title: [GameClient] Control-bar tutorial arrow transition finishes immediately
description:
## C++
`ControlBarArrowTransition` in `GameWindowTransitionsStyles.cpp` lasts `CONTROLBARARROWTRANSITION_END` frames. `update()` only sets `m_isFinished` on START (used during init reset) and END. `draw()` blits `TheControlBar->getArrowImage()` sliding down onto `ControlBar.wnd:ButtonGeneral`, then fades it.

## Rust
`ControlBarArrowTransition::update` in `src/gui/game_window_transitions.rs` always sets `self.is_finished = true` on every frame after init. `draw()` fills a hardcoded 16x16 white rectangle instead of the control-bar arrow image (`draw_rect` with RGBA 255,255,255).

## Evidence
Rust: `fn update(&mut self, frame: i32) { self.draw_state = frame; self.is_finished = true; }` and `renderer.draw_rect(rect, rgba_from_components(255, 255, 255, 255), 0.0)`. C++: `TheDisplay->drawImage(m_arrowImage, ...)`.

## Player-visible effect
The tutorial/control-bar arrow that should slide onto the Generals button is a one-frame white square (or never seen), not the real arrow graphic over ~22 frames.
close_reason: ControlBarArrowTransition finishes only on START/END frames (22-frame duration) and draws GenArrow image. Files: game_window_transitions.rs

title: [GameLogic] EMP blast never tints or flashes the pulse drawable
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/EMPUpdate.cpp` `EMPUpdate::update` saturates `m_startColor`/`m_endColor` and calls `drawable->colorTint` until `m_tintEnvPlayFrame`, then `drawable->colorFlash` while `doDisableAttack()` runs. Killed airborne aircraft also get `setTintStatus(TINT_STATUS_DISABLED)`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/emp_update.rs` `update_simple` only lerps `current_scale` onto the instance matrix, then disables/kills. Parsed StartColor/EndColor are unused. Aircraft kill path never sets disabled tint.

## Evidence
Rust update has no `color_tint` / `color_flash` / `set_tint_status` calls despite storing `start_color`/`end_color` and `tint_env_play_frame`.

## Player-visible effect
EMP/neutron pulse grows but stays uncolored; disabled aircraft do not go dark/black like Zero Hour.
close_reason: EMPUpdate::update_simple now saturates StartColor/EndColor and calls drawable.color_tint until tint_env_play_frame, then color_flash (9999, fade, sustain) plus do_disable_attack. Airborne aircraft kill path sets TintStatus::DISABLED. Files: emp_update.rs, drawable.rs (color_tint/color_flash/set_instance_scale).

title: [GameLogic] Strategy Center plan change is silent and buttons ignore the active plan
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/BattlePlanUpdate.cpp` `BattlePlanUpdate::setStatus(TRANSITIONSTATUS_UNPACKING)` plays `TheRadar->createPlayerEvent(..., RADAR_EVENT_BATTLE_PLAN)`, `TheInGameUI->message(...)`, unpack/pack/idle/announcement `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`, and `drawable->setAnimationLoopDuration`. `getCommandOption()` returns OPTION_ONE/TWO/THREE from `m_desiredPlan`. `isPowerCurrentlyInUse` always returns false.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/battle_plan_update.rs` parses Bombardment/HoldTheLine/SearchAndDestroy message labels and announcement names but `set_status` / `apply_unpacking_states` only flip model-condition door flags. `get_command_option()` always returns `NONE`. `is_power_currently_in_use()` returns `is_active()`.

## Evidence
Rust unpacking path never calls radar, InGameUI, or audio. Command-option helper is a constant none.

## Player-visible effect
Switching Strategy Center battle plans has no radar blip, no on-screen message, no announcement/unpack audio, and command buttons cannot show (or may block) the selected plan.
close_reason: BattlePlanUpdate now matches C++ setStatus/getCommandOption/isPowerCurrentlyInUse: desired plan maps to OPTION_ONE/TWO/THREE, is_power_currently_in_use always false, unpacking plays radar BattlePlan blip + UI message + unpack/announcement audio, packing/idle play named events and stop on leave, drawable animation loop duration set on unpack/pack. Live file: GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/object/behavior/battle_plan_update.rs

title: [GameLogic] EMP disables civilian structures that Zero Hour skips
description:
## C++
`EMPUpdate::doDisableAttack` (`EMPUpdate.cpp`) after the vehicle/structure/spawns filter: if victim is KINDOF_STRUCTURE and `!isFactionStructure()`, continue (skip). Only faction buildings take EMP.

## Rust
`EMPUpdate::do_disable_attack` in `object/behavior/emp_update.rs` applies `set_disabled_until(DisabledEmp)` to every KINDOF_STRUCTURE that passes the own-building / reject-allies filters. No `is_faction_structure()` check.

## Evidence
C++ lines ~251-255 skip non-faction structures. Rust loop has no equivalent branch.

## Player-visible effect
Civilian/neutral buildings (oil derricks, huts, tech buildings that are not faction structures) get EMP-disabled when they should be immune.
close_reason: do_disable_attack now skips KINDOF_STRUCTURE victims that fail is_faction_structure(), matching C++ EMPUpdate.cpp:251-255. Civilian/tech buildings are immune. File: emp_update.rs

title: [GameLogic] Transport attack orders never fire the hull weapon
description:
## C++
`TransportAIUpdate::privateAttackObject` / `privateForceAttackObject` / `privateAttackPosition` (`TransportAIUpdate.cpp`) first relay the order to fire-allowed passengers (skipping EMP/hacked Overlord gattling), then always call `AIUpdateInterface::privateAttack*` so the transport hull itself attacks.

## Rust
`object/update/ai_update/transport_ai_update.rs` `private_attack_object` / `private_force_attack_object` / `private_attack_position` only `relay_attack_to_passengers`. They never invoke the base AI attack on the transport.

## Evidence
Rust functions return after the passenger loop; no `ai.ai_attack_object` on the owner.

## Player-visible effect
Overlord/Battle Bus/Scorpion (and any armed transport) passengers may fire, but the hull gun/cannon does not shoot when the player issues an attack or attack-ground order.
close_reason: False positive: UnitAIUpdate::execute_command in object/unit/ai_commands.rs issues the hull attack via ai_do_command/give_attack_order, then calls TransportAIUpdate::private_attack_* only to relay to passengers. Both sides fire in the same command.

title: [W3D] Fullscreen movies never blit to the display
description:
## C++
`W3DDisplay::draw` advances the video stream and `drawVideoBuffer` (`W3DDisplay.cpp:2829`) blits the current frame across the display. `playLogoMovie` / `playMovie` plus copyright hold times are part of the same path.

## Rust
Production `Display::play_movie` / `play_logo_movie` open a stream and allocate `SoftwareVideoBuffer`. `update_movie_playback` decompresses frames, but `Display::draw` never samples `video_buffer` or submits a fullscreen quad. Gadget `draw_video_buffer` is a separate UI path (cameos/buttons), not the display movie.

## Evidence
Display::draw (display.rs:697-976) has no video blit. `update_movie_playback` is never called from `draw`.

## Player-visible effect
Intro, logo, and scripted fullscreen movies stay black even when a stream is open; only gadget-sized videos can appear.
close_reason: Display caches decompressed movie RGBA and blit_video_rgba draws a fullscreen textured quad plus copyright string (C++ drawVideoBuffer).

title: [W3D] Cliff cells use unstretched tile UVs
description:
## C++
`WorldHeightMap::getUVData` / `getUVForTileIndex` (`WorldHeightMap.cpp` 1663–1953):
- Looks up `m_tileNdxes` then `getUVForNdx` for the atlas quarter-tile.
- If `m_cliffInfoNdxes[ndx] != 0` and the cliff’s `tileIndex` is in the same texture class, replaces UVs with `TCliffInfo` u0–u3/v0–v3 (mutant/flip mapping).
- Else `DO_OLD_UV` stretches UVs when cell height delta exceeds `STRETCH_LIMIT` / `TALL_STRETCH_LIMIT` / `DIAMOND_STRETCH_LIMIT` so steep faces do not repeat a flat tile.
- `getAlphaUVData` (2042) also uses this stretch and may flip the triangle split when cliff-stretched.

## Rust
Production `GameClient/src/terrain/height_map.rs` has `tile_ndxes` / blend arrays but **no** `cliff_info`, `get_uv_data`, or stretch path.
Device `height_map/world_height_map.rs` stores `cliff_info` / `cliff_info_ndxes` and `init_cliff_flags_from_heights` (pathfind bits only) — it never computes cliff UVs.
Live `terrain.wgsl` samples `tex_coords` with no cliff remap.

## Evidence
Grep of `GameClient/src/terrain` for `get_uv_data|getUVForNdx|cliff_info|is_cliff_mapped` is empty. Distinct from hq-eenv (which is “tileNdx must drive splat slots”); this is the UV warp on already-selected tiles.

## Player-visible effect
Cliffs and steep banks show the same unstretched ground tile tiled up the face instead of the retail stretched/mutant cliff mapping.
close_reason: HeightMap::get_uv_for_tile_index DO_OLD_UV + TCliffInfo; cell_uv_at_world on GPU verts

title: [W3D] Shoreline water-edge tiles never feather into water
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/BaseHeightMap.cpp`
- `updateShorelineTile` / `updateShorelineTiles` (1565–1680) scan every cell that straddles the water plane within `transparentWaterDepth * minWaterOpacity`, pack verts + per-corner depth `t0..t3`.
- `initDestAlphaLUT` builds a 256×1 dest-alpha gradient texture.
- `renderShoreLines` / `renderShoreLinesSorted` (2419+) re-draw those tiles with dest-alpha so land fades into water.
- `W3DTerrainVisual::setShoreLineDetail` (1126) rebuilds the set when the option is toggled.
- `HeightMapRenderObjClass::Render` (2080) always calls `renderShoreLines` after the base pass.

## Rust
Device `height_map/base_height_map.rs` only defines `ShoreLineTileInfo` / `ShoreLineTileSortInfo` structs. No `update_shoreline_tiles`, no dest-alpha LUT, no shoreline draw.
Production `GameClient/src/terrain/` has zero shoreline symbols. `terrain_visual/` has no `set_shore_line_detail`. Live `terrain.wgsl` has no water-edge dest-alpha pass.

## Evidence
Grep of production `GameClient/src/terrain` for `shoreline|shore_line|renderShore|updateShore` is empty. Device comment says shoreline rendering is “deferred to terrain_rendering.rs” but that file never implements the C++ scan/sort/draw.

## Player-visible effect
Where terrain meets rivers/lakes/ocean the ground cuts off as a hard line instead of the retail soft depth-fade shoreline.
close_reason: rebuild_shoreline ports updateShorelineTiles; dest-alpha shoreline mesh drawn before/with water

title: [Recorder] Replay CRC mismatch is never reported because frame is hardcoded 0
description:
## C++
`RecorderClass::handleCRCMessage` (Recorder.cpp 957-994) compares live CRC to playback CRC using `TheGameLogic->getFrame()`. On mismatch it flags desync, logs, and can copy the replay for debug.

## Rust
`common/recorder.rs` `handle_crc_message` (1633-1635): `let frame = 0; // Would come from TheGameLogic->getFrame()` then `if frame > 0 && new_crc != playback_crc`. The `frame > 0` guard is always false.

## Evidence
Hardcoded `frame = 0` makes the mismatch branch dead.

## Player-visible effect
Watching a replay never shows a desync warning even when simulation diverged. Players think the replay is valid while units teleport/act differently than recorded.
close_reason: Recorder::handle_crc_message uses get_current_frame() instead of hardcoded 0. File: Common/src/common/recorder.rs

title: [W3D] Occluded-unit player-color, heat vision, and frenzy never draw
description:
## C++
`RTS3DScene` (`W3DScene.cpp`) visibility-classifies occluders/occludees, `flagOccludedObjects`, then `flushOccludedObjectsIntoStencil` draws behind-building units in their player color. `renderOneObject` applies shroud, heat-vision, heat-vision-only, and frenzy material passes (`m_heatVisionMaterialPass`, `m_frenzyMaterialPass`, `m_occludedMaterialPass[MAX_PLAYER_COUNT]`).

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/scene.rs` ports the CPU queues and emits `RenderEvent`s, but live `Display::draw` never constructs or flushes a `W3DScene`. It culls via `drawable_manager` and records a single drawable pass with no extra material/stencil passes. Legacy `wthree_d_scene.rs` notes missing stencil state.

## Evidence
Display::draw (display.rs:792-826) is one drawable pass. No heat-vision/frenzy/occluded-color submit. Scene module is unused by the production frame.

## Player-visible effect
Units hidden behind buildings never show the colored silhouette; infrared/heat-vision and frenzy tints never replace or overlay the model.
close_reason: Display shadow_pass collects occluded player-color and heat-vision overlays; volumetric/occlusion casters can be registered; heat-vision second-pass opacity is surfaced for the overlay path.

title: [W3D] Viewport B&W, motion-blur, and crossfade filters never render
description:
## C++
`W3DView::draw` (`W3DView.cpp:1509`) calls `W3DShaderManager::filterPreRender` / `filterPostRender` for `FT_VIEW_BW_FILTER`, `FT_VIEW_MOTION_BLUR_FILTER`, and `FT_VIEW_CROSSFADE`. Filters render the scene to a texture then composite (death-cam B&W, superweapon zoom-blur, circle/mask crossfade). `setFadeParameters` drives BW/crossfade fades.

## Rust
Production `View::set_view_filter` / `set_view_filter_mode` only store enums. `Display::draw` never starts render-to-texture or applies a screen filter. `ViewTrait::draw_view` is a no-op (`force_redraw`). Legacy `wthree_d_shader_manager.rs` `BlackWhiteFilter` / `MotionBlurFilter` / `CrossFadeFilter` update CPU fade counters in `post_render` and never bind a wgpu pass. Production Display does not call the shader manager.

## Evidence
view.rs:1033-1044 stores filter state. display.rs:697-976 has no filterPreRender/postRender. Shader manager filters return `self.initialized` without drawing.

## Player-visible effect
Death-cam black-and-white, motion-blur zooms, and scripted crossfades never appear; the viewport stays unfiltered.
close_reason: View filter_composite drives Display blit of B&W/motion-blur/crossfade overlays (fade + mode tints). View-side hook lives on View; live Display composites. Files: display/view.rs, display/display.rs

title: [W3D] Camera reset ignores map ground height
description:
## C++
`W3DView::initHeightForMap` (`W3DView.cpp:2354`) samples `TheTerrainLogic->getGroundHeight`, caps at 120, and sets `m_cameraOffset` from `TheGlobalData->m_cameraHeight` / pitch. `setZoomToDefault` (`W3DView.cpp:1952`) computes desired zoom from max height vs current ground so default zoom is the legal max at that spot.

## Rust
Production `View` has no `init_height_for_map`. `set_zoom_to_default` (view.rs:731-733) only `set_zoom(self.max_zoom)`. `set_default_view` updates `max_height_above_ground` from GlobalData but never rebuilds a 3D camera offset from the map.

## Evidence
No `init_height` / `initHeightForMap` on `display/view.rs`. Zoom default ignores terrain height under the camera.

## Player-visible effect
Starting a map or pressing default-zoom leaves the camera at a generic height instead of the ZH pitched offset for that terrain, so some maps start too close or clip into hills.
close_reason: Added init_height_for_map (ground sample, cap 120, cameraOffset from GlobalData) and set_zoom_to_default from max height vs cameraOffset.z. Files: display/view.rs

title: [GameClient] IME never hooks OS input or opens candidate window
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/IMEManager.cpp` `IMEManager::serviceIMEMessage` handles Win32 `WM_IME_*` via IMM32 (`ImmGetContext` / `ImmGetCompositionStringW`). On `IMN_OPENCANDIDATE` it calls `openCandidateList`, which loads `IMECandidateWindow.wnd` and fills the candidate listbox. Composition chars are sent to the attached text-entry as `GWM_IME_CHAR`. `GadgetTextEntrySystem` (`GadgetTextEntry.cpp`) attaches `TheIMEManager` on focus and detaches on blur. `enable()` calls `ImmAssociateContext`.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/gui/ime_manager.rs` `ImeManager::service_ime_message` only mutates in-memory `ImeMessage` enum state. `attach()` stores a `Weak` pointer and never associates an OS IME context. `enable()`/`disable()` flip a bool. There is no `openCandidateList` that creates `IMECandidateWindow.wnd`. Candidate gadgets are only clicked by residual `simulate_*` / `drive_os_wnd_*` test helpers. `src/gui/gadgets/text.rs` has `ime_composition` fields labeled "placeholder for IME" and never calls `get_ime_manager().attach`.

## Evidence
Rust `service_ime_message` match arms update `composition_string` / `candidates` only; they never `winSendInputMsg(..., GWM_IME_CHAR, ...)`. C++ `GadgetTextEntryInput` ignores keys while IME is composing; Rust text-entry never consults the IME manager.

## Player-visible effect
CJK / IME users cannot compose or pick candidates in chat, login, or other text fields. Candidate window never appears. Only Latin keyboard input works.
close_reason: IME attach associates OS IME context, enable/disable use disable-count, service_ime_message dispatches IME_CHAR and opens/closes IMECandidateWindow.wnd; text-entry focus attaches/detaches. Files: ime_manager.rs, window_impl_input.rs, gadgets/text.rs

title: [Common] ThingTemplate ignores Add/Remove/Replace module overrides
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/Thing/ThingTemplate.cpp` parse table (`AddModule`/`RemoveModule`/`ReplaceModule`/`InheritableModule`/`OverrideableByLikeKind`, lines 213-218) and parsers (`parseAddModule` 715-729, `parseRemoveModule` 734-754, `parseReplaceModule` 759-786, `parseInheritableModule` 791-804, `OverrideableByLikeKind` 810-823). Faction/general Object.ini overrides add, remove, or replace tagged modules on the inherited template.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/Common/src/common/thing/thing_template.rs`: those tokens are listed in `CPP_OBJECT_FIELDS` (lines 141-145) but `load_modules_from_properties` only accepts `Behavior`/`Body`/`Draw`/`ClientUpdate`. The parse match falls through to `_ if is_cpp_object_field(key) => {}` (lines 2991-2993) and silently drops the override blocks. `_module_parsing_mode` exists but is never switched to add/remove/replace.

## Evidence
Comment at 2991: "Valid C++ fields not yet wired to Rust state are accepted here so they are not mistaken for unknown tokens." No `parse_add_module` / `remove_module_info` path.

## Player-visible effect
Zero Hour general-specific units keep the default faction modules. Replaced weapons, extra behaviors, and removed modules never apply (wrong unit stats, missing specials, leftover default modules).
close_reason: ThingTemplate now applies Add/Remove/Replace/Inheritable/OverrideableByLikeKind module overrides from INI (thing_template.rs, thing_factory.rs).

title: [Common] Object Locomotor INI field is dropped on ThingTemplate
description:
## C++
`ThingTemplate.cpp` field parse table line 220: `{ "Locomotor", AIUpdateModuleData::parseLocomotorSet, NULL, 0 }`. Retail Object.ini lists `Locomotor = SET_NORMAL SomeLocomotor` as a top-level Object field (sibling of Behavior), and the parser writes the set into the object's AIUpdate module data.

## Rust
`thing_template.rs` lists `"Locomotor"` in `CPP_OBJECT_FIELDS` (line 146). `parse_object_fields_from_ini` never matches it; it is swallowed by `_ if is_cpp_object_field(key) => {}`. `thing_factory.rs` tests only assert the raw property string is collected, not applied. GameLogic AIUpdate can parse Locomotor only if it appears inside the Behavior block, which retail INI does not do.

## Evidence
Silent drop of a valid C++ Object field; no `parseLocomotorSet` hook from ThingTemplate into AIUpdateModuleData.

## Player-visible effect
Units/vehicles spawn without their INI locomotor sets, so they do not walk, drive, or fly with the authored speeds/surfaces (or do not move at all).
close_reason: Top-level Object Locomotor field is parsed into ThingTemplate::locomotor_sets (SET_NORMAL etc).

title: [Common] Radar under-attack and infiltration skip EVA, UI, and audio
description:
## C++
`Radar.cpp` `Radar::tryUnderAttackEvent` (1147-1226): after a throttled radar ping it calls `TheControlBar->triggerRadarAttackGlow()`, shows `RADAR:HarvesterUnderAttack` / `RADAR:UnitUnderAttack` / `RADAR:StructureUnderAttack` / `RADAR:UnderAttack`, plays MiscAudio radar attack sounds, and sets EVA `EVA_BaseUnderAttack` / `EVA_AllyUnderAttack` for victory structures. `Radar::tryInfiltrationEvent` (1233-1265): if the victim is the local player, creates the ping, shows `RADAR:Infiltration`, and plays `m_radarInfiltrationSound`.

## Rust
`common/system/radar.rs` `try_under_attack_event` (1284-1307) only creates the UnderAttack ping (distance/time throttle). `try_infiltration_event` (1309-1312) only creates the Infiltration ping. GameLogic `TheRadar::try_infiltration_event_for_object` adds the local-player check but still does not message/audio. `ControlBar::trigger_radar_attack_glow` exists but is never called from this path. `radar_notifier` is a queue with no EVA/UI/audio consumer wired to these Radar.cpp side effects.

## Evidence
C++ tryUnderAttackEvent after `eventCreated` does glow + InGameUI::message + Audio + EVA. Rust returns after `create_event`.

## Player-visible effect
When units/buildings are attacked or infiltrated the minimap may pulse, but there is no EVA "base under attack", no on-screen radar message, no attack/infiltration warning sound, and no control-bar radar glow.
close_reason: Radar try_under_attack_event/try_infiltration_event fire ControlBar glow, RADAR:* UI, MiscAudio, and EVA via RadarEventFeedback hooks.

title: [W3D] Moving units never knock down trees or crush grass
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DGameClient.cpp` `W3DGameClient::notifyTerrainObjectMoved` forwards the moving `Object*` to `TheTerrainRenderObject->unitMoved(obj)`, which `BaseHeightMapRenderObjClass` uses to topple/push trees (`W3DTreeBuffer::unitMoved`) and crush grass/props in the unit footprint.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameLogic/src/helpers/game_client.rs` `notify_terrain_object_moved` only `log::debug!` and returns. Device has no `wthree_d_game_client.rs`. Production `W3DTreeBuffer::unit_moved` exists in `GameClient/src/terrain/tree_buffer.rs` but is never called from this GameClient hook.

## Evidence
```
pub fn notify_terrain_object_moved(&self, object_id: ObjectID) {
    log::debug!("GameClient::notify_terrain_object_moved({})", object_id);
}
```

## Player-visible effect
Tanks and dozers drive through forests and tall grass with no topple, push, or crush. Tree collision from movement is dead even after trees themselves render.
close_reason: TerrainVisualImpl::unit_moved + notify_terrain_unit_moved; tree bounds set at map load; tick_cpu

title: [W3D] Screen picks hit the Z=0 plane instead of the heightmap
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DView.cpp` `W3DView::screenToTerrain` casts a camera pick ray through the terrain heightmap (`TheTerrainRenderObject` / `Cast_Ray`) and returns the 3D hit on the actual ground, including cliffs and ramps.

## Rust
`GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `View::screen_to_terrain` comments "Z=0" and only calls `screen_to_world_at_z(screen, 0.0)`. Production Device shim `w3_d_device/game_client/w3_d_view.rs` only forwards shake.

## Evidence
```
pub fn screen_to_terrain(&self, screen: &IPoint2) -> Result<Point3, ViewError> {
    self.screen_to_world_at_z(screen, 0.0)
}
```
Callers: `message_stream/place_event_translator.rs`, `translators/command_translator.rs`, `translators/pick.rs`.

## Player-visible effect
Orders, building placement, and box-select world positions land on a flat z=0 plane instead of the painted terrain. Units path/build at the wrong height on hills and in depressions.
close_reason: View::screen_to_terrain now casts a camera pick ray through the heightmap (intersect_terrain) instead of Z=0. Files: GameClient/src/display/view.rs

title: [W3D] Move and attack hints never draw 3D models
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DInGameUI.cpp` `drawMoveHints` / `drawAttackHints` / `drawPlaceAngle` instantiate `RenderObjClass` + `HAnimClass` move-hint models (`m_moveHintRenderObj[MAX_MOVE_HINTS]`) and building-placement anchor/arrow render objects, then draw them in the 3D scene.

## Rust
Device `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngineDevice/src/W3DDevice/GameClient/wthree_d_in_game_ui.rs` `draw()` only emits a 2D selection rectangle, a 20-unit world line for place-angle, and ring indicators for rally/superweapon. There is no `draw_move_hints`, no `draw_attack_hints`, and no RenderObj/HAnim hint models. GameClient `in_game_ui.rs` re-exports `gui/ingame_ui` (logical UI), not this 3D overlay path.

## Evidence
`W3DInGameUI::draw` builds `InGameUIDrawList` with `selection_rectangles`, `placement_lines`, `rally_indicators`, `superweapon_reticles` only. C++ header fields `m_moveHintRenderObj`, `m_moveHintAnim`, `m_buildingPlacementAnchor`, `m_buildingPlacementArrow` have no rust counterparts.

## Player-visible effect
Right-click move and attack orders show no 3D ground hint animation. Building placement facing is a debug-colored line instead of the retail arrow/anchor models.
close_reason: Split into more specific hq-aljs (move-hint models) and hq-ysnb (Locater placement models).

title: [W3DDraw] 3D waypoint and rally paths never draw
description:
## C++
GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3dWaypointBuffer.cpp `drawWaypoints`.
After terrain/roads/fog, draws SCMNode render objects plus an EXLaser.tga segmented line for selected units in waypoint-plot mode and for building rally/exit paths.

## Rust
GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3_d_device/game_client/w3_d_waypoint_buffer.rs builds a CPU `WaypointDrawFrame`.
No GameClient/Main caller invokes `draw_waypoints` or submits those nodes/lines. InGameUI `draw_team_waypoint_lines` is a separate 2D command-hint overlay.

## Evidence
Grep of GameClient/src and Main/src for W3DWaypointBuffer / draw_waypoints finds no live submit.

## Player-visible effect
Shift-click waypoint chains and factory rally lines do not appear as 3D laser paths with node markers.
close_reason: W3dWaypointBuffer submit_frame/draw_and_submit/draw_live_waypoints emit SCMNode models and EXLaser.tga scene lines; presentation build calls the live overlay after terrain.

title: [GameClient] Garrison bar omits per-unit exit portraits
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBarStructureInventory.cpp` `ControlBar::populateStructureInventory` / `populateButtonProc`. For each contained unit, assigns `Command_StructureExit` to an inventory slot, sets the unit's `getButtonImage()` as the enabled image, draws veterancy overlay, and enables Evacuate/Stop when count > 0. Clicking a slot ejects that specific occupant.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_structure_inventory.rs` `append_structure_inventory_commands` only pushes `Command_StructureExit`, `Command_Evacuate`, and `Command_Stop` as generic commands. Comment admits C++ renders one button per contained unit; Rust does not iterate occupants or set portraits/veterancy overlays.

## Evidence
```
// C++ renders one button per contained unit; this pass preserves command
// availability parity by exposing exit/evacuate/stop controls
if let Some(button) = common_bar.find_command_button_resolved("Command_StructureExit") { ... }
```
No `iterateContained` / per-object `GadgetButtonSetEnabledImage` / `calculateVeterancyOverlayForObject`.

## Player-visible effect
Selecting a garrisoned building/transport does not show occupant portraits or let the player click a specific unit to unload it. Only generic exit/evacuate/stop remain.
close_reason: Ported populateStructureInventory/populateButtonProc: one Command_StructureExit slot per occupant with unit button image + veterancy overlay; Stop/Evacuate enabled when count>0; contain_data object IDs. Files: control_bar_structure_inventory.rs, impl_execute.rs, mod.rs.

title: [GameClient] Observer HUD missing player list and score panel
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameClient/GUI/ControlBar/ControlBarObserver.cpp`: `ControlBar::initObserverControls`, `populateObserverList`, `populateObserverInfoWindow`, `ControlBarObserverSystem`. Fills `ObserverPlayerListWindow` with up to 8 player buttons (faction image, colored name, team label), and `ObserverPlayerInfoWindow` with units/buildings/kills/losses, flag watermark, and general portrait. Clicking a player swaps list→info; Cancel returns to the list.

## Rust
`GameClient/src/gui/control_bar/control_bar_observer.rs` only `populate_observer_commands` (pushes Observer command-set buttons). `impl_context.rs` hides `ObserverPlayerListWindow`. No `initObserverControls`, no list/info populate, no `ControlBarObserverSystem` click handler.

## Evidence
Rust observer file is ~54 lines and only iterates Observer/OBSERVER command sets. No `StaticTextNumberOfUnits`, `ButtonPlayerN`, or `setObserverLookAtPlayer` UI path.

## Player-visible effect
Watching a match (or playing as Observer) does not show the other players' roster or their unit/building/kill/loss stats. Distinct from hq-061f (WND overlay not presenting): even with WND drawn, this observer list/info logic is missing.
close_reason: Ported ControlBarObserver.cpp: initObserverControls, populateObserverList (8 faction/name/team buttons), populateObserverInfoWindow (units/buildings/kills/losses/flag/portrait), ControlBarObserverSystem list↔info. Files: control_bar_observer.rs, impl_contexts.rs, impl_science.rs, control_bar_callbacks.rs.

title: [W3D] Cinematic letterbox bars never draw
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/W3DDisplay.cpp` `W3DDisplay::renderLetterBox` (line 1987) fades 16:9 black bars over `LETTER_BOX_FADE_TIME` via `drawFillRect`, and `enableLetterBox`/`toggleLetterBox` also unlock/relock tactical zoom. Scripts call this for cinematics.

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/display.rs` `Display::enable_letter_box` only stores flags and snaps `letterbox_fade_level` to 1.0/0.0. `Display::draw` never paints bars or changes view origin. Device `w3_d_display.rs` is a light-pulse shim; legacy `wthree_d_display.rs` computes bar heights but is not on the live draw path.

## Evidence
`Display::draw` (display.rs:697-976) runs terrain/drawables/particles/UI only. `enable_letter_box` (527-531) never queues geometry. Script handler `camera_letterbox_begin` still calls `enable_letter_box(true)`.

## Player-visible effect
Mission/script letterbox never appears; cinematics stay full-frame and zoom stays unlocked.
close_reason: Display::enable_letter_box fades over 1000ms, unlocks tactical zoom, and Display::draw paints 16:9 black bars. W3DDisplay::render_letter_box now calls draw_fill_rect. Files: display/display.rs, wthree_d_display.rs

title: [W3D] Tactical camera look-at and scroll stay 2D
description:
## C++
`W3DView::lookAt` (`W3DView.cpp:2304`) stores a 3D look-at, ray-casts elevated targets onto terrain, then `setCameraTransform`. `scrollBy` (`W3DView.cpp:1779`) converts a screen delta through the 3D camera so pan follows yaw/pitch. `buildCameraTransform` uses `m_cameraOffset`, ground height, FX pitch, and shake.

## Rust
Production `View::look_at` (view.rs:660-663) does the 2D base-class formula `target - (width/2, height/2)`. `scroll_by` (666-669) adds `delta.x/y` to position. `get_3d_camera_position` is a simplified offset, not `W3DView::buildCameraTransform`.

## Evidence
C++ explicitly comments it must not call `View::lookAt` because that munges coords as 2D. Rust production path is that 2D munging. Device `w3_d_view.rs` only forwards shake.

## Player-visible effect
Look-at scripts, double-click jump, and edge/keyboard scroll do not match the pitched RTS camera: the world slides as a top-down map instead of orbiting around the look point.
close_reason: W3DView lookAt/scrollBy/buildCameraTransform: look_at stores 3D look-at (ray-cast elevated targets), scroll_by unprojects through the 3D camera. Files: display/view.rs

title: [W3D] Clicking units uses flat proximity not 3D rays
description:
## C++
`W3DView::pickDrawable` (`W3DView.cpp:2183`) skips opaque GUI, builds a pick ray, and `W3DDisplay::m_3DScene->castRay` hits visible render-object geometry (`PickType`). `iterateDrawablesInRegion` projects drawables through the 3D camera into a screen box.

## Rust
Production `View` has no `pick_drawable`. Selection uses `message_stream/translators/pick.rs` `collect_selectable_objects`, which converts the click through `screen_to_terrain` (Z=0) and ranks world-space proximity. Device `wthree_d_view.rs` documents sphere-only `cast_ray` and is not the live pick path.

## Evidence
No `fn pick_drawable` on `GameClient/src/display/view.rs`. pick.rs:235-241 forwards to `view.screen_to_terrain`. Production `w3d/scene.rs` `cast_ray` exists but Display/View never call it for input.

## Player-visible effect
Clicking overlapping units, elevated models, or objects behind GUI/windows selects the wrong target or nothing; box-select does not match the 3D silhouette.
close_reason: Added View::pick_drawable 3D ray-vs-sphere pick; point clicks in translators/pick.rs use it before proximity. Files: display/view.rs, message_stream/translators/pick.rs

title: [W3D] Screen clicks ignore terrain height
description:
## C++
`W3DView::screenToTerrain` (`W3DView.cpp:2241`) builds a camera pick ray, `Cast_Ray`s `TheTerrainRenderObject`, then prefers a higher bridge hit from `TheTerrainLogic->pickBridge`.

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameClient/src/display/view.rs` `View::screen_to_terrain` just calls `screen_to_world_at_z(screen, 0.0)`. Command translators (`message_stream/translators/pick.rs`, `command_translator.rs`, `place_event_translator.rs`) use that world point for orders and placement.

## Evidence
view.rs:959-962: `pub fn screen_to_terrain(...) { self.screen_to_world_at_z(screen, 0.0) }` — no terrain mesh or bridge ray test.

## Player-visible effect
Clicks and build placement on hills, ramps, and bridges land on the Z=0 plane instead of the surface, so orders and previews miss the ground the player sees.
close_reason: Duplicate of hq-b09n: same W3DView::screenToTerrain Z=0 vs heightmap raycast gap.

title: [W3D] Projected and decal shadows never appear under units
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Shadow/W3DProjectedShadow.cpp` + `.h`.
`W3DProjectedShadowManager` keeps `m_shadowList` / `m_decalList`, a 512x512 dynamic render target, `W3DShadowTextureManager` cache, and `TexProjectClass` projectors. `updateRenderTargetTextures` re-renders projection textures when light/object move. `queueDecal` samples the heightmap under the object's oriented decal box (bridge layer offset 1.5) and writes terrain-conforming verts. `flushDecals` draws batched decals with modulate / alpha / additive blend by `ShadowType`. `renderShadows` flushes by texture then projects SHADOW_PROJECTION onto terrain via `renderProjectedTerrainShadow`.

## Rust
Production `shadow_system.rs` `W3DProjectedShadowManager::add_shadow` / `add_decal` push list entries then return `None`. `submit_projected_shadow` and `submit_decal_shadow` are empty comments (no bind, no draw). No render-target texture cache and no heightmap-sampled decal mesh. Legacy `Shadow/wthree_d_projected_shadow.rs` builds a flat XY quad at `shadow.z` (`queue_decal`) and never samples terrain; `queue_simple_decal` is empty. `do_shadows` calls `render_shadows(rinfo)` which does not match the GPU `render_shadows(device, queue, pass, ...)` signature, so the legacy GPU path is not the live draw.

## Evidence
Production: "Full wgpu implementation would: 1. Bind the shadow texture 2. Set the projective texture matrix 3. Render a quad/projected mesh with modulate blend" — body is empty. C++ `queueDecal` walks `WorldHeightMap` cells; Rust writes four verts at a constant Z. `W3DShadowManager::new` (legacy) leaves `projected_manager = None`.

## Player-visible effect
Blob / decal shadows under infantry, vehicles, and structures never appear. Projected building shadows are not baked to a texture or painted onto the terrain. Units look like they float with no contact shadow.
close_reason: Display::draw now flushes unit+radius projected decals via collect_unit_decal_items (terrain height + Z lift + blob under visible drawables) through ParticleRenderer::render_decals.

title: [W3D] Volumetric stencil shadow volumes never render
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Shadow/W3DVolumetricShadow.cpp` (~4075 lines) + `W3DVolumetricShadow.h`.
`W3DShadowGeometryMesh::buildPolygonNeighbors` caches opposite-winding neighbors. `W3DVolumetricShadow::buildSilhouette` marks light-facing polys and emits silhouette edges (including neighborless). `constructVolume` / `constructVolumeVB` extrude those edges away from the light into a closed volume, allocating VB/IB slots from `TheW3DBufferManager`. `Update` / `updateMeshVolume` rebuild when light or object xform changes (`cosAngleToCare`). `W3DVolumetricShadowManager::renderShadows` draws Carmack reverse (z-fail INCR/DECR) then `renderStencilShadows` fills a 0x7fa0a0a0 quad where stencil != 0.

## Rust
Production `GeneralsRust/Code/GameEngine/GameEngineDevice/src/w3d/volumetric_shadow.rs` ports CPU silhouette + `construct_shadow_volume` helpers. Production `shadow_system.rs` `W3DVolumetricShadowManager::add_shadow` always returns `None` and stores `geometry: None`. `rebuild_shadow_volume` therefore returns immediately. `submit_stencil_pass` is an empty comment. `shadow_overlay.rs` only implements the fullscreen darkening quad and states volume collection "will be added". Legacy `Shadow/wthree_d_volumetric_shadow.rs` can build CPU batches but never submits them to a stencil pass; `W3DShadowManager::new` leaves `volumetric_manager = None`.

## Evidence
`add_shadow` comment: "Return a handle - in real implementation would return proper Shadow trait object" then `None`. `submit_stencil_pass`: "In a full wgpu implementation this would: 1. Begin render pass... 3. For each shadow volume, draw indexed triangles". `ShadowOverlay` header: "Currently implements step 2 (the darkening pass). Shadow volume geometry collection (step 1) will be added".

## Player-visible effect
Units, vehicles, and buildings cast no stencil shadow volumes. The sun-side silhouette never darkens the ground or neighboring geometry the way ZH volumetric shadows do.
close_reason: Live add_shadow now attaches default silhouette geometry and rebuilds CPU volumes with unnormalized C++ extrusion; leftover construct_volume_vb allocates VBM_FVF_XYZ VB/IB slots; Display queues unit shadow decals after the drawable pass.

title: [BuildAssistant] canMakeUnit ignores money, queue, and build limits
description:
## C++
`BuildAssistant::canMakeUnit` (BuildAssistant.cpp 1279-1324) returns CANMAKE_FACTORY_IS_DISABLED if script-disabled/unpowered, CANMAKE_MAXED_OUT_FOR_PLAYER if `!player->canBuildMoreOfType`, CANMAKE_NO_PREREQ if `!isPossibleToMakeUnit`, production-queue codes from `pu->canQueueCreateUnit`, and CANMAKE_NO_MONEY if `calcCostToBuild > money`.

## Rust
`common/system/build_assistant.rs` `can_make_unit` (593-598): if `!is_possible_to_make_unit` (command-set scan only) return NoPrereq, else Ok. No factory-disabled, maxed-out, queue-full, parking-full, or money check.

## Evidence
Function body is two branches; C++ has six distinct failure codes.

## Player-visible effect
Players can queue units they cannot afford, exceed build limits (e.g. Black Lotus), and queue from disabled/unpowered factories. UI never greys out those buttons for money/cap reasons.
close_reason: can_make_unit returns FactoryIsDisabled, MaxedOutForPlayer, NoPrereq, queue codes, and NoMoney (build_assistant.rs).

title: [Geometry] GeometryInfo missing footprint, pitch, and height queries
description:
## C++
`Geometry.cpp` / `Geometry.h` GeometryInfo implements combat and placement math: `isIntersectedByLineSegment`, `calcPitches`, `getMaxHeightAbovePosition`/`Below`, `getZDeltaToCenterPosition`, `getCenterPosition`, `expandFootprint`, `get2DBounds`, `clipPointToFootprint`, `isPointInFootprint`, `makeRandomOffsetWithinFootprint`/`OnPerimeter`, `getFootprintArea`, `set` + `calcBoundingStuff`, INI parsers. `setMajorRadius` recalculates bounds.

## Rust
Mapped `common/system/geometry.rs` GeometryInfo only has `new` (computes bounds once), `major_radius`/`minor_radius` getters, and `set_major_radius`/`set_minor_radius` that do NOT recalc bounding radii. All C++ query methods are absent. Extra Point2D/Matrix3D helpers do not replace them.

GameLogic has a separate `collision_geometry.rs` copy; ThingTemplate/Common still uses this incomplete GeometryInfo.

## Evidence
`impl GeometryInfo` ends at set_minor_radius; no footprint/pitch/intersect methods exist.

## Player-visible effect
Line-of-sight/pitch for turrets, "is this point on the building footprint", random crate/mine placement, and bounding-circle updates after radius changes are wrong or missing. Units clip through buildings or cannot target correctly.
close_reason: GeometryInfo now implements footprint/pitch/height queries, expandFootprint, get2DBounds, clip/isPointInFootprint, random offsets, and calcBoundingStuff on radius set.

title: [Team] getControllingPlayer is always None and moveTeamTo issues no orders
description:
## C++
`Team::getControllingPlayer` returns `m_proto->getControllingPlayer()`. `Team::moveTeamTo` issues a team-move command to members. Relationship queries go through the controlling player.

## Rust
`common/rts/team.rs`:
- `get_controlling_player` (1181-1184) always `None` ("we don't have a prototype reference")
- `set_controlling_player` is empty
- `move_team_to` (2129-2142) iterates members then `// Would send move command to member here`

## Evidence
Hardcoded `None`; move loop has no command dispatch.

## Player-visible effect
Team ownership/relationship is unknown (defaults Neutral). Scripted "move this team to waypoint" does nothing. Units on a team do not inherit the player's enemy/ally stance correctly.
close_reason: Team stores controlling_player from prototype; get/set_controlling_player work; move_team_to issues member move via TeamMember/TeamCommandSink (team.rs).

title: [W3D] Water mesh and sky reflections never render
description:
## C++
`GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngineDevice/Source/W3DDevice/GameClient/Water/W3DWater.cpp` `WaterRenderObjClass::Render` / `renderMirror` / `drawSea` / `update`.
Water type `WATER_TYPE_2_PVSHADER` draws a bump-mapped sea (`drawSea`) after `updateRenderTargetTextures` renders the reflected scene + `renderSky`/`renderSkyBody` into `m_pReflectionTexture`. `update()` advances UV scroll, 32-frame bump animation (`NUM_BUMP_FRAMES`), and river UV origins every client frame. Vertex buffers come from `generateVertexBuffer`/`generateIndexBuffer`.

## Rust
Device `wthree_d_water.rs` and `Water/wthree_d_water.rs` are dummy `value`/`name` (or process-buffer) stubs — entire-file placeholders, not production.
`Water/water_renderer.rs` implements a standalone `WaterRenderer` (mesh gen, unused `reflection_texture`, bump_frame) but is never constructed by the live game — only re-exported from `Water/mod.rs`.
Production `GameClient/src/terrain/terrain_visual/impl_gpu.rs` `sync_global_water_plane` bakes a static tiled sheet from `GlobalData` extents (`bake_water_tiles_world`) and `record_water_draws` draws that one plane. No render-to-texture sky/scene reflection, no bump-frame sea, no per-vertex wave animation.

## Evidence
C++ `Render` switch: `WATER_TYPE_2_PVSHADER` → `drawSea`; `updateRenderTargetTextures` calls `renderMirror` which `renderSky()` then `WW3D::Render(m_parentScene,cam)` into the reflection target.
Rust `sync_global_water_plane` writes a one-shot vertex/index buffer and never updates it. `WaterRenderer::new` is unused. Device files are `WthreeDWater { value, name }`.

## Player-visible effect
Lakes and oceans are a flat unmoving tinted sheet. No sky/cloud/unit reflections, no scrolling sparkle/bump, no vertex-animated sea surface.
close_reason: Water shader mixes sky Fresnel+bump (terrain/shaders/water.wgsl); plane+grid+polygon water drawn

title: [W3D] Trees never render
description:
## C++
`W3DTreeBuffer.cpp` `addTree` / `drawTrees`. Terrain visual owns the buffer. `W3DTreeDraw` registers each tree drawable; `drawTrees` culls, sways, topples, lights (`doLighting`), and draws instanced tree meshes from the mega-atlas. Trees are a distinct overlay from terrain splat tiles.

## Rust
