title: Preserve C++ known-zero Drawable barrel-count semantics
description: Discovered during hq-pi6 v4 snapshot/barrel review. C++ Weapon::privateFireWeapon queries Drawable::getBarrelCount immediately before each shot; when count is zero, m_curBarrel >= 0 always resets m_curBarrel=0 and m_numShotsForCurBarrel=ShotsPerBarrel before that shot (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Weapon.cpp:2577-2581), then normal post-shot decrement occurs. W3DModelDraw returns zero for an empty/missing valid barrel vector (W3DModelDraw.cpp:3665-3669), and Drawable can allow another module to handle FireFX (Drawable.cpp:4216-4238). Active Main has an exact cached known-zero per-slot answer after a successful topology lookup (Option array in assets/manager.rs), but world_combat/weapon_barrel_topology.rs maps it to one via unwrap_or(1), and Object::set_weapon_barrel_count_for_slot clamps zero to one. This makes only the emitted barrel index happen to stay 0; it fails to reset ShotsPerBarrel cadence before each zero-topology shot, so a later model-condition state with nonzero barrels resumes a divergent cursor/cadence and v4 saved state is wrong. Represent known zero distinctly from unavailable cache/no topology, retain it in the slot cursor, and apply exact C++ pre-fire reset while it is active. Do not use max(1) as an equivalence. Acceptance: an authored ShotsPerBarrel=3 slot fires twice under validated zero topology and each post-shot state has cursor 0/shots_left 2; after transition to a valid two-barrel topology, subsequent fire follows the C++ prefire and postfire sequence; snapshot/restore while zero topology preserves that state.

WeaponBarrelState preserves zero and mirrors the C++ prefire guard by resetting cursor and ShotsPerBarrel cadence before every zero-topology shot. Added focused regression for ShotsPerBarrel=3, two zero-topology shots, then transition to two barrels. title: Persist transactional shroud/FOW state across staged save restore
description: Discovered from hq-pi6 v4 snapshot review. C++ persists fog-of-war in the logic snapshot: PartitionCell::xfer writes m_shroudLevel[MAX_PLAYER_COUNT] (GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/PartitionManager.cpp:1485-1500), and PartitionManager::xfer serializes every cell plus m_pendingUndoShroudReveals and refreshes local shroud on load (lines 4558-4645). Active Main WorldSnapshot has no shroud payload. Worse, host staged load mutates process-global shroud before commit: CnCGameEngine::stage_saved_world_for_restore in Main/src/cnc_game_engine/host_authority.rs creates staged GameLogic then calls staged.load_map; GameLogic::load_map_with_progress initializes get_shroud_manager().lock().init_shroud_grid(world_width, world_height) (Main/src/game_logic/world_save.rs:2120-2122) and load-map completion invokes update_main_crate_vision, revealing map-spawned staging objects. SnapshotBuilder::restore_from_snapshot replaces staged objects but never restores the singleton; host_replace_game_logic only swaps GameLogic and clears renderer state. Successful loads therefore leak staging-map visibility into the saved world; any future stage failure after map load can also leave the still-active old GameLogic paired with staged global FOW. Implement an explicit shroud snapshot of persistent per-cell player levels and pending undo reveals, and a transaction boundary: staging must not mutate the live singleton, or the singleton must be fully snapshotted/restored on failure and atomically install the loaded shroud only with successful host world replacement. Do not rebuild only from restored object vision: that loses explored/fog and queued temporary reveals, unlike C++. Map exact APIs: GameLogic::load_map_with_progress; GameLogic::update_main_crate_vision in Main/src/game_logic/world_objects/spawn_templates.rs; gamelogic::system::shroud_manager::{get_shroud_manager, ShroudManager::init_shroud_grid, clear_all, do_shroud_reveal, queue_undo_shroud_reveal}; host_authority::{stage_saved_world_for_restore, host_replace_game_logic}. Acceptance: (1) save/load preserves hidden/explored/visible per-cell FOW and pending reveal expiry, (2) successful stage cannot retain map-start staging reveals, (3) injected staged-load failure leaves active GameLogic and global shroud unchanged, (4) integration test covers a same-map load with differing save-time FOW.
notes:
Static API map and minimal boundary: ShroudManager owns private Option<ShroudGrid> with width, height, cell_size, and Vec<PartitionCell>. Each PartitionCell owns CellShroudLevel[MAX_PLAYER_COUNT], whose full state is current_shroud plus active_shroud_level. SightingInfo is where_pos, how_far, for_whom, expiration_frame in pending_undo_shroud_reveals. Existing public snapshot_grid_for_player returns only derived Hidden/Explored/Visible bytes and is insufficient: C++ ShroudLevel Xfers both counters in Display.h lines 18-22, so overlapping lookers or active shrouders would be lost. Add a narrow GameLogic-side ShroudSnapshot and ShroudManager snapshot_state/replace_state that preserve grid dimensions, full per-cell levels, undo queue, and pre-grid full/permanent reveal queues if retained; visible/explored object sets are caches and should rebuild after install. Smallest safe host transaction without broad singleton removal: capture old singleton before stage_saved_world_for_restore, use an RAII rollback guard across map load plus snapshot restore, return staged ShroudSnapshot with staged GameLogic, restore old singleton before returning, then extend host_replace_game_logic or adjacent single host boundary to install staged logic and shroud together. This prevents success and error leaks. Snapshot schema needs an explicit new world tail/version plus exact bincode predecessor/direct-Xfer gate; do not encode a presentation-only grid.
Source audit follow-up: staged restore mutates more process-global gameplay state than ShroudManager. stage_saved_world_for_restore calls staged.load_map; fast/legacy map sync resets and loads gamelogic terrain singleton in Main/src/game_logic/world_save.rs around 1280-1283 and 1432-1435, replaces ThePlayerList around 1533-1535, and resets/rebuilds get_team_factory around 1554-1605. A later snapshot error therefore leaves active GameLogic paired with staged terrain/player/team globals; successful restore also retains map-default globals unless snapshot/commit owns them. Treat these singleton mutations as part of the same stage transaction: either isolate map loading from active singleton state or capture/restore all affected global state on failure and atomically commit the staged set after snapshot success. NamedObjectTracker is additionally mutated only for Shell map objects, so it is lower-priority for offline mission/skirmish but should be audited with the same boundary.
2026-08-13 transaction checkpoint: implemented the raw staged restore boundary without changing snapshot v4.  moves exact gameplay singleton contents out while the candidate map/snapshot restores; Main  now transactionally takes/restores/discards the complete 36-queue TLS closure reachable from staged map load + snapshot restore, including model_mesh/kind_of, conditional object/map-upgrade/snapshot queues, and pending+LAST_DRAIN for move/attack. Forced post-restore failure regression preserves terrain/player/team/sides/shroud/script/named/area/AI/integration globals plus all queue state. Validation: shared  green; focused  green (1 passed, 8019 filtered). Snapshot FOW persistence/schema remains a separate unfinished hq-zz2 acceptance item; no schema version bump claimed.

title: [Audio] Listener orientation stored but never applied so camera yaw does not pan
description:
## C++
`MilesAudioManager::setDeviceListenerPosition` (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:2627-2636`) applies both `AIL_set_3D_orientation(m_listener, m_listenerOrientation.x/y/z, 0, 0, -1)` and `AIL_set_3D_position`. `AudioManager::update` (`GameAudio.cpp:281+`) writes listener pos + camera-forward orientation from `TheTacticalView`. Miles then pans positional samples left/right as the camera yaws.

## Rust
Live `set_listener_position` (`game_audio.rs:1277-1287`) stores `listener_orientation` but the playback hook only receives position (`hook.set_listener_position(new_listener_pos)`). `RodioPlaybackHook` (`:2755-2765` / `:2582-2598`) uses listener pos for distance gain only — no pan / no orientation.

## Evidence
MilesAudioManager.cpp:2629-2630 vs game_audio.rs:1287 (orientation never forwarded). Closed hq-mcvi7 was listener **position** from the live camera; this is orientation / stereo pan.

## Player-visible
Rotating the camera never moves a nearby unit or explosion between the left and right speakers. Everything stays centered (or only fades by distance). Retail pans with yaw.
close_reason: set_listener_position forwards orientation; Rodio SpatialSink applies stereo_pan from camera yaw

title: [Audio] stopAudio only pauses so music-stop leaves zombie sinks
description:
## C++
`MilesAudioManager::stopAudio` (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:471-524`) is terminal: drop EOS callbacks, `AIL_stop_sample` / `AIL_stop_3D_sample` (2D/3D) or `AIL_pause_stream` (music/speech), then `m_status = PS_Stopped`. Next `processPlayingList` / `processStoppedList` (`:2459-2471`) releases the channel and event. Music-stop hotkey (`DEMO_TOGGLE_MUSIC`) uses this so the track is gone, not parked.

## Rust
Live `AudioManager::stop_audio` (`game_audio.rs:1767-1779`) only `hook.pause(handle)`. Events stay in `active_audio_events`. Rodio `is_playing` is `!sink.empty()`, so a paused sink never drains and never releases. Live caller: `GameClient/.../dispatch.rs:906-908` music-stop hotkey.

## Evidence
MilesAudioManager.cpp:487-520 vs game_audio.rs:1774-1778. Closed hq-d10n is pauseAudio discarding pending Play requests — different function.

## Player-visible
Music-stop (and any other `stop_audio`) leaves the track paused and still occupying the playing list / Limit counts. Resume can bring the old track back; C++ has already released it. Extra same-name Limits then fail because the zombie still counts.
close_reason: stop_audio release_playing_handle instead of pause so music-stop does not leave zombie sinks

title: [Audio] has3DSensitiveStreamsPlaying treats positional SFX as streams so zoom never retunes
description:
## C++
`AudioManager::set3DVolumeAdjustment` (`GameAudio.cpp:741-753`) writes `m_sound3DVolume` then sets `m_volumeHasChanged` only when `!has3DSensitiveStreamsPlaying()`. Miles override (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:2381-2404`) walks **streams**: empty → FALSE; any non-`AT_Music` stream (speech) or music whose name does not start with `Game_` → TRUE. Ordinary positional 3D samples are not streams, so zoom still flags volume-changed during combat. Next `processPlayingList` reapplies zoom to playing 3D sounds.

## Rust
Live `set_3d_volume_adjustment` (`game_audio.rs:1265-1274`) uses the same gate, but `has_3d_sensitive_streams_playing` (`:2134-2152`) returns TRUE if **any positional 3D event** is playing. Streams are never positional, so the C++ stream test is never run. During a match there is almost always a positional SFX, so `volume_has_changed` stays false.

## Evidence
MilesAudioManager.cpp:2381-2404 (stream + `Game_` prefix) vs game_audio.rs:2138-2146 (`is_positional_audio`). Closed hq-k20a was flag propagation; this is the predicate inversion that prevents the flag from being set.

## Player-visible
Zooming the camera during play does not retune already-playing 3D unit/weapon/ambient volume. Sounds stay at the zoom they started with until they end. Retail updates them every zoom change except while a speech/non-`Game_` stream is up.
close_reason: has_3d_sensitive_streams_playing walks music/speech streams (Game_ music excluded) not positional SFX so zoom retunes 3D volume

title: [FXList] FXListAtBonePos uses pristine logical bones not current client bones
description:
## C++
`FXListAtBonePosFXNugget::doFXObj` (`FXList.cpp:678-691`) calls `doFxAtBones(primary, 0)` then `doFxAtBones(primary, 1)`.

`doFxAtBones` (`FXList.cpp:711-728`):
- `Drawable::getCurrentClientBonePositions(m_boneName, start, …, MAX_BONE_POINTS=40)` — **current animated** client bones
- `W3DModelDraw::getCurrentBonePositions` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:3545-3603`): `start==0` queries only the unadorned name; `start>=1` walks `Name01`… until the first missing bone (`Get_Bone_Index==0` breaks)
- `obj->convertBonePosToWorldPos` then `FXList::doFXPos(m_fx, &p, &m, 0, NULL, 0)`
- `m_orientToBone` is parsed (default **true**) but **never read** — always the converted bone world matrix

## Rust
Live `FXListAtBonePosFXNugget::do_fx_obj` (`fx_list.rs:1591-1601`) walks `bone_query_names()`: unadorned + `Name01`…`Name40` **unconditionally** (does not stop at first miss).

Each name uses `Object::get_single_logical_bone_position` (`object_triggers.rs:85-115`) → `get_pristine_bone_positions` / `get_pristine_bone_transforms` (bind pose, start=0, max=1), then `convert_bone_pos_to_world_pos`.

`#[derive(Default)]` sets `orient_to_bone: false`. When false, `execute_fx_at_bone` (`fx_list.rs:1569-1574`) uses the **object** transform instead of the bone matrix. C++ always uses the bone world matrix.

Leftover `fxlist_integration.rs` already has `FXBoneQuery::current_client_bone_positions` with start 0 then 1 (C++-shaped), but the live GameClient runner never uses it.

## Evidence
- C++ `FXList.cpp:678-728`, `W3DModelDraw.cpp:3581-3592`
- Rust `fx_list.rs:1540-1601`, `object_triggers.rs:97-107`
- Leftover adapter unused: `fxlist_integration.rs:73-80`, `:437-454`
- Distinct from closed `hq-azxp` (ricochet matrix) and `hq-ryug9` (weapon fire victimPos)

## Player-visible
Nested FXListAtBonePos effects (multi-barrel muzzle, exhaust, bone-attached sparks) spawn at bind-pose logical bones, not the animated turret/recoil/walk pose. Numbered bones after a gap still fire. When INI omits `OrientToBone` (C++ default true / unused), nested FX inherit the hull orientation instead of the bone.
close_reason: Live FXListAtBonePos do_fx_obj now doFxAtBones(start=0) then start=1 using Drawable::get_bone_local_transform (current client bones), stop at first miss, always bone world matrix. Default OrientToBone=true unused like C++. Leftover fxlist_integration already had FXBoneQuery start 0 then 1.

title: [FXList] SoundFXNugget doFXObj never sets controlling player index
description:
## C++
`SoundFXNugget::doFXObj` (`FXList.cpp:90-99`) builds `AudioEventRTS(m_soundName)` then, when primary is non-null:
- `sound.setPlayerIndex(primary->getControllingPlayer()->getPlayerIndex())`
- `sound.setPosition(primary->getPosition())`
- `TheAudio->addAudioEvent(&sound)`

`AudioEventRTS::getPlayerIndex` (`AudioEventRTS.cpp:803-820`) returns that stored index when the event is not object/drawable-owned. Miles/GameAudio locality (`ST_PLAYER` / `ST_ALLIES` / `ST_ENEMIES`) uses it so object-based FX sounds (death, hit, upgrade `doFXObj`) only play for the owning/related listener.

`doFXPos` (`FXList.cpp:78-87`) is position-only — no player index. This gap is specifically the object form.

## Rust
Live `SoundFXNugget::do_fx_obj` (`GameClient/src/fx_list.rs:1118-1135`) only forwards `(sound_name, position)`:
- registered `with_audio` hook gets name + coord
- fallback `dispatch_positional_sound` (`gameplay_audio_dispatch.rs:114-120`) is name + xyz only — comment even cites `doFXPos`, not `doFXObj`

No `set_player_index` / controlling-player lookup. Default `AudioEventRts.player_index` is `-1`. Leftover `fxlist_integration.rs` Sound nugget has no `do_fx_obj` override (defaults to pos-only). Leftover Common `ini_damage_fx.rs` `play_sound_nugget` sets `object_id` but is skipped when the GameClient runner is registered.

## Evidence
- C++ `FXList.cpp:90-99` vs Rust `fx_list.rs:1118-1135`
- `game_audio.rs:1861-1907` locality: `ST_PLAYER` requires `owning_player_index == local_player_index`; `-1` never matches a real local player
- Distinct from closed `hq-mooqn` (template name vs Sound nugget name) and `hq-br7up` (runner never called)

## Player-visible
Object-triggered FXList sounds (death, impact, upgrade) authored as player/ally/enemy-local never filter correctly: enemy death voices leak to you, or your own unit-only FX stay silent. World 3D unfiltered events still play.
close_reason: SoundFXNugget::do_fx_obj builds AudioEventRts, set_player_index(controlling player), set_position, TheAudio add_audio_event (FXList.cpp:90-99). Leftover SoundFXNugget now has do_fx_obj override through TheAudio.

title: [Bridge] Leftover BridgeBehavior OCL create uses INVALID owner so debris never spawn
description:
## C++
`BridgeBehavior::doAreaEffects` (`BridgeBehavior.cpp:577`) creates OCL as `ObjectCreationList::create(ocl, getObject(), &pos, NULL, INVALID_ANGLE)` — the bridge is the owner so LIKE_EXISTING / team / producer resolve.

`BridgeBehavior::update` delayed `BridgeDieOCL` (`:781`, `:791`, `:806`) likewise always passes `us` (ParentObject, bone, and random-surface cases).

## Rust
Leftover `execute_ocl_at_position` (`bridge_behavior.rs:1425-1431`) calls `ocl.create_at_position(position, OBJECT_INVALID_ID)`.

Leftover `ObjectCreationList::create_at_position` (`effects.rs:167-182`) looks up the owner and if none, `return Ok(())` with zero objects created.

Call sites:
- `do_area_effects` (`:1108`) on every leftover body-state transition
- leftover `update` Position branch (`:1968`) for delayed BridgeDieOCL (bone / random surface)

Only `Bone:ParentObject` uses `execute_ocl_on_object` with `self.object_id` and can spawn.

This is a leftover BridgeBehavior call-site bug, not generic leftover OCL. Distinct from hq-h2wq4 / hq-aczqb (those are dispatch; after dispatch is wired this still no-ops). Distinct from closed hq-3xw1 (sounds).

## Evidence
C++ always passes `getObject()` / `us`. Leftover hard-codes `OBJECT_INVALID_ID`. `create_at_position` fail-closed on unresolved owner.

## Player-visible
When leftover BridgeBehavior actually runs: damage/repair TransitionToOCL / RubbleToOCL debris never appear; delayed BridgeDieOCL rubble/debris never appear unless the INI line uses `Bone:ParentObject`.
close_reason: Leftover BridgeBehavior::execute_ocl_at_position passes owner_object_id into ObjectCreationList::create_at_position (C++ create(ocl, getObject(), pos) BridgeBehavior.cpp:577/781).

title: [Partition] SWITCH_BORDER fog snapshot reads unused GameLogic 40wu grid
description:
## C++
`TerrainLogic::setActiveBoundary` stores/restores fog via `PartitionManager::storeFoggedCells` / `restoreFoggedCells` (`PartitionManager.cpp:4804-4881`) on the same PartitionCell array that `doShroudReveal` / `addLooker` write. Every cell for every player is snapshotted (STORE_FOG / STORE_PERMANENTLY_REVEAL). Live lookers and SWITCH_BORDER share one grid.

## Rust
hq-l8ci closed by wiring `set_active_boundary` (`terrain.rs:2790-2882`) to `capture_shroud_status_store` + `store_fogged_cells` on **GameLogic** `partition.rs` (40wu `PartitionShroudGrid`). Live lookers never stamp that grid:
- `Object::look` (`object_vision.rs:199-205`) → `ThePartitionManager::do_shroud_reveal` → `ShroudManager` (50wu)
- `store_fogged_cells` (`game_logic_impl/partition.rs:443-458`) only iterates **occupied object cells** (`self.grid.keys()`)
- Missing cells are shrouded (`partition_shroud.rs` comment), so the extent walk sees SHROUDED everywhere

## Evidence
C++ one PartitionCell array. Rust lookers: `helpers/object_queries.rs:696-700` shroud_manager. Snapshot: `terrain.rs:2898-2923` + `partition.rs:443-472`. Distinct from closed hq-l8ci (now calls store) and hq-4her/hq-bfby9 (50 vs 40 looker size).

## Player-visible
SWITCH_BORDER on multi-boundary maps (GLA-01 style) resets explored/fog to full shroud. Units that already revealed the next playable strip lose their map memory; only cells that happen to contain registered objects can keep fog.
close_reason: Lookers stamp leftover+live 40wu PartitionShroudGrid; store_fogged_cells walks known shroud cells not occupied object cells so SWITCH_BORDER shares one grid.

title: [Partition] isClearLineOfSightTerrain empty-gates false even with explicit positions
description:
## C++
`PartitionManager::isClearLineOfSightTerrain` (`PartitionManager.cpp`, header `:1436`) lifts each object to eye height (`pos.z + geom.maxHeightAbovePosition`) when an Object* is provided, then `TheTerrainLogic->isClearLineOfSight`. When only positions are passed, it uses those coords. Terrain LOS does not consult an object registry.

## Rust
Leftover `PartitionManager::is_clear_line_of_sight_terrain` (`object/collide/partition_manager.rs:951-1008`) Wave-324 empty-gates **before** using the supplied positions:
```
if dual_world_registry_unavailable() { return false; }
```
Callers that pass `None` IDs still fail:
- leftover weapon `weapon_instance.rs:1119-1237` (`None, origin, None, victim`)
- leftover AI `ai/mod.rs:1733` / `:1925`
- leftover `PartitionFilterLineOfSight` (`partition_filters.rs:329`)

Live host has a separate `world_save.rs` LOS that fail-opens when height data is missing. Leftover crate/AI/weapon path is the blocked one.

## Evidence
C++ terrain LOS with explicit positions. Rust returns false whenever OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty, including objectless calls. Distinct from Wave-324 honesty residual (documents the gate) and host LOS.

## Player-visible
Leftover weapon/AI treat every shot and acquire as hill-blocked on the host-only path. Units will not fire or acquire across open ground when the leftover PartitionManager LOS is consulted.
close_reason: Leftover is_clear_line_of_sight_terrain no longer empty-gates false; explicit positions go to TheTerrainLogic (C++ 4464-4535).

title: [AIPlayer] Host never expires or disbands queued teams
description:
## C++
`AIPlayer::checkQueuedTeams` (`AIPlayer.cpp:2810-2870`) expires `TeamInQueue` by build-time: minimum-built + complete → ready queue; else **disband**. All-built also prepends ready. Idle members with `m_executeActions` run the production-condition script **while still queued**.

## Rust
Live crate `check_queued_teams` matches that. Live host has no expire/disband path. `process_team_queue` (`Main/src/ai.rs:1602-1718`) only removes a team when every work order is complete. `check_ready_teams` (`:1755-1766`) can set `completed=true` after 60s while orders are still short; those teams then sit in `team_queue` forever (`should_build_new_team` caps at `len() >= 3`).

## Evidence
C++ `isBuildTimeExpired` → `disband` vs host no `disband` / no ready-queue move. Host queue cap `ai.rs:1975`.

## Player-visible effect
An AI team that cannot finish (missing factory, cash, tech) occupies a queue slot indefinitely. After three stuck teams the AI stops producing new squads.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: check_queued_teams expires 180s leftover teams; min-built+complete -> ready else disband

title: [AIPlayer] Host acquireEnemy always retargets closest, no keep-healthy or gang-up
description:
## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer::acquireEnemy` (`AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:461-522`) keeps `m_currentEnemy` if that player still has units **and** a build facility. Otherwise it scores enemies by structure-bounds midpoint distance, fudges crippled players to `HUGE_DIST²*0.5`, adds `500²` if another skirmish AI already targets them, subtracts `25²` if they are attacking us. `getAiEnemy` only calls this every 5s.

## Rust
Live crate `acquire_enemy` (`skirmish_player.rs:1566-1705`) matches that. Live host `update_enemy_assessment` (`Main/src/ai.rs:685-726`) every 5s always picks the closest of slots 0-3 with `player.team != self.team && player.is_alive`. No keep-if-healthy, no `hasAnyObjects` / relationship ENEMIES, no gang-up penalty, no counter-attack preference.

## Evidence
C++ `if (m_currentEnemy && !inBadShape) return;` + 500/25 fudges vs host `if distance < best_distance { best_enemy = Some(player_id) }`.

## Player-visible effect
In FFA / multi-AI skirmish every computer dogpiles the geographically nearest human and will flip targets every 5s if another base is slightly closer. Retail AIs split pressure and finish a healthy current enemy.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: acquireEnemy keep-healthy + structure-bounds score + 500/25 gang-up fudges

title: [AIPlayer] Host cluster mines use value-grid not approach-path
description:
## C++
`AISkirmishPlayer::computeSuperweaponTarget` (`AISkirmishPlayer.cpp:1111-1153`) special-cases `SPECIAL_CLUSTER_MINES` / `NUKE_SPECIAL_CLUSTER_MINES`: pick `SkirmCenter`/`SkirmFlank`/`SkirmBackdoor` + start index, `getClosestWaypointOnPath` from `m_baseCenter`, else enemy structure-bounds center; offset by `m_baseRadius` along that vector so mines land on the AI's own approach.

## Rust
Live crate `AISkirmishPlayer::compute_superweapon_target` (`skirmish_player.rs:565-653`) matches that. Live host `try_fire_ready_special_powers` (`Main/src/ai.rs:2615-2665`) sends **every** ready power — including cluster mines — through leftover `compute_superweapon_target` (`:2670-2787`), which is only the solo value-grid (enemy structure bounds / map extent). No `SkirmCenter`/`Flank`/`Backdoor` path.

## Evidence
C++ `if (power->getSpecialPowerType() == SPECIAL_CLUSTER_MINES || ... NUKE_...)` vs host `self.compute_superweapon_target(game_logic, enemy_team, 50.0, !sneak)` for all powers.

## Player-visible effect
China/GLA cluster mines drop on the enemy value centroid instead of mining the AI's own front/flank/backdoor approach. Players walk into empty approach lanes; mines appear inside the enemy base.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: ClusterMines/NukeDrop target own approach ring not value-grid centroid

title: [AIPlayer] Host skillset is hardcoded SkillSet1, never random AISideInfo
description:
## C++
`AIPlayer::doUpgradesAndSkills` (`AIPlayer.cpp:2908-2977`) early-outs without science points, finds `AISideInfo` for the player's side, then if `m_skillsetSelector == INVALID` picks among defined SkillSet2-5 (`limit` 0-4). Skirmish uses `GameLogicRandomValue(0, limit)`; solo stays 0. It then purchases each science in that skillset via `isCapableOfPurchasingScience` / `attemptToPurchaseScience`.

## Rust
Live crate `do_upgrades_and_skills` (`impl_runtime.rs:451-573`) matches that. Live host `try_purchase_skillset_science` (`Main/src/ai.rs:1812-1823`) walks a hardcoded per-faction name list (`skillset_science_candidates`, `:1778-1809`) that is always SkillSet1-shaped (Paladin/Nuke/Scud path). It never reads `AISideInfo`, never randomizes SkillSet2-5, never calls `selectSkillset`.

## Evidence
C++ `m_skillsetSelector = GameLogicRandomValue(0, limit)` vs host `for name in self.skillset_science_candidates()`. Leftover Common `Player::set_skillset` (`player.rs:3823-3826`) is still `// Would call ai.selectSkillset()`.

## Player-visible effect
Every skirmish AI on a side buys the same general powers. Retail SkillSet2-5 variants (different airstrikes / bounties / artillery ranks) never appear.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: random AISideInfo SkillSet1-5 selector + select_skillset + purchase chosen set

title: [AIPlayer] Host checkReadyTeams only marks completed after 60s
description:
## C++
`AIPlayer::checkReadyTeams` (`AIPlayer.cpp:2729-2803`) walks the **ready** queue. A team activates when all members are idle, when any member is idle and the prototype has `m_executeActions` plus a production-condition script action, or when `m_frameStarted + 60*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND` has passed. Activation `setActive()`s the team (OnCreate scripts), `joinTeam()`s reinforcements, and `clearTeamFlags()` for skirmish.

## Rust
Live crate `AIPlayer::check_ready_teams` (`impl_runtime.rs:100-240`) matches that. The **live host** (`Main/src/ai.rs:332-343`) ticks leftover `AIPlayer::check_ready_teams` (`ai.rs:1755-1766`) instead: it only walks the **build** queue and sets `team.completed = true` after 60s from enqueue. No idle check, no execute-actions shortcut, no `setActive` / OnCreate, no reinforcement join.

## Evidence
C++ ready-queue activate vs host `if current_time - started >= 60.0 { team.completed = true; }`. Host `process_team_queue` (`ai.rs:1713-1717`) then just `remove`s completed teams. GameLogic crate is unused on the live tick (`world_tick/step.rs:931-937`).

## Player-visible effect
Scripted AI team OnCreate never fires. Teams that have already gathered stay unactivated until an arbitrary 60s from *queue time*, then vanish from the host queue without becoming an active team.
close_reason: Main/src/ai.rs: check_ready_teams walks ready queue; activate on idle/execute-actions/60s

title: [Garrison] Live SUBDUED occupants still fire from garrison
description:
## C++
`isPassengerAllowedToFire` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1691-1699`) returns FALSE when the container is `DISABLED_SUBDUED` (flashbang / neutron / similar).

## Rust
Leftover crate `garrison_contain.rs:514-522` ports the subdued check.
Live `try_garrison_residual_fire` (`drones_and_garrison.rs:574-743`) fires each occupant’s current weapon from a ring point with no subdued / passenger-allowed gate.

## Evidence
C++ `:1694-1698`. Leftover `:516-521`. Live residual fire has no `DisabledSubdued` check.

## Player-visible
Flashbang / neutron-subdued garrisoned buildings keep shooting.
close_reason: try_garrison_residual_fire returns when container disabled_subdued (C++ isPassengerAllowedToFire)

title: [Garrison] Live enter ignores ReallyDamaged, zero HP, and NO_GARRISON
description:
## C++
`isValidContainerFor` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:529-558`): OpenContain kind mask, then health `<= 0` reject, `BODY_REALLYDAMAGED` reject unless `KINDOF_GARRISONABLE_UNTIL_DESTROYED`, then `!KINDOF_NO_GARRISON` plus capacity.

## Rust
Leftover crate `garrison_contain.rs:446-473` ports those extra checks.
Live host `can_contain` / `has_capacity_for` / `garrison_unit` (`orders.rs:533+`, `:802-828`, `buildings.rs:1005-1016`) only require alive + constructed + infantry + distance + `max_garrison`. No body-state, no zero-health, no `KindOf::NoGarrison`.

## Evidence
C++ `:536-556`. Live `buildings.rs:1005-1016`, `orders.rs:802-817`.

## Player-visible
Infantry can walk into a 20% HP house (C++ ejects and refuses re-entry). Heroes / NO_GARRISON units can garrison.
close_reason: can_contain/garrison_unit reject health<=0, ReallyDamaged unless GarrisonableUntilDestroyed, NoGarrison occupants

title: [Garrison] Live stealth garrison still looks occupied to enemies
description:
## C++
`recalcApparentControllingPlayer` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1201-1244`): if every occupant is stealth and the first is not DETECTED, `m_hideGarrisonedStateFromNonallies=true` and MODELCONDITION_GARRISONED is set only when the local player is the apparent controller (or the occupant is detected). Enemies see an empty civilian building.

## Rust
Leftover crate `garrison_contain.rs:1105-1189` ports the hide flag, then Wave 260 no-ops on the live host.
Live presentation Wave 504 (`host_live_presentation_garrison_contain_residual_wave504.rs`) stamps `MODELCONDITION_GARRISONED` whenever `occupant_count > 0`.

## Evidence
C++ `:1201-1244`. Live residual comment: occupant_count > 0 stamps MODELCONDITION_GARRISONED.

## Player-visible
Stealth infantry in a civilian building still show the garrisoned model and occupied pip to enemies. Pathfinders/Jarmen cannot hide in houses.
close_reason: hide_garrisoned_state freeze zeros occupant_count and uses original team color for non-allies

title: [Garrison] GarrisonGun window barrels never appear
description:
## C++
`putObjectAtGarrisonPoint` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:172-194`) creates ThingTemplate `"GarrisonGun"` at the FIREPOINT, copies shroud, then `updateEffects` (`:808-881`) sets `MODELCONDITION_FIRING_A` for `MUZZLE_FLASH_LIFETIME` (except poison). Missing template is a warning; placement still succeeds.

## Rust
Leftover crate `create_garrison_effect` (`garrison_contain.rs:2359-2385`) returns `Err` if `GarrisonGun` is missing, and `put_object_at_garrison_point` (`:1737`) propagates that error after already incrementing `garrison_points_in_use`.
Live host `drones_and_garrison.rs` residual fire never creates a GarrisonGun drawable.

## Evidence
C++ `:172-194`, `:846-851`. Leftover `:2369-2370`, `:1736-1737`. Live `try_garrison_residual_fire` has no effect drawable.

## Player-visible
Occupied windows show no gun barrels or muzzle flashes. Enclosing buildings look empty while shooting.
close_reason: leftover create_garrison_effect warns if GarrisonGun missing; live fire spawns gun + FIRING_A

title: [Garrison] Live ReallyDamaged eject uses Harvestable not GARRISONABLE_UNTIL_DESTROYED
description:
## C++
`onBodyDamageStateChange` (`GarrisonContain.cpp:1724-1732`) is an edge: `newState == BODY_REALLYDAMAGED && !isKindOf(KINDOF_GARRISONABLE_UNTIL_DESTROYED)` then `orderAllPassengersToExit(CMD_FROM_AI, FALSE)`. Firebase/bunkers with that KindOf stay occupied until destroyed.

## Rust
Leftover crate `garrison_contain.rs:1021-1037` uses `KindOf::GarrisonableUntilDestroyed`.
Live host `crates_radar_power.rs:889-968` `check_building_damage_states` comments GARRISONABLE_UNTIL_DESTROYED but skips `KindOf::Harvestable`, then ejects whenever `health.percentage() <= 0.3` (not a body-state edge).

## Evidence
C++ `:1728-1731`. Leftover `:1028-1036`. Live `:906-919`.

## Player-visible
AmericaFireBase / GARRISONABLE_UNTIL_DESTROYED bunkers dump occupants at 30% HP. Harvestable structures (if garrisoned) never dump.
close_reason: check_building_damage_states uses GarrisonableUntilDestroyed + HostBodyDamageType::ReallyDamaged not Harvestable

title: [Rebuild] Hole spawn does not copy the dying building geometry
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleExposeDie::onDie` (`RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:122-126`):
`hole->setGeometryInfo(us->getGeometryInfo());`
Comment: preserve the same amount of space for the rebuilding process. Hole collision / selection / pathfind footprint matches the original palace/CC/scud, not the tiny hole template.

## Rust
Live leftover `maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:1414-1438`) sets team, orientation, health, `is_rebuild_hole`, template, ready frame. It never copies `geometry` from the dying structure. Crate `RebuildHoleExposeDie::create_hole` does `hole_guard.set_geometry_info(geometry)` but is dual-world gated off the live host tick.

## Evidence
C++: `hole->setGeometryInfo(us->getGeometryInfo());`
Leftover spawn: no geometry assignment; hole uses `create_object(hole_name)` template extents (or a synthetic Structure fallback with default size).

## Player-visible effect
A GLA palace / command center / scud hole is the size of the generic hole template. Units walk through the original footprint, selection/targeting box is wrong, and the reconstructed building no longer occupies the reserved pad C++ kept.
close_reason: maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole copies dying geometry+selection_radius (rebuild_dozer.rs)

title: [Experience] AwardXPForTriggering leftover never applied on host
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate` trigger (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1252-1254`) calls `xpTracker->addExperiencePoints(data->m_awardXPForTriggering)` using the object's real `ExperienceRequired` ladder. Retail values include Ranger capture 15, Rebel capture 12, Black Lotus capture 20 (`AwardXPForTriggering` INI).

## Rust
Leftover crate `special_ability_update.rs:1134-1142` grants `award_xp_for_triggering` but (1) is gated off when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty (Wave 296 host-only path) and (2) passes `DEFAULT_EXPERIENCE_REQUIRED` `[0,100,300,600]` instead of the owner template. Live host capture completion (`world_objects/support_states.rs:2396-2450` / `finish_capture_channel`) records academy/EVA/audio and never calls `gain_experience` / `award_experience`. Honesty-only constants `CAPTURE_AWARD_XP=15`, `REBEL_CAPTURE_AWARD_XP=12`, `LOTUS_CAPTURE_AWARD_XP=20` are unused by any grant path.

## Evidence
C++ `addExperiencePoints(m_awardXPForTriggering)` on trigger. Host capture `did_capture` block has no XP grant. `rg CAPTURE_AWARD_XP` is honesty asserts only.

## Player-visible
Rangers, Rebels, and Black Lotus never gain unit XP from capturing buildings. Other `AwardXPForTriggering` abilities (Burton/Jarmen specials that award XP) likewise never promote the unit on the live host.
close_reason: Host capture/SA trigger now calls award_ability_trigger_experience with retail AwardXPForTriggering (Ranger 15, Rebel 12, Lotus 20). support_states.rs + award_experience.

title: [Experience] Host XP scalar is AdvancedTraining name, not tracker field
description:
## C++
`ExperienceTracker` stores `m_experienceScalar` (ctor 1.0). `addExperiencePoints` multiplies `amountToGain *= m_experienceScalar` when `canScaleForBonus` (`ExperienceTracker.cpp:143-145`). Sink forward always multiplies the raw gain by the *source* scalar first (`:133`), then the sink may scale again. `ExperienceScalarUpgrade::upgradeImplementation` (`ExperienceScalarUpgrade.cpp:52-62`) does `setExperienceScalar(get + m_addXPScalar)`. Retail America AdvancedTraining is AddXPScalar 1.0 (net 2×).

## Rust
Leftover crate tracker has `experience_scalar` and applies it on add + sink forward (`experience/tracker.rs:249-270`). Leftover residual `ExperienceTrackerResidual` / `add_experience_points_residual` do the same. Crate `ExperienceScalarUpgrade::apply_upgrade` (`object/upgrade/experience_scalar_upgrade.rs:140-143`) returns false when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty (Wave 448 host-only).

Live host `Object` has no `experience_scalar` field. `gain_experience` (`object/update.rs:489-497`) only doubles XP when an upgrade *name* matches AdvancedTraining. `award_experience` forwards the raw amount with no source scalar. Any other `AddXPScalar` (or stacked scalars) cannot apply.

## Evidence
C++ scalar is a tracker field mutated by any ExperienceScalarUpgrade. Host `rg experience_scalar` under `object/` is empty. Host AdvancedTraining is a string match (`has_advanced_training_xp_scalar`). Dual-world empty gate prevents the crate upgrade from writing a tracker scalar on the live path.

## Player-visible
Non-AdvancedTraining `ExperienceScalarUpgrade` modules never change XP rate. Projectile/rider sink forwards ignore the source unit's scalar (C++ applies source × dest). Only USA AdvancedTraining name-tags get 2×, and only on the destination of `gain_experience`.
close_reason: Host Object.experience_scalar (ctor 1.0); gain_experience and award_experience multiply by tracker scalar; apply_upgrade_tag adds ExperienceScalarUpgrade AddXPScalar. No AdvancedTraining name match on gain.

title: [Rebuild] Completed rebuild never transfers the hole script name
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleBehavior::update` when reconstruction finishes (`RebuildHoleBehavior.cpp:298-310`):
`TheScriptEngine->transferObjectName(hole->getName(), reconstructing);` then destroy worker + hole.
Named campaign/script buildings keep their script name across GLA hole rebuild.

## Rust
hq-ypr5w fixed building→hole transfer at spawn (`maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole` + `transfer_script_object_name`). Completion does not:
leftover `update_rebuild_holes` finished branch (`rebuild_dozer.rs:1564-1582`) clears reconstructing flags, `destroy_object(worker)`, then `holes_to_remove.push` / `self.objects.remove(&hid)`. No `transfer_script_object_name(hole, reconstructing)`.
Crate `finish_reconstruction` does call `transfer_object_name` but is dual-world gated off the live host tick.

## Evidence
C++: `TheScriptEngine->transferObjectName(hole->getName(), reconstructing);`
Leftover complete path: no transfer; `rebuild_hole_transfers_script_name_and_skips_defeated_player` only asserts spawn-time name.

## Player-visible effect
A script-named GLA structure (e.g. NamedTunnel) dies, hole inherits the name (fixed), rebuild completes, and scripts that watch that name go deaf — the new building is unnamed and the hole is gone.
close_reason: leftover complete path transfer_script_object_name(hole, reconstructing) (rebuild_dozer.rs)

title: [Rebuild] Captured GLA buildings never expose a rebuild hole
description:
## C++
`RebuildHoleExposeDie::onDie` (`RebuildHoleExposeDie.cpp:108-151`) is module-based, not faction-based. Gate is: controlling player != Neutral AND `isPlayerActive()` AND not `OBJECT_STATUS_UNDER_CONSTRUCTION`. Then `TheThingFactory->newObject(HoleName, us->getTeam())` so the hole belongs to whoever currently owns the dying building. A USA-captured GLA barracks still has the die module and still drops a hole on the USA team.

## Rust
Live leftover `maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:1377-1384`) after Neutral/active checks still does `if !matches!(team, Team::GLA) { return None; }`. Crate `RebuildHoleExposeDie::on_die` has no GLA-team gate (only Neutral + `is_player_active` + under-construction) but is dual-world gated; leftover host is the live death path (`destroy_list_bounty.rs:110-111`).

## Evidence
C++: no KINDOF_GLA / team==GLA test; only Neutral + isPlayerActive + !UNDER_CONSTRUCTION.
Leftover: `if !matches!(team, Team::GLA) { return None; }`

## Player-visible effect
Capture a GLA barracks/palace/tunnel and then destroy it: ZH leaves a rebuild hole you (or the new owner) auto-rebuild from. Rust the building is just gone — no hole, no free rebuild. Same for any non-GLA owner of a template that authors RebuildHoleExposeDie.
close_reason: removed leftover team==GLA gate; captured GLA exposes hole on owner team (rebuild_dozer.rs)

title: [Rebuild] Hole/scaffold death never destroys the generated worker
description:
## C++
Three sites always `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(worker)`:
1. `RebuildHoleBehavior::onDie` (`RebuildHoleBehavior.cpp:319-330`) when the hole is killed.
2. `newWorkerRespawnProcess` (`:100-105`) when reconstruction dies (`Object::onDie` RECONSTRUCTING → `startRebuildProcess` → kill existing worker) or when a new worker cycle starts.
3. `~RebuildHoleBehavior` (`:77-89`) for non-death destroy.

## Rust
Crate `on_delete` was fixed (hq-h71k, closed). Live leftover host is still wrong:
- `destroy_list_bounty.rs` hole death: `maybe_spawn_rebuild_hole` early-returns on `is_rebuild_hole`; no worker destroy.
- `handle_reconstructing_death` (`rebuild_dozer.rs:1265-1266`) only sets `rebuild_worker_id = None`.
- `update_rebuild_holes` recon-dead branch (`:1586-1588`) same ID-clear, no `destroy_object`.
Worker is destroyed only on successful complete (`:1576-1579`).

## Evidence
C++ `newWorkerRespawnProcess`: `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(existingWorker)`.
Leftover recon-death: `hole.rebuild_worker_id = None;` with the worker object left in `self.objects`.

## Player-visible effect
Kill the reconstructing GLA building or the hole itself: ZH removes the UNSELECTABLE worker. Rust leaves a stray unselectable worker on the map (and after delay may spawn a second one). Distinct from closed hq-h71k (crate destructor only).
close_reason: leftover destroy_rebuild_hole_worker on hole die + recon death (rebuild_dozer.rs)

title: [Projectile] Live missiles skip IgnitionDelay and are always armed
description:
## C++
`MissileAIUpdate` state machine (`MissileAIUpdate.h:58-68`, `.cpp:434-474`): LAUNCH holds locomotor accel/turn at 0 for `IgnitionDelay` frames; IGNITION then plays `IgnitionFX`, attaches exhaust, sets `m_isArmed = true`, starts `FuelLifetime`, and enters ATTACK_NOTURN. `projectileHandleCollision` (`:284-286`) returns immediately while unarmed — the warhead is inert until ignition.

## Rust
Leftover `do_launch_state` / `do_ignition_state` (`missile_ai_update.rs:968-1006`) match C++ but `do_ignition_state` no-ops when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty, so leftover never arms in a host-only session.

Live `HostProjectileLifecycle::Missile` (`projectile_lifecycle.rs:25-132`) parses only `TryToFollowTarget`, `FuelLifetime`, `DetonateOnNoFuel`, `KillSelfDelay`. It does **not** parse `IgnitionDelay`. `CombatSystem` projectiles have no armed flag; `update_projectiles_with_countermeasures` (`combat.rs:1114-1444`) can collide/detonate on the spawn frame. Exhaust is a name peel, not an ignition-gated attached system.

## Evidence
Distinct from closed fuel/KILL_SELF residual already in `lifecycle_step` (`combat.rs:362-415`). Closed hq-jg62 is victim `reportMissileForCountermeasures`, not ignition arming.

## Player-visible
TOW/Patriot/Missile Defender/Comanche rockets fly and explode immediately. Retail missiles drop/coast for IgnitionDelay, then ignite (FX + trail) and only then arm — they will not detonate if they clip geometry during the drop.
close_reason: Live parses IgnitionDelay; warhead stays inert and pose-holds until delay then arms. Leftover do_ignition_state now sets is_armed even when OBJECT_REGISTRY is empty.

title: [Projectile] Live missiles never enter LockDistance KILL snap
description:
## C++
`MissileAIUpdate::doAttackState` (`MissileAIUpdate.cpp:506-530`): if `DistanceToTargetForLock` (default 75) > 0, measure 2D center distance to goal object (tracking) or goal position (coord shot). Non-tracking shots **halve** lock range. Inside that radius: coord shots `aiMoveToPosition(originalTargetPos)` then `switchToState(KILL)`. `doKillState` (`:557-611`) sets `OBJECT_STATUS_BRAKING` so the locomotor cheats onto the target and detonates when idle and within one pristine-speed of the goal.

## Rust
Leftover `handle_lock_distance` / `do_kill_state` (`missile_ai_update.rs:1046-1267`) port this but gate on empty dual-world.

Live `HostProjectileLifecycle::Missile` does not parse `DistanceToTargetForLock`. CombatSystem hit test (`combat.rs:1320-1324`) is `distance <= 5.0` with no BRAKING snap and no 75 / 37.5 lock. Homing only refreshes `target_position` (`:1136-1144`). GameWorld named missile residuals (Humvee TOW, MiG, Raptor, Missile Defender) integrate fuel/Bezier-or-linear peels without a KILL/braking state.

## Evidence
Closed hq-s1mx is leftover physics BRAKING integration (fixed). Closed hq-4hus was leftover lock-distance (closed as implemented in the crate). Live host never consumes that crate path.

## Player-visible
Retail missiles that reach ~75 (or ~37.5 vs ground) are guaranteed hits. Live missiles can sail past, miss, or explode 5 units off a moving jet/tank because there is no lock-distance braking cheat.
close_reason: Live parses DistanceToTargetForLock (default 75, halved for non-tracking), enters KILL and cheats onto goal within one pristine-speed. Leftover lock uses last_known_pos when dual-world is empty.

title: [Projectile] Live projectiles never detonate on bridge decks
description:
## C++
Both modules detonate when an armed projectile leaves a non-GROUND layer for GROUND while still over that layer's XY (`DumbProjectileBehavior::update` `:648-670`; `MissileAIUpdate::update` `:713-739`). They use `getHighestLayerForDestination` (slightly below a bridge → GROUND), then re-query at `z=9999` to confirm the bridge XY, snap to `layerHeight + 2` fudge, and `detonate()`. Comment at MissileAI `:714-716`: needed so Comanche rocket-pod missiles target bridges.

## Rust
Leftover ports both (`dumb_projectile_behavior.rs:742-769`, `missile_ai_update.rs:864-905`) but leftover update is dual-world gated / unused live.

Live CombatSystem `Projectile` has no pathfind layer. GameWorld Bezier residuals only `set_position` + yaw from delta; no `getHighestLayerForDestination`, no bridge snap, no layer-transition detonate. Structure intercept in `combat.rs:1214-1255` is KindOf::Structure footprint, not bridge deck layers.

## Evidence
Terrain leftover (bridge decks on the pathfind grid) is a different topic (closed hq-5s9pt). This is projectile-vs-bridge-deck detonation.

## Player-visible
Shells and missiles fly through bridge decks and explode on the river/ground below. Retail armed projectiles that drop through a bridge XY detonate on the deck (Comanche pods vs bridges, artillery hitting elevated roads).
close_reason: Live finish_flight_step uses TheTerrainLogic getHighestLayerForDestination; armed projectiles leaving non-GROUND for GROUND while still over the old XY snap to layerHeight+2 and detonate.

title: [Projectile] Live DumbProjectile FlightPathAdjust never retargets movers
description:
## C++
`DumbProjectileBehavior::update` (`DumbProjectileBehavior.cpp:577-606`): when `victimID` is valid and `FlightPathAdjustDistPerSecond` (parsed via `parseVelocityReal` into per-frame) > 0, re-read the victim geometry center, clamp the end-point move to that per-frame budget, then `calcFlightPath(false)` so remaining Bezier segments retarget the moving unit. Used by long-arc artillery (Neutron/Nuke/Inferno-style shells).

## Rust
Leftover `update` (`dumb_projectile_behavior.rs:1128-1162`) ports the clamp + `init_flight_path(false, false)` but is dual-world gated.

Live `HostProjectileLifecycle::DumbProjectile` does not parse `FlightPathAdjustDistPerSecond`. CombatSystem only homes when `is_homing` (Missile `TryToFollowTarget`). GameWorld shell residuals freeze `*_aim` at spawn (`update_inferno_shell_projectiles` reads `inferno_shell_aim` once; same for flashbang/nuke/neutron). `host_neutron_shell.rs:26` honesty: "Not full FlightPathAdjustDistPerSecond live seeker retarget matrix".

## Evidence
Not closed under Bezier/entity-model beads. Distinct from missile TryToFollowTarget (already in live lifecycle). This is the DumbProjectile moving-victim end-point slide.

## Player-visible
Inferno/Nuke/Neutron shells land on the launch-time aim point. A tank that drives out from under the reticle during the long arc is not followed; retail shells drag their impact up to the authored adjust speed each frame.
close_reason: Live parses FlightPathAdjustDistPerSecond (per-frame) and slides DumbProjectile path_end toward the live victim center each frame then recalcFlightPath(false).

title: [ControlBar] setLowControlBarConfig leftover never moves bar or resizes tactical view
description:
## C++
`setDefaultControlBarConfig` (`ControlBar.cpp:3001-3014`) sets stage DEFAULT, `TheTacticalView->setHeight(0.80 * displayHeight)`, restores `CP_MASTER` to `m_defaultControlBarPosition`, `winHide(FALSE)`, `repopulateBuildTooltipLayout`, `setUpDownImages`.

`setLowControlBarConfig` (`:3030-3046`) sets stage LOW, moves `CP_MASTER` to `(default.x, displayHeight - 0.1 * displayHeight)`, `TheTacticalView->setHeight(full display height)`, `winHide(FALSE)`, `setUpDownImages`.

`toggleControlBarStage` (`:2968-2974`) DEFAULT↔LOW (ButtonLarge / NonCommand_UpDown). Replay playback refuses stage changes (`:2981-2982`).

## Rust
`switch_control_bar_stage` (`impl_science.rs:354-381`) for DEFAULT only `reveal_ingame_command_window()`; for LOW only `ControlBarParent.hide(false)`; for Hidden `hide(true)`. No `winSetPosition`, no tactical-view height 80%/100%, no `setUpDownImages` swap of ButtonLarge up/down art.

`toggle_control_bar_stage` (`:397-403`) matches DEFAULT↔LOW but inherits the no-op move.

Closed `hq-9q8k` was scheme + DEFAULT stage never applied on InGame *enter*. Leftover remaining is the LOW stage contract after enter.

## Evidence
C++ SQUISHED arm is commented out (`:2987-2989`); not filing SQUISHED. LOW is live retail (ButtonLarge).

## Player-visible
Pressing the enlarge/shrink control-bar button does not drop the HUD into a thin bottom strip or expand the world view to full height. The bar stays at the default 80% viewport.
close_reason: setLowControlBarConfig leftover moves ControlBarParent to displayHeight-10% and sets tactical view to full height; DEFAULT restores 80% view and default pos (impl_science.rs).

title: [ControlBar] updateContextPurchaseScience leftover never writes ProgressBarExperience
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::updateContextPurchaseScience` (`ControlBar.cpp:434-444`) looks up `GeneralsExpPoints.wnd:ProgressBarExperience` under `CP_PURCHASE_SCIENCE` and `GadgetProgressBarSetProgress` to
`(skillPoints - skillPointsLevelDown) * 100 / (skillPointsLevelUp - skillPointsLevelDown)`.

Called from `ControlBar::update` while the science panel is up.

## Rust
`update_context_purchase_science` (`impl_science.rs:279-290`) only copies `player.get_science_purchase_points()` into `science_state.available_points`. `experience_progress` is set to `0.0` once in `populate_purchase_science` (`:143`) and never recomputed from skill-point level bounds. No leftover lookup of `ProgressBarExperience`.

## Evidence
Not covered by `hq-5n2p` (command-set bind) or science auto-buy beads. Distinct from the overlay show/hide leftover: even if the panel is forced visible, the exp bar stays empty.

## Player-visible
The generals experience progress bar never fills as the player earns skill points toward the next rank.
close_reason: update_context_purchase_science leftover writes GeneralsExpPoints.wnd:ProgressBarExperience from (skill-down)*100/(up-down) (impl_science.rs).

title: [ControlBar] Radar attack glow leftover never toggles ControlBar.wnd:WinUAttack
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::init` binds `m_radarAttackGlowWindow` to `ControlBar.wnd:WinUAttack` (`ControlBar.cpp:1219`).

`triggerRadarAttackGlow` (`:3169-3177`) arms `RADAR_ATTACK_GLOW_FRAMES` and `winEnable(FALSE)` if currently enabled.

`updateRadarAttackGlow` (`:3179-3197`) decrements each frame; on expiry `winEnable(TRUE)`; every `RADAR_ATTACK_GLOW_NUM_TIMES` frames toggles `winEnable` so the attack pip blinks.

Called from `ControlBar::update` (`:1362`). Radar events call `TheControlBar->triggerRadarAttackGlow()`.

## Rust
Leftover `TheControlBar::trigger_radar_attack_glow` (`GameLogic/src/helpers/leftover.rs:447-455`) only stores an atomic. Live `update_radar_attack_glow` (`impl_portrait.rs:66-89`) consumes the atomic and counts frames, then at the blink cadence has an empty comment `// C++ toggles winEnable on/off for glow effect` — never looks up `ControlBar.wnd:WinUAttack` or calls `winEnable`.

`WinUAttack` exists in `gameplay_layout.rs` name list but has no leftover enable toggle.

## Evidence
`RADAR_ATTACK_GLOW_FRAMES = 150` / `NUM_TIMES = 15` are ported (`types.rs:8-9`). The leftover blink math runs; the WND apply does not. No existing bead for radar-attack glow.

## Player-visible
When a unit/structure is attacked, the radar attack pip never blinks. The leftover flag is set from EVA/radar feedback and then discarded.
close_reason: trigger/update_radar_attack_glow leftover winEnable-toggles ControlBar.wnd:WinUAttack at RADAR_ATTACK_GLOW_NUM_TIMES (impl_portrait.rs).

title: [ControlBar] Generals star leftover never swaps ButtonGeneral images
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::getStarImage` (`ControlBar.cpp:1621-1647`) stops flashing when SPP dropped or is 0, then every frame sets `ControlBar.wnd:ButtonGeneral` enabled image to `m_generalButtonHighlight` for half a second and `m_generalButtonEnable` otherwise.

`onPlayerRankChanged` / `onPlayerSciencePurchasePointsChanged` (`:1651-1682`) (local player only) set `TheTransitionHandler->setGroup("ControlBarArrow")` when SPP increased, then `m_genStarFlash = TRUE` and `markUIDirty()`.

`ControlBar::update` (`:1361`) calls `getStarImage()` every frame.

## Rust
`update_star_image` (`impl_portrait.rs:10-33`) updates `gen_star_flash` / `last_flashed_at_point_value` then, when it should flash, has an empty comment `// C++ flashes the general button highlight` — no `GadgetButtonSetEnabledImage` / `ButtonGeneral` image swap.

`on_player_rank_changed` / `on_player_science_purchase_points_changed` (`impl_science.rs:476-484`) only set `gen_star_flash = true` and mark dirty. No `ControlBarArrow` transition group.

## Evidence
`ButtonGeneral` is listed in the wave133 leftover control-name table but the leftover never applies star on/off images. `m_generalButtonEnable` / `m_generalButtonHighlight` are scheme-fed in C++ (`updateUpDownImages`); leftover `update_star_image` never reads them.

## Player-visible
Gaining a generals point does not flash `ButtonGeneral` or play the ControlBar arrow cue. Players get no HUD signal that the purchase-science panel has new points.
close_reason: update_star_image leftover swaps ControlBar.wnd:ButtonGeneral enabled image; rank/SPP change sets ControlBarArrow (impl_portrait.rs / impl_science.rs).

title: [ControlBar] Shortcut leftover update always Available; never writes ready-count text
description:
## C++
`ControlBar::updateSpecialPowerShortcut` (`ControlBar.cpp:3511-3636`) shows/hides the shortcut parent from `hasAnyShortcutSelection()` or `player->hasAnyShortcutSpecialPower()`, then per visible button runs `getCommandAvailability` (most-ready shortcut SP, or select-all + clock overlay from the unit CommandSet SP). Applies `winHide` / `winEnable` / `WIN_STATUS_NOT_READY` / `WIN_STATUS_ALWAYS_COLOR`.

`drawSpecialPowerShortcutMultiplierText` (`:3639-3690`) writes `countReadyShortcutSpecialPowersOfType` as button text when `numReady > 1`.

## Rust
`update_special_power_shortcut_availability` (`impl_science.rs:591-618`) hides if the player is inactive, otherwise sets every visible shortcut to `CommandAvailability::Available` with an explicit comment that `count_ready_shortcut_special_powers_of_type` is not ported.

`SpecialPowerShortcutState.multiplier_count` is initialized to `1` (`:514`, `:707`) and never written. There is no leftover `drawSpecialPowerShortcutMultiplierText` / `GadgetButtonSetText` path.

Presentation honesty (`apply_honesty.rs:529-536`) even asserts leftover shortcuts stay `Available`.

## Evidence
Closed shortcut beads (`hq-2k2b`, `hq-66lf`) cover command-processing source object / reselection, not this ControlBar.cpp leftover update/draw. Closed `getCommandAvailability` beads cover ButtonCommand windows, not the shortcut strip.

## Player-visible
When a shortcut slot exists, superweapons always look ready (no clock). Multiple Paladins / A-10s never show a "2"/"3" ready count.
close_reason: update_special_power_shortcut leftover runs getCommandAvailability and writes ready-count text when count>1 (impl_science.rs).

title: [Bridge] Leftover BridgeBehavior teardown never destroys remaining towers
description:
## C++
`BridgeBehavior::~BridgeBehavior` (`BridgeBehavior.cpp:242-261`) `destroyObject`s any of the four towers still in the world. This is the safety net when the span is removed without `onDie` (script `DestroyObject`, engine reset, destruction-list order).

`Object::onDestroy` (`Object.cpp:722-738`) first walks every behavior module `onDelete`. `BridgeBehavior::onDelete` (`BridgeBehavior.cpp:291-297`) only clears the scaffold ID list; tower destruction is the destructor.

## Rust
Leftover `BridgeBehaviorModule::on_delete` (`bridge_behavior.rs:2103`) is an empty body. Inner `BridgeBehavior::on_delete` (`:743-745`) only clears the scaffold list and is never forwarded from the EngineModule hook.

There is no `Drop` impl to destroy remaining towers. `TemplateModuleBehavior::on_destroy` only runs when the module mask has `DESTROY` (not `DIE`).

Even if leftover `onDie` were wired, silent `destroyObject` / map reset of the span would still leak towers.

## Evidence
C++ dtor loop `TheGameLogic->destroyObject(tower)` vs leftover empty `EngineModule::on_delete` and no Drop.

## Player-visible
Script-destroy or map-reset of a leftover GameLogic bridge leaves four orphan, still-targetable towers in the world.
close_reason: Leftover BridgeBehavior::destroy_remaining_towers on Drop + EngineModule::on_delete (C++ ~BridgeBehavior.cpp:242-261); onDelete still clears scaffolds.

title: [Audio] Leftover TheAudio prefers static position and drops object follow
description:
## C++
`AudioEventRTS::setObjectID` / `setPosition` / `setDrawableID` (`AudioEventRTS.cpp:529-580`) are exclusive: once `m_ownerType` is `OT_Object` (or Drawable), later `setPosition` is a no-op. `getCurrentPosition` (`:705-742`) then follows the live object/drawable each frame and flips to `OT_Dead` when the owner is gone (Decay tail at last pos).

Callers set one owner:
- PUC (`ParticleUplinkCannonUpdate.cpp:1116-1168`) `setObjectID` only (annihilation uses `setDrawableID`; `setPosition` is commented out).
- Train clickety (`RailroadGuideAIUpdate.cpp:119-121,1453-1455`) `setObjectID` at init; later `setPosition` is ignored because owner is already Object.

## Rust
Leftover `AudioEventRts` (`GameLogic/src/common/audio.rs:36-47`) stores `object_id` and `position` independently — no exclusive owner.

Leftover `TheAudio::add_audio_event` (`helpers/audio.rs:369-380`) builds a live event with `with_position` whenever leftover `position` is `Some`, and only copies `object_id` when `position.is_none()`. Live `set_object_id` (`audio_event_rts.rs:851-857`) also refuses once owner is `Positional`.

Leftover PUC helper (`particle_uplink_cannon_update.rs:917-923`) sets **both** object_id and position, so leftover TheAudio always submits a static `Positional` event. After the first leftover clickety, leftover `set_position` (no exclusive owner) makes every later clickety static too.

## Evidence
C++ exclusive owner vs leftover independent fields + TheAudio position-wins mapping. Live `get_current_position` (`audio_event_rts.rs:1463-1496`) would follow Object if leftover TheAudio had set it.

## Player-visible
Particle Uplink / train clickety (and any leftover loop that later stamps a position) stay glued to a spawn/last point instead of following the unit. When the building dies the leftover event never becomes Dead, so the Decay tail is skipped or plays at the wrong spot.
close_reason: leftover AudioEventRts exclusive owner + leftover TheAudio maps Object/Drawable follow not stamped position (helpers/audio.rs leftover_event_to_engine)

title: [Audio] Leftover TheAudio overwrites leftover volume with INI volume
description:
## C++
`AudioEventRTS` default volume is `-1` meaning “use AudioEventInfo”. Callers that want a per-play scale call `setVolume` before `TheAudio->addAudioEvent`. `AudioManager::addAudioEvent` (`GameAudio.cpp:421-425`) copies the whole event; `generatePlayInfo` does **not** overwrite volume. `getVolume` then returns the caller scale (then volumeShift).

Train crush (`RailroadGuideAIUpdate.cpp:465-466`) `impact.setVolume(volAdjust)` from mass/vel μ-law, then `addAudioEvent`. Clickety (`:1453-1455`) plays then `setVolume(speed/10)` so the **next** join uses the speed scale (event volume is preserved on the reused AudioEventRTS).

## Rust
Leftover `AudioEventRts` default `volume` is `1.0` (`common/audio.rs:67`), not unset. Leftover `TheAudio::add_audio_event` (`helpers/audio.rs:398-400`) always `engine_event.set_volume(info.volume)` and never copies leftover `event.volume`.

Live `generate_play_info` (`audio_event_rts.rs:762-806`) does not restore a caller volume. Live `get_volume` (`:860-868`) would honor a copied leftover scale (`volume != -1`).

Railroad leftover (`railroad_guide_ai_update.rs:832-843`) still `impact.set_volume(volume)` then `TheAudio::add_audio_event`. Clickety (`:1541-1549`) still `set_volume(speed/10)` after play for the next join — leftover TheAudio throws that scale away.

## Evidence
Leftover TheAudio line 400 overwrites every leftover play with INI volume. C++ GameAudio.cpp:421 copies caller volume through.

## Player-visible
Train-vs-unit impacts always play at the INI loudness (a scout crush as loud as a tank). Track-join clickety never gets quieter/louder with speed.
close_reason: leftover volume default -1; leftover TheAudio copies caller setVolume and no longer overwrites with INI volume

title: [Audio] play_audio_event never steal-kills lowest priority when sample pool is empty
description:
## C++
`MilesAudioManager::playAudioEvent` (`MilesAudioManager.cpp:750-833`): after optional `handleToKill`, `getFirst3DSample` / `getFirst2DSample` pop a Miles channel from the AudioSettings.ini pool (`m_num2DSamples` / `m_num3DSamples`). If the pool is empty it calls `killLowestPrioritySoundImmediately` (`:2027-2074`) → `findLowestPrioritySound` and `releasePlayingAudio` on that playing entry, then retries `getFirst*Sample`. New higher-priority fire/UI can evict a quieter ambient.

## Rust
Live `AudioManager::play_audio_event` (`game_audio.rs:1563-1607`) only hard-stops `handle_to_kill` (per-event Limit, already closed as hq-g8vta) then `hook.play`. No `getFirst2D/3DSample`, no `killLowestPrioritySoundImmediately`. `RodioPlaybackHook` (`:2490-2618`) keeps an unbounded `HashMap` of sinks.

`SoundManagerImpl::get_available_samples` exists for bookkeeping but is never consulted to steal a channel.

## Evidence
MilesAudioManager.cpp:753-763 and :823-833 vs game_audio.rs:1574-1585. Closed hq-ljhj / hq-g8vta only cover per-event Limit / oldest same-name handle, not the hardware sample-pool steal.

## Player-visible
Busy battles keep every low-priority ambient/footstep/world SFX instead of evicting the quietest channel for a new weapon/UI sound. Mix is muddier than retail; C++ would drop the lowest-priority sample once the 2D/3D pool is full.
close_reason: game_audio.rs play_audio_event steal-kills lowest-priority 2D/3D sample when Miles sample pool is empty

title: [Audio] Window deactivate notify_audio_focus_change never calls loseFocus
description:
## C++
`WinMain.cpp:451-464` `WM_ACTIVATE` / `WA_INACTIVE` calls `TheAudio->loseFocus()`, activate calls `regainFocus()`. `AudioManager::loseFocus` (`GameAudio.cpp:1071-1082`) snapshots the four system sliders and `setVolume(0, AudioAffect_All | AudioAffect_SystemSetting)`. `regainFocus` (`:1086-1100`) restores them. Alt-tab / deactivate mutes the whole mix.

## Rust
Live `AudioManager::lose_focus` / `regain_focus` (`game_audio.rs:1685-1716`) match C++. Leftover `TheAudio` (`helpers/audio.rs`) does not expose either.

Host `GameMessageHandler::handle_focus_change` (`Main/src/platform/unified.rs:137-161`) maps `WindowEvent::Focused(false)` to `notify_audio_focus_change(false)`. `SubsystemManager::notify_audio_focus_change` (`subsystem_manager.rs:1761-1776`) only logs “Audio focus change handled by AudioManager subsystem” and never calls live `lose_focus` / leftover TheAudio.

## Evidence
WinMain.cpp:455-464 + GameAudio.cpp:1071-1100 vs subsystem_manager.rs:1768-1774 (comment: “In a complete implementation, AudioManager would implement focus handling”). Live lose_focus exists but is unreachable from the window focus path.

## Player-visible
Alt-tab / unfocus leaves music, speech, and world SFX at full slider volume. Retail silences the mix until the window is active again.
close_reason: leftover TheAudio lose_focus/regain_focus; subsystem_manager notify_audio_focus_change calls them on window deactivate

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover capture is not aborted on a new player order
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::update` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:204-226`): if `ai->getLastCommandSource() != CMD_FROM_AI`, `onExit(false)` immediately — any player/script order cancels the special (clears `IS_USING_ABILITY`, ends prep audio, kills non-persistent special objects). Capture also aborts if `isMoving() && isPowerCurrentlyInUse() && !m_facingInitiated` for `SPECIAL_INFANTRY_CAPTURE_BUILDING` / `SPECIAL_BLACKLOTUS_CAPTURE_BUILDING`.

## Rust
Leftover `abort_capture_channel` is only called from the `AIState::Capturing` arm (missing target, illegal capture, failed start-prep). `update_support_states` (`:1140-1151`) clears `pending_special_abilities` and HDB when `ai_state != SpecialAbility`, but **does not** clear `capture_channel` or `using_ability` when the unit leaves `Capturing` (player move/attack). `capture_channel` and `IS_USING_ABILITY` therefore stick until the unit is put back into `Capturing` or the object dies.

## Evidence
C++: `if (ai->getLastCommandSource() != CMD_FROM_AI) { onExit(false); return; }`
Rust leftover: no capture abort on AI-state change; only HDB/pending specials are cleared.

## Player-visible effect
Issuing a move during a 20s Ranger capture (or Lotus 6s hack) does not cancel the capture machine. The unit can walk away still marked `USING_ABILITY` (staying decloaked) and a later return to `Capturing` can resume a stale channel.
close_reason: leftover capture abort on new player order (clear channel + using_ability)

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover missile-defender laser skips prep/persist/abort
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate` for `SPECIAL_MISSILE_DEFENDER_LASER_GUIDED_MISSILES` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:284-298`, `973-986`, `1142-1172`, `1276-1293`): `StartAbilityRange 200`, `AbilityAbortRange 250`, `PreparationTime 1000`ms, `PersistentPrepTime 500`ms. `startPreparation` creates `LaserBeam` SpecialObject and `initLaser`. `update()` aborts if the target is a `KINDOF_STRUCTURE` or stealth-undetected. `triggerAbilityEffect` temp-locks `SECONDARY_WEAPON` and `aiAttackObject`. Persistent prep keeps the beam alive and re-triggers.

## Rust
Leftover `activate_missile_defender_laser_guided` (`missile_defenders.rs:143-203`) if `dist <= 200` immediately `set_active_weapon_slot(1)` + `engage_target_decision_aware` + spawn a residual beam. No 1s prep, no 0.5s persist, no `AbilityAbortRange 250`, no structure abort. Constants `LASER_GUIDED_PREP_MS` / `LASER_GUIDED_ABORT_RANGE` are honesty-only. Crate path is dual-world gated.

## Evidence
C++: approach → 1s prep laser → persist every 500ms → abort structures / stealth / abort range.
Rust leftover: instant secondary lock at 200 wu.

## Player-visible effect
Missile Defender laser-guided fires the moment the target is inside 200 wu, including vs buildings (C++ aborts structures). There is no 1s paint laser before the missile, and the lock does not drop at 250 wu.
close_reason: leftover MD laser 1s prep / 500ms persist / abort 250 / reject structures

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover capture never plays DoCaptureFX flash
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::continuePreparation` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1175-1234`) for infantry/Lotus capture: if `DoCaptureFX`, each prep frame advances `m_captureFlashPhase` by `(1 - prepFrames/prepTotal)/3`. On a falling odd/even edge it saturates the owner's indicator color by `m_selectionFlashSaturationFactor` and `targetDraw->flashAsSelected(&myHouseColor)` plus `m_defectorTimerTickSound`. This is the accelerating house-color flash on the building being stolen.

## Rust
Leftover capture channel (`support_states.rs:2085-2450`) runs authored unpack/prep/pack and fires EVA/infiltration at `start_capture_preparation`. During `CaptureChannelPhase::Preparing` it only decrements `remaining_seconds` and (infantry) `start_power_recharge`. No `captureFlashPhase`, no house-color `flashAsSelected` during prep. `flash_as_selected` runs once on successful defect (`:2364`). `CAPTURE_DO_FX = true` is honesty-only.

## Evidence
C++: `m_captureFlashPhase += increment/3; if (lastPhase && !thisPhase) flashAsSelected(houseColor)`.
Rust leftover prep: timer decrement only.

## Player-visible effect
A building being captured by a Ranger/Rebel/Lotus does not flash faster and faster in the attacker's color during the 6–20s prep. Retail that flash is the defender's warning that the steal is in progress.
close_reason: leftover capture DoCaptureFX flash during prep

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover C4/TNT plant never trips booby trap
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::triggerAbilityEffect` for `SPECIAL_TANKHUNTER_TNT_ATTACK` / `SPECIAL_TIMED_CHARGES` / `SPECIAL_BOOBY_TRAP` / `SPECIAL_REMOTE_CHARGES` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1301-1327`, `1506-1517`) calls `target->checkAndDetonateBoobyTrap(getObject())` before placing the charge. If the mine kills the target or planter, the plant is cancelled.

## Rust
Leftover capture and CarBomb check booby traps (`support_states.rs:2306-2327`, `3124-3165`). `PlantTimedDemoCharge` / `PlantRemoteDemoCharge` (`3003-3080`) call `place_*_demo_charge` with no `detonate_booby_trap_at`. Crate `trigger_ability_effect` ports the check but is Wave 296 gated.

## Evidence
C++: `if (target->checkAndDetonateBoobyTrap(getObject())) { if (dead) return; }` then `createSpecialObject` + `initStickyBomb`.
Rust leftover plant: no booby probe.

## Player-visible effect
Planting Burton C4 or Tank Hunter TNT on a Rebel-booby-trapped building does not trip the mine. Retail the trap detonates and can kill the planter / cancel the plant.
close_reason: leftover C4/TNT plant checkAndDetonateBoobyTrap before place

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover DisableVehicleHack rejects already-hacked
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::triggerAbilityEffect` `SPECIAL_BLACKLOTUS_DISABLE_VEHICLE_HACK` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:1352-1399`) does not refuse an already-hacked target. It `setDisabledUntil(DISABLED_HACKED, now + EffectDuration)` again (INI **15000**ms → 450 frames), refreshing the timer. Allies abort; stealth-undetected abort is in `update()` before trigger.

## Rust
Leftover `AIState::SpecialAbility` (`support_states.rs:2591-2599`) cancels `DisableVehicleHack` when `target_is_hacked || target_is_unmanned`. Command executor `is_legal_disable_vehicle_target` (`abilities.rs:768-776`) also rejects `already_hacked`. Unmanned reject matches C++ ActionManager; already-hacked reject does not match `triggerAbilityEffect`.

## Evidence
C++: `target->setDisabledUntil(DISABLED_HACKED, TheGameLogic->getFrame() + m_effectDuration);` no already-hacked gate.
Rust leftover: `if DisableVehicleHack && (target_is_hacked || target_is_unmanned) { pending.remove; continue; }`

## Player-visible effect
A vehicle Black Lotus just disabled cannot be re-hacked to refresh the 15s timer. Retail lets her re-apply the hack to keep the vehicle locked down.
close_reason: leftover DisableVehicleHack refreshes already-hacked timer

title: [SpecialAbilityUpdate] Leftover plant range is selection radii, not StartAbilityRange
description:
## C++
`SpecialAbilityUpdate::isWithinStartAbilityRange` (`SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp:797-874`) uses INI `StartAbilityRange` vs `PartitionManager::getDistanceSquared(..., FROM_BOUNDINGSPHERE_2D)`. Burton timed/remote C4 and Tank Hunter TNT author `StartAbilityRange = 5` (contact class: range after `PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE*0.25` undersize becomes 0 and requires a real collision with the target). `ApproachRequiresLOS` defaults TRUE.

## Rust
Leftover generic special branch (`support_states.rs:2661-2684`) uses `BLACK_LOTUS_START_ABILITY_RANGE` (150) for Lotus, `BOOBY_START_ABILITY_RANGE + selection_radius + target_radius` for booby, else `selection_radius + target_radius + SPECIAL_ABILITY_RANGE_PADDING` (**4**). Burton/TNT/snipe/hijack take the else arm. No LOS test. Crate range helper is dual-world gated.

## Evidence
C++: `fDistSquared <= startAbilityRange²` (5 wu bounding-sphere / contact).
Rust leftover: `position.distance(target) > selection_radius + target_radius + 4`.

## Player-visible effect
Burton and Tank Hunters plant C4/TNT from well outside retail contact range — often a building's selection radius plus the planter's radius plus 4 wu — so they never have to walk up to the wall.
close_reason: leftover plant StartAbilityRange 5 vs bounding-sphere 2D
