title: [OCL] Live host weapon OCL drops whole list if any nugget needs leftover physics
description:
## C++
`ObjectCreationList::createInternal` runs every nugget (CreateObject/CreateDebris/FireWeapon/Attack/DeliverPayload/ApplyRandomForce). Generic debris applies SEND_IT_FLYING/UP/OUT, RANDOM_FORCE, FLOATING, WHIRLING, PutInContainer, ParticleSystem, fade, DiesOnBadLand, RequiresLivePlayer.

## Rust
Leftover GameLogic implements those nuggets. Live host `execute_parsed_weapon_ocl_at` (`ocl_and_scud.rs`) fail-closes the entire OCL unless every nugget is a generic CreateObject that `supports_host_weapon_generic_ocl` accepts. That helper rejects CreateDebris, flying/out/up/random/float/whirl dispositions, PutInContainer, ParticleSystem, contain-inside, spread, fade, DiesOnBadLand, and RequiresLivePlayer.

## Evidence
C++ ObjectCreationList.cpp:1509-1550 vs leftover nuggets.rs/advanced_nuggets.rs vs live ocl_and_scud.rs:9-84.

## Player-visible
FireOCL / ProjectileDetonationOCL lists that include debris, physics dispositions, or mixed nuggets spawn nothing instead of the authored objects.
close_reason: ocl_and_scud.rs execute_parsed_weapon_ocl_at walks every nugget independently (C++ ObjectCreationList.cpp:1524-1534). Leftover-physics CreateDebris/dispositions are skipped individually instead of fail-closing the whole FireOCL/ProjectileDetonationOCL list.

title: [OCL] RequiresLivePlayer leftover still creates when source or player is missing
description:
## C++
`GenericObjectCreationNugget::reallyCreate` returns NULL when `m_requiresLivePlayer && (!sourceObj || !sourceObj->getControllingPlayer() || !sourceObj->getControllingPlayer()->isPlayerActive())` so dead/missing players cannot spawn useful objects (ObjectCreationList.cpp:1298-1299).

## Rust
Leftover `nuggets.rs` `really_create` only returns None when source exists AND controlling player exists AND `is_player_active()` is false. Missing source, missing player, or a failed player lock fall through and still create.

## Evidence
C++ ObjectCreationList.cpp:1298-1299 vs leftover nuggets.rs requires_live_player block (~308-318). Retail eject/OCL lists set RequiresLivePlayer=Yes.

## Player-visible
RequiresLivePlayer OCLs (eject pilots, leftover death/create) can still spawn units when the source object or controlling player is gone.
close_reason: leftover object_creation_list/nuggets.rs really_create now returns None when RequiresLivePlayer and source is missing, controlling player is missing, player lock fails, or is_player_active is false (C++ ObjectCreationList.cpp:1298-1299).

title: [OCL] ExtraFriction leftover parse stores per-sec not per-frame
description:
## C++
`ObjectCreationList.cpp` GenericObjectCreationNugget field parse uses `parseFrictionPerSec` for ExtraFriction: `fricPerSec * SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL` (1/30) then `setExtraFriction` on SEND_IT_OUT / SEND_IT_FLYING / SEND_IT_UP / RANDOM_FORCE.

## Rust
Leftover `object_creation_list/store.rs` `apply_nugget_property` `"EXTRAFRICTION"` assigns `parse_first_real` with no per-frame conversion. Leftover `nuggets.rs` applies that raw value via `physics.set_extra_friction`. The leftover parse test asserts `ExtraFriction = -0.3` stays `-0.3` (C++ would store `-0.01`).

## Evidence
C++ ObjectCreationList.cpp:703-708,811,1086,1122 vs leftover store.rs ExtraFriction arm and nuggets.rs apply_properties_to_object.

## Player-visible
Leftover OCL create (CreateObjectDie/SlowDeath/InstantDeath/OCLSpecialPower leftover paths) applies ~30× ExtraFriction so debris/objects stop almost immediately instead of sliding.
close_reason: leftover object_creation_list/store.rs ExtraFriction parse uses parseFrictionPerSec: per-sec * SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL (1/30) so ExtraFriction=-0.3 stores -0.01 (C++ ObjectCreationList.cpp:703-708).

title: [CommandXlat] Force-attack leftover unused; live skips canObjectForceAttack spawn/rider
description:
## C++
`evaluateForceAttack` (`CommandXlat.cpp:1315-1391`) uses `canAnyForceAttack` → `canObjectForceAttack` (`:152-244`). Object force-attack is `getAbleToAttackSpecificObject(ATTACK_NEW_TARGET_FORCED, ...)`. Immobile / `KINDOF_SPAWNS_ARE_THE_WEAPONS` re-test the closest spawn slave or contained rider (`getClosestSlave` / `getClosestRider`) before allowing the order. Invalid shot on hint is `MSG_IMPOSSIBLE_ATTACK_HINT`; DO_COMMAND does not post if not possible.

## Rust
Leftover `force_attack_object_result_for_attacker` / `force_attack_position_result_for_attacker` (`attack.rs:291-384`) ports slave/rider rescue but uses `AbleToAttackType::NewTarget` instead of `NewTargetForced`. `evaluate_force_attack_command` (`command_translator.rs:348-378`) withholds the order on NotPossible. Unused on the live OS path.

Live `host_issue_force_attack_from_left_click` (`mouse.rs:514-531`) always queues `ForceAttackObject` or `ForceAttackGround` with no `canObjectForceAttack` / spawn / rider / range gate. Ctrl+LMB and command_system ForceAttack mode do the same (`system_impl.rs:303-325`).

## Evidence
C++ :163-196 `ATTACK_NEW_TARGET_FORCED` + spawn/rider. Leftover `attack.rs:291-384` / `command_translator.rs:348-378`. Live `mouse.rs:527-531` unconditional. Distinct from hq-rq5wu (spawn execution forwarding).

## Player-visible
Ctrl+click / force-attack always issues the order. Stinger sites, Fire Bases, and other immobile / spawn-weapon units accept out-of-range or otherwise illegal force-attacks that C++ would refuse (no-op / invalid cursor).
close_reason: Live host_issue_force_attack_from_left_click and handle_context_click ForceAttack now gate on host_selection_can_force_attack / presentation_object_can_force_attack (C++ canObjectForceAttack CommandXlat.cpp:152-244) including spawn-slave/rider rescue. Leftover force_attack_object_result_for_attacker uses AbleToAttackType::NewTargetForced.

title: [CommandXlat] Double-click attack-move leftover unused; live never issues DoGuardPosition

Terrain double-click falls through to ordinary move/context. `handle_right_click` has no double-click path. Main never reads `UseDoubleClickAttackMove` / `double_click_attack_move`.

title: [CommandXlat] SELECT_NEXT/PREV_WORKER leftover missing; live cycle never lookAt and includes harvesters

## C++

Live host `cycle_friendly_worker_selection` (`selection.rs:158-202`) is presentation-only: idle workers first, then busy, including harvesters; empty list fail-opens to general unit cycle. It `host_set_selection` + select SFX and never `lookAt`/`host_center_camera_on` (unlike `cycle_friendly_selection` for units).

## Evidence
C++ :2599 / :2649 / :2705 / :2765 `KINDOF_DOZER` + :2614 / :2673 / :2718 / :2790 `lookAt`. Leftover `command_translate.rs:168-174` `_` pass-through. Live `hotkeys.rs:1024-1031` Ctrl+Up/Down → `cycle_friendly_worker_selection`; body :172-201 no camera.

title: [W3DModelDraw] LOOP_PINGPONG never reverses; wraps like LOOP
description:
## C++
`AnimClass` / `HLod` playback (`animobj.cpp:941-963`) for `ANIM_MODE_LOOP_PINGPONG` reverses `animDirection` at both clip ends and reflects the overflow frame so the clip plays forward then backward. `W3DModelDraw` states authored `AnimationMode = LOOP_PINGPONG` use this HLOD mode (`W3DModelDraw.cpp` `adjustAnimation` / `Set_Animation`).

## Rust
Leftover Device has no per-frame tick (`wthree_d_model_draw.rs`: `animation_complete` is never set true in production; `current_anim_frame` never advances), so ping-pong never happens. Live `advance_anim_mode` (`anim_playback.rs:33-35`) lumps `AnimMode::LoopPingPong` with `Loop` as `(current + 1).rem_euclid(num_frames)` — a hard wrap from last frame to 0. No reverse direction is stored.

## Evidence
C++: `case ANIM_MODE_LOOP_PINGPONG:` reflects frame and flips `direction`.
Live: `AnimMode::Loop | AnimMode::LoopPingPong => { current = (current + 1).rem_euclid(num_frames); }`.
Leftover: no playback tick.

## Player-visible
ConditionStates with `AnimationMode = LOOP_PINGPONG` (radar dishes, sensor sweeps, oscillating props) snap from the last frame back to frame 0 instead of smoothly reversing.
close_reason: Live advance_anim_mode treats LoopPingPong separately from Loop: reflects overflow and flips anim_direction at both clip ends (C++ Animatable3DObjClass::Compute_Current_Frame ANIM_MODE_LOOP_PINGPONG, animobj.cpp:941-963). W3DModelDraw.anim_direction persisted across ticks.

title: [W3DModelDraw] Attach-bone offset applied to launch pos not turret pivots
description:
## C++
`CACHE_ATTACH_BONE` is defined (`W3DModelDraw.h:254`). Compiled `getProjectileLaunchOffset` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:3282-3372`) does **not** add the attach-bone offset to `launchPos` (that `Adjust_Translation` is in the `#else`). It **does** add `getAttachToDrawableBoneOffset` to `turretRotPos` and `turretPitchPos` (`:3338-3371`).

## Rust
Leftover Device has no `get_projectile_launch_offset`. Live implements the uncompiled `#else` branch: it rotates the attach-bone pivot by object orientation and adds it to `launch_pos.w_axis` (`trait_impl.rs:409-417`, `:469-471`) and never adds any attach offset to `turret_rot_pos` / `turret_pitch_pos` (`:419-436`). Distinct from closed `hq-a9by` (`adjustTransformMtx` visual attach).

## Evidence
C++ compiled path: offset → turret rot/pitch only.
Live: offset → launch matrix translation only.
Leftover: function missing.

## Player-visible
Units with `AttachToBoneInAnotherModule` plus a turreted weapon (technicals, Overlord riders, attached turrets) spawn projectiles shifted by the attach pivot, while weapon aim uses turret pivots that miss that same offset.
close_reason: Live get_projectile_launch_offset now follows compiled CACHE_ATTACH_BONE (W3DModelDraw.cpp:3282-3372 / getAttachToDrawableBoneOffset): attach offset is added to turret_rot_pos and turret_pitch_pos only, not launch_pos.w_axis.

title: [AIAttack] FireWeapon leftover never seeds AttackCommonTarget team victim
description:
## C++
`AIAttackFireWeaponState::onEnter` (`AIStates.cpp:5153-5156`):
`if (victim && obj->getTeam()->getPrototype()->getTemplateInfo()->m_attackCommonTarget) { if (obj->getTeam()->getTeamTargetObject()==NULL) obj->getTeam()->setTeamTargetObject(victim); }`
The first shot from a common-target team seeds the shared victim so squadmates pile on.

## Rust
Live `AIAttackFireWeaponState::classic_on_enter` (`states/attack_machine.rs:984-1008`) leftover-does mood check, `IsFiringWeapon`, and `pre_fire_current_weapon` only. No `set_team_target_object`. Hunt (`states/hunt.rs:187`) still writes the team target; player/AI `AIAttackState` fire does not.

## Evidence
C++: `setTeamTargetObject(victim)` when team target is NULL.
Rust attack_machine.rs FireWeapon onEnter: no `set_team_target_object` (`rg` only hits hunt.rs).

## Player-visible
Teams with `AttackCommonTarget` (many AI squads) do not share the first unit's victim during a normal attack. Squadmates pick independent targets instead of focusing fire, unless they were issued Hunt.
close_reason: C++ AIAttackFireWeaponState::onEnter (AIStates.cpp:5153-5156) now matched by Rust seed_team_target_if_attack_common in states/attack_machine.rs classic_on_enter; leftover ai_states/combat.rs AIAttackState::on_enter also seeds when team target is empty.

title: [AIIdle] doInitIdle leftover skips pathfinder restake for ultra-accurate and loco-less units
description:
## C++
`AIIdleState::doInitIdleState` (`AIStates.cpp:1320-1358`): when `isIdle() && isDoingGroundMovement()` and the unit has a nonzero position, the **first** `pathfinder()->updateGoal(obj, &goalPos, obj->getLayer())` always runs. `ultraAccurate` (loco non-null AND `isUltraAccurate()`) only gates the later `goalPosition` snap. A loco-less unit has `ultraAccurate == false` and still restakes.

## Rust
Live `AIIdleState::do_init_idle_state` (`states/idle.rs:120-157`) leftover-nests **both** `update_goal_for_object` calls under `get_cur_locomotor() == Some` **and** `!ultra_accurate`. Ultra-accurate movers and loco-None units skip the first restake entirely. `set_locomotor_goal_none` / `set_current_victim(None)` still run.

## Evidence
C++: `updateGoal` at `:1346` is outside `if (!ultraAccurate && goalPosition(...))` (`:1347`).
Rust idle.rs:121-124: `if let Some(loco) = ... { if !ultra_accurate { update_goal_for_object(...) } }`.

## Player-visible
Stop a POW truck, parachutist, Spectre/DeliverPayload, railed unit, or loco-less helo mid-move. The pathfinder keeps a phantom goal cell at the abandoned destination, so other AI traffic congests / path-around a unit that is no longer going there.
close_reason: states/idle.rs + leftover move_states.rs: first pathfinder restake always runs; ultraAccurate only gates snap

title: [AIGuard] AttackAggressor leftover prefers machine goal over last-damage source
description:
## C++
`AIGuardAttackAggressorState::onEnter` (`AIGuard.cpp:788-796`) **always** prefers last damage:
`if (body && getLastDamageInfo()->in.m_sourceID) { nemID = sourceID; setNemesisID(nemID); }`
then `findObjectByID(getNemesisID())`. A pre-existing inner/team nemesis is overwritten by the unit that just hit us.

## Rust
Live `AIGuardAttackAggressorState::classic_on_enter` (`guard.rs:1785-1805`) leftover-reads `get_machine_goal_object_id()` first and only consults `get_last_damage_info().source_id` when that goal is `INVALID_ID`. It never `set_nemesis_to_attack` from last damage when a goal is already set.

## Evidence
C++: lastDamageInfo overwrites nemesis unconditionally when sourceID is set.
Rust: `if nemesis_id == INVALID_ID { /* last damage */ }`.

## Player-visible
A unit already Guard-fighting A that gets shot by B stays on A instead of switching to the aggressor. The player who tagged the guard to peel it off A does not get the retaliate switch retail does.
close_reason: guard.rs: AttackAggressor last-damage source overwrites nemesis unconditionally (AIGuard.cpp:791-796)

title: [InGameUI] Radar playMovie never feeds LeftHUD videoBuffer
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::playMovie` (`InGameUI.cpp:3874-3897`) opens `TheVideoPlayer` and allocates `TheDisplay->createVideoBuffer()` onto `m_videoBuffer`. `update()` (`:1598-1608`) decompresses/renders and auto-stops when `frameIndex()==0`. `W3DLeftHUDDraw` (`W3DControlBar.cpp:41-55`) blits `TheInGameUI->videoBuffer()` into `ControlBar.wnd:LeftHUD`, replacing the radar for the duration. Cameo is a separate path (`playCameoMovie` + `W3DCameoMovieDraw` on RightHUD). Script `doMoviePlayRadar` uses this leftover InGameUI movie, not `Display::playMovie`.

## Rust
Leftover crate `play_movie` (`leftover.rs:632-656`) allocates a software buffer on the crate `InGameUI` but never attaches it to LeftHUD, and live `TheInGameUI::play_movie` (`helpers.rs:1683-1693`) never calls that leftover method. Live backend `InGameUISubsystem::play_radar_movie` (`subsystems.rs:1586-1605`) plays via `WindowVideoManager` on `ControlBar.wnd:CameoMovieWindow` or `RightHUD` — the cameo window, not LeftHUD. Rust `w3d_left_hud_draw` (`hud.rs:93-103`) would blit `inst_data.video_buffer` if one were attached; leftover/live never attach InGameUI's radar buffer there.

## Evidence
C++: `VideoBuffer *video = TheInGameUI->videoBuffer();` then `drawVideoBuffer` in LeftHUD. Rust leftover `play_movie` has no LeftHUD attach; live `play_radar_movie` target list is CameoMovieWindow/RightHUD. Distinct from closed hq-d22kx / hq-x6ax (fullscreen Display movies).

## Player-visible
Campaign/script radar movies (`PLAY_MOVIE_RADAR` / demo objectives) do not play in the minimap well. They either fail to start or appear in the right-hand cameo/portrait HUD instead of covering LeftHUD, so the radar never yields to the briefing clip.
close_reason: C++ InGameUI::playMovie + W3DLeftHUDDraw videoBuffer: leftover InGameUI::play_movie attaches SoftwareVideoBuffer to ControlBar.wnd:LeftHUD; live InGameUISubsystem::play_radar_movie targets LeftHUD instead of RightHUD.

title: [InGameUI] popupMessage skips UpdateDiplomacyBriefingText
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::popupMessage` (`InGameUI.cpp:5145-5181`) always calls `UpdateDiplomacyBriefingText(identifier, FALSE)` before fetching the string, converting percent coords, pausing, and loading `InGamePopupMessage.wnd`. Every campaign/script popup is therefore appended to the in-game diplomacy briefing history.

## Rust
Live leftover helper `TheInGameUI::popup_message_with_color_and_host_generation` (`helpers.rs:1883-1935`) fetches text, clamps x/y, pauses, and creates `InGamePopupMessage.wnd`, but never calls `update_diplomacy_briefing_text`. Grep of `helpers.rs` finds zero `update_diplomacy_briefing` references. Leftover crate `leftover.rs` has no popupMessage at all. ## Evidence

Script/campaign popup messages appear as a modal, then vanish. Opening Diplomacy later does not list those lines in the briefing history, so players cannot re-read mission popups.
close_reason: C++ InGameUI::popupMessage (InGameUI.cpp:5150) UpdateDiplomacyBriefingText: TheInGameUI::popup_message_with_color_and_host_generation now calls update_diplomacy_briefing_text(identifier, false) before fetch.

title: [InGameUI] Pause setInputEnabled does not clear force/waypoint/shift/camera modes
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::setInputEnabled` (`InGameUI.cpp:3382-3409`): if `!enable`, `setSelecting(FALSE)`. On the `wasEnabled && !enable` edge it clears force-attack, force-move, waypoint, prefer-selection, and camera rotate/zoom. `GameLogic.cpp:4195-4198` pause calls `setInputEnabled(FALSE)` so releasing Ctrl/Alt/Shift/numpad during pause cannot leave those modes stuck. Distinct from script `DISABLE_INPUT` cinematic teardown (closed hq-pnvs).

## Rust
Live `TheInGameUI::set_input_enabled` (`helpers.rs:1231-1241`) only writes `input_enabled` and clears scrolling. Leftover `set_input_enabled_and_clear_modes` (`impl_input.rs:589-606`) implements the C++ mode clear but has zero callers. Pause hooks call the helper that does not clear modes.

## Evidence
Grep: `set_input_enabled_and_clear_modes` is only defined, never called. Pause path uses `TheInGameUI::set_input_enabled`. hq-pnvs is cinematic mouse-hide / deselect / control-bar tooltip teardown, not this pause mode-clear edge.

## Player-visible
Pause (or any non-cinematic input disable) while holding Ctrl/Alt/Shift/numpad camera, then release during pause: after unpause force-attack, waypoint-queue, add-to-selection, or camera rotate/zoom stay on until the key is pressed again.
close_reason: Live TheInGameUI::set_input_enabled now matches C++ InGameUI::setInputEnabled (InGameUI.cpp:3382-3409): !enable cancels selecting; wasEnabled&&!enable clears force-attack, force-move, waypoint, prefer-selection, and camera rotate/zoom. Leftover InGameUI::set_input_enabled_and_clear_modes uses the same falling edge. Pause GameClientPauseHooks already calls TheInGameUI::set_input_enabled(false).

title: [InGameUI] Double-click attack-move never arms the fading guard-area ring
description:
## C++
`InGameUI::triggerDoubleClickAttackMoveGuardHint` (`InGameUI.cpp:1314-1318`) sets `m_duringDoubleClickAttackMoveGuardHintTimer = 11` and stashes `screenToTerrain` at the click. `handleRadiusCursor` (`:1298-1301`) pins the GUARD_AREA decal at that stash with `opacity = timer * 0.1`. `createCommandHint` (`:2526-2534`) predecrements the timer and holds `FORCE_ATTACK_GROUND` + `RADIUSCURSOR_GUARD_AREA`. `CommandXlat.cpp:3648` / `:3711` call `trigger` after `MSG_DO_GUARD_POSITION` when `UseDoubleClickAttackMove` is on.

## Rust
No `trigger_double_click_attack_move_guard_hint` exists. Leftover timer is constructed as `0` (`impl_update.rs` ctor) and only consumed (`impl_input.rs:745-751`, `:1014-1023`). `handle_radius_cursor` fade (`radius_cursor.rs:126-135`) never runs because the timer stays 0. Crate `CommandTranslator::try_double_click_guard_command` posts `DoGuardPosition` and never arms the timer or stashes the click.

## Evidence
Repo-wide search: `double_click_attack_move_guard_timer` is never assigned except ctor `0`. No `triggerDoubleClick` / `trigger_double_click` symbol in Rust. Distinct from closed hq-d77h (radius overlay never draws at all) — this is the leftover InGameUI arming/stash path.

## Player-visible
With UseDoubleClickAttackMove, double-clicking ground still issues guard, but the fading guard-area ring at the click and the held force-attack-ground cursor never appear; the cursor can flicker back to move immediately.
close_reason: Added InGameUI::trigger_double_click_attack_move_guard_hint and TheInGameUI::trigger_double_click_attack_move_guard_hint matching C++ InGameUI.cpp:1314-1318 (timer=11 + screenToTerrain stash). Leftover handle_radius_cursor fades opacity=timer*0.1 at the stash; create_command_hint consumes leftover+live timers and holds FORCE_ATTACK_GROUND + GUARD_AREA. CommandTranslator::try_double_click_guard_command calls TheInGameUI::trigger after DoGuardPosition.

title: [AIAttack] Team-change abort leftover does not clear the team's common target
description:
## C++
`AIAttackState::update` (`AIStates.cpp:5587-5626`) when `victim->getTeam() != m_victimTeam` and the source no longer considers the victim `ENEMIES`:
`ai->friend_setGoalObject(NULL);`
`if (victim==source->getTeam()->getTeamTargetObject()) source->getTeam()->setTeamTargetObject(NULL);`
`ai->notifyVictimIsDead();`
`return STATE_FAILURE;`

The same team-target clear is in the empty-garrison failsafe just above (`:5605-5607`).

## Rust
Live `AIAttackObjectState::classic_on_update` (`states/attack.rs:827-847`) leftover-handles the relationship abort (`set_goal_object(None)` + `notify_victim_is_dead`) but never `set_team_target_object(INVALID_ID)`. Guard inner/aggressor do clear team target on **their** onExit (`guard.rs:1058-1065`, `:1894-1901`); the main attack state used by player/AI attack orders does not.

## Evidence
C++: `source->getTeam()->setTeamTargetObject(NULL)` inside the team-change abort.
Rust attack.rs:836-843: only `set_goal_object(None)` + `notify_victim_is_dead`.

## Player-visible
When a victim is captured/converted mid-attack, teammates whose team prototype has `AttackCommonTarget` keep the old building as the shared team target and immediately re-acquire it.
close_reason: C++ AIAttackState::update team-change abort (AIStates.cpp:5605-5626) clears team target via clear_team_target_object_if_victim in states/attack.rs classic_on_update; leftover combat.rs abort uses the same helper.

title: [AIGuard] Idle leftover follows a moving guardee at 4 cells Euclidean, not 2 cells per axis
description:
## C++
`AIGuardIdleState::update` (`AIGuard.cpp:717-731`) when guarding an object:
`delta = m_guardeePos.x - pos.x; if (delta*delta > 4*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F) { m_guardeePos = pos; return STATE_FAILURE; }`
then the same for `y`. That is **per-axis** `|d| > 2 * PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE`. Either axis alone trips a return-to-post.

## Rust
Live `AIGuardIdleState::classic_on_update` (`guard.rs:1218-1230`) leftover-uses a 2D hypotenuse:
`threshold = PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F * 4.0;`
`if Vector3Ext::length_sqr(&delta) > threshold * threshold` → Failure.
That is Euclidean distance `> 4` cells (and never updates `guardee_pos` before leaving).

## Evidence
C++: two independent `delta*delta > 4*cell*cell` tests (threshold 2 cells on X or Y).
Rust guard.rs:1227-1229: `PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F * 4.0` then `length_sqr`.

## Player-visible
Units told to Guard a moving object (dozer, hero, vehicle, captured building being packed) wait until the target has wandered ~4 cells away before they follow, instead of ~2 cells on one axis. The protected unit walks out of the inner guard ring with no escort.
close_reason: guard.rs: Idle guardee follow uses per-axis 2-cell threshold (4*cell*cell) not 4-cell Euclidean

title: [AIAttack] Nested AttackStateMachine leftover never picks up a parent goal change
description:
## C++
`AIAttackState::update` (`AIStates.cpp:5629-5633`):
`if (victim != m_attackMachine->getGoalObject()) { m_attackMachine->setGoalObject(victim); }`
Parent-machine retargets (script `transferAttack`, AI hunt/area re-scan that writes the parent goal, another order that only swaps the goal object) are forwarded into the nested `AttackStateMachine` without restarting `AIAttackState`.

## Rust
Live `AIAttackObjectState::classic_on_update` (`states/attack.rs:775-906`) leftover-reads `self.target_id` captured on enter and never compares it to `attack_machine`’s goal. There is no `notify_new_victim_chosen` path on this state (`AIAttackState::notifyNewVictimChosen` in C++ `:5455-5461` sets both parent and nested goals). Leftover `ai/ai_states/combat.rs` `AIAttackState` has no nested machine at all.

## Evidence
C++: `if (victim != m_attackMachine->getGoalObject()) m_attackMachine->setGoalObject(victim);`
Rust `states/attack.rs` classic_on_update: no `get_goal_object` / `set_goal_object` on `attack_machine` after enter.

## Player-visible
A unit mid-attack whose parent goal is swapped (hunt/area re-scan, `transferAttack`, script retarget) keeps approaching/firing the **old** object until the whole attack state is torn down.
close_reason: C++ AIAttackState::update (AIStates.cpp:5629-5633) parent goal is forwarded into AttackStateMachine by forward_parent_goal_to_nested_machine in states/attack.rs classic_on_update.

title: [AIAttack] onExit leftover never clears leech-range mode
description:
## C++
`AIAttackState::onExit` (`AIStates.cpp:5668-5701`) always calls `obj->clearLeechRangeModeForAllWeapons()` after clearing `IS_FIRING/IS_AIMING/IS_ATTACKING/IGNORING_STEALTH` and `MODELCONDITION_ATTACKING`. Leech-range weapons (Stinger, etc.) get their temporary infinite/extended range turned off when the attack state ends.

## Rust
Live `AIAttackObjectState::classic_on_exit` (`states/attack.rs:909-941`) leftover-clears the same status/model bits, victim, turret targets, and goal object, but never calls `Object::clear_leech_range_mode_for_all_weapons` (exists at `object/object_combat.rs:1831`). Leftover `ai/ai_states/combat.rs` `AIAttackState::on_exit` only clears `IsAttacking` / `IgnoringStealth`.

## Evidence
C++: `obj->clearLeechRangeModeForAllWeapons();`
Rust attack.rs:909-941: no `clear_leech_range_mode` call. `rg clear_leech` in `states/attack.rs` is empty.

## Player-visible
After an attack ends (target dead, stop, new order), a leech-range weapon stays in leech mode. The unit can keep firing at far-away targets as if still locked on, until something else rebuilds the weapon set.
close_reason: C++ AIAttackState::onExit (AIStates.cpp:5690) clearLeechRangeModeForAllWeapons is called from AIAttackObjectState::classic_on_exit in states/attack.rs; leftover AIAttackState::on_exit already calls Object::clear_leech_range_mode_for_all_weapons.

title: [Team] tryToRecruit ignores per-unit AI isRecruitable
description:
## C++
`Team::tryToRecruit` (`Team.cpp:2350-2352`) skips a unit when `getAIUpdateInterface() && !ai->isRecruitable()`. Scripts/AI can mark a live unit unrecruitable even if its team is recruitable.

## Rust
Leftover `try_to_recruit` (`common/rts/team.rs:1891-1969`) has an `is_ai_recruitable` callback but only walks `self.members` (not the player's world objects).
Live `Team::try_to_recruit` (`team/team_members.rs:141-256`) walks `OBJECT_REGISTRY` and checks team recruitability / `DISABLED_HELD`, but never `AIUpdateInterface::is_recruitable`. `set_is_recruitable` exists (`object_queries.rs:202`, `ai_update_interface.rs:2667-2672`) and is unused here.

## Evidence
C++ `Team.cpp:2350-2352`. Live recruit loop `team_members.rs:178-253` has no AI recruitable test.

## Player-visible
AI team-building can steal units that scripts marked unrecruitable (guards, scripted heroes, units mid-mission), pulling them off their assigned team.
close_reason: live try_to_recruit skips units with AIUpdateInterface && !is_recruitable; leftover walks world candidate_ids and already honors TeamMember::is_ai_recruitable. files: team/team_members.rs, common/rts/team.rs, modules/ai_update.rs, object/unit/ai_interface.rs

title: [Team] getTeamTargetObject never clears an invalid common target
description:
## C++
`Team::getTeamTargetObject` (`Team.cpp:1494-1523`) is non-const. If the stored ID is stealthed-undetected-undisguised, effectively dead, contained, or `KINDOF_AIRCRAFT`, it sets `m_commonAttackTarget = INVALID_ID` and returns NULL. The team forgets that target permanently.

## Rust
Leftover `get_team_target_object` (`common/rts/team.rs:1340-1341`) returns the raw ID with no filters.
Live `get_team_target_object` (`team/team_identity.rs:172-208`) is `&self`: it applies the C++ filters and returns `INVALID_ID` but cannot clear `common_attack_target`. Hunt/guard (`ai/states/hunt.rs:107`, `ai/guard.rs:686`) re-query every frame.

## Evidence
C++ mutates `m_commonAttackTarget` on reject. Live method is immutable and leaves the ID. Leftover has no stealth/dead/contain/aircraft checks.

## Player-visible
A team common-attack target that cloaks, dies, garrison, or is an aircraft is forgotten in retail and remembered in Rust. When stealth drops or the occupant exits, the whole team resumes focusing that unit.
close_reason: live get_team_target_object clears Cell common_attack_target on stealth/dead/contained/aircraft/missing; leftover get_team_target_object is &mut and clears via TeamMember filters. files: team/team_identity.rs, team/team_struct.rs, team/snapshot.rs, common/rts/team.rs

title: [Team] team delete skips notifyOfTeamDestruction and preTeamDestroy
description:
## C++
`Team::~Team` (`Team.cpp:1336-1370`) calls `TheScriptEngine->notifyOfTeamDestruction(this)`, then every `Player::preTeamDestroy` (`Player.cpp:1618-1623` → `aiPreTeamDestroy`). `TeamFactory::teamAboutToBeDeleted` (`Team.cpp:386-393`) also walks prototypes (`removeOverrideTeamRelationship`) and `PlayerList::teamAboutToBeDeleted` (`PlayerList.cpp:243-248` `removeTeamRelationship`).

## Rust
Leftover `TeamFactory::team_about_to_be_deleted` (`common/rts/team.rs:3238-3241`) only drops the instance from the prototype list.
Live `TeamFactory::team_about_to_be_deleted` (`team/factory.rs:661-663`) only `self.teams.remove(&team_id)`. Empty-team cleanup (`factory.rs:140-142`) uses that path. `ScriptEngine::notify_of_team_destruction` (`named_trackers.rs:1195`) exists and is never called from team delete. `AIPlayer::ai_pre_team_destroy` exists and is not invoked from `~Team`.

## Evidence
No `notify_of_team_destruction(` callers outside its definition. Live factory delete does not touch PlayerList relationships or AI queues.

## Player-visible
When a non-singleton team empties or is deleted, sequential team scripts keep running, AI build queues are not dropped via the destructor, and leftover team-relationship overrides still apply.
close_reason: live team_about_to_be_deleted notifies ScriptEngine, Player::preTeamDestroy/aiPreTeamDestroy, prototype override + PlayerList removeTeamRelationship, then setTeam(NULL). leftover factory sink + prototype remove_override. files: team/factory.rs, common/rts/team.rs, skirmish_player.rs

title: [Team] transferUnitsTo moves IDs without Object::setTeam
description:
## C++
`Team::transferUnitsTo` (`Team.cpp:2284-2292`) walks members and calls `obj->setTeam(newTeam)` so each object updates team pointer, player membership, and `becomingTeamMember`.

## Rust
Leftover `Team::transfer_units_to` (`common/rts/team.rs:1876-1884`) drains IDs onto the target list only.
Live `Team::transfer_units_to` (`team/team_actions.rs:8-17`) clones member IDs, `add_member`/`remove_member` on the Team structs, and never calls `Object::set_team`. `TeamInQueue::disband` (`ai_player/team_in_queue.rs:187`) uses the live path.

## Evidence
C++ `setTeam` vs live ID shuffle. No `set_team` / `setTeam` in `team_actions.rs`. Disband then `delete_team` on the emptied instance.

## Player-visible
Cancelled/disbanded AI teams leave units believing they are still on the old team. Default-team member lists and object team IDs diverge; those units miss default-team scripts, recruit rules, and player membership updates.
close_reason: live transfer_units_to calls Object::set_team on factory Arc then add/remove members; leftover transfer_units_to calls TeamCommandSink::set_object_team. files: team/team_actions.rs, common/rts/team.rs

title: [Particle] Moving emitters skip inter-frame burst spread
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystem::generateParticleInfo` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1734-1758`) spreads a burst along the emitter’s last-to-current motion:

```
emissionAdjustment = (1 - particleNum/particleCount) * (m_pos - m_lastPos);
info.m_pos = (m_transform * localPos) - emissionAdjustment;
```

`m_isFirstPos` seeds `m_lastPos` on the first non-identity generate (`:1737-1740`). Vehicle exhaust, missile trails, and dozer dirt therefore stitch along the path instead of stacking at the current pose.

## Rust
Live `generate_particle_info` (`particle_system.rs:1998-2058`) computes local volume pos/vel and never subtracts `(pos - last_pos)`. `set_position` (`:1483-1489`) does keep `last_position`, but generate does not read it. Leftover Main emit has no inter-frame adjustment.

## Evidence
C++ `:1742-1758` vs live generate with no `last_position` / `particle_num` term. `is_first_pos` is stored/xfer’d (`:835`) but unused in generate.

## Player-visible
Moving emitters (tank exhaust, jet trails, missile smoke, dozer dirt) dump each burst on a single point. At 30 Hz the trail looks clumpy / dotted instead of a continuous streak.
close_reason: particle_system.rs: generate_particle_info subtracts (1-num/count)*(pos-last_pos) after transform, matching ParticleSys.cpp:1734-1758

title: [Particle] Wind is applied before velocity integrate
description:
## C++
`Particle::update` (`ParticleSys.cpp:336-356`) order is: accel→vel, vel*=damp, pos += vel+drift, **then** `doWindMotion()` if `windMotion != WIND_MOTION_NOT_USED`. Wind strength uses distance from the **post-integrate** position to the wind origin (`:513-540`).

## Rust
Live `update_particles` (`particle_system.rs:1927-1940`) applies gravity, then `do_wind_motion` on the **old** position, then `particle.update` integrates vel/pos. Wind is therefore one integrator step early and the 75/200 falloff is evaluated at last frame’s pose.

hq-rju8 (closed) fixed wind **defaults** / ping-pong / circular wrap and the NotUsed gate. It did not change this order.

Leftover Main (`:385-392`) adds a scaled wind **velocity** instead of C++’s direct position nudge.

## Evidence
C++ wind is inside `Particle::update` after pos+=vel. Live wind is outside, before `Particle::update`. Same 75/200 constants, wrong evaluation pose.

## Player-visible
Ping-pong / circular wind (flags, smoke, fire, dust) lags the emitter by one frame and uses the wrong falloff, so gusts look stiffer and trails detach from moving units.
close_reason: particle_system.rs: do_wind_motion runs after Particle::update integrate, matching ParticleSys.cpp:336-356

title: [Particle] Sphere/hemisphere sampling is polar, not C++ cube-reject
description:
## C++
`computePointOnUnitSphere` (`ParticleSys.cpp:1351-1365`) rejection-samples a cube `[-1,1]^3` and normalizes (comment: density is not uniform). Used by:

- SPHERE volume (`:1553-1566`): hollow uses full radius, solid uses `Random(0, radius)` times that unit vector (linear radius, denser at center).
- SPHERICAL velocity (`:1478-1486`)
- HEMISPHERICAL velocity (`:1489-1507`): cube sample with `z in [0,1]`, then normalize. Speed comes from the spherical/hemispherical union field.

## Rust
Live `compute_particle_position` sphere (`particle_system.rs:2111-2130`) uses uniform θ∈[0,2π], φ∈[0,π] (pole-clustered). Solid sphere uses `r = u^(1/3) * radius` (uniform **volume**, not C++ linear radius).

Hemispherical velocity (`:2183-2191`) uses φ∈[0, π/2] spherical coords, not the C++ cube-octant reject.

Leftover Main uses the same spherical-coord style.

## Evidence
C++ cube-reject + linear radius vs live θ/φ + cube-root radius. Hemisphere: C++ `Random(-1,1)` x/y and `Random(0,1)` z vs live polar.

## Player-visible
Spherical explosions/smoke cluster differently (poles vs cube corners). Solid sphere bursts fill the volume instead of piling toward the center. Hemispherical spray (fountains, dirt) has a different angular density.
close_reason: particle_system.rs: sphere/hemisphere use cube-reject normalize + linear radius, matching ParticleSys.cpp:1351-1566

title: [Particle] Line volume omits VolLineStart offset
description:
## C++
`computeParticlePosition` LINE (`ParticleSys.cpp:1618-1634`):

```
start = m_emissionVolume.line.start;
end   = m_emissionVolume.line.end;
newPos = start + t * (end - start);
```

`VolLineStart` / `VolLineEnd` are parsed into that pair (`:2649-2650`). The segment is then scaled by particleScale and transformed.

## Rust
Live `compute_particle_position` (`particle_system.rs:2070-2072`):

```
EmissionVolume::Line { start, end } => (end - start) * t
```

`start` is ignored. The segment is parallel to the authored line but originates at local 0. Leftover Main has no LINE volume.

## Evidence
C++ includes `start +`. Live multiplies only the delta. INI fields `VolLineStart`/`VolLineEnd` are parsed (`particle_ini_loader.rs` VolumeType LINE) but start never reaches spawn.

## Player-visible
Line emitters not centered on the origin (beam sparks, muzzle streaks, scorch lines) spawn shifted by `-VolLineStart`. A line from (-5,0,0)–(5,0,0) becomes (0,0,0)–(10,0,0).
close_reason: particle_system.rs: LINE volume is start + t*(end-start), matching ParticleSys.cpp:1618-1634

title: [Particle] Solid cylinder radius is area-uniform, not C++ linear
description:
## C++
Solid CYLINDER volume (`ParticleSys.cpp:1536-1548`):

```
radius = GameClientRandomValueReal(0.0f, cylinder.radius);  // linear, not sqrt
angle  = GameClientRandomValueReal(0, 2π);
z      = GameClientRandomValueReal(-halfLength, halfLength);
```

Hollow uses the full radius on the shell. This over-samples the axis (C++ “bug”, but retail look).

## Rust
Live solid cylinder (`particle_system.rs:2142-2146`):

```
let r = rng.gen::<f32>().sqrt() * radius;  // uniform area
```

Hollow surface path matches C++. Leftover Main has no hollow/solid cylinder split.

## Evidence
C++ `:1542` linear `Random(0, radius)` vs live `:2144` `sqrt`. Distinct from sphere sampling (different volume type).

## Player-visible
Solid cylinder emitters (smokestacks, shockwave rings, some weapon flashes) look disk-uniform instead of C++’s center-heavy column.
close_reason: particle_system.rs: solid cylinder radius is Random(0,radius) linear, matching ParticleSys.cpp:1536-1548

title: [Particle] setLifetimeRange is a no-op so weld sparks ignore weld duration
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystem::setLifetimeRange` (`ParticleSys.cpp:2352-2354`) writes `m_lifetime.setRange(min, max)` so subsequent `generateParticleInfo` samples that range.

Only caller: `SlavedUpdate` welding sparks (`SlavedUpdate.cpp:621-623`):

```
weldingSys->setPosition(&pos);
Real time = (Real)(m_framesToWait * LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND);
weldingSys->setLifetimeRange(time, time);
```

Repair sparks live for `weldFrames * 30` particle frames.

## Rust
Live `ParticleSystem::set_lifetime_range` (`particle_system.rs:1793-1796`) clones `template.info()`, mutates the clone, and drops it — a no-op.

`SlavedUpdate::spawn_welding_fx` (`slaved_update.rs:965-996`) creates the system and `set_particle_system_position` but never calls `set_lifetime_range`.

## Evidence
C++ `m_lifetime.setRange`. Live clone-and-drop. Welding spawn has no lifetime call. Distinct from DeletionUpdate/LifetimeUpdate `set_lifetime_range` (those are object modules, not ParticleSystem).

## Player-visible
Chinook / worker / dozer repair weld sparks use the INI template Lifetime (often a short puff) instead of lasting the whole weld pulse, so the spark stream dies while the unit is still welding.
close_reason: particle_system.rs: set_lifetime_range writes template lifetime via make_mut so generate samples the new range

title: [Particle] Drawable-attached systems never take drawable shroud
description:
## C++
`ParticleSystem::update` drawable attach (`ParticleSys.cpp:1854-1861`):

```
if (attachedTo->getFullyObscuredByShroud())
    isShrouded = true;
```

Object attach (`:1883-1884`) uses `getShroudedStatus(localPlayer) >= OBJECTSHROUD_FOGGED`. Shrouded systems skip emission (`:1970`).

## Rust
Live `resolve_attached_parent` object branch (`particle_system.rs:1719-1726`) sets `is_shrouded` from `get_shrouded_status >= Fogged`. The **drawable** branch (`:1699-1711`) copies position/yaw and returns — it never writes `is_shrouded`.

hq-lf92 (closed) added object fog + destroy-on-missing-parent. Drawable `getFullyObscuredByShroud` is still missing.

## Evidence
C++ `:1860-1861` vs live drawable path with no shroud assignment. `is_shrouded` is only assigned in the object `if` (`:1726`).

## Player-visible
FX attached to drawables (client-only debris, bone systems, some death FX) keep emitting under fog/shroud. C++ goes silent once the drawable is fully obscured.
close_reason: particle_system.rs: drawable attach sets is_shrouded from bound object fog (C++ getFullyObscuredByShroud)

title: [W3DModelDraw] ReceivesDynamicLights=No never disables drawable lights
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw` ctor (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:1745-1750`): if module data `m_receivesDynamicLights` is false, `draw->setReceivesDynamicLights(FALSE)`. INI `ReceivesDynamicLights` is parsed at `:1194`. Drawable defaults the flag true (`Drawable.cpp:425`) and lets this module turn it off. Scene lighting then skips object lights for those drawables.

## Rust
Live parses `RECEIVESDYNAMICLIGHTS` into `W3DModelDrawModuleData.receives_dynamic_lights` (`module_data.rs:180-182`, default true). Neither `W3DModelDraw::new` nor `on_drawable_bound_to_object` (`trait_impl.rs:2-8`) ever calls `set_receives_dynamic_lights`. Leftover Device `wthree_d_model_draw.rs` has no ReceivesDynamicLights apply at all. GameClient `BasicDrawable` already has the flag and the scene path already skips lights when it is false (`scene.rs:1211-1213`) — the ModelDraw ctor never sets it.

## Evidence
C++: `if (!getW3DModelDrawModuleData()->m_receivesDynamicLights) draw->setReceivesDynamicLights(FALSE)`.
Live: field is parsed and unused. Leftover: no apply path.

## Player-visible
Objects authored `ReceivesDynamicLights = No` (props, some effects, authored exceptions) still pick up muzzle flashes, explosions, and other dynamic lights.
close_reason: ReceivesDynamicLights=No applied on bind via client_visual hook; leftover Device apply/setter

title: [SupplyTruck] WarehouseScanDistance unused; AI never gets 2x range
description:
## C++
`SupplyTruckAIUpdate::getWarehouseScanDistance` (`SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:219-226`) returns INI `SupplyWarehouseScanDistance`, doubled for `PLAYER_COMPUTER`. `ResourceGatheringManager::findBestSupplyWarehouse` (`ResourceGatheringManager.cpp:141-163`) then rejects warehouses whose 3D-center distance squared is ≥ that scan² (preferred player dock may override). Wanting with no warehouse in range fails into Regrouping.

## Rust
Crate leftover `ResourceGatheringManager` and `truck_ai.rs:313-320` know scan + 2× AI, but the live host never calls them. Host `find_nearest_harvestable_supply` (`object_queries.rs:40-97`) picks the nearest harvestable pile with `f32::MAX` — no scan cap, no AI 2×. `SupplyTruckMetadata.warehouse_scan_distance` is parsed (`spawn_templates.rs:1192-1195`) and unused on gather retarget.

## Evidence
C++ `SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:219-226`, `ResourceGatheringManager.cpp:141-163`. Host `object_queries.rs:89-96` (`pick_nearest_residual_target` + `|_| f32::MAX`). Distinct from open dozer bored-scan bead `hq-1q4tb`.

## Player-visible
Human trucks drive across the map to any pile. AI trucks do not get the retail 2× scan. Retail trucks give up (and regroup) when every remaining pile is beyond scan range.
close_reason: host find_nearest_harvestable_supply_within + collector_warehouse_scan 2x AI; leftover ResourceGatheringManager already scanned

title: [SupplyTruck] Last-crate SuppliesDepletedVoice never plays
description:
## C++
`SupplyTruckAIUpdate::gainOneBox` (`SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:132-171`): after incrementing `m_numberBoxes`, if `remainingStock == 0` it asks `ResourceGatheringManager::findBestSupplyWarehouse`. Play `m_suppliesDepletedVoice` when there is no next warehouse, or when that warehouse is farther than `getWarehouseScanDistance()/4` (AI scan is already 2×). INI `SuppliesDepletedVoice` is parsed on `SupplyTruckAIUpdateModuleData` (`SupplyTruckAIUpdate.h:127`).

## Rust
Leftover crate `supply_system/truck_ai.rs` `gain_one_box` implements the far/missing-warehouse test and `audio.play_voice_event`, but Wave 298 `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` returns `false` before any increment when `OBJECT_REGISTRY` is empty (the host path). Host live `support_states.rs` Gathering transfers cash via `SUPPLY_BOX_VALUE` and never plays a depleted voice. Host `SupplyTruckMetadata` (`thing.rs` / `spawn_templates.rs:1190-1204`) parses MaxBoxes / scan / delays only — `SuppliesDepletedVoice` is dropped.

## Evidence
C++ `SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:141-161`. Crate leftover `truck_ai.rs:202-206` empty-gate then `:215-252` voice. Host `support_states.rs` warehouse transfer ~3388-3443 (no audio). Host metadata `spawn_templates.rs:1190-1204`.

## Player-visible
Taking the last crate from a pile is silent. Retail plays the authored depleted voice when the next pile is far or gone.
close_reason: leftover gain_one_box no empty-gate; host parses SuppliesDepletedVoice and plays when next pile missing or > scan/4

title: [SupplyCenter] Dropoff never shows GUI:AddCash floating text
description:
## C++
`SupplyCenterDockUpdate::action` (`SupplyCenterDockUpdate.cpp:112-137`): after a positive deposit, hide the popup only when the **center** is `OBJECT_STATUS_STEALTHED` and not locally controlled and not `DETECTED`. Otherwise `TheGameText->fetch("GUI:AddCash")` formatted with the value, at docker XY and **terrain ground height**, color `ownerPlayer->getPlayerColor() | GameMakeColor(0,0,0,230)`.

## Rust
Crate leftover `supply_system/center.rs:115-123` hardcodes `format!("+${}")` at the docker position (no GameText, no ground Z, no stealth hide). Live crate `production/dock_update.rs:1519-1557` adds the stealth hide but still uses `+$N` at docker pos, not ground height / `GUI:AddCash`. Host live dropoff (`support_states.rs:3513-3606`) `credit_supplies` + `record_supply_dropoff_event` only — no floating text. Oil/black-market/hacker residuals spawn `GUI:AddCash`; supply-center dock does not.

## Evidence
C++ `SupplyCenterDockUpdate.cpp:112-137`. Crate leftover `center.rs:115-123`. Live crate `dock_update.rs:1519-1557`. Host `support_states.rs:3598-3606` / `authority.rs:106-119` (`SupplyDropoffEvent` has no text). Distinct from closed crate ScoreKeeper `hq-uuwa` and stealth-grant `hq-53bo`.

title: [SupplyTruck] Wanting failure never regroups to base
description:
## C++
`SupplyTruckWantsToPickUpOrDeliverBoxesState::update` (`SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:487-529`) returns `STATE_FAILURE` when no warehouse/center is found. That failure enters `RegroupingState::onEnter` (`:533-595`): ignore obstacle, pick closest `KINDOF_CASH_GENERATOR` then `KINDOF_COMMANDCENTER` then `KINDOF_STRUCTURE`, and if farther than `REGROUP_SUCCESS_DISTANCE_SQUARED` (225) `findPositionAround` (radius 100) + `aiMoveToPosition`. On idle, success returns to Wanting.

## Rust
Crate leftover `truck_states.rs` `RegroupingState` / `find_regroup_target` ports the kind-of walk, but host never runs that machine. Live host `support_states.rs`: dead/empty source with no next pile (`:3329-3341`, `:3645-3647`) `stop_attack` + `AIState::Idle` in place. Host `SupplyTruckState` has no Regrouping variant (`thing.rs`).

## Evidence
C++ `SupplyTruckAIUpdate.cpp:528-595`. Crate leftover `truck_states.rs:292-390`, `:748-787`. Host `support_states.rs:3329-3341` and `:3645-3647`. Host enum `thing.rs` `SupplyTruckState` Idle/Wanting/DockingWarehouse/DockingCenter only.

## Player-visible
When every pile is gone or out of reach, trucks sit in the field. Retail sends them home to the nearest supply center / command center / building and retries Wanting from there.

title: [SupplyWarehouse] Host collects from 14 units; no close-enough twitch
description:
## C++
`SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate::action` (`SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate.cpp:74-86`): transfer is refused unless 2D bounding-sphere distance² ≤ `(docker->getGeometryInfo().getBoundingCircleRadius()*2)²`. If too far, twitch docker XY by `GameLogicRandomValue(-range, range)` with `range = 0.4*PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F` (4 world units) and return FALSE so AIDock retries. Collection is adjacent, not a 14-unit support radius.

## Rust
Crate leftover `supply_system/warehouse.rs:60-70` decrements a box with no distance test. Live crate `production/supply_warehouse_dock.rs:237-256` ports close-enough + twitch, but Wave 405 `dual_world_registry_unavailable()` no-ops `action` on the host path. Host Gathering (`support_states.rs:1080`, `:3345-3347`) uses `INTERACT_RANGE = HOST_REPAIR_INTERACT_RANGE` (14, the dozer/pad residual) from the warehouse **center** and transfers as soon as that is met. No twitch.

## Evidence
C++ `SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate.cpp:74-86`. `PATHFIND_CELL_SIZE_F` is 10 (`AIPathfind.h:416`). Crate leftover `warehouse.rs:60-70`. Live crate `supply_warehouse_dock.rs:219-256` + empty gate `:432-435`. Host `support_states.rs:1080` / `:3345-3398`.

## Player-visible
Trucks and workers vacuum crates from 14 units away instead of docking against the pile. Retail units that stop short twitch in place until they are actually adjacent.
close_reason: leftover warehouse close-enough+twitch; live crate dock empty-gate removed; host Gathering (r*2)^2 + 4u twitch not 14u

title: [SupplyWarehouse] setDockCrippled never kills or retries ground dockers
description:
## C++
`SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate::setDockCrippled(true)` (`SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate.cpp:118-148`): if there is an `m_activeDocker`, and `m_dockerInside`, **kill** the victim unless `isUsingAirborneLocomotor()` (Chinooks survive). If the victim is only between Approach and Enter, `aiIdle(CMD_FROM_AI)` + `setForceWantingState(TRUE)` so they retry later. Then the base `DockUpdate::setDockCrippled` latch.

## Rust
Crate leftover `supply_system/warehouse.rs:94-101` only sets `is_crippled` and comments that kill/retry is “handled by the AI system” — it is not. Live crate `production/supply_warehouse_dock.rs:474-507` ports kill + idle/force-wanting, but Wave 405 empty dual-world returns `Ok(())` before any of that. Host Gathering never consults warehouse cripple state and has no docker-kill / force-wanting retry.

## Evidence
C++ `SupplyWarehouseDockUpdate.cpp:118-148`. Crate leftover `warehouse.rs:94-101`. Live crate `supply_warehouse_dock.rs:474-481` empty-gate then `:483-506`. Distinct from closed `hq-mo09` (extra `isDockOpen`/`isClearToEnter` gates) — this is the kill/retry side effect of `setDockCrippled`.

## Player-visible
Ground collectors standing in a warehouse that becomes crippled (really-damaged / script) keep living and keep collecting. Retail workers/trucks die inside; approaching ones bounce out and try again. Chinooks should still survive.
close_reason: leftover setDockCrippled returns kill/retry; live crate empty-gate removed; host kills inside ground dockers on ReallyDamaged

title: [W3DModelDraw] Hidden/shrouded doDraw early-return freezes anim and recoil
description:
## C++
`W3DModelDraw::doDrawModule` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:2016-2087`) never early-returns on hidden or shroud. It always: pauses from `getShouldAnimate`, advances completed ONCE/transition/`IdleAnimation`/`RESTART_ANIM_WHEN_COMPLETE`, `adjustAnimSpeedToMovementSpeed`, `Set_Transform`, `handleClientTurretPositioning`, `recalcBonesForClientParticleSystems`, optional `updateBonesForClientParticleSystems`, `handleClientRecoil`. Hide is only `m_renderObject->Set_Hidden` from `setHidden`.

## Rust
Leftover Device `do_draw_module` (`wthree_d_model_draw.rs:320-543`) matches C++ and keeps ticking. Live `DrawModule::do_draw_module` (`trait_impl.rs:50-56`) does `if self.fully_obscured_by_shroud || self.hidden { return; }` after pause, skipping anim complete, AllowToFinish next-state, idle re-pick, movement-speed, turret, particles, recoil, and submit. Distinct from closed `hq-5l6k` science-latch (that unlatched `hidden`); this is the remaining early-return freeze.

## Evidence
C++: no hidden/shroud return in `doDrawModule`.
Leftover: continues the full pipeline.
Live: `if self.fully_obscured_by_shroud || self.hidden { return; }`.

## Player-visible
Stealthed, transported, or fully fogged units freeze mid-anim. AllowToFinish transitions never complete while hidden. Recoil never settles. When the unit is revealed the pose/transition pops instead of continuing from the C++ timeline.
close_reason: live do_draw_module no longer early-returns on hidden/shroud so anim/recoil keep ticking

title: [W3DModelDraw] ParticleSysBone spawn uses bind pose not live bone
description:
## C++
`recalcBonesForClientParticleSystems` (`W3DModelDraw.cpp:2584-2608`) looks up the live render-object bone, temporarily sets the HLOD transform to identity×drawable scale, then `Get_Bone_Transform` so the spawn offset is the **current animation pose in model space**. It then restores the world transform, `setPosition`/`rotateLocalTransformZ`, and `attachToDrawable`. `updateBonesForClientParticleSystems` (`:2653-2699`) only runs when `ParticlesAttachedToAnimatedBones` is set.

## Rust
Leftover Device `recalc_bones_for_client_particle_systems` / `update_bones_for_client_particle_systems` (`wthree_d_model_draw.rs:777-787`) are empty stubs ("not yet wired"). Live does create systems (`draw.rs:421-484`) but samples `find_pristine_bone_by_name` (bind-pose cache), not the current HLOD bone under an identity transform. Live `update_bones_for_client_particle_systems` (`:487-525`) only runs when `particles_attached_to_animated_bones` is true — same gate as C++ — so the common ParticleSysBone case never corrects the bind-pose spawn.

## Evidence
C++: `Set_Transform(identity*scale); Get_Bone_Transform(boneIndex)`.
Leftover: no-op stubs.
Live: `state.find_pristine_bone_by_name(info.bone_name)` then attach.

## Player-visible
Exhaust, smoke, fire, and other `ParticleSysBone` systems spawn at the rest-pose bone, not the current anim pose. On walking/working units the plume sits at the bind-pose attachment (often the origin or a parked turret) instead of the moving pipe/exhaust.
close_reason: ParticleSysBone spawn samples live bone under identity*scale; leftover recalc/update uses live hierarchy

title: [ChinookAI] Repair lands by altitude instead of MOVE_TO_AND_LAND at the airfield
description:
## C++
`privateGetRepaired` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1177-1196`): ignore if already landing/landed; `canGetRepairedAt`; `setAirfieldForHealing`; `findPositionAround` the depot; `setMyState(MOVE_TO_AND_LAND)` which is `AIMoveToState` then `LANDING` at that XY. Healing `setHealee` only while `CHINOOK_LANDED` at that airfield (`:1042-1056`); full health → takeoff.

## Rust
Leftover `private_get_repaired` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1552-1596`) sets airfield + movement target then **immediately** `set_flight_status(Landing)`. `update_flight_status` flips to Landed as soon as `height <= 1.0`, ignoring XY to the depot. A low Chinook "lands" short of the airfield; `set_healee(true)` can arm while not at the pad.

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:1177-1196`, `:822`, `:1042-1056`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:1552-1596`, `:1860-1863`

## Player-visible
Sending a damaged Chinook to an airfield can put it on the ground anywhere its altitude dips, so it never docks/heals — or starts the heal timer in the wrong place.
close_reason: private_get_repaired MOVE_TO_AND_LAND at pad; land at 3D dest; healee only while LANDED

title: [ChinookAI] Rappellers never get INI RappelSpeed
description:
## C++
`ChinookCombatDropState::update` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:580-584`) after exit: `rappellerAI->setDesiredSpeed(d->m_rappelSpeed)` then `aiRappelInto`. INI `RappelSpeed` (retail 30) is parsed as velocity. `AIRappelState::onEnter` (`AIStates.cpp:511-512`) uses `m_rappelRate = -min(getDesiredSpeed(), gravity*FPS*2.5)`.

Module default rappel speed is `fabs(gravity)*LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECOND*0.5`.

## Rust
Leftover parses `RappelSpeed` into `data.rappel_speed` but `update_combat_drop` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:898-907`) only `execute_command(RappelInto)`. Never `set_desired_speed`. Leftover `UnitAIUpdate` defaults `desired_speed: FAST_AS_POSSIBLE` (`ai_core.rs:197`). `AIRappelIntoState` (`rappel.rs:188-189`) therefore clamps to `gravity*FPS*2.5` (~2.5× retail).

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:580-584`, `:860`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:898-907` (rappel_speed unused at drop)
- Leftover `rappel.rs:188-189`, `ai_core.rs:197`

## Player-visible
Rangers slam down the rope at max rappel rate instead of the authored 30 speed. Drops look instant and miss the staggered rope timing.
close_reason: update_combat_drop set_desired_speed(rappel_speed) before RappelInto; host apply_rappel_speed 30

title: [ChinookAI] Takeoff/landing is height-only — no pad search, supply dump, or layer
description:
## C++
`ChinookTakeoffOrLandingState::onEnter` (`ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:206-260`): set flight status, **while landing `loseOneBox()` until empty**, `scrubVelocity2D(0)`, precise-Z + ultra-accurate, dest XY = current, dest Z = layer height (land) or + preferred height (takeoff). Landing: `findPositionAround` (radius = bounding circle * 100) + `adjustToLandingDestination`, recompute highest **healthy** bridge layer, `setLayer`. Success at 3-unit 3D threshold. `onExit`: taxiing loco if landed; `LAYER_GROUND` after takeoff; restore lift unless dead.

## Rust
Leftover has no `ChinookTakeoffOrLandingState`. `update_flight_status` (`chinook_ai_update.rs:1835-1866`) only compares `pos.z - ground` to preferred-1 (takeoff) or `<= 1.0` (land). `set_flight_status` toggles loco flags but never dumps boxes, never searches a pad, never sets layer, never scrubs velocity.

## Evidence
- C++ `ChinookAIUpdate.cpp:206-313`
- Leftover `chinook_ai_update.rs:1025-1050`, `:1835-1866`

## Player-visible
A supply Chinook that lands to pick up troops keeps its crates. Landing can sit inside other geometry or under a bridge. Takeoff/land is a vertical hop in place, not a searched pad.
close_reason: takeoff/landing loseOneBox, findPositionAround+adjustToLanding, layer dest, 3-unit 3D

title: [AutoHeal] UpgradeMux TriggeredBy never activates heal
description:
## C++
`AutoHealBehaviorModuleData::buildFieldParse` adds `UpgradeMuxData::getFieldParse()` (`AutoHealBehavior.h:81`) so INI `TriggeredBy` / `ConflictsWith` / `RequiresAllTriggers` / `RemovesUpgrades` / `FXListUpgrade` bind. Interface mask includes UPGRADE. Completing the named upgrade calls `upgradeImplementation()` which `setWakeFrame(UPDATE_SLEEP_NONE)`.

## Rust
`AUTO_HEAL_BEHAVIOR_FIELDS` has no mux tokens (`auto_heal_behavior.rs:408-457`); `parse_from_ini` never fills `upgrade_mux_data`. `module_upgrade_kind` has no `AutoHealBehaviorModule` arm and returns None (`object/mod.rs:1142-1307`), so `apply_upgrade_modules` never calls AutoHeal `apply_upgrade` even though the factory UPGRADE bit puts the entry on `upgrade_module_handles`.

## Evidence
Other mux modules (FireWeaponWhenDamaged, MaxHealthUpgrade) parse TriggeredBy and are in `module_upgrade_kind`. AutoHeal is neither. Ctor still honors StartsActive via `give_self_upgrade`.

## Player-visible effect
StartsActive=No AutoHeal modules that wait on an upgrade never turn on. Upgrade-gated heal (and mux FX / ConflictsWith removal) is dead.
close_reason: AUTO_HEAL_BEHAVIOR_FIELDS parse TriggeredBy/ConflictsWith/RequiresAllTriggers/RemovesUpgrades/FXListUpgrade; module_upgrade_kind AutoHeal arm

title: [AutoHeal] Leftover ambulance heal is continuous same-team HP/s
description:
## C++
AmericaVehicleMedic has two StartsActive AutoHeal modules: infantry 4 HP / 1000ms / Radius 100 / KindOf=INFANTRY, and vehicle 5 HP / 1000ms / Radius 100 / KindOf=VEHICLE / ForbiddenKindOf=AIRCRAFT / SkipSelfForHealing. `update()` radius path uses PartitionFilterRelationship ALLOW_ALLIES + Alive + SameMapStatus, FROM_CENTER_2D, then `pulseHealObject` → `attemptHealingFromSoleBenefactor(amount, healer, healingDelay)`.

## Rust
Host leftover `update_ambulance_auto_heal` (`gps_and_fields.rs:1051-1183`) applies `HOST_AMBULANCE_*_HEAL_HP_PER_SEC * dt` every tick, name-matches ambulance/medic templates, and gates with `healer_team == target_team`. Sole-benefactor map is a fresh `HostAmbulanceHealExclusivity` each call (first-healer-wins for one tick only). Comments: fail-closed vs full ally filter / sole-benefactor window / pulse phase.

## Evidence
`host_heal.rs` constants match retail amounts/radius but convert to continuous HP/s. Live `auto_heal_behavior.rs` pulse path exists but Wave 306 empty-registry leftover short-circuits it on the host-only path.

## Player-visible effect
Ambulance heal is a smooth drip instead of 1-second pulses. Allied-other-player units in range are skipped (same-team only). A second ambulance can steal the target next frame instead of losing to the first healer for HealingDelay.
close_reason: update_ambulance_auto_heal pulses amount/delay, ALLOW_ALLIES via player_relationship, sole-benefactor HealingDelay frames

title: [AutoHeal] Held/garrisoned units stop regenerating
description:
## C++
`AutoHealBehavior::getDisabledTypesToProcess()` returns `MAKE_DISABLED_MASK(DISABLED_HELD)` (`AutoHealBehavior.h:115`). Sleepy update still runs while the object is HELD (garrisoned / contained).

## Rust
`AutoHealBehavior` does not override `get_disabled_types_to_process`. The trait default is `DisabledMaskType::empty()` (`lifecycle.rs:311-313`). `ModuleUpdateProxy::dispatch_disabled_mask` does downcast `AutoHealBehaviorModule` and reads that empty mask (`object/mod.rs:2043`).

## Evidence
Countermeasures/StealthDetector correctly return `DisabledMaskType::HELD`. AutoHeal does not. Sleepy update skips modules whose disabled types do not include the object's current disable bits.

## Player-visible effect
Garrisoned infantry and other HELD units with DefaultAutoHealBehavior stop regenerating while inside a building or transport. C++ keeps pulsing heal while held.
close_reason: AutoHealBehavior get_disabled_types_to_process = DisabledMaskType::HELD

title: [GameLogic] PropagandaCenter get_contain is never wired
description:
## C++
`PropagandaCenterBehavior` *is* a `PrisonBehavior` / `OpenContain`. `Object::getContain()` returns that module. `POWTruckAIUpdate::unloadPrisonersToPrison` then `destContain->addToContain(obj)` on the propaganda center.

## Rust
`object_modules.rs:897-916` installs `get_contain()` only from `POWTruckBehaviorModule` or `PrisonBehaviorModule`. `PropagandaCenterBehaviorModule` (which has `contain_handle()`) is never downcast. A propaganda-center object's `get_contain()` stays `None` unless some other contain module exists.

## Evidence
Wiring loop: POWTruck then Prison only. No `PropagandaCenterBehaviorModule` arm. Unload then does `prison_guard.get_contain()` and skips `contain_object` when None.

## Player-visible
Even if the truck list were populated, docking at a Propaganda Center drops prisoners out of the truck and never adds them to the building, so brainwash never starts.
close_reason: object_modules.rs get_contain wires PropagandaCenterBehaviorModule.contain_handle; propaganda_center_behavior.rs handle returns real contained IDs

title: [GameLogic] Prison addToContain skips HELD and yard visuals
description:
## C++
`OpenContain::addToContain` ends in the virtual `onContaining`. `PrisonBehavior::onContaining` (`PrisonBehavior.cpp:145-159`) extends the base, then `setDisabled(DISABLED_HELD)` and, if `ShowPrisoners`, `addVisual` (yard drawable at a random yard-bone point).

## Rust
`PrisonBehavior::contain_object` / handle `contain_object` (`prison_behavior.rs:378-380, 548-553`) call `self.contain.contain_object`, which runs `OpenContain::on_containing` only. `PrisonBehavior::on_containing` (HELD + `add_visual`) is never invoked on the dock/unload `contain_object` path. Same for `add_to_contain`.

## Evidence
C++ virtual dispatch from `addToContain` → `PrisonBehavior::onContaining`. Rust OpenContain `add_to_contain` (`open_contain.rs:784`) calls its own `on_containing`, not the prison override.

## Player-visible
Prisoners delivered into a ShowPrisoners yard never appear as yard models and are not HELD. They can walk/act inside the prison instead of standing as disabled yard visuals.
close_reason: prison_behavior.rs contain_object/add_to_contain/on_containing apply DISABLED_HELD + ShowPrisoners yard visual after OpenContain add

title: [GameLogic] POW truck findBestTarget ignores path existence
description:
## C++
`POWTruckAIUpdate::findBestTarget` (`POWTruckAIUpdate.cpp:625-679`) scans every object, then refuses a candidate unless `isQuickPathAvailable(other->getPosition())` and `TheAI->pathfinder()->quickDoesPathExist(ai->getLocomotorSet(), us->getPosition(), other->getPosition())`. Closest reachable surrendered infantry wins.

## Rust
Live `find_best_target` (`pow_truck_ai_update.rs:791-849`) walks `OBJECT_REGISTRY` and keeps the closest `validate_target` hit. There is no `is_quick_path_available` / `quick_does_path_exist` gate. Leftover file re-exports this.

## Evidence
C++: two pathfinder predicates before accepting closest. Rust: `if true { dist_sq ... closest_target = Some(obj_id) }`.

## Player-visible
Automatic POW trucks drive toward surrendered infantry they cannot path to (water, cliffs, blocked geometry) and stall instead of picking a reachable prisoner or returning home.
close_reason: pow_truck_ai_update.rs find_best_target gates on is_quick_path_available then THE_AI.pathfinder().client_safe_quick_does_path_exist; leftover re-exports

title: [GameLogic] Player commands do not cancel POW truck task
description:
## C++
`POWTruckAIUpdate::aiDoCommand` (`POWTruckAIUpdate.cpp:90-141`): any `CMD_FROM_PLAYER` first `aiIdle(CMD_FROM_AI)` and `setTask(POW_TRUCK_TASK_WAITING)`, then handles `AICMD_PICK_UP_PRISONER` / `AICMD_RETURN_PRISONERS` or falls through to `AIUpdateInterface::aiDoCommand`. A player move/stop therefore cancels collecting/returning.

## Rust
`UnitAIUpdate::execute_command` (`object/unit/ai_commands.rs`) has no POW-truck player-source hook. Only `PickUpPrisoner` / `ReturnPrisoners` touch `pow_truck_ai`. A player `MoveToPosition` / `Idle` leaves `current_task` as `CollectingTarget` or `ReturningPrisoners`. Next `pow_ai.update` (`ai_interface_update.rs:276-282`) still runs `update_collecting_target` / `update_return_prisoners` and re-issues pickup/dock.

## Evidence
C++ player branch: idle + `setTask(WAITING)` before the switch. Rust execute_command: no `set_task(Waiting)` on `FromPlayer`.

## Player-visible
Click-moving or stopping a POW truck does not cancel its POW AI. The truck resumes chasing the old prisoner or redocking after the player's order.
close_reason: pow_truck_ai_update.rs on_player_command set_task(Waiting); ai_commands.rs execute_command FromPlayer hook (hubbed Guard/Attack)

title: [HordeUpdate] Leftover infantry count includes non-HordeUpdate infantry
description:
## C++
`PartitionFilterHordeMember::allow` (`HordeUpdate.cpp:62-87`) requires `getHUI(other)` (the other object has a HordeUpdate module), plus KindOf / AlliesOnly / ExactMatch / off-map match. Workers, hackers, officers, and foreign infantry without HordeUpdate do not count.

## Rust
`update_china_infantry_horde_status` (`tanks_and_upgrades.rs:502-551`) snapshots **all** living `KindOf::Infantry` and counts them via `counts_toward_infantry_horde` (alive + same team + infantry + Radius 30). Recipients are hardcoded `is_china_infantry_horde_unit` (Red Guard / Tank Hunter / MiniGunner), but the **count** is any infantry. GW `infantry_snapshot` (`status_timers.rs:27-44`) is the same KindOf Infantry bit.

## Evidence
C++ filter explicitly `if (!hui) return false`. Leftover comment "any ally infantry counts" is ExactMatch=No, but it also drops the HordeUpdate-module requirement. `bd search` HordeUpdate / in_horde: no matching bead.

## Player-visible
One Red Guard standing with four China Hackers/Workers (or other non-horde infantry) gets leftover horde ROF. Retail does not treat those as horde-mates, so the blob bonus appears when the player has not actually formed a horde.
close_reason: Leftover infantry snapshot now only is_china_infantry_horde_unit / leftover_infantry_is_horde_neighbor (C++ getHUI). Workers/hackers/officers no longer count.

title: [HordeUpdate] Leftover vehicle horde only covers Battlemaster
description:
## C++
`HordeUpdate` is a generic update module. Every object whose INI includes `Behavior = HordeUpdate` runs the Radius/Count/RubOff/decal path and `evaluateMoraleBonus`. Retail China ExactMatch vehicles share that module, not only Battlemaster.

## Rust
Host leftover vehicle membership is only `update_battlemaster_horde_status` (`air_and_mig.rs:1471-1517`, ticked from `world_tick/step.rs:333-340`) filtered by `is_battlemaster_template`. Dragon / Inferno / Gattling tank / Overlord leftovers (`host_dragon_tank.rs`, `host_inferno_cannon.rs`, `host_gattling_tank.rs`, `host_overlord_gun.rs`) have no horde tick. Live crate HordeUpdate is generic but Wave 378-gated on host-only.

## Evidence
Grep of those vehicle leftover modules: no `HordeUpdate` / `weapon_bonus_horde`. Only Battlemaster + three China infantry templates ever set leftover `weapon_bonus_horde`. `bd search` HordeUpdate: no open bead; closed hq-gq4 is the Battlemaster residual task, not this gap.

## Player-visible
Other China HordeUpdate vehicles never get the 150% horde ROF or horde ring when five same-type allies clump. Only Battlemasters (and the three infantry leftovers) do.
close_reason: Leftover vehicle horde snapshot uses is_china_vehicle_horde_unit + same_vehicle_horde_family ExactMatch (Battlemaster/Dragon/Inferno/Gattling/Overlord). Portable payloads excluded.

title: [HordeUpdate] Leftover omits RubOffRadius honorary membership
description:
## C++
When the Radius query does not reach `Count-1` neighbors, `HordeUpdate::update` (`HordeUpdate.cpp:267-288`) still walks that iterator. If any neighbor `isTrueHordeMember()` and 2D-center distance² ≤ `sqr(m_rubOffRadius)`, the unit sets `m_inHorde` (honorary) while leaving `m_trueHordeMember` false. Default `m_rubOffRadius` is 20 (`:101`); INI `RubOffRadius` overrides. Live crate `check_horde_status` (`horde_update.rs:478-504`) ports this pass.

## Rust
Host leftover `is_in_horde` / `is_in_infantry_horde` (`host_battlemaster.rs:337-343`, `host_red_guard.rs:310-313`) is only `nearby + 1 >= Count`. `update_battlemaster_horde_status` and `update_china_infantry_horde_status` comments say "RubOff residual omitted (fail-closed)". GW shadow ticks (`status_timers_specials.rs:317-389`) use the same Count-only test. Honesty files list "Not full HordeUpdate RubOffRadius honorary-member".

## Evidence
No `bd search` hit for RubOff / honorary / HordeUpdate. PLAYABILITY_CURRENT_STATE still lists RubOffRadius as residual. Live crate implements the pass but is Wave 378-gated on host-only.

## Player-visible
A Red Guard or Battlemaster on the edge of a dense blob (inside Radius of the group but not Count-1 neighbors, yet within RubOffRadius of a true member) never gets the 150% horde ROF. Retail grants honorary horde to those edge units.
close_reason: Leftover evaluate_leftover_horde_blob implements C++ RubOffRadius honorary membership (default 20) after Count-1 true-member pass. Host + GW ticks use it.

title: [UnitCrate] Live invents missing templates and skips findPositionAround
description:
## C++
`UnitCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`UnitCrateCollide.cpp:32-67`) looks up `TheThingFactory->findTemplate(m_unitType)` and returns FALSE if missing. For each of `m_unitCount` it `newObject`s on `other->getControllingPlayer()->getDefaultTeam()`, then `ThePartitionManager->findPositionAround` with `maxRadius = 20` from the picker, copies orientation, and plays `MiscAudio::m_crateFreeUnit`.

## Rust
Leftover `unit_crate_collide.rs:112-196` matches that (find_template fail → false, find_position_around 20, default team) but is leftover-only.

Live `execute_unit_crate_behavior` (`world_tick/crates.rs:807-849`) if `!self.templates.contains_key(unit_type)` invents a `ThingTemplate` from the name (`Tank`/`Vehicle` → Vehicle, `Jet`/`Aircraft` → Aircraft, else Infantry) and inserts it. Spawns at `origin + (cos/sin)*(8+i*4)` with no partition legal-position search. Team is host faction `p.team`, not the player's default team.

## Evidence
C++: `if (unitType == NULL) return FALSE;` + `findPositionAround(..., maxRadius=20)`.
Rust live: name-heuristic `add_kind_of` + spiral offset (`crates.rs:820-841`). Retail 2FreeCrusadersCrate is `UnitName = AmericaTankCrusader` / count 2.

## Player-visible
A unit crate whose ThingTemplate failed to load still drops fake infantry/vehicles. Spawned Crusaders (or any unit crate) can stack on the picker or inside geometry instead of finding a clear 20-unit ring. Same-faction teammates can receive the units if host team ≠ per-player team.
close_reason: live unit crate returns 0 if template missing; find_position_around_xz maxRadius 20

title: [HealCrate] Live heals faction Team not picker player
description:
## C++
`HealCrateCollide::executeCrateBehavior` (`HealCrateCollide.cpp:30-40`) does `other->getControllingPlayer()->healAllObjects()`. `Player::healAllObjects` (`Player.cpp:1756-1763`) walks that player's team prototypes and `Team::healAllObjects` (`Team.cpp:1652-1657`) `healCompletely()`s each member. Only objects owned by the picker player are healed.

## Rust
Leftover `heal_crate_collide.rs:239-257` calls `player_guard.heal_all_objects()` (player-scoped) but is not the live path.

Live `execute_heal_crate_behavior` (`world_tick/crates.rs:780-801`) heals every living object whose `o.team == picker.team` (`Team::USA` / `China` / `GLA`). Host `Team` is faction, not a per-player RTS team. Comment at `:26` even says "picker's team".

## Evidence
C++: `cratePlayer->healAllObjects()` on controlling `Player`.
Rust live: `filter(|(_, o)| o.team == team && o.is_alive())` then `write_object_health_authority_aware(o, max)`.

## Player-visible
In a 2v2 or FFA with two USA (or two China/GLA) players, picking a heal crate fully heals the ally's (or rival same-faction) army as well as the picker's. C++ heals only the picker player's units.
close_reason: live heal crate filters owner_player_id not faction Team

title: [CrateCollide] Live pickup skips PickupScience and KindOf PARACHUTE
description:
## C++
`CrateCollide::isValidToExecute` (`CrateCollide.cpp:127-168`) rejects: null/ground, neutral, no `AIUpdateInterface` unless `BuildingPickup`+`KINDOF_STRUCTURE`, `isKindOfMulti(required, forbidden)`, dead, crate `isAboveTerrain` (except building pickup), `ForbidOwnerPlayer` same controlling player, `HumanOnly` unless `PLAYER_HUMAN`, `PickupScience` unless `hasScience`, and `other->isKindOf(KINDOF_PARACHUTE)` (the parachute *object* KindOf, not `OBJECT_STATUS_PARACHUTING`).

Retail SalvageCrate authors `PickupScience = SCIENCE_GLA` (host residual `SALVAGE_PICKUP_SCIENCE_RESIDUAL`).

## Rust
Leftover `crate_collide.rs:249-317` implements those gates (PARACHUTE maps to `KindOf::Parachute` after closed hq-sbxp) but is dual-world empty-gated (`OBJECT_REGISTRY.is_empty()`) and is not the live pickup path.

Live `update_money_crate_collides` (`crates_radar_power.rs:212-393`) is a radius residual: living non-neutral pickers, salvage needs `KindOf::Salvager`/`WeaponSalvager`/`ArmorSalvager`, projectile + `is_parachuting() || name.contains("parachute")` rejected, airborne crates blocked for units. `SALVAGE_PICKUP_SCIENCE_RESIDUAL` is never read. No `HumanOnly`, `ForbidOwnerPlayer`, `RequiredKindOf`/`ForbiddenKindOf` (except projectile), or AI-module requirement.

## Evidence
C++: `md->m_pickupScience` + `isKindOf(KINDOF_PARACHUTE)`.
Rust live: `is_parachute_picker = obj.is_parachuting() || template_name.contains("parachute")` (`crates_radar_power.rs:293-296`). Grep of Main: `SALVAGE_PICKUP_SCIENCE_RESIDUAL` only in `host_gamedata_lobby_residual.rs` honesty.

## Player-visible
A non-GLA player who controls a salvager (captured/hijacked) can pick salvage crates; C++ requires SCIENCE_GLA. Parachuting infantry (status set, not KindOf PARACHUTE) are wrongly blocked from picking crates after landing while the flag lingers. HumanOnly mission crates and ForbidOwnerPlayer death crates are unrestricted.
close_reason: live pickup KindOf::Parachute not parachuting status; salvage requires SCIENCE_GLA PickupScience

title: [Parking] Live+leftover miss HeliPark01 exit/rally contract
description:
## C++
`exitObjectViaDoor` for `KINDOF_PRODUCED_AT_HELIPAD` (`ParkingPlaceBehavior.cpp:752-814`) reads bone `HeliPark01` for hangar/parking pose, then `aiMoveToPosition` to `getRallyPoint()` if set, else to that parking space. `getExitPosition` / `getNaturalRallyPoint` (`859-870`) both return `HeliPark01`. `setRallyPoint` / `getRallyPoint` store `m_heliRallyPoint`.

## Rust
Leftover `exit_object_via_door` does look up `HeliPark01` and follows heli rally. Leftover `ExitInterface` / `ModuleExitInterface` have no `get_exit_position` / `get_natural_rally_point`, so rally-placement UI / default-rally callers cannot read `HeliPark01`. Live `reserve_produced_aircraft_parking_space` only assigns a slot index; no `HeliPark01`, no heli rally, no `getExitPosition`.

## Evidence
